  • Decide, unfreeze and roll back: answer the questions Pacto asks
  • Ladder reference: the exact rules, fields and commands

docs.title: Export services to Backstage
docs.text: pacto export backstage writes the services Pacto knows as one multi-document YAML file of Backstage catalog entities. You commit that one file and point Backstage at it, so no repository needs its own catalog-info.yaml. Every entity says how Pacto knows it, when and how completely.

docs.title: Run the export
docs.text:
The command reads the same sources as pacto fleet: --oci, --root, --k8s, --target-state and the rest. It scans a local directory only when you pass --local, so drafts and fixtures in the working directory never reach the catalog:

pacto export backstage --oci ghcr.io/acme/payments --oci ghcr.io/acme/ledger \
  -o catalog/pacto-entities.yaml

Run it as a scheduled sync job. When a source cannot be read, or the fleet is empty, the command writes nothing, leaves an existing -o file as it was and exits with code 2. A source outage would otherwise drop the services it holds and Backstage would orphan their entities. Pass --allow-partial to write the file anyway; each entity then says partial. A --namespace scope whose namespaces were all read is not an outage: the command writes the file and each entity says partial, since services in other namespaces are unknown.

docs.title: Who sees the file
docs.text: Everyone who reads the file sees what the exporter's credentials could read. Run the job with a reader-scoped kubeconfig or --namespace, and list the --oci sources explicitly. With --k8s the command prints to standard error which namespaces it read.

docs.title: Point Backstage at the file
docs.text:
Commit the file to a repository Backstage can read and add a location to app-config.yaml:

catalog:
  locations:
    - type: url
      target: https://github.com/acme/catalog/blob/main/catalog/pacto-entities.yaml

A Backstage instance that runs next to a checkout can use type: file with the path instead.

docs.title: Serve entities from the dashboard
docs.text:
A dashboard with a fleet serves GET /api/backstage/entities, the same YAML pacto export backstage writes over the same sources, with only what the reader may read, so Backstage needs no file or sync job.

On a dashboard with sign-in, the reader is a ServiceAccount: the chart's pacto-viewer, or one you bind to get and list on pactos.pacto.trianalab.io. Mint its token for the dashboard and rotate it before it expires:

kubectl -n pacto create token pacto-viewer --audience pacto-dashboard --duration 720h

A token minted without --audience pacto-dashboard is refused with TokenAudienceRequired. Backstage's url reader sends no Authorization header, so a Backstage proxy endpoint in app-config.yaml adds it:

proxy:
  endpoints:
    /pacto:
      target: http://pacto-dashboard.pacto.svc:3000
      headers:
        Authorization: Bearer ${PACTO_READER_TOKEN}
      credentials: dangerously-allow-unauthenticated

Block /api/proxy/pacto at Backstage's ingress so only its own backend reads it. The catalog then reads the entities through that endpoint:

backend:
  reading:
    allow:
      - host: localhost:7007
        paths: [/api/proxy/pacto/api/backstage/]
catalog:
  locations:
    - type: url
      target: http://localhost:7007/api/proxy/pacto/api/backstage/entities

Backstage shows the reader's scope to every Backstage user. A namespace-scoped reader sees no service known only from a registry, so give a reader that should see the whole fleet a cluster-wide grant. A namespace grant shows that namespace in its own cluster only (Multi-cluster).

Open and local dashboards serve the route without a token. Whenever pacto export backstage would write nothing, the route answers 503 naming why, and Backstage keeps the entities it had. A reader whose grants show nothing gets an empty catalog and Backstage drops every entity, so check the reader's RoleBinding first when Backstage empties. The browser demo answers 503 on purpose: its edge-cluster source is down. On a laptop, a partial bundle cache or an unreachable cluster does the same; try --no-cache or another kubeconfig.

docs.title: What each entity is
docs.text:
Pacto Backstage entity A service Component of type service An interface of the service's current revision API named <component>-<interface>, listed in providesApis An external system Resource with its class as type A business domain System, set as the Component's spec.system An observed caller with no contract stub Component tagged pacto-observed

Golden paths run nowhere and consume nothing, so they are left out.

docs.title: Names and owners
docs.text:
An entity's name is the service name with every character Backstage rejects replaced by -, cut to fit 63 characters. When two services share a name, every one of them gets - and 8 hex digits of a hash of its full service key, so a name never moves to another service when a second registry joins. The full key is in pacto.trianalab.io/service-key. A stub Component always carries its suffix, so it never takes a service's name. Every entity lives in namespace default.

A team owner becomes group:default/<team> and a DRI user:default/<dri>. Pacto never rewrites an owner: when the name is not a valid Backstage name, spec.owner is unknown, pacto.trianalab.io/owner holds the raw value and pacto.trianalab.io/owner-unmapped is "true". Two owners claiming one service also give unknown, with pacto.trianalab.io/owner-conflict. An inferred owner never fills spec.owner. An API copies its Component's owner and owner annotations.

docs.title: Lifecycle, system and relations
docs.text:
spec.lifecycle is deprecated when the running revision deprecates the service, else unknown; a running target never becomes production. spec.system is the declared business domain. An unknown domain sets pacto.trianalab.io/business-domain: unknown and no system.

spec.dependsOn lists the services and external systems the running revisions declare or that traces observed. consumesApis lists the interfaces a dependency requires that the resolved provider revision and the provider's running revision both declare, so every ref names an API in the file. A dependency only an older, unused revision declares is left out. Each ref's provenance is in pacto.trianalab.io/relation-provenance as <ref>=declared, <ref>=observed@<time> or <ref>=declared+observed@<time>, where the time is when a trace last saw the call. An edge Pacto only inferred never enters spec; it is listed in pacto.trianalab.io/inferred-depends-on.

docs.title: Inferred and observed entities
docs.text: Backstage's catalog table cannot filter on annotations, so entities Pacto did not read from a contract also carry a tag: pacto-inferred on every inferred entity, and pacto-observed on every stub and on a service Pacto only sees running, with no contract it could read. Filter them out of the catalog table with the tag picker. A stub whose name matched more than one contracted service adds pacto.trianalab.io/caller-ambiguous: "true" and is partial.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
Annotation Meaning pacto.trianalab.io/provenance How Pacto knows the entity: declared, observed, declared+observed or inferred pacto.trianalab.io/as-of When the snapshot was built pacto.trianalab.io/completeness complete or partial pacto.trianalab.io/service-key The full service key pacto.trianalab.io/owner-provenance Where the owner comes from: declared, declared-via-target, attested or inferred pacto.trianalab.io/owner The raw owner when it is not a valid Backstage name pacto.trianalab.io/owner-unmapped "true" when the owner could not become a ref pacto.trianalab.io/owner-conflict "true" when two owners claim the service pacto.trianalab.io/business-domain unknown when the domain is unknown pacto.trianalab.io/name-provenance inferred when the service name was inferred pacto.trianalab.io/name-source Where an inferred name came from pacto.trianalab.io/relation-provenance Provenance of each dependsOn ref pacto.trianalab.io/inferred-depends-on Edges Pacto only inferred pacto.trianalab.io/hidden-relations How many relations your view hides pacto.trianalab.io/unresolved-dependencies How many declared dependencies, configuration or policy references did not resolve pacto.trianalab.io/external-key The external system's key pacto.trianalab.io/caller The observed caller's identity pacto.trianalab.io/caller-ambiguous "true" when the caller matched more than one service

A Component is partial when the snapshot is partial, your view hides some of its relations, a declared dependency did not resolve or owners conflict. A hidden service or edge is only ever counted, never named.

docs.title: An exported Component
docs.text:
This Component comes from the demo:

kind: Component
metadata:
  name: fulfillment-service
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    pacto.trianalab.io/as-of: "2026-11-16T12:00:00Z"
    pacto.trianalab.io/completeness: complete
    pacto.trianalab.io/owner-provenance: declared
    pacto.trianalab.io/provenance: declared
    pacto.trianalab.io/relation-provenance: component:default/event-bus=declared,component:default/inventory-service=declared,component:default/shipping-rates=declared
    pacto.trianalab.io/service-key: fulfillment-service
spec:
  type: service
  lifecycle: unknown
  owner: group:default/logistics-team
  system: fulfillment
  dependsOn:
    - component:default/event-bus
    - component:default/inventory-service
    - component:default/shipping-rates
  providesApis:
    - api:default/fulfillment-service-shipment-events
    - api:default/fulfillment-service-shipments
  consumesApis:
    - api:default/inventory-service-stock-events

docs.title: Agents read the same data
docs.text: Agents find the same services with pacto_fleet_search and read each one with pacto_fleet_get; the provenance names (declared, observed, declared+observed, inferred, and for owners declared-via-target and attested) are identical. Owner provenance is in pacto_fleet_get's ownerProvenance and in pacto_fleet_entity's ownership.provenance; search hits do not carry it.

docs.title: Generate contracts from what you already have
docs.text:
pacto init reads the files a service folder already holds and writes a contract for it. It takes many folders in one run. This guide takes a folder of existing services, such as services/* in a monorepo, to one checked contract per service.

Every command here runs on your machine. It writes plan.json, files in the service folders and, with --cluster, drafts in the --out folder. It publishes nothing.

docs.title: 1. Take an inventory
docs.text:
Plan every folder at once. --plan changes nothing:

pacto init --plan --output-format json services/* > plan.json
jq -r '.results[] | [.service, .mode, (.unknown | length)] | @tsv' plan.json

checkout  pactify  2
ledger    blank    3
notifier  blank    2
payments  pactify  2

Each entry in results has a mode. pactify means init found a Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests and read the contract from them. blank means it found neither and plans a starter template with placeholder values. The found, dependencies, unknown and next lists say what init read, which services the workload calls, what it could not tell and what a person still has to do. List every open question across the fleet:

jq -r '.results[] | .service as $s | .unknown[] | "\($s): \(.)"' plan.json

docs.title: What init reads
docs.text:
Input Contract fields Dockerfile (or Dockerfile.*, *.Dockerfile) publish.build in the inferred record: pacto ci --publish builds the image with it Kubernetes YAML with a Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job or CronJob service.name and workload from the workload; publish.deploy in the inferred record, and a found line naming the image tag as the version a first publish can declare The team label on the workload service.owner.team The workload's environment, with the ConfigMaps in the folder that it reads a configuration schema at configuration/schema.json with each key and its type, no values; sensitive keys are writeOnly An environment value that names another in-cluster service dependencies, each with compatibility: unknown and, from that service's contract in --fleet, a proposed range in a comment A readiness, liveness or startup probe a health capability An OpenAPI document at any path in the folder one openapi interface; AsyncAPI and gRPC files go to the inferred record kustomization.yaml publish.deploy in the inferred record: the deploy artifact keeps the folder layout

These fill in the contract. Init also reads Helm charts, Kustomize, Compose, CODEOWNERS, catalog-info.yaml and environment files into the inferred record (the full list). State stays for you to write. Every dependency range is a proposal: init writes compatibility: unknown with the proposal in a comment, and the dependency is named under unknown.

Init skips the files and folders that the service's .pactoignore lists. When it looks for manifests, it also skips every folder that holds a Chart.yaml, and documents in the backstage.io and skaffold API groups, such as catalog-info.yaml and skaffold.yaml.

docs.title: Configuration keys and sensitive values
docs.text:
Init reads the environment values to find types and dependencies and writes only keys and types. A key is sensitive when its name holds password, passwd, secret, token, key, credential, private or dsn in any case, when the workload reads it from a Secret or when its value is a URL with a password. A sensitive key is a string with writeOnly: true and a description. Schema summaries and schema diffs show its default and any other schema value as (sensitive). A value you declare under configurations[].values or in an environment file is shown as written, so keep secrets out of it. Init never reads the values of a Secret.

When a manifest or ConfigMap in the folder sets a sensitive key to a literal value, init names the file and the key under next steps. The bundle publishes that file to anyone who can pull it, so read the key from a Secret instead. Init keeps a configuration/schema.json that is already there: remove any default that holds a secret and publish a new version.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the folders init cannot read
docs.text:
Init keeps a pacto.yaml that is already there, so prepare these folders before step 3.

Helm charts. Init reads charts statically and never renders them. It skips each chart's templates, subcharts and CRDs as manifests, and reads its Chart.yaml, values files and templates for images, ports, configuration keys and environments. What it reads is listed under found and kept in the inferred record, and a chart dependency with no Chart.lock digest is a finding (what init reads). A chart-only folder plans as blank. To have init write the workload from the chart, render the chart into the folder, then init reads the result:

mkdir -p services/ledger/k8s
helm template --include-crds ledger services/ledger/chart \
  > services/ledger/k8s/rendered.yaml

Once init has written the contract, delete the rendered file: pacto ci --publish publishes the chart itself as the deploy artifact, and a folder with both a chart and manifests is a finding that asks for a publish section.

Compose files. Init reads the image, ports and environment keys of compose.yaml into the inferred record, and a Compose-only folder still gets the blank template. The blank template writes no publish section and no service.version: pacto ci --publish derives both, publishing to the registry it resolves or the one --registry names.

docs.title: 3. Write the contracts
docs.text:
pacto init services/*

Init prints what it found per folder and ends with a summary table. It only adds files and missing .pactoignore lines, so you can run it again after you fix a folder.

Check the build command before you publish

Init treats any other YAML file with an apiVersion and a kind as a Kubernetes manifest, such as a kind cluster configuration, and lists it in the manifests artifact's build.command. List such a file in the folder's .pactoignore before you run init. In a pacto.yaml that init already wrote, read the cp list and remove any file that is not a manifest your cluster applies.

docs.title: 4. Fill in what init could not tell
docs.text:
Work through the unknown list of each service.

  • Owner. Write service.owner.team, or pass --owner when one team owns every folder in the run.

  • Interfaces. The openapi-infer plugin writes interfaces/openapi.yaml from FastAPI or Huma code and needs the pacto.yaml from step 3. Run it from the service folder with the project's dependencies installed:

    cd services/payments
pacto generate openapi-infer . -o .

    Then add the interface to pacto.yaml:

    interfaces:
  - name: api
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/openapi.yaml

  • Configuration. Init's schema lists the environment only. schema-infer writes a JSON Schema from a config file (For developers).

  • Dependencies. Replace each compatibility: unknown with the versions the service accepts. Until you do, impact cannot tell whether a change to that dependency breaks the service: its verdict is unknown, and a BREAKING change to the dependency stays unverified.

Then check every contract and see who declares each service:

for d in services/*/; do pacto validate "$d"; done
pacto init --plan services/payments --fleet services

--fleet reads the other contracts and lists the services that declare this one under Used by.

docs.title: Draft from a running cluster
docs.text:
pacto init --cluster --namespace <ns> --out <dir> drafts a contract for each workload in the namespace that no Pacto resource describes, in <dir>/<ns>/<name>, from your current kubeconfig context. Without --namespace it reads every namespace, kube-system included. It lists Services, EndpointSlices, Pactos and node runtime observations in every namespace even with --namespace. It never lists or reads a Secret or a ConfigMap.

  • The read lists each kind of object in pages and stops at --max-items items per kind (10000 by default).
  • --call-window sets how far back a call counts as a dependency (24h by default).
  • A run --max-items stopped while listing workloads prints a Continue: line with the same command and --continue <token>. Another kind of object cut short stays partial, and a resumed run lists it again. Run it to resume the read where it stopped. A token made for other namespaces is refused.
  • A kind of object your identity may not list reads as failed with forbidden, and the run goes on. The run fails only when it reads no workload at all.
  • The Coverage: line names each kind of object the read did not see whole, with its state, partial or failed, and a reason. A draft built from a partial read can miss dependencies and callers, so treat what it lacks as unknown.

Each draft holds a manifests.yaml with the workload and its Services as the cluster returns them, without namespace, uid or status. It also holds a pacto.yaml and a .pactoignore. --plan writes nothing. A workload that a Pacto targets is skipped. When the Pactos were not all read, the draft of a workload says under Unknown that a Pacto may already describe it. A container environment variable that sets a sensitive key to a literal value is read in the draft from the Secret <name>-env; create it before you apply the draft with kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic <name>-env --from-env-file=<file>, from a file of KEY=value lines. When such a value is a URL, the draft no longer lists the service it names as a dependency, and next steps ask you to add it. A literal secret in a container's command or args, such as --db-password=hunter2, moves to the same Secret: the draft reads it through $(DB_PASSWORD) from an environment variable of that container.

docs.title: The inferred record of a draft
docs.text:
Each draft also holds a pacto.inferred.yaml, completed by the engine pacto ci uses, with one entry per field Pacto could tell (Inferred record).

  • Each entry names its source: manifest or label for what the draft's manifests.yaml shows, runtime for what the pods ran and called, and fleet for the versions the Pactos of a called Service report.
  • Each cluster entry carries asOf, when it was read. A runtime or fleet entry also carries its completeness: partial when not every node the workload ran on was observed or a source was cut short.
  • coverage gives the state of each kind of object read, and hidden counts the callers and Services a read on behalf of a viewer may not show.
  • The running image digest of each container is recorded as image.digest[<container>]. It is never declared and never becomes a deploy artifact.
  • A proposed range sits in a proposed value beside compatibility: unknown, never declared.
  • When the draft folder already holds a pacto.inferred.yaml, it is kept and next steps say to delete it to record what the cluster shows now.
  • pacto validate, pacto explain and pacto publish recompute the record from the folder, so the cluster facts stay in the draft. A published bundle whose record carries cluster facts fails validation with INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID, unless the record holds a declaration.
  • pacto declare <workload> --registry <registry> publishes the draft as a contract-only version you sign, with its cluster facts; a key or an ambient token writes a draft-<n> tag a person accepts (Declare a running service).

docs.title: Dependencies of a draft
docs.text: With the node agent, the Services a workload's pods were seen calling become dependencies with compatibility: unknown. Each gets a proposed range from the lowest version the reconciled Pactos describing the called Service report, and none when those Pactos disagree on the contract. Without the agent, dependencies come only from environment values, as in a folder. The draft holds no ConfigMaps, so each one the workload reads is named under unknown and its keys stay out of the configuration schema. A value such as host:6443 matches whether or not host is a Service, so a control-plane endpoint can become a dependency. Check each one.

docs.title: From an agent
docs.text:
The MCP tool pacto_create with pactify: true and paths plans the same contracts for an agent. It plans only, unless the agent sets dry_run to false (AI assistants).

  • With cluster, it takes max_items, call_window and continue, the --max-items, --call-window and --continue flags. A read stopped by max_items returns continue, and the next call passes it back to resume the read.
  • pacto_declare plans a declaration of a running workload. An agent's write is a draft-<n> tag, and the person it acts for accepts it with pacto declare <workload> --from-draft draft-<n> (the agent write contract).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Goal Page Publish a contract and connect it to delivery Pactify a service Check every change in CI Put it in your repository Write the fields init leaves out Contract sections

docs.title: From an imperative pipeline to one step
docs.text: A pipeline that installs Pacto and runs pacto validate, pacto diff, pacto impact and pacto publish as separate steps becomes one pacto ci step: a plan on every pull request and pacto ci --publish on every merge to the default branch. This page maps each old step to what pacto ci does and shows the result for GitHub, GitLab and a monorepo. Every example on it is a file that Pacto's own CI runs.

docs.title: What each step becomes
docs.text:
Old step With pacto ci curl -fsSL .../get-pacto.sh \| bash The reusable workflow and the GitLab component install a pinned Pacto release and check its sha256 pacto validate . Every pacto.yaml under the root is validated as part of the plan pacto diff oci://ghcr.io/acme/contracts/my-service . Each service is compared with its last published version; CLASSIFICATION shows the result. With the reusable workflow's defaults a BREAKING change with consumers reads unverified and passes with a warning, where pacto diff failed; fail-on: unverified keeps the check red continue-on-error: true on the diff before the first publish A service with no published version plans as a first publish pacto impact ... --root ./services/checkout The organization index names the consumers; --root is needed only for one that is not published yet. Without the delivery trust config a change with consumers reads unverified, a warning under the default fail-on: blocked docker buildx create plus pacto publish pacto ci --publish builds with the tool the folder shows, Docker Buildx included, and publishes every changed service COSIGN_KEY written to cosign.key Keyless signing by default; the sign-key secret keeps signing with your key Raising service.version by hand The version is derived from the change since the last published one pacto push of the contract alone Declare publish.bundle and pacto ci --publish publishes the contract

Keep your key while you move. A first keyless publish over versions signed with a key finds no baseline it can verify and stops with no verifiable baseline in <repo>. Keep the sign-key secret until a version signed keyless exists, or declare publish.sign in pacto.yaml. A repository that already published keyless from its own workflow keeps verifying.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
Delete the jobs that installed Pacto, validated, diffed, ran impact and published, and commit the caller pacto ci init writes:

on: [pull_request, push]
permissions: {contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, pull-requests: write}
jobs:
  pacto:
    uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions/.github/workflows/ci.yml@8b64cfe46f01f82a1b990afc5b64a01a73d0f4d0 # v2.0.0

To post the plan on the pull request as well, add one line:

jobs:
  pacto:
    uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions/.github/workflows/ci.yml@<sha> # v2.0.0
    with: {comment: true}

The publish job builds with Docker on the runner. A service built with ko, Jib or buildpacks builds in a job of your own and pins its image by digest in its manifests, which pacto ci --publish then uses without a build. See GitHub Actions for every input.

docs.title: GitLab
docs.text:
Delete the Pacto jobs from .gitlab-ci.yml and let pacto ci init add the component to the include list:

include:
  - remote: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/pacto-actions/8b64cfe46f01f82a1b990afc5b64a01a73d0f4d0/templates/pacto.yml

pacto-plan runs in the test stage on merge request pipelines and keeps the plan as the pacto plan artifact. pacto-publish runs in the deploy stage on the default branch with an ID token for keyless signing; it builds with a Docker-in-Docker service, so its runner must allow privileged jobs. The stage-plan and stage-publish inputs name other stages. A self-managed instance that blocks raw.githubusercontent.com copies templates/pacto.yml from pacto-actions into a project and includes it from there.

docs.title: Any other CI
docs.text:
The same command, with the same exit codes, runs anywhere Pacto is installed:

#!/bin/sh
# One pacto ci step for any CI system: Buildkite, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines,
# Jenkins or a plain shell. Run it with pacto on PATH and the repository
# checked out; pass the root and any pacto ci flag as arguments.
#
#   sh examples/ci/any-ci.sh . --registry ghcr.io/acme
#
# On a pull request it plans; on the merged default branch set
# PACTO_PUBLISH=true and it publishes every changed service.
#
# The exit status is pacto ci's own:
#   plan     0 clear, 1 blocked, 2 unverified
#   publish  0 every changed service published, 1 otherwise
set -eu

if [ "${PACTO_PUBLISH:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  exec pacto ci --publish "$@"
fi
exec pacto ci "$@"

docs.title: A monorepo
docs.text: pacto ci walks every folder under the root, so a repository of many services needs no per-service job. The root .pactoignore names the folders to skip (how). In the demo monorepo, examples/demo/monorepo, one service has an empty pacto.yaml and the other has two lines naming its owner. Its first plan:

docs.title: pacto ci plan
docs.text:
• CI: none
  • Registry: ghcr.io/acme (from --registry)
  • Base: none
  • Consumer source: none (IMPACT reads unverified)
  • Ranges: no dependency edges
SERVICE CHANGED VERSION CLASSIFICATION IMPACT INFERRED billing yes - -> 1.0.0 (derived) - unverified (first publish of ghcr.io/acme/billing: name inferred; declare service.name) 4 fields orders yes - -> 1.0.0 (derived) - unverified (first publish of ghcr.io/acme/orders: name inferred; declare service.name) 6 fields

Both rows read unverified because each name is inferred from the folder, and an inferred name never clears the gate. Declare service.name in each pacto.yaml, pass the registry (the registry input, or --registry) and the first publish reads clear.

docs.title: Put it in your repository
docs.text: Add Pacto to your build pipeline (CI) as one step. On every pull request it plans each service of the repository and fails the check when a change breaks a consumer it sees running. With the reusable workflow's and the GitLab component's defaults it cannot see where consumers run, so a breaking change with consumers reads unverified and passes with a warning; fail-on: unverified or the delivery trust config turns it red (Who breaks). On every merge to the default branch it publishes each changed service. This page assumes you have a contract, pacto.yaml, from Pactify a service. An empty contract plans, and it publishes once it declares service.name, which still fits in two lines.

docs.title: What to commit
docs.text:
Commit what pacto init wrote, any files the contract points to, such as an OpenAPI document, and the CI file pacto ci init writes. No signing key goes in the repository: keyless signing needs none, and a key lives in a CI secret.

If your contract lists dependencies, also run pacto lock . and commit the pacto.lock it writes. It records the exact published build of every contract yours depends on, so every build checks against the same ones. It is optional: without it, Pacto looks dependencies up fresh each time. See Lockfile.

docs.title: Declare your API first
docs.text:
pacto ci sees API changes only in the interfaces the contract declares. If pacto init did not find your OpenAPI document, add it to pacto.yaml yourself, with the path from the repository root:

interfaces:
  - name: rest-api
    type: openapi
    ref: api/openapi.yaml
    visibility: public          # other teams may call it

Other interface types and fields are in Contract sections.

docs.title: Add Pacto to your pipeline
docs.text:
From the root of your repository:

pacto ci init

It reads which CI the repository uses, writes the caller into the working tree and prints it. Review the file and commit it yourself: Pacto never commits, pushes or needs write access to your Git host. --dry-run prints the file and writes nothing; --platform github or --platform gitlab picks one when the repository has both or neither.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
pacto ci init writes .github/workflows/pacto.yml:

on: [pull_request, push]
permissions: {contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, pull-requests: write}
jobs:
  pacto:
    uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions/.github/workflows/ci.yml@8b64cfe46f01f82a1b990afc5b64a01a73d0f4d0 # v2.0.0

It calls the pacto-actions reusable workflow, pinned by commit, which Dependabot can keep current. The permissions line is the most any of its jobs may use. Inputs, secrets and the jobs are in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: GitLab CI/CD
docs.text:
pacto ci init adds one entry to the include list of .gitlab-ci.yml and leaves every other line as it was:

include:
  - remote: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/pacto-actions/8b64cfe46f01f82a1b990afc5b64a01a73d0f4d0/templates/pacto.yml

The component adds a pacto-plan job to the test stage and a pacto-publish job to the deploy stage. Run pacto ci init again to move the pin to a newer commit.

docs.title: Other CI systems
docs.text:
Buildkite, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines and Jenkins run the same command with Pacto installed (installer script):

#!/bin/sh
# One pacto ci step for any CI system: Buildkite, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines,
# Jenkins or a plain shell. Run it with pacto on PATH and the repository
# checked out; pass the root and any pacto ci flag as arguments.
#
#   sh examples/ci/any-ci.sh . --registry ghcr.io/acme
#
# On a pull request it plans; on the merged default branch set
# PACTO_PUBLISH=true and it publishes every changed service.
#
# The exit status is pacto ci's own:
#   plan     0 clear, 1 blocked, 2 unverified
#   publish  0 every changed service published, 1 otherwise
set -eu

if [ "${PACTO_PUBLISH:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  exec pacto ci --publish "$@"
fi
exec pacto ci "$@"

From an imperative pipeline to one step maps each step of an existing pipeline to pacto ci.

docs.title: What the plan shows
docs.text:
pacto ci finds each pacto.yaml under the root, skips ignored and too-deep folders and compares each with its last published version. The plan writes nothing to the registry, so it needs only read credentials: the workflow's token on GitHub, else PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME and PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD.

The plan prints each value it detected with its source:

  • CI: GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, from GITHUB_ACTIONS or GITLAB_CI
  • Registry: --registry, else ghcr.io/<owner> on GitHub Actions or CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE on GitLab CI
  • Base: the target branch or merge-request base, shown for context only; Pacto reads no Git history and works on a shallow checkout
  • Consumer source: each source of consumers you named and what it answered, or not read when no changed service has a published baseline
  • Index: the organization index read and how complete the read was; the index alone is no consumer source
  • Ranges: how many dependency edges of the services it walked declare a range or carry an accepted one, then each unknown range with the range Pacto proposes

Then one row per service:

Column Shows SERVICE the service name CHANGED whether its content differs from the published version VERSION published version -> the version it would publish CLASSIFICATION NON_BREAKING, POTENTIAL_BREAKING or BREAKING IMPACT clear, blocked (...) or unverified (...) INFERRED how many fields Pacto read from the folder

docs.title: pacto ci plan
docs.text:
• CI: none
  • Registry: ghcr.io/acme (from --registry)
  • Base: none
  • Consumer source: targets-6f1e0000-cccc-4000-8000-000000000003 (available, asOf <time>)
  • Consumer source: targets-6f1e0000-cccc-4000-8000-000000000003-workloads (empty, asOf <time>)
  • Index: 1 from ghcr.io/acme/pacto-index (listed by tag, complete)
  • Ranges: 0 declared and 0 accepted of 1 dependency edges (0%)
  • unknown: reports -> ledger (proposed ^2.4.0)
SERVICE CHANGED VERSION CLASSIFICATION IMPACT INFERRED ledger yes 2.4.0 -> 3.0.0 BREAKING clear 1 field payments yes 1.4.2 -> 1.4.3 (derived) NON_BREAKING unverified (possible break (inferred): interfaces[api]; declare it to classify) 6 fields reports no - - - 2 fields
  • possible break (inferred) payments api openapi/v1.yaml:1: openapi.paths[/payments].methods[GET].parameters[currency:query] GET /payments query param 'currency' added; consumers (inferred, unknown): none
Declare api 
interfaces:
  - name: api
    type: openapi
    ref: openapi/v1.yaml
  • skipped: services/legacy (from .pactoignore:1)
  • ledger: break accepted for reports (ana@acme.com, ghcr.io/acme/reports@<digest>); expires 2026-12-14 (commit 92b546ad6e54 + 30d, inferred)
  • payments: baseline unverified in plan mode

A folder Pacto cannot read makes the run unverified. It reads the target snapshot as pacto impact does; a changed service with none reads unverified (no consumer source) until you name its consumers with the flags pacto impact takes, such as --root.

pacto ci --explain payments shows why one row reads as it does: its baseline, what changed, each inferred field with its source and the consumers. It exits with that row's code. --output-format json prints the plan as JSON.

pacto ci reads the organization catalog from --external-catalog or PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG only, never from a pacto config file in the working directory, which a pull request can change.

  • On GitHub Actions the plan is also added to the job summary, and each service that does not read as unchanged gets an annotation on its pacto.yaml.
  • On GitLab CI it is written to pacto-plan.md, which the component keeps as the pacto plan merge request artifact. Without the component, keep it with artifacts: paths: [pacto-plan.md].

docs.title: Older contracts
docs.text:
pacto ci raises an older pactoVersion in the bundle only, when that adds no validation finding. Its row says:

  • ledger: pacto.yaml is 2.4, publishes as 2.5 (migrated in memory)
  • kept at 2.4 (<finding>): published as written when it declares a publish section; with none, the row fails until you fix the finding and raise pactoVersion
  • published as 2.4 (raises to 2.5 when it next changes): a raise alone never republishes

No note changes the exit code. The bundle records the raise in pacto.inferred.yaml (Migrations), shown as inferred in the dashboard. pacto migrate rewrites the file itself.

docs.title: Accept proposed ranges
docs.text:
pacto ci proposes, in pacto.inferred.yaml and with a source:

  • A dependency by name gets its ref from the organization index entry of the service of that name in your domain (index:<repo>:<tag>).
  • A dependency whose range is absent or unknown gets ^MAJOR.MINOR.0 of the provider version this service runs with in the target snapshot (snapshot:<repo>@sha256:<hex>).
  • A proposal publishes as compatibility: unknown: it reads unverified and never clears the gate.
  • A changed spec file that is only inferred may print possible break (inferred) with the YAML that declares the interface. The row stays unverified until you declare it; see a possible break on an inferred interface.

The service owner accepts them:

pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --proposed --dry-run    # the plan and its intent digest
pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --proposed --intent sha256:...
  • --proposed accepts every proposed range of the newest published version. A proposed ref is accepted only by naming it, --field 'dependencies[ledger].ref', and --field 'dependencies[ledger].compatibility=^2.0.0' accepts another range.
  • Only your interactive Sigstore login (a browser, or --device) signs. The record is attached to that version in its own bundle repository with your registry credentials: a referrer, or on a registry without the Referrers API, such as GHCR, a write-once pacto-accept-<hex>-<hex> tag.
  • Only a record signed by the service's declared owner (its DRI or an email contact) counts. One by anybody else reads waiting for the owner of reports with who may accept. A key, an ambient OIDC token in CI or an agent through pacto_accept writes a pacto-accept-draft-<n> that a person accepts with --draft.
  • A counted range reads accepted in the Ranges: line. The next pacto ci --publish pins it into the published pacto.yaml, where it reads declared, and cites the record in inputs.acceptances. A range your pacto.yaml declares wins; compatibility: unknown declares none. A declared service.version that is already published pins nothing until you bump it.
  • One command accepts ranges or a break, never both.

  • The dashboard's service page offers Accept all proposed ranges inside Inferred by Pacto to a signed-in or local viewer: it shows the plan and the pacto accept command, and never signs or writes.

  • --policy on pacto ci and pacto impact sets how a BREAKING change treats what no range covers. The default warn adds a POLICY_WARNING note. unknown-range=fail blocks while a direct consumer's range is unknown and not accepted (POLICY_UNKNOWN_RANGE). uncontracted=fail:7d blocks while a caller no contract describes was seen in the last 7 days (POLICY_UNCONTRACTED).

docs.title: Who breaks
docs.text:
pacto ci checks each changed service against its consumers and whether they run. It finds them through the organization index that every publish keeps at ghcr.io/acme/pacto-index, so it needs no --root, and checks them against the signed target snapshot each cluster's operator publishes. A snapshot counts only when the job has the delivery trust config (PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST), never cluster credentials. The reusable workflow and the GitLab component pass none, so there a BREAKING change with consumers reads unverified. To clear it, run pacto ci or, for one contract, pacto impact in a job you write:

- name: Check who the change breaks
  run: |
    pacto impact oci://ghcr.io/acme/contracts/my-service . \
      --output-format json > impact.json || [ $? -eq 2 ]
    jq -r '.consumers[] | select(.compatibilityVerdict == "incompatible") | "\(.service) (owner \(.owner // "unknown")) accepts \(.compatibility)"' impact.json
    jq -e '.classification != "BREAKING" or all(.consumers[]; .compatibilityVerdict != "incompatible")' impact.json
    jq -e '.classification != "BREAKING" or .completeness == "complete"' impact.json
  env:
    PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST: pacto-trust.yaml   # committed: public keys only

The first jq lists each consumer whose compatibility range rejects the new version, with its owner; the second fails the step when a BREAKING change has an incompatible consumer. A range Pacto cannot evaluate reads unknown and passes. The third fails a BREAKING change whose answer is partial, such as an untrusted snapshot or an index with no target snapshot.

pacto impact exits 0 clear, 1 blocked and 2 unverified, as does a BREAKING change with compatible consumers. || [ $? -eq 2 ] lets the step reach the jq checks; a 1 still fails it.

docs.title: Consumers from the organization index
docs.text:
Every published version writes one entry, and impact reads each service's newest (how):

Consumers: 41 from ghcr.io/acme/pacto-index (listed by tag, complete)

It says complete only when a target snapshot was read; with --k8s or --target-state alone a row reads unverified (CONSUMER_INDEX_UNCHECKED). --root replaces the index. With --publish, --index also names where the run writes its entries and --index none turns them off. A run that finds a version already published writes its missing entry; an entry it cannot write is a note on its row.

An entry exposes each published service's name, version, bundle reference and dependency references. On GitHub the first publish creates the pacto-index package: in its Manage Actions access settings, grant write to each repository that publishes and read to each that runs impact. Internal visibility shows those names and the dependency graph to every organization member, even for packages they cannot read. A publish without access succeeds with a warning.

docs.title: Where consumers come from
docs.text:
Pacto tries pacto-targets under each repository prefix, deepest first, and reads every cluster-<uid> snapshot in the first that exists (JSON fields registry and targetSnapshots):

Registry: ghcr.io/acme (found ghcr.io/acme/pacto-targets, 1 cluster read)
Targets: ghcr.io/acme/pacto-targets@sha256:4f1c... (cluster 6f1e2a90, asOf 3m, complete, signed by installation-6f1e2a90 (publisher system:serviceaccount:pacto-system:pacto-operator))

Snapshots are pinned by digest; only a verified one clears a BREAKING change:

  • unverified: the job has no trust config. The answer is partial and a BREAKING change with consumers exits 2.
  • not scoped to this cluster: the key that signed has no streams entry for the cluster's UID, so another cluster's operator could hold it. Partial.
  • stale: older than 15 minutes, because its operator stopped publishing or its tag was moved back. Partial.
  • A bad signature, a cluster other than its tag, a registry error or a timeout: the snapshot is unused and the answer is partial.
  • No pacto-targets repository or no cluster tag: the Registry line says so (not found, denied (check registry read credentials) or no cluster tag) and consumers come only from the sources you name.

The trust config holds one key per cluster, scoped to its kube-system UID (a bare PEM key is unscoped). Target snapshot shows where each cluster advertises its key:

keys:
  - name: installation-6f1e2a90
    streams: ["6f1e2a90-5b7d-4c1e-8a3f-2d6b0e9c7a41/pacto-targets/snapshot"]
    publicKey: |
      -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
      ...
      -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
  • --delivery-trust or $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST names the file.
  • auto, the default, reads only the clusters whose snapshot exists at that moment, so a cluster that stopped publishing drops its consumers. Pin the clusters you expect, once per cluster: --target-snapshot oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid>. A pinned tag that is missing makes the answer partial.
  • --target-snapshot with a repository reads it when the derivation cannot find it, and --target-snapshot off reads none.
  • Pull on pacto-targets reads every cluster's Pacto status and workload shape regardless of Kubernetes RBAC and, where the Evidence Server is on, every target, provisioning and usage record (cost included) it accepted. Give that repository its own read ACL.

docs.title: Consumers that run nowhere yet
docs.text: A consumer deployed nowhere is in no snapshot. The index finds it once it is published; name an unpublished one with --root ./services/checkout. A BREAKING change that reaches only these exits 2.

docs.title: After a merge: publish
docs.text:
On a push to the default branch the publish job runs pacto ci --publish. It derives each changed service's version, builds its image with the tool the folder shows and signs it; see Publish from CI.

  • Signing is keyless by default. Only the publish job has id-token: write. The CI mints a short-lived token for it, which the Pacto CLI in that job exchanges with Sigstore for a certificate; the token never leaves the job, and the Pacto installation never holds it.
  • Keyless signing records the repository, workflow and commit in the public Rekor log. A private repository that must not appear there sets the sign-key secret, or declares publish.sign with a private log; see Publish a version.
  • One publish runs per repository at a time; a version lost to a concurrent run is planned again.
  • The publisher identity is your repository on its default branch, also when the workflow that signs is the shared pacto-actions one, so a newer pin keeps earlier versions verifying.
  • Publishing never turns delivery on: a cluster rolls out a published version only once you set up delivery.

docs.title: A breaking change you need to ship
docs.text:
Announce a deliberate break, with a new major version (2.4.0 becomes 3.0.0), in breaks:

breaks:
  - consumers: [reports]
    reason: Amounts move from cents to euros; read amount_eur.
  • pacto ci shows each announced consumer announced for reports, not accepted and the gate holds the change.
  • Each consumer owner accepts with pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --break ledger@3.0.0, signed as for proposed ranges. Before ledger 3.0.0 is published, --from ../ledger (its checkout or a pushed oci:// ref) reads the announcement.
  • A consumer also reads accepted when its own published ranges admit the new version, a source shows where it runs and no revision that refuses it runs there.
  • The gate clears (BREAKING_ACCEPTED) once every consumer accepted. Nobody overrides a failed check.
  • An announcement without expires expires 30 days after the commit time, recorded in pacto.inferred.yaml. An expired break blocks again.
  • A plain pacto publish carries no acceptance forward, so one stays found only while the accepted version is the consumer's newest or runs on a target. pacto ci --publish carries it.
  • Gate on pacto ci or pacto impact: pacto diff still fails on the change, because it is still breaking.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Run 0 1 2 pacto ci (plan) clear blocked unverified pacto ci --publish every changed service published anything else

On GitHub, the reusable workflow's fail-on input decides what fails the plan job: blocked (the default) passes on 2 with a warning annotation for each unverified service; unverified fails on it. On GitLab, pacto-plan passes with a warning on 2 (allow_failure: exit_codes: [2]). An unverified plan never reads as a plain pass.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Every command accepts -v / --verbose for debug-level logging and --help for detailed usage. --output-format is a global flag taking text (the default), json or markdown.

What --output-format guarantees

Read this before you parse Pacto's output in a script.

  • json describes a successful result. When a command fails to produce its result, for example because a reference is unreachable or pacto.lock is missing, the error goes to stderr as plain text and stdout stays empty, whatever --output-format says. A negative verdict is still a result: pacto validate on an invalid contract and pacto diff on a breaking change both print their whole JSON document to stdout and exit 1. An empty stdout tells you there is nothing to parse. Read stdout when it is non-empty, and read the exit code for the verdict.
  • Only pacto diff implements markdown, for posting a diff as a CI comment. Every other command renders text.
  • Keys are camelCase in every command ("path", "valid", "errors", "upToDate"). Before v4, init, validate, pack, pull and push emitted capitalised keys ("Path", "Valid").
  • An unrecognised value is rejected. --output-format yaml exits 1 with unsupported output format "yaml" before the command runs.

The interactive and side-effecting commands (login, logout, update, mcp, dashboard) inherit the flag from the root command and always emit text.

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
--config string           config file path
  -h, --help[=true|false]       help for pacto
      --no-anim[=true|false]    disable animations
      --no-cache[=true|false]   disable OCI bundle cache
      --output-format string    output format (text, json, markdown) (default "text")
  -v, --verbose[=true|false]    enable verbose output

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Pacto exits 0, 1 or 2, apart from pacto run (below). 0 means the command produced its result and the result was acceptable. 1 means the check failed or the command could not run, so the exit status alone cannot distinguish "the check failed" from "the command could not run". 2 means pacto impact could not show that a change or an event is safe, and no other command exits 2 for its own result. pacto run exits with the exit code of the command it wraps, whatever it is, or 1 when that command exits 0 and the final verdict fails --fail-on. Recording a run record (--stats-registry, --stats-file) never changes an exit code. pacto stats publish exits 1 when a file could not be published.

Exits 1 Exits 0 pacto diff where the overall classification is BREAKING a POTENTIAL_BREAKING or NON_BREAKING diff pacto validate reporting at least one error validation that reported only warnings pacto lock --check on a stale lockfile, or with none at all (LOCK_MISSING) a lockfile that is up to date pacto impact where the gate is blocked: a BREAKING change reaches a consumer that does not accept the new version and runs on a known target, or a policy referrer that fails the new policy does pacto impact where the gate is clear: the change is not BREAKING and every policy referrer was checked and passes the new policy, or the snapshot is complete and no service depends on the changed one; an event (--unavailable, --removed or --regressed) when the complete snapshot shows nothing depends on the service pacto stats publish when a file could not be read, parsed or published pacto stats publish that published every file pacto migrate when a pacto.yaml could not be read or written, or --to names an unsupported version pacto migrate that rewrote, kept or left every file, 1.x files included any command that could not run, for example on an unresolvable reference, an unreadable bundle or an unknown flag Exits 2 pacto impact where the gate is unverified: a BREAKING change that nothing is shown to block, on a partial answer or with consumers none of which is shown to be safe; or a change of any classification with a policy referrer that fails the new policy and runs nowhere known, could not be checked or could not be resolved pacto impact --unavailable, --removed or --regressed when anything depends on the service or the answer is partial. An event never exits 1 for its result

Two cases affect CI gates:

  • A pacto diff against a missing reference exits 1, the same as a breaking change.
  • pacto impact exits 1 only when the change is breaking and a source that knows where services run shows an incompatible consumer on a target. Sources that know no targets, such as --local alone, cannot show that, so a breaking change with consumers exits 2. A job that gates on deployed impact alone can treat 2 as a pass; any other job fails on it.

Use stdout to tell a verdict from a failure. A command that produced a verdict writes it to stdout and puts a one-line summary on stderr. A command that could not run leaves stdout empty:

Invocation Exit stdout stderr pacto diff --output-format json OLD NEW (breaking) 1 the full JSON result breaking changes detected pacto diff --output-format json oci://…/absent:1.0.0 NEW 1 empty old contract: artifact not found: …

In a script, branch on stdout when it is non-empty, and treat an empty stdout with exit 1 as a tool failure.

docs.title: OCI version resolution
docs.text:
All commands that accept oci:// references support automatic version resolution. When a reference omits the tag (for example oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc-pacto with no :1.0.0), pacto queries the registry for available tags and selects the highest semver version.

For dependency references declared with a compatibility constraint, only tags satisfying the constraint are considered. For example, a dependency with compatibility: "^2.0.0" and available tags 1.0.0, 2.0.0, 2.3.0, 3.0.0 resolves to 2.3.0.

Resolution ignores non-semver tags such as latest and main. Digest-pinned references (@sha256:...) and explicitly tagged references are used as-is.

Constraints apply to the CLI's dependency graph

The CLI applies compatibility constraints when it resolves a contract's declared dependencies, for example in pacto graph. The dashboard's version discovery selects the highest semver tag and ignores per-dependency compatibility constraints. Root-contract pulls (a tagless top-level oci:// ref) also select the highest semver tag with no constraint.

docs.title: pacto accept
docs.text:
Plans an acceptance record for the newest published version of a service: a bundle repository (oci://host/path) or the service's checkout, whose publish.bundle names it.

--proposed accepts every dependency range pacto ci proposed in the inferred record. A field, positional or with --field, accepts one proposed field: dependencies[<name>].compatibility, optionally with =<range> to accept another range, or dependencies[<name>].ref, which --proposed never accepts. --break <provider>@<version> accepts a break the provider announces for this service in breaks[], read from that published version, or from --from (the provider's checkout or a pushed oci:// ref) before it is published.

The plan names every field with its value and source, who may accept (the service's declared owner), the acceptances already attached and the intent digest. Without --dry-run, the record is signed and attached to that version in its own bundle repository with your registry credentials. Only your interactive Sigstore login (a browser, or a device code with --device) signs the record, and only a record a person who owns the service signs counts. Every other signer (--sign-key, an ambient OIDC token in CI) writes a draft, pacto-accept-draft-<n>, that a person accepts.

--draft <repo>:pacto-accept-draft-<n> accepts a draft an agent or CI wrote: its record is planned again against the registry now, refused when anything moved since the draft was written, shown with the person it names in on_behalf_of, and signed by you after a Sigstore login.

pacto accept <service-ref-or-dir> [field...] [flags]

Examples:

  # Plan accepting every proposed range of reports
  pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --proposed --dry-run

  # Accept the plan you reviewed, signed after a Sigstore login
  pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --proposed --intent sha256:...

  # Accept the break ledger 3.0.0 announces, before it is published
  pacto accept ./reports --break ledger@3.0.0 --from ../ledger

  # Accept the draft an agent wrote, signed after a Sigstore login
  pacto accept oci://ghcr.io/acme/reports --draft ghcr.io/acme/reports:pacto-accept-draft-1

Flags:

      --break string             accept the break this provider version announces, as <provider>@<version>
      --device[=true|false]      log in with a device code instead of a browser
      --draft string             accept this acceptance draft, as <repo>:pacto-accept-draft-<n>, signed by you
      --dry-run[=true|false]     print the plan and write nothing
      --field stringArray        a proposed field to accept, as <key> or <key>=<range>; repeat it for more
      --from string              the provider's checkout or oci:// ref to read an unpublished break from
      --fulcio-url string        Fulcio to get the signing certificate from (default "https://fulcio.sigstore.dev")
  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for accept
      --intent string            the intent digest of the plan you reviewed: a different plan is refused
      --oidc-client-id string    OpenID Connect client of the Sigstore login (default "sigstore")
      --oidc-issuer-url string   OpenID Connect issuer of the Sigstore login (default "https://oauth2.sigstore.dev/auth")
      --proposed[=true|false]    accept every proposed dependency range
      --rekor-url string         Rekor transparency log the signature is recorded in (default "https://rekor.sigstore.dev")
      --sign-key string          sign with this key file: a key names no person, so the run writes a draft
      --timestamp-url string     timestamp authority to date the signature with
      --trusted-root string      Sigstore trusted root JSON to verify with (default: public-good Sigstore)

docs.title: pacto agent
docs.text:
Runs until interrupted. Watches TCP listeners and outbound connection outcomes with an eBPF program, attributes each socket to the workload that created it (a Kubernetes pod, a container, a systemd unit or a pacto run session, from its cgroup, or from its network namespace when the cgroup names none) and publishes a snapshot every --publish-interval. --sink kubernetes writes the node's NodeRuntimeObservation status (pods only; what the Pacto operator's node agent DaemonSet runs); --sink stdout prints one JSON snapshot per line.

--sink local and --sink evidence check workloads against their contracts on this host. The workloads come from --bindings (a YAML list of {match: {unit|container|cgroup|session|pid}, contract, host, interfaces: {name: port}, dependencies: {name: host:port}}) and with --docker from running containers labelled dev.pacto.contract=, dev.pacto.bind.<interface>=<port> and dev.pacto.dep.<dependency>=. Interfaces and dependencies are judged from the kernel's view, health and metrics capabilities by probing the bound port; a negative is reported once it persists for --stabilization-window. --sink local prints every target's compliance and findings each interval in --output-format; --sink evidence signs each target's evidence and sends it to an Evidence Server, which needs contracts pinned as oci://...@sha256:<digest>. Envelope sequences start at the wall clock in nanoseconds and count up, so they keep increasing across restarts as long as the clock does.

Needs Linux 5.11 or later with BTF, or 5.8 or later with BTF and root or CAP_SYS_RESOURCE; root (or BPF, PERFMON and SYS_PTRACE); and the host's /proc and cgroupfs.

pacto agent [flags]

Examples:

  pacto agent --sink stdout --publish-interval 5s
  pacto agent --sink kubernetes --cgroup-root /host/sys/fs/cgroup
  pacto agent --sink local --docker --cgroup-root /host/sys/fs/cgroup
  pacto agent --sink evidence --bindings bindings.yaml --evidence-url https://evidence.example.com \
    --evidence-key agent.key --evidence-key-id k1 --evidence-producer host-1

Flags:

      --bindings string                   with --sink local or evidence: YAML file binding workloads to contracts
      --cgroup-root string                where the host cgroup v2 hierarchy is mounted; empty attributes by network namespace only (default "/sys/fs/cgroup")
      --docker[=true|false]               with --sink local or evidence: check running containers labelled dev.pacto.contract (Docker Engine API on /var/run/docker.sock)
      --docker-label-filter stringArray   with --docker: only check containers that also carry this label (key=value or key; repeatable, all must match), e.g. com.docker.compose.project=demo
      --enable-probing[=true|false]       also probe the wire protocol of every interface found listening
      --evidence-key string               with --sink evidence: private key file envelopes are signed with
      --evidence-key-id string            with --sink evidence: key id (must match the server's trust entry)
      --evidence-producer string          with --sink evidence: producer id
      --evidence-url string               with --sink evidence: Evidence Server base URL
  -h, --help[=true|false]                 help for agent
      --namespace string                  namespace the NodeRuntimeObservation is written to with --sink kubernetes (default $POD_NAMESPACE)
      --node-name string                  name of this host; with --sink kubernetes also the NodeRuntimeObservation name (default $NODE_NAME)
      --proc-root string                  where the host /proc is mounted (a pod needs hostPID, a container --pid=host) (default "/proc")
      --publish-interval duration         how often a snapshot is published (whole seconds) (default 30s)
      --resync-interval duration          how often workloads, network namespaces and listeners are re-read from /proc (default 1m0s)
      --ringbuf-size uint32               kernel ring buffer size in bytes; a power of two and a multiple of the page size (default 262144)
      --sink string                       where snapshots go: one of [kubernetes stdout local evidence] (default "stdout")
      --stabilization-window duration     how long a negative must persist before it is reported (default 2m0s)

docs.title: pacto ci
docs.text:
Walks root (default .) for pacto.yaml, skipping the folders the root .pactoignore names, and prints one plan: the CI platform, the registry and the base, each with its source, then one row per service: whether it changed against its published baseline, the version it would publish, the classification of the change and its impact on the consumers the fleet source flags name.

The registry is --registry, else the registry the installation advertises in what the operator detected (--detected, used only when it is fresh and no PACTO_REGISTRY_* credential is set, since those answer any host), else the CI platform's registry, else the one registry every image names.

On GitHub Actions the plan is also appended to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; on GitLab CI it is written to pacto-plan.md in $CI_PROJECT_DIR. --output-format json writes the plan as one JSON document.

Without --publish the run is a plan: it reads the registry and the consumer sources you name and writes nothing to them. A run record goes to --stats-file only, one file per impacted service.

The exit status follows the plan: 0 clear, 1 blocked, 2 unverified. A repository with no pacto.yaml, or a folder it cannot read, exits 2.

A pacto.yaml that declares an older pactoVersion is raised to the current one in memory when that keeps its meaning, recorded in the bundle's pacto.inferred.yaml and noted on its row; the file in the repository is never rewritten.

--publish publishes every changed service on the merged commit, through the engine pacto publish runs, providers before the services that depend on them. A service that fails blocks only the services of the run that depend on it; a version lost to a concurrent run is planned again, up to 3 times. A pull or merge request pipeline is refused before any token is asked for or anything is built. Each service leaves a run record. With --publish the exit status is 0 when every changed service is published, else 1.

pacto ci [root] [flags]

Examples:

  # Plan every service of this repository against a registry
  pacto ci --registry ghcr.io/acme

  # Check the impact on the consumers a target-state file names, as JSON
  pacto ci --registry ghcr.io/acme --target-state targets.yaml --output-format json

  # Why the payments row reads as it does
  pacto ci --registry ghcr.io/acme --explain payments

  # On the merged commit: publish every changed service, payments from an image built elsewhere
  pacto ci --publish --image payments=ghcr.io/acme/payments@sha256:<digest>

Flags:

      --cache[=true|false]                 include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray                kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --delivery-trust string              the trust config target snapshots are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string                    add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray           base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --explain string                     explain one service's row: its folder, baseline, why it changed, its inferred fields and its consumers
      --external-catalog string            organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string                a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --freshness duration                 mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]                  help for ci
      --image stringArray                  with --publish: the image <service> deploys, pinned by digest, as <service>=<repo>@sha256:...; Pacto builds, signs and copies none. A bare <repo>@sha256:... needs exactly one changed service
      --index string                       organization index pacto impact and pacto ci read consumers from, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the provider reference; none reads none; skipped when --root names the consumers; pacto ci --publish also writes its entries there; other fleet commands ignore it)
      --k8s[=true|false]                   include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray                  local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --mira-source stringArray            base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable)
      --namespace string                   namespaces to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces)
      --no-transparency-log[=true|false]   with --publish and --sign-key: keep the signatures out of the transparency log
      --oci stringArray                    registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --policy stringArray                 range policy for a BREAKING change, repeatable: unknown-range=warn|fail and uncontracted=warn|fail:<window> (such as fail:7d); default warn
      --publish[=true|false]               publish every changed service, on the merged commit only
      --registry string                    registry the services publish to, for example ghcr.io/acme; default from the installation advertisement or the CI platform
      --root stringArray                   contract root whose whole dependency closure joins the snapshot: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --sign-key string                    with --publish: sign the services whose contract declares no publish section with this cosign key file instead of keyless
      --stats-context string               comma-separated context to include in the run record: repository, run-url, environment=<name>; nothing is included unless named
      --stats-file string                  write the run record to this file for pacto stats publish, replacing the record it holds, so give each command its own file; default $PACTO_STATS_FILE
      --stats-registry string              publish an unsigned run record (statistics, never evidence) to this repository, for example ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats; default $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY
      --target-snapshot stringArray        signed target snapshot(s) to read targets from: an oci:// pacto-targets repository, or :cluster-<uid> tags or digests to pin the clusters CI expects (repeatable); pacto impact, pacto ci and pacto_impact on a stdio pacto mcp also take auto (the default: derived from the provider ref) and off
      --target-state stringArray           offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray                 OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)

docs.title: pacto ci init
docs.text:
Writes the CI caller that runs pacto ci into the repository at dir (default .). With a .github folder it writes .github/workflows/pacto.yml, five lines that call the pacto-actions reusable workflow pinned by commit. With .gitlab-ci.yml it adds the pacto-actions GitLab component to its include list, or moves the commit of the entry already there, and leaves every other byte of the file as it was. --platform picks one when the repository has both or neither.

pacto ci init writes into the working tree only: you review and commit the file. An existing GitHub caller with other content is replaced only with --force. With --output-format json, content is the whole file written or to write and lines counts the lines of the caller it adds.

To plan a folder named init, run pacto ci ./init.

pacto ci init [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  # Write the caller for the CI platform this repository uses
  pacto ci init

  # Print the GitHub caller without writing it
  pacto ci init --platform github --dry-run

Flags:

      --dry-run[=true|false]   print the caller without writing it
      --force[=true|false]     replace a GitHub caller that has other content
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for init
      --platform string        the CI platform to write the caller for, github or gitlab; default from the .github folder or .gitlab-ci.yml
