docs.title: pacto dashboard
docs.text:
Launches an operational dashboard over the fleet snapshot: the same operational graph the CLI's pacto fleet commands query, served as a web UI.

The dashboard is the exploration and observability layer of the Pacto system. It visualizes the same contracts the CLI manages and the operator verifies, organised around four workflows: an operational Overview, the Services inventory, the Operational Graph and Change analysis.

Each positional argument is a contract source reference: - oci://registry/repo → OCI registry source (can be repeated) - ./path/to/dir → local filesystem source (at most one)

When no arguments are given, sources are auto-detected: - local: enabled if pacto.yaml is found in the working directory - cache: enabled if the OCI bundle cache (~/.cache/pacto/oci) holds bundles - k8s: enabled if a kubeconfig or in-cluster config resolves - oci: from the positional arguments, the PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO env var, or the status.contract.resolvedRef of the cluster's Pacto resources

When running alongside the Kubernetes operator, OCI repositories are automatically discovered from the status.contract.resolvedRef fields of Pacto CRD resources on every refresh. The result combines runtime state from the operator with contract content from OCI.

Every source contributes to one snapshot, rebuilt in the background, and each answer carries the as-of time and the completeness of the sources behind it.

pacto dashboard [sources...] [flags]

Examples:

  # Start dashboard with auto-detected sources
  pacto dashboard

  # Start from a specific directory
  pacto dashboard ./services

  # Include OCI repositories
  pacto dashboard oci://ghcr.io/org/order-service oci://ghcr.io/org/payment-service

  # Mix local and OCI sources
  pacto dashboard ./services oci://ghcr.io/org/payment-service

  # Custom port
  pacto dashboard --port 9090

  # Read only some Kubernetes namespaces (default: all namespaces)
  pacto dashboard --namespace payments,ledger

Flags:

      --allow-anonymous[=true|false]      serve beyond loopback without sign-in: everyone who reaches the address reads the whole fleet (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS)
      --context stringArray               kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from (repeatable, each cluster read once); outside a pod the named contexts replace the current one and people sign in against the first (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_CONTEXT)
      --cors-origin string                explicit cross-origin allowed to call the API (default: same-origin only)
      --delivery-namespace string         namespace Pacto delivery runs in, whose published identity policy (agent, break-glass and human groups, team prefix) says who is an agent and who may answer (default "pacto-delivery")
      --delivery-trust string             the trust config delivery records are verified with, so History reads signed records (the recorder's PEM public key or a YAML trust config; default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string                   what the operator detected, shown as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_DETECTED)
      --external-catalog string           organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST; a tag is refused (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_CATALOG)
      --fingerprints string               a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_FINGERPRINTS)
  -h, --help[=true|false]                 help for dashboard
      --host string                       bind address for the dashboard server (default "127.0.0.1")
      --mira-source stringArray           base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable; also PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES)
      --mira-url string                   Mira's address, to link health-check citations and open a service in Mira
      --namespace string                  Kubernetes namespaces to read, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces); delivery reads narrow to it only when it names one
      --oidc-ca-file string               PEM bundle of the CAs that sign the issuer's certificate, trusted on top of the system roots (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CA_FILE)
      --oidc-client-id string             OpenID Connect client id of the dashboard
      --oidc-display-name string          the identity provider's name on the sign-in button, as in Sign in with Keycloak (default OIDC; also PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME)
      --oidc-extra-scopes strings         scopes to ask for beyond openid, profile and groups
      --oidc-groups-claim string          ID token claim the API server takes the groups from; must match its claim mapping (default groups)
      --oidc-groups-prefix string         prefix the API server puts before every group; must match its claim mapping
      --oidc-internal-issuer-url string   address the dashboard reaches the issuer at when it differs from the public issuer URL browsers use, such as an in-cluster Service; ID tokens must still name the public issuer (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_INTERNAL_ISSUER_URL)
      --oidc-issuer-url string            OpenID Connect issuer people sign in with before the dashboard shows anything; every view then shows what the signed-in person's Kubernetes RBAC lets them read, and every action runs as them (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER_URL; the client secret comes from PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET)
      --oidc-redirect-url string          the dashboard's /auth/callback as browsers reach it (https)
      --oidc-username-claim string        ID token claim the API server takes the username from; must match its claim mapping (default sub)
      --oidc-username-prefix string       prefix the API server puts before the username; must match its claim mapping (default the issuer URL and #, none for the email claim; - for none)
      --owner-policy string               the mounted owner policy (the chart's declare block as policy.json) that decides who may set a service owner (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_OWNER_POLICY)
      --port int                          port for the dashboard server (default 3000)
      --review string                     how people are reviewed: cluster asks once about every namespace and needs a ClusterRole; local asks in each --namespace only, which a namespaced Role grants, and then services without a namespace show to nobody (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_REVIEW) (default "cluster")
      --session-idle-timeout duration     a session without a request for this long ends (default 1h)
      --session-max-age duration          a session ends this long after sign-in, renewed or not (default 12h)
      --stats-registry string             stats repository the Metrics page reads run records from (unsigned statistics; also PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY); a public repository is read anonymously, otherwise with the dashboard's registry credentials
      --token-login[=true|false]          let people sign in with a Kubernetes token: a ServiceAccount token minted with --audience pacto-dashboard reads the fleet only, and a person's own token acts as them (also PACTO_DASHBOARD_TOKEN_LOGIN)
      --trace-source stringArray          named offline OTLP/JSON trace source as NAME=PATH, where NAME is its stable data-source identity (repeatable; also PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES)
      --traces stringArray                OTLP/JSON trace file to fold observed dependencies from (repeatable; also PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES)

It auto-detects sources: pass OCI repositories as arguments, or run it next to the operator (with a kubeconfig) and it discovers OCI repositories from each Pacto resource's status.contract.resolvedRef. Use --no-cache for a cold start (it skips scanning pre-existing cached bundles; bundles fetched during the session are still cached).

For a tour of what the dashboard surfaces, see For platform engineers; to run it as a container, see Dashboard container.

docs.title: pacto declare
docs.text:
Declares a workload the cluster runs as a service with a contract. The workload is name, namespace/name, namespace/Kind/name or k8s:namespace/Kind/name. Its contract is drafted from the cluster with your kubeconfig credentials, as pacto init --cluster does, or read from --dir, a folder pacto init --cluster wrote (its cluster facts are read again).

Without --yes it prints the plan and writes nothing: the version (0.1.0 for a first declaration, else the published baseline raised by the change), contract only with the baseline's deploy artifact reused or none, every dependency range and who signs. Proposed ranges stay unknown unless you name the dependency with --accept. The plan ends with its intent digest.

--yes prints the plan, then publishes it: a contract-only bundle signed keyless by you through an interactive Sigstore login (a browser, or a device code with --device). Nothing is built, no deploy tag is written and no Git access is needed. Only that login writes a declared version: a key, an ambient OIDC token (SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN included) or a CI identity writes the next draft-<n> tag instead, and the output names the command a person runs to accept it with --from-draft. --intent refuses the run when the plan differs from the one you reviewed.

Setting, changing or removing service.owner (in a --dir folder or an accepted draft) takes a person who belongs to the current owner, declared or attested, or a default approver of the installation's owner policy; anyone else is refused before anything is pushed. The owner policy is read from the signed target snapshots in <registry>/pacto-targets, verified with --delivery-trust. An owner read from the workload's team label stays in pacto.inferred.yaml as inferred.

pacto declare <service> [flags]

Examples:

  # What declaring invoices would publish
  pacto declare billing/invoices --registry ghcr.io/acme

  # Accept the proposed range of ledger and publish, signed by you
  pacto declare billing/invoices --registry ghcr.io/acme --accept ledger --yes

  # Accept a draft an agent wrote
  pacto declare invoices --registry ghcr.io/acme --from-draft draft-3 --yes

Flags:

      --accept strings           a dependency whose proposed range you accept as declared; repeat it for more
      --call-window duration     how far back a call counts as a dependency (at least 1m, default 24h)
      --delivery-trust string    the trust config the target snapshots that carry the owner policy are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --device[=true|false]      log in with a device code instead of a browser
      --dir string               a folder pacto init --cluster wrote, declared instead of a new draft
      --from-draft string        accept this draft-<n> tag: the workload is read again and you sign
      --fulcio-url string        Fulcio to get the signing certificate from (default "https://fulcio.sigstore.dev")
  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for declare
      --intent string            the intent digest of the plan you reviewed: a different plan is refused
      --max-items int            the most items read per kind of object; a kind cut short reads as partial (default 10000)
  -n, --namespace string         the namespace of the workload (default: every namespace the name is found in)
      --oidc-client-id string    OpenID Connect client of the Sigstore login (default "sigstore")
      --oidc-issuer-url string   OpenID Connect issuer of the Sigstore login (default "https://oauth2.sigstore.dev/auth")
      --registry string          the registry the contract is published to, as host/path
      --rekor-url string         Rekor transparency log the signature is recorded in (default "https://rekor.sigstore.dev")
      --sign-key string          sign with this key file: a key names no person, so the run writes a draft
      --timestamp-url string     timestamp authority to date the signature with
      --trusted-root string      Sigstore trusted root JSON to verify with (default: public-good Sigstore)
      --yes[=true|false]         publish the plan (or write a draft) after printing it

docs.title: pacto delivery
docs.text:
Pacto delivery decides which version each environment (a Stage) runs. Every change is an Operation: plan it to see what the promoter will do and who must agree, propose it, and a person approves only when the contracts say a consumer would break, Pacto cannot see enough or the Stage asks for approval on every promote.

There is no approve tool for agents. approve is for people.

pacto delivery [flags]

Flags:

      --delivery-namespace string   namespace Pacto delivery runs in, whose published identity policy (agent, break-glass and human groups, team prefix) says who is an agent and who may answer (default "pacto-delivery")
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for delivery
  -n, --namespace string            namespace of the Stage and its Operations (default "default")
      --trust string                the trust config delivery records are verified with: the recorder's PEM public key, or a YAML file of keys and the streams each may sign (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)

docs.title: pacto delivery approve
docs.text:
Record your decision on a held operation, as the person your kubeconfig signs you in as. When the installation accepts signed approvals (delivery.identities.signers) and the Stage keeps an approvals repository, the command instead logs you in again in your browser, signs the decision keyless with that login alone and pushes the signed approval record to the registry; it never reads SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN or a CI token. When the promoter asks for a fresh login (delivery.promoter.authFreshness), the command instead makes you log in again in your browser (prompt=login, max_age=0) with its own OpenID Connect client and sends the Approval with that login's token, never your kubeconfig's: an agent running in your shell cannot approve as you without you typing your password at that moment. The token is not stored. With --intent and no operation name it reads no kubeconfig: it approves the operation a verified intent record names, signed keyless.

pacto delivery approve [<operation>] [flags]

Flags:

      --decision string             approve, reject or accept-unknown (default "approve")
      --fulcio-url string           Fulcio to get the signing certificate from, when the installation's signer names none (default "https://fulcio.sigstore.dev")
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for approve
      --intent string               approve the operation this intent record names (<repository>:<tag> or <repository>@<digest>) with no kubeconfig: the intent must verify with --trust, and the decision is signed keyless under a signer --signers names
      --keyless[=true|false]        sign the decision keyless into the Stage's approvals repository when the installation accepts signed approvals; false records it in the cluster (default true)
      --note string                 why, for the record
      --oidc-ca-file string         PEM bundle of the CAs that sign the issuer's certificate, trusted on top of the system roots (also PACTO_DELIVERY_OIDC_CA_FILE)
      --oidc-client-id string       OpenID Connect client used only for approvals, never by a kubeconfig (a confidential client's secret comes from PACTO_DELIVERY_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET) (default "pacto-approve")
      --oidc-extra-scopes strings   scopes to ask for beyond openid, profile and groups
      --oidc-issuer-url string      OpenID Connect issuer the cluster trusts, to log in again with (also PACTO_DELIVERY_OIDC_ISSUER_URL)
      --oidc-redirect-port int      loopback port the identity provider sends the browser back to (default: a free port)
      --signers string              the installation's identity policy (JSON or YAML, the pacto-delivery-identities ConfigMap's policy) whose signers verify an approval a person signed; used with a record reference
      --timestamp-url string        timestamp authority to date the signature with, when the installation's signer names none

docs.title: pacto delivery autonomy
docs.text:
How many of the services Pacto has seen have a contract, how many promotions in each Stage's window no person asked for or approved, each Stage's level with the next level Pacto proposes and its newest would-have decision, and the blockers with a fix to copy. It only reads: a level moves through a proposed and approved operation.

It runs the dashboard's own autonomy view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery autonomy [flags]

Flags:

      --blockers int        Where the page of blockers starts; limit and q apply to it too
      --domain string       With service: the service's registry domain, empty for the default. A Stage that names another domain is left out; one that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for autonomy
      --level string        Keep only the Stages at this level; none keeps those that report no level the ladder knows. It narrows the Stages, never byLevel or the blockers (observe, advise, auto-nonbreaking, autonomous, none)
      --limit int           How many per page; 0 means the list's default
      --offset int          Where the page starts. Past the end answers the last page
      --q string            Keep only what contains this text, ignoring case
      --service string      Keep only the Stages of the service with exactly this name; it narrows byLevel too, never the blockers or promotionsWithoutPerson

docs.title: pacto delivery blame
docs.text:
Say who put a version in place on a Stage: who asked, for whom, who approved and what every gate said

pacto delivery blame [flags]

Flags:

      --digest string       the version to blame (defaults to the one the Stage runs)
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for blame
      --stage string        the Stage (required)

docs.title: pacto delivery caller
docs.text:
The caller as the API server names them, their actor class (human, agent, break-glass or controller) and how it was decided, when they last logged in, whether a question that names no team has nobody who may answer it and whether owner teams narrow who may answer.

It runs the dashboard's own caller view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery caller [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for caller

docs.title: pacto delivery cancel
docs.text:
Cancel an operation that has not moved the pointer yet

pacto delivery cancel <operation> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for cancel

docs.title: pacto delivery candidates
docs.text:
List the versions a Stage may be promoted to: what pacto publish published that its candidate source offers

pacto delivery candidates [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for candidates
      --stage string        the Stage (required)

docs.title: pacto delivery describe
docs.text:
Show what an operation type checks, when a person is needed and how it is undone

pacto delivery describe <type> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for describe

docs.title: pacto delivery environments
docs.text:
Service by environment: the digest and version each Stage runs and whether it is verified, failed, frozen, held or on auto-hold. With service it also says, per Stage, which actions the caller may take and why, including freeze and undo.

It runs the dashboard's own environments view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery environments [flags]

Flags:

      --domain string        With service: the service's registry domain, empty for the default. A Stage that names another domain is left out; one that names none matches any
      --environment string   Keep only the services with a Stage in this environment, and only those Stages
      --except stringArray   Leave out the Stages in these environments (repeat the parameter), and the services left with none: the figure's folded station lists every environment but the ones it draws
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for environments
      --limit int            How many per page; 0 means the list's default
      --offset int           Where the page starts. Past the end answers the last page
      --q string             Keep only what contains this text, ignoring case
      --service string       Keep only the Stages of the service with exactly this name; with service, each row also offers freeze and undo
      --state string         Keep only the services with a Stage in this state (the one counts.byEnvironment counts it in), and only those Stages (failed, frozen, autohold, waiting, unverified, empty, verified)
      --tier string          Keep only the services with a Stage in an environment whose name says this tier (inferred from the name, never an order), and only those Stages (dev, test, prod)

docs.title: pacto delivery explain
docs.text:
Explain an operation: where it is, every verdict with its citation and how to run it again

pacto delivery explain <operation> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for explain

docs.title: pacto delivery get
docs.text:
Show an operation: phase, outcome, verdicts and the question a person is asked

pacto delivery get <operation> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for get

docs.title: pacto delivery history
docs.text:
List what happened on a Stage, from its signed records when the recorder runs, otherwise from the cluster

pacto delivery history [flags]

Flags:

      --all[=true|false]        walk every Stage in the namespace given with -n, or in every namespace you can list
      --at string               what each Stage ran at this RFC 3339 time, or this long before now, from its signed records; with --stage or --all
      --cause string            only changes whose cause (reason, operation or cited verdict) names this text, ignoring case; it narrows the timeline too
      --correlation-id string   only changes with exactly this correlation id; it narrows the timeline too
      --domain string           with --service, its registry domain; a Stage that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]       help for history
      --service string          with --all, only the Stages of this service
      --since string            only changes at or after this RFC 3339 time, or this long before now (2h)
      --stage string            the Stage (this or --all)
      --until string            only changes at or before this RFC 3339 time, or this long before now (30m)

docs.title: pacto delivery inbox
docs.text:
Held operations whose decision by the caller the promoter would count: the caller may update the Stage's workload and, when owner teams narrow who may answer, is in a team the question names (break-glass also gets those that name no team), with the decision asked and the affected services; a change whose update rights could not be checked marks the answer partial. Also the frozen Stages of the caller's services (every frozen Stage they can read when owner teams do not narrow) and the Errored operations on them.

It runs the dashboard's own inbox view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery inbox [flags]

Flags:

      --domain string        With service: the service's registry domain, empty for the default. A Stage that names another domain is left out; one that names none matches any
      --environment string   Keep only what waits to enter this environment: items on Stages whose spec.environment is this
      --errored int          Where the page of Errored changes starts
      --except stringArray   Leave out what waits to enter these environments (repeat the parameter); an empty value names held changes on Stages the caller cannot read. Like environment, it never narrows byEnvironment
      --frozen int           Where the page of frozen Stages starts
      --held int             Where the page of held changes starts
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for inbox
      --limit int            How many of each section per page; 0 means 25
      --q string             Keep only what names this text (namespace, Stage, service or change), ignoring case
      --service string       Keep only the Stages of the service with exactly this name and the changes on them; it narrows byEnvironment too, and a change on a Stage the caller cannot read is left out

docs.title: pacto delivery lifecycle
docs.text:
Follows one artifact of a service, named by exactly one of --digest, --version or --contract, through every Stage of the service you can see: whether pacto publish published it (Flux or the registry watch verified its signature) and, on each Stage, when it arrived, was verified, re-checked, rolled back or left, each from its signed record or the Operation's unsigned status. Without -n it reads every namespace you can list; one you cannot makes the answer partial and is named.

pacto delivery lifecycle [flags]

Flags:

      --contract string     its contract: a manifest digest or a digest-pinned reference
      --digest string       the artifact digest Stages point at
      --domain string       the service's registry domain; a Stage that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for lifecycle
      --service string      the service the version belongs to (required)
      --version string      the version its contract declares

docs.title: pacto delivery plan
docs.text:
Predict what the promoter will do: verdicts, the approval floor, the one question for a person and what must move first

pacto delivery plan [flags]

Flags:

      --cause-verdict pacto delivery explain --output-format json   a verdict (JSON, as pacto delivery explain --output-format json prints it) you cite as the cause; the promoter runs it again and refuses a cause that does not hold

docs.title: pacto delivery published
docs.text:
Per service the caller can see Stages of: the versions its Stages know, whether Flux or the registry watch verified their signature and which Stages run or verified each.

It runs the dashboard's own published view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery published [flags]

Flags:

      --domain string       With service: the service's registry domain, empty for the default. A Stage that names another domain is left out; one that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for published
      --limit int           How many per page; 0 means the list's default
      --offset int          Where the page starts. Past the end answers the last page
      --q string            Keep only what contains this text, ignoring case
      --service string      Keep only the versions of the service with exactly this name; it narrows counts too
      --signed string       yes: keep only the services whose every version is signed; no: keep only the services with an unsigned version, and only those versions; unknown: keep only the services with no unsigned version and a version whose signature Pacto cannot tell, and only those versions (yes, no, unknown)

docs.title: pacto delivery record
docs.text:
Work with the signed records of operations

pacto delivery record [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for record

docs.title: pacto delivery record get
docs.text:
Reads one signed record of a Stage's stream by its full id or by the short id a text history prints (sha256: and 12 hex characters), when only one record starts with it. A record reference (<repository>:<tag> or <repository>@<digest>) reads any record, approvals and intents included, with no kubeconfig.

pacto delivery record get <id-or-ref> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for get
      --signers string      the installation's identity policy (JSON or YAML, the pacto-delivery-identities ConfigMap's policy) whose signers verify an approval a person signed; used with a record reference
      --stage string        the Stage whose stream holds the record (with a record id)

docs.title: pacto delivery record verify
docs.text:
Verifies every record of a Stage's stream against the trust config and checks the chain. With a record reference (<repository>:<tag> or <repository>@<digest>) it reads no kubeconfig: it verifies that one record, an approval or intent included, and for an approval says whether the operation record lists it (counted).

pacto delivery record verify [<ref>] [flags]

Flags:

      --all[=true|false]    verify every Stage's stream in the namespace given with -n, or in every namespace you can list
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for verify
      --signers string      the installation's identity policy (JSON or YAML, the pacto-delivery-identities ConfigMap's policy) whose signers verify an approval a person signed; used with a record reference
      --stage string        the Stage (this or --all)

docs.title: pacto delivery refusals
docs.text:
Recent publishes Pacto refused, newest first, with the check that refused each and the version bump the change needs. recorded false means this cluster keeps no record of refused publishes, so an empty list proves nothing.

It runs the dashboard's own refusals view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery refusals [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for refusals

docs.title: pacto delivery status
docs.text:
Lists every Stage of one service you can see, in promotion order from each Stage's spec.candidates: the version it runs, its state as the dashboard counts it, its upstream, its candidate, its newest re-check, its level and the actions you may ask for (promote, unfreeze, freeze, undo), each with why or why not. Without -n it reads every namespace you can list; one you cannot makes the answer partial and is named. With --why it also plans the promote of each candidate, proposes nothing and says what holds it back.

pacto delivery status [flags]

Flags:

      --domain string       the service's registry domain; a Stage that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for status
      --service string      the service whose Stages to show (required)
      --why[=true|false]    also plan the promote of each Stage's candidate (proposing nothing) and say what holds it back

docs.title: pacto delivery targets
docs.text:
Work with the signed target snapshots CI reads without cluster credentials

pacto delivery targets [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for targets

docs.title: pacto delivery targets publish
docs.text:
Signs a target snapshot document and pushes it to <registry>/pacto-targets:cluster-<cluster>. The document is the JSON predicate of delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/target-snapshot/v1: the cluster UID, its completeness and limitations, the Pacto objects as the read contract and the workloads no Pacto targets. The command sets asOf to now, the publisher to the signing key and the registry mode to the one detected on the cluster's existing tag.

Production clusters publish from the operator once the chart's registry value is set. This command is for demos, tests and installations that build the document themselves.

--key takes a PEM private key or a pacto evidence keygen seed. After a push the command writes <key>.pub.pem when it is absent; it refuses to publish while that file holds another key. A reader verifies the snapshot only with a trust entry that holds that public key and is scoped to the cluster (streams: ["<cluster>//"]).

pacto delivery targets publish <file> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for publish
      --key string          the signing key: a PEM private key or a seed that pacto evidence keygen wrote
      --registry string     registry host and path the snapshot is written under, as <registry>/pacto-targets

docs.title: pacto delivery trust
docs.text:
Per service with a Stage that watches the registry and the caller can see: the installation's publisher rule or signed policy, the identities a person pinned, the CI signers waiting for a person to confirm them and the newest verdicts, each saying which source decided. Pins or a policy that could not be read mark the answer partial.

It runs the dashboard's own trust view with your kubeconfig identity, so the apiserver decides what you see. Without -n it reads the namespaces you may list Stages in and leaves out, without naming them, those outside your permissions; a namespace that refuses the list makes the answer partial and is named in unreadable. The answer is the dashboard's JSON in every output format.

pacto delivery trust [service] [flags]

Flags:

      --domain string       With service: the service's registry domain, empty for the default. A Stage that names another domain is left out; one that names none matches any
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for trust
      --limit int           How many per page; 0 means the list's default
      --offset int          Where the page starts. Past the end answers the last page
      --q string            Keep only what contains this text, ignoring case
      --service string      Keep only the service with exactly this name

docs.title: pacto delivery types
docs.text:
List the operation types you may propose

pacto delivery types [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for types

docs.title: pacto delivery undo
docs.text:
Plan how to undo an operation; it proposes nothing and prints the command that would

pacto delivery undo <operation> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for undo
      --stage string        the operation's Stage, needed only when the Operation was deleted and must be found in the records

docs.title: pacto diff
docs.text:
Compares two contracts (local paths or oci:// references) and produces a classified change set (BREAKING, POTENTIAL_BREAKING, NON_BREAKING).

pacto diff <old> <new> [flags]

Examples:

  # Compare a remote contract with a local one
  pacto diff oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc-pacto:1.0.0 my-service

  # Markdown output for CI comments
  pacto diff --output-format markdown oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc-pacto:1.0.0 my-service

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for diff
      --new-set stringArray      set a value on the new contract (e.g. --new-set service.version=2.0.0)
      --new-values stringArray   values file to merge into the new contract (can be repeated)
      --old-set stringArray      set a value on the old contract (e.g. --old-set service.version=1.0.0)
      --old-values stringArray   values file to merge into the old contract (can be repeated)
      --stats-context string     comma-separated context to include in the run record: repository, run-url, environment=<name>; nothing is included unless named
      --stats-file string        write the run record to this file for pacto stats publish, replacing the record it holds, so give each command its own file; default $PACTO_STATS_FILE
      --stats-registry string    publish an unsigned run record (statistics, never evidence) to this repository, for example ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats; default $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY

Exit code: 1 when the overall classification is BREAKING, and also when the diff could not be produced. A non-zero exit alone is therefore no contract verdict. See Exit codes for how to tell the two apart. A POTENTIAL_BREAKING result exits 0, so a CI gate that stops on it must read the classification.

The diff engine performs deep comparison of referenced OpenAPI specs, detecting changes at the path, method, parameter, request body and response level. The optional docs/ directory is ignored: documentation changes produce no diff entries and leave the compatibility classification unchanged.

When both bundles include an sbom/ directory with recognized SBOM files (.spdx.json or .cdx.json), pacto diff reports package-level changes: added, removed or modified packages (version and license). SBOM changes are informational and leave the overall classification and exit code unchanged.

When dependencies change between the old and new contracts (version upgrades, additions or removals), a dependency graph diff section is displayed showing the tree of affected nodes.

See Change Classification for the full rules.

docs.title: pacto doc
docs.text:
Reads a pacto.yaml in the given directory (or oci:// reference) and generates structured Markdown documentation.

pacto doc [dir | oci://ref] [flags]

Examples:

  # Print documentation to stdout
  pacto doc my-service

  # Write documentation to a file
  pacto doc my-service -o docs/

  # Serve documentation in the browser
  pacto doc my-service --serve

  # Serve on a custom port
  pacto doc my-service --serve --port 9090

  # Launch an interactive API explorer (Swagger UI)
  pacto doc my-service --ui swagger

  # Select a specific interface
  pacto doc my-service --ui swagger --interface public-api

  # Point try-it-out requests to a running backend
  pacto doc my-service --ui swagger --target http://localhost:3000

  # Per-interface target mapping
  pacto doc my-service --ui swagger --target public-api=http://localhost:3000 --target admin-api=http://localhost:3001

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for doc
      --interface string     interface name to display (used with --ui)
  -o, --output string        output directory for generated Markdown; a NAME.html value writes a static documentation site to a NAME/ directory instead
      --port int             port for the documentation server (used with --serve or --ui) (default 8484)
      --serve[=true|false]   serve the offline dashboard-grade documentation site over a local HTTP server
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --target stringArray   target server URL for try-it-out requests; supports interface=url mapping (used with --ui)
      --ui string            UI type for the interactive API explorer (one of: swagger)
  -f, --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

The header line reports the contract's own state. pacto doc reads a bundle and observes no cluster. A contract that has never been runtime-evaluated therefore reads status NotEvaluated, and one that declares no workload reads compliance REFERENCE. Both are the expected result for a freshly scaffolded contract. See Compliance states.

Markdown prints to stdout by default. -o DIR writes DIR/<service>.md. -o NAME.html writes a self-contained static documentation site (a directory) that reuses the dashboard UI offline.

--serve serves that static site locally. --ui swagger launches an interactive API explorer.

--serve, --ui and -o are mutually exclusive. Use --interface to pick one OpenAPI interface with --ui. --target and --target iface=url point try-it-out at a backend.

Sibling dependencies are resolved in parallel. OCI bundles cache under ~/.cache/pacto/oci/. --no-cache bypasses the cache.

docs.title: pacto evidence
docs.text:
Produce and verify the signed, versioned envelopes that carry a Pacto EvidenceSet from a remote or disconnected environment to a platform that ingests it. Keys are Ed25519; the wire format is defined by pkg/evidenceenvelope.

pacto evidence [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for evidence

docs.title: pacto evidence keygen
docs.text:
Writes the private seed to <keyId>.key (base64, 0600) and the public key into --out. With --producer, the public key is written as <producer>__<keyId>.pub, which binds the key to that producer in the trust store. Hand that file to the platform. Sign with the SAME --producer and --key-id. With no --producer, a bare <keyId>.pub binds the key to a producer named after the key id (the single-producer default).

pacto evidence keygen [flags]

Flags:

      --force[=true|false]   overwrite existing key files instead of failing
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for keygen
      --key-id string        key id (defaults to a fingerprint of the public key)
      --out string           directory to write the keypair into (default ".")
      --producer string      producer id to bind the key to (writes <producer>__<keyId>.pub)

docs.title: pacto evidence provisioned
docs.text:
Writes an EvidenceSet that reports the provisioning state of the resource a consumer's configuration reference or dependency asked for. Sign it with pacto evidence sign and post it with pacto evidence send. Any adapter (a CI job, a controller, a script) can run it; Pacto keeps no provider-specific code. The subject defaults to <repository>//<kind>/<name>, so each resource keeps its own latest report. Prints the EvidenceSet JSON. 

pacto evidence provisioned [flags]

Flags:

      --collector string       collector id recorded as provenance (defaults to pacto)
      --configuration string   consumer configuration (with a ref) that asked for the resource
      --contract string        consumer contract revision: oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest>
      --dependency string      consumer dependency that asked for the resource
      --environment string     consumer environment the resource serves
      --external-ref string    opaque handle of the resource at the provider (at most 253 printable bytes)
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for provisioned
      --observed-at string     observation timestamp (RFC3339; defaults to now)
      --outcome string         collection outcome: Observed, Unsupported, Failed, Stale or Insufficient; anything but Observed carries no phase (default "Observed")
      --phase string           provisioning phase: Requested, Provisioning, Ready, Failed or Deleting
      --provider string        provider slug (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens)
      --subject string         EvidenceSet subject (defaults to <repository>/<environment or default>/<kind>/<name>)

docs.title: pacto evidence send
docs.text:
Reads a signed envelope JSON file and POSTs it to an ingestion host's --url. Prints the host's JSON response and exits non-zero on a non-2xx status.

pacto evidence send <envelope.json> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for send
      --url string          ingestion host envelope endpoint URL

docs.title: pacto evidence serve
docs.text:
Starts an HTTP host that accepts signed evidence envelopes at POST /api/evidence/v1/envelopes, verifies them against --trust, evaluates the carried evidence against its resolved contract and publishes accepted records to the contract registry as OCI 1.1 referrers of the exact contract revision each report is about. Every --subject is an immutable oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest> reference; the registry is the only durable store, so the host keeps no local state and survives restarts. GET .../health is an always-200 liveness probe; .../ready reports 503 while a subject cannot be resolved or its referrers enumerated; .../producers advertises trusted producer ids; .../targets exposes the latest accepted targets. Registry credentials come from the same sources as pacto pull. Exactly one server may write to a subject set. Serves until interrupted.

pacto evidence serve [flags]

Flags:

      --cluster-id string            the kube-system namespace UID of the cluster this server runs in; the operator sets it
      --cluster-name string          display name of that cluster (needs --cluster-id)
      --cluster-name-source string   how the name was found: node-label, context, file or uid (needs --cluster-id)
  -h, --help[=true|false]            help for serve
      --listen-address string        host:port to listen on (supersedes --port)
      --port int                     port to listen on (127.0.0.1); superseded by --listen-address (default 8686)
      --producer stringArray         advertised trusted producer id (repeatable)
      --subject stringArray          exact contract revision evidence is stored on: oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest> (repeatable, required)
      --trust string                 trust store: a public-key file or a directory of <keyId>.pub files

docs.title: pacto evidence sign
docs.text:
Reads an EvidenceSet JSON file (- reads stdin), wraps it in an Ed25519-signed envelope and prints the envelope JSON. Only --issued-at is non-deterministic (it defaults to now), so pinning it is enough to make re-signing the same evidence produce a byte-identical envelope.

pacto evidence sign <evidence.json> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]         help for sign
      --id string                 envelope id (defaults to a hash over the API version, producer id, sequence and evidence, so two producers reporting identical evidence never collide)
      --issued-at string          issued-at timestamp (RFC3339; defaults to now)
      --key string                path to the private key file
      --key-id string             producer key id (must match the trust-store entry)
      --producer string           producer id
      --producer-version string   producer version (optional)
      --sequence uint             producer-scoped monotonic sequence; each report must be strictly greater than the producer's last
      --ttl duration              validity window; 0 disables expiry (default 24h0m0s)

docs.title: pacto evidence usage
docs.text:
Writes an EvidenceSet that reports how much of the resource a consumer's configuration reference or dependency asked for is used, and what it costs. Sign it with pacto evidence sign and post it with pacto evidence send; the signing key needs ResourceUsage in allowedObservationKinds. Pacto never sums or converts the figures. The subject defaults to <repository>//usage/<kind>/<name>, so a usage report never replaces the resource's provisioning report. Prints the EvidenceSet JSON. 

pacto evidence usage [flags]

Flags:

      --collector string       collector id recorded as provenance (defaults to pacto)
      --configuration string   consumer configuration (with a ref) that asked for the resource
      --contract string        consumer contract revision: oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest>
      --cost string            cost as amount:CURRENCY:period, such as 212.40:USD:P30D (ISO 4217 code, ISO 8601 period from P1D to P1Y)
      --dependency string      consumer dependency that asked for the resource
      --environment string     consumer environment the resource serves
      --external-ref string    opaque handle of the resource at the provider (at most 253 printable bytes)
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for usage
      --metric stringArray     a measured quantity as name=value[:unit], such as storage-used=31:Gi (repeatable, at most 16)
      --observed-at string     observation timestamp (RFC3339; defaults to now)
      --outcome string         collection outcome: Observed, Unsupported, Failed, Stale or Insufficient; anything but Observed carries no figures (default "Observed")
      --provider string        provider slug (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens)
      --subject string         EvidenceSet subject (defaults to <repository>/<environment or default>/usage/<kind>/<name>)

docs.title: pacto evidence verify
docs.text:
Decodes an envelope and verifies its signature, freshness and trust against a --trust public-key file or directory of <keyId>.pub files. Exits non-zero when verification fails.

pacto evidence verify <envelope.json> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for verify
      --trust string        trust store: a public-key file or a directory of <keyId>.pub files

docs.title: pacto explain
docs.text:
Parses a pacto.yaml in the given directory (or oci:// reference) and produces a human-readable summary of the service contract. Each configuration lists its effective values per environment: its inline values with that environment's file merged on top. With two or more environments it also lists the values they disagree on, for every environment or the ones --environments names. Last it lists what Pacto inferred from the service's folder, apart from the contract, each value with its source and the YAML that would declare it.

pacto explain [dir | oci://ref] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto explain my-service
  pacto explain oci://ghcr.io/acme/orders@sha256:<digest> --output-format json
  pacto explain my-service --environments test,production

Flags:

      --environments strings   compare the effective configuration values of two or more environments, such as test,production
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for explain
      --set stringArray        set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray     values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

What it covers. The text output summarises identity, workload, state, capabilities, interfaces, dependencies and readiness. To read configurations and policies, use pacto doc or open pacto.yaml. metadata is carried by --output-format json only; the text output omits it.

Readiness output. When the contract declares a readiness section (a pactoVersion: "2.0" feature), explain adds a Readiness block: the derived Score, the Gate result (PASS/FAIL with score / minScore), Earned and Total Weight, the partial credit multiplier, the assessment expires date with countdown (or an Expired state) and a per-check table showing each check's declared status (done/partial/not-done/deferred), category, weight, earned weight and evidence. The Readiness block also includes a revision-history table when history[] is present. --output-format json includes the same data plus doneCount, partialCount, notDoneCount, deferredCount and expired (boolean). Readiness status is time-dependent: the score is 0 when the current date is past the assessment-level expires.

docs.title: pacto export
docs.text:
Write what Pacto knows in another tool's format

pacto export [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for export

docs.title: pacto export backstage
docs.text:
Write the services Pacto knows as one multi-document YAML file of Backstage catalog entities: a Component per service, an API per interface, a Resource per external system, a System per business domain and a stub Component, tagged pacto-observed, per observed caller with no contract. Every entity says how Pacto knows it (pacto.trianalab.io/provenance), when (as-of) and how completely (completeness); an inferred value never fills spec.owner, spec.system, spec.dependsOn or spec.consumesApis.

The export reads the same sources as pacto fleet, except that it scans no local directory unless --local is set. When a source could not be read, or the fleet is empty, it writes nothing and exits 2, so a scheduled sync never drops the services that source holds; --allow-partial writes the file anyway. A --namespace scope whose namespaces were all read is not a failure: the file is written and each entity says partial.

pacto export backstage [flags]

Examples:

  pacto export backstage --oci ghcr.io/acme/payments --oci ghcr.io/acme/ledger > catalog/pacto-entities.yaml
  pacto export backstage --root oci://ghcr.io/acme/platform --k8s -o catalog/pacto-entities.yaml

Flags:

      --allow-partial[=true|false]    write the file even when the fleet is partial or empty
      --cache[=true|false]            include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray           kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --delivery-trust string         the trust config target snapshots are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string               add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray      base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --external-catalog string       organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string           a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --freshness duration            mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]             help for backstage

docs.title: pacto fleet attention
docs.text:
Lists what needs attention, most severe first, each item with its reason and next step. --category undeclared lists runtime calls no contract declares and callers with no contract. --category lifecycle lists services that use a deprecated or past-sunset provider, or whose range refuses its successor.

docs.title: pacto fleet entities
docs.text:
Lists services, owners, business domains and platform offerings, paged, or the one --kind you name. A filter that applies to one kind only (--readiness, --scope, --source-kind, --source-health) lists that kind when --kind is empty. Use --kind owner to learn the owner keys (team:NAME, dri:NAME) that --owner-key takes.

pacto fleet entities [text] [flags]

Flags:

      --capability string                services whose revisions declare this capability key, such as health or acme.io/cost
      --class string                     with --kind external, external systems of this class (vendor-api, managed-cloud, legacy, unclassified, other-egress)
      --cluster string                   entities in this cluster, by its UID as meta.clusters lists it: targets, services with a target or an inferred workload there and revisions a target there runs; other kinds ignore it
      --consumes string                  services that depend on or reference a provider of this platform offering
      --created-from string              services created from this golden path, by key; (none) for no declared origin or (unresolved) for an origin that resolves to no golden path

      --domain string                    exact registry path, the domain part of a service key
      --environment string               with --kind target, targets in this environment (the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/environment label); with --consumes and --phase, only the consumers whose status in that phase is in this environment

docs.title: pacto fleet entity
docs.text:
Inspect one entity. For a service, --reached also reads, with your cluster credentials, when each change's revision first reached each Stage you may read, from delivery history. A --local fleet keys revisions by content, so their changes match no delivery record.

pacto fleet entity <kind> <key> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for entity
      --reached[=true|false]   read when each change reached a Stage from signed delivery records, with your cluster credentials
      --trust string           with --reached: the trust config delivery records are verified with (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)

docs.title: pacto fleet explain
docs.text:
Explain the deterministic reasons for a service or target state. Give external:<identity> to list the sources that declare an external system and the catalog entry that classified it.

pacto fleet explain <subject> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for explain

docs.title: pacto fleet get
docs.text:
Inspect a logical service by name, an external system by external:<identity> (a vendor, managed service or legacy host no Pacto contract describes) or an operational target with --target.

pacto fleet get [service] [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for get
      --target string       inspect an operational target by key or name

docs.title: pacto fleet graph
docs.text:
Traverse the operational graph from an explicit root. Give a service name to aggregate across its revisions, or --revision/--target to root an exact revision (never 'latest'). The walk also follows observed runtime calls, so services no contract connects appear too; each node reports its provenance (declared, observed or declared+observed, or inferred for an external system's consumer known only from its configuration or a runtime call one of whose ends no contract describes). Those inferred calls are listed after the nodes with the sources that saw them, and a service asked for by the key of an inferred service it replaced says so first. Give external:<identity> to list the consumers of an external system (its only direction is dependents).

pacto fleet graph <service> [flags]

Flags:

      --direction string          traversal direction (dependencies, dependents); unset means dependencies, or dependents for an external: root
  -h, --help[=true|false]         help for graph
      --max-depth int             maximum transitive depth (0 = unlimited)
      --revision string           root an exact contract revision key
      --target string             root the revision linked to this target key or name
      --transitive[=true|false]   traverse transitively (cycle-safe)

docs.title: pacto fleet neighborhood
docs.text:
Shows who a service depends on and who depends on it, to the requested depth, each with its owner and status, then the edges between them: each says whether a contract declares it, telemetry observed it or both, and how the two compare. A runtime call one of whose ends no contract describes is listed as inferred, with the sources that saw it, and never satisfies a dependency. The service is a name, or its key when the name is used in more than one domain.

pacto fleet neighborhood <service> [flags]

Flags:

      --depth int           how many hops to walk (0 = 1, at most 6)
      --direction string    which side to walk (dependencies, dependents, both) (default "both")
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for neighborhood
      --max-edges int       maximum edges (0 = 120, at most 1000)
      --max-nodes int       maximum services (0 = 60, at most 500)
      --views string        comma-separated knowledge views (expected, observed, differences) (default "expected,observed")

docs.title: pacto fleet overview
docs.text:
Summarizes the organization in one answer: target compliance (with how many compliant targets rest on stale evidence), operational health, the knowledge gaps the contracts leave, ownership, evaluation coverage, the business domains and where to look next. A target is failing when its own health check reports it is not healthy and unknown when Pacto cannot tell; unknown is never a pass.

pacto fleet overview [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for overview

docs.title: pacto fleet providers
docs.text:
Lists what Pacto detected in each source it read: the evidence it found, what it uses each provider for and its status, with the limitations that make a row partial. A Kubernetes source Pacto could not read is listed as not read, never as nothing detected.

pacto fleet providers [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for providers

docs.title: pacto fleet publish-inferred
docs.text:
Builds the fleet snapshot from the source flags and, for every external system it knows with at least one consumer, publishes an inferred contract to <registry>/pacto-inferred/<identity>: a pacto.yaml naming the external and a pacto.inferred.yaml listing the hosts, ports and client majors the fleet sees, each with the sources that saw it. A new 0.0.<n> tag is pushed only when that surface changed, annotated run.pacto.contract.provenance: inferred and signed with --key. It names no consumer, and a range is never checked against it.

Clusters publish from the operator once the chart's registry value is set. This command is for installations that run no operator, such as the Compose demo; never run it against a registry an operator already writes.

--key takes a PEM private key or a pacto evidence keygen seed. Readers recognise its signature as the operator's only when their --detected advertisement names its public key; otherwise they say the signature could not be checked.

pacto fleet publish-inferred [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for publish-inferred
      --key string          the installation signing key: a PEM private key or a seed that pacto evidence keygen wrote
      --registry string     registry host and path the installation repositories live under, as <registry>/pacto-inferred/<identity>

docs.title: pacto fleet reconcile

docs.title: pacto generate
docs.text:

docs.title: pacto graph
docs.text:
Resolves the dependency tree from a pacto.yaml in the given directory (or oci:// reference) and displays the graph, cycles and version conflicts.

pacto graph [dir | oci://ref] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto graph my-service
  pacto graph --with-references
  pacto graph --only-references

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]              help for graph
      --only-references[=true|false]   Show only config/policy reference edges (no dependencies)
      --set stringArray                set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray             values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

Dependencies resolved from local paths are annotated with [local]. Shared dependencies (referenced by multiple parents) are annotated with (shared).

Reports cycles, version conflicts and unreachable dependencies.

Sibling dependencies are resolved in parallel. OCI bundles are cached locally in ~/.cache/pacto/oci/ for faster subsequent operations. Use --no-cache to bypass the cache.

docs.title: pacto impact
docs.text:
Composes a semantic contract diff (old→new) with the operational graph to answer which consumers a change really affects, how strong the evidence is and whether their declared compatibility still holds.

When no fleet source holds the changed service, the new revision is added to the snapshot so the services that depend on it are found.

With --running, impact judges <new> against the revisions of its service that run on known targets instead of an <old> revision, and keeps the worst gate. A running consumer whose range rejects <new> blocks it whatever the classification, and a partial answer never clears. A local <new> takes the fleet domain that holds its service name; a name several domains hold exits 1 with their keys (judge the oci:// reference instead). With no running revision the new one is a first version: it is blocked when a running consumer's range rejects it, and clear only on a complete answer whose running consumers all accept it. A running revision Pacto could not link, pull or trust, one linked by tag only, an inferred workload of the service, a workload source Pacto could not read and a local <new> in no fleet domain each make the answer unverified at best. Running revisions are pulled only from the hosts of the target snapshots and of an oci:// <new>, plus the comma-separated hosts in $PACTO_RUNNING_REGISTRIES.

With --unavailable, --removed or --regressed, impact answers what happens if that service becomes unavailable, is removed or a revision of it regressed. --unavailable and --removed also take offering:<name>, which asks the same of every service that provides the platform offering. Consumers are graded breaks (every edge on their path is required), may degrade (an optional edge) or unknown. The gate is unverified (exit 2) when anything depends on the service and clear (exit 0) only when the complete snapshot shows nothing does. --regressed with an artifact digest reads delivery's recorded failures with your own cluster credentials when a cluster is reachable.

The answer ends in a release gate, and the exit status follows it: 0 clear: the change is not BREAKING and every service that references its policy passes the new policy, or the snapshot is complete and no service depends on the changed one. 1 blocked: a consumer that runs on a known target does not accept the new version of a BREAKING change, or its contract fails the changed service's new policy, whatever the classification. 2 unverified: nothing is shown to block the change, but the answer cannot clear it: a BREAKING change whose answer is partial or whose consumers none is shown to be safe, or a service that references the changed policy and fails it running nowhere known, could not be checked or could not be resolved. A run over --local bundles alone knows no targets, so a BREAKING change with consumers exits 2. A command that could not run also exits 1, with nothing on stdout. Add --target-state (or a live source) so the gate can tell deployed impact apart.

Pacto finds consumers only in the sources you pass, such as --local, --root, --oci, --cache, --k8s, --evidence-url, --traces and the target snapshot. With --local alone Pacto sees only the contracts in those folders, so "No affected consumers" is not evidence of safety.

When you pass no --k8s, --target-state, --evidence-url or --target-snapshot, impact reads the signed target snapshot each cluster's operator publishes (--target-snapshot auto, the default): from the oci:// ref of the change it tries <prefix>/pacto-targets under each path prefix of its repository, deepest first and at most three segments deep (the registry value the operator publishes under), then <host>/pacto-targets, and prints a Registry line saying where it looked and a Targets line per cluster snapshot it read. auto reads only the clusters whose snapshot exists at that moment, so CI that knows its clusters pins them with --target-snapshot oci://<registry>/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid> (repeatable). --delivery-trust names the trust config that verifies each snapshot; an unverified or stale snapshot never clears a BREAKING change. --target-snapshot off reads none.

From the same ref impact also reads the consumers published to the organization index, <host>//pacto-index then <host>/pacto-index, checks them against the target snapshot it reads and prints a Consumers line; --index names another <registry>/pacto-index, --index none reads none, a --root list skips it and a pair of --local folders reads no index. 

pacto impact <old> <new> | --running <new> | --unavailable <service> | --removed <service> | --regressed <service>@<revision> [flags]

Examples:

  # Impact of upgrading a local service against the local fleet
  pacto impact ./svc-v1 ./svc-v2 --local .

  # Impact of a published service against the clusters that run it, read
  # from the target snapshot next to its registry
  pacto impact oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc:1.0.0 ./svc --delivery-trust trust.yaml

  # Judge a folder's contract against the revisions that run in the pinned
  # clusters, as a GitOps render gate does
  pacto impact --running . --target-snapshot oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid> --delivery-trust trust.yaml

  # Include observed (runtime) evidence and emit JSON
  pacto impact oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc:1.0.0 ./svc --include-observed --output-format json

  # What breaks if redis becomes unavailable, or postgresql is removed
  pacto impact --unavailable redis --local .
  pacto impact --removed postgresql --local . --target-state targets.yaml

  # What breaks if every provider of the postgresql offering becomes unavailable
  pacto impact --unavailable offering:postgresql --local .

  # What a regressed artifact affects, with delivery's recorded failures
  pacto impact --regressed payments-service@sha256:<digest> --local .

Flags:

      --cache[=true|false]              include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray             kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --delivery-trust string           the trust config target snapshots are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string                 add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray        base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --external-catalog string         organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string             a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --freshness duration              mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]               help for impact
      --include-observed[=true|false]   let observed (runtime) relationships raise consumer confidence
      --index string                    organization index pacto impact and pacto ci read consumers from, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the provider reference; none reads none; skipped when --root names the consumers; pacto ci --publish also writes its entries there; other fleet commands ignore it)
      --k8s[=true|false]                include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray               local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --mira-source stringArray         base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable)
      --namespace string                namespaces to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces)
      --new-set stringArray             set a value on the new contract (e.g. --new-set service.version=2.0.0)
      --new-values stringArray          values file to merge into the new contract (can be repeated)
      --oci stringArray                 registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --old-set stringArray             set a value on the old contract (e.g. --old-set service.version=1.0.0)
      --old-values stringArray          values file to merge into the old contract (can be repeated)
      --policy stringArray              range policy for a BREAKING change, repeatable: unknown-range=warn|fail and uncontracted=warn|fail:<window> (such as fail:7d); default warn
      --regressed string                what happens if <service>@<revision> regressed; an artifact digest reads delivery's recorded failures
      --removed string                  what happens if this service (a fleet service key, or a name only one domain holds) is removed; offering:<name> asks it of every provider of an offering
      --root stringArray                contract root whose whole dependency closure joins the snapshot: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --running[=true|false]            judge <new> against the revisions of its service that run on known targets instead of an <old> revision; a running revision with the new digest is not a baseline; with no running revision only consumers' ranges are checked
      --stats-context string            comma-separated context to include in the run record: repository, run-url, environment=<name>; nothing is included unless named
      --stats-file string               write the run record to this file for pacto stats publish, replacing the record it holds, so give each command its own file; default $PACTO_STATS_FILE
      --stats-registry string           publish an unsigned run record (statistics, never evidence) to this repository, for example ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats; default $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY
      --target-snapshot stringArray     signed target snapshot(s) to read targets from: an oci:// pacto-targets repository, or :cluster-<uid> tags or digests to pin the clusters CI expects (repeatable); pacto impact, pacto ci and pacto_impact on a stdio pacto mcp also take auto (the default: derived from the provider ref) and off
      --target-state stringArray        offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces string                   OTLP/JSON trace file; its observed edges corroborate and surface consumers (implies --include-observed)
      --unavailable string              what happens if this service (a fleet service key, or a name only one domain holds) becomes unavailable; offering:<name> asks it of every provider of an offering

docs.title: pacto init
docs.text:
Writes the contract for the service in dir (default: the current folder).

An empty or new folder gets a blank contract with the bundle structure (interfaces/, configuration/) and the owner and domain you pass; with no --owner the owner is a commented placeholder that Unknown names. A folder that already holds a service gets a contract read from its Dockerfile and Kubernetes manifests, and a list of what Pacto found and what it could not tell (Unknown). The workload's environment, including the ConfigMaps it reads, becomes a configuration schema of keys and types, with no values: a key read from a Secret, named like a password, secret, token, key, credential, private key or DSN, or holding a URL with credentials is marked writeOnly, and a literal value for one is named under next steps. A URL in the environment that names another service in the cluster becomes a dependency with compatibility unknown: with that service's contract in --fleet, its bundle and a proposed range from its version in a comment; without it, the comment says no range was proposed. Vendors, managed services and legacy hosts that the folder names (the environment, Helm values files, Compose, Kustomize generators, SDK manifests and lockfiles, Terraform resources and Crossplane objects) are classified with the external catalog and listed under External dependencies as inferred: they go in pacto.inferred.yaml, never in pacto.yaml. --external-catalog merges an organization catalog, pinned by digest, over the default. Only their host and port are shown; a Secret gives its name and key names, never a value. A readiness, liveness or startup probe becomes a health check. A folder that already holds pacto.yaml at pactoVersion 2.5 (or none) is completed, never with --cluster: Pacto never changes it and lists what the folder adds, which pacto pack and pacto publish put in pacto.inferred.yaml. An older pacto.yaml is not completed, and the plan says to raise its pactoVersion.

Neither contract has a publish section or a service.version: pacto ci --publish derives both, and the image tag is named under Found as the version to declare for a first publish. --describe-only changes only the next steps, which say how to validate the contract instead of how to publish it. --delivery also writes the cluster pieces, reading the repositories pacto ci --publish publishes to under --registry (default: the workload's image registry, else the registry.example placeholder): the Pacto resource that checks the running service, and per environment a Stage with the Flux OCIRepository and Kustomization it applies through. Each Stage verifies an identity that matches nothing until you set the one pacto ci --publish signs as. Each Stage starts at observe: it plans every new version and moves nothing, and the OCIRepository stays pinned to the tag you deploy, so GitOps keeps applying what it did. The last environment's Stage also asks a person to approve every promote.

--owner is the team's bare name, such as billing: usually the team label on the workload. --domain is the business domain, such as payments. An AI agent is a service too: its tools are an mcp interface, the model it calls is a dependency and its eval suite is a checks entry; see https://pacto.run/latest/contract-reference/checks/#an-agent-is-a-service.

Several folders are each pactified, with a summary at the end. --cluster drafts a contract for every workload in the namespaces that no Pacto describes yet, in <out>/<namespace>/<name>: its manifests are read from the cluster, and the services its pods were seen calling become dependencies with compatibility unknown and a proposed range, in a comment, from the lowest version the Pactos describing each one report, when they agree on one contract. Ranges are proposed, never declared: declare each one. Each draft also gets pacto.inferred.yaml, completed by the engine pacto ci uses, with when each cluster fact was read and whether every node was observed. --max-items bounds each kind of object read; a kind cut short is listed under Coverage, and a run it stopped while listing workloads prints the command that resumes with --continue. Drafts are only written, never published, and a draft that is not valid fails the command.

With --from the service is created from a golden path: an oci:// reference or a directory whose contract declares service.template. The path's contract is copied with its identity reset: the name, version 0.1.0, --owner (required) and --domain, with --values and --set applied over any field and service.origin recording the path it came from. A path read from a registry is pulled by digest; when the trust config (--trust, else $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST) names a template key, the path must be signed by one or nothing is created, and otherwise the signature is reported Unknown. The created contract is validated with its references resolved before anything is written, and the Status block says what was checked and what Pacto cannot tell yet. Each plugin the path names is listed with the binary it resolves to; only the ones you name with --run-plugins run, never with --plan, and the files they return are added like the path's own. --delivery plans the cluster pieces from the created contract when the path publishes manifests under publish.deploy; otherwise the delivery step says why none were planned.
