It only adds files and missing .pactoignore lines; any other file already there is yours and is left as it is, so running it twice is safe. --plan shows exactly what would be added and changes nothing.

pacto init [dir...] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto init my-service
  pacto init my-service --owner billing --domain payments --registry ghcr.io/acme
  pacto init --plan
  pacto init --describe-only --owner billing
  pacto init --delivery --owner payments --fleet ../contracts
  pacto init --delivery --insecure-registry
  pacto init --delivery --registry-secret registry-creds
  pacto init services/checkout services/payments --plan
  pacto init --cluster --namespace shop --out drafts
  pacto init gift-cards --from oci://ghcr.io/acme/paths/http-service:1.0.0 --owner checkout --domain commerce

Flags:

      --call-window duration               with --cluster: how far back a call counts as a dependency (at least 1m, default 24h)
      --cluster[=true|false]               draft a contract for every workload in the cluster that no Pacto describes, reading the current kubeconfig context
      --continue string                    with --cluster: resume the read where a run --max-items stopped while listing workloads left off
      --delivery[=true|false]              also declares each --env in pacto.yaml with an empty values file, and writes the cluster pieces of a manifests deploy: the Pacto resource, a Stage per environment and a Flux OCIRepository and Kustomization; a chart deploy gets no applier object
      --describe-only[=true|false]         write a contract that only describes the service: its next steps say how to validate it, never how to publish it
      --domain string                      business domain, such as payments
      --env strings                        environments for --delivery: declared in the contract and given a Stage each, in promotion order (default [test,prod])
      --external-catalog string            organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST; a tag is refused (also PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG)
      --fleet strings                      folders of other services' contracts to find the services that use this one
      --from string                        a golden path to create the service from: an oci:// reference or a directory
  -h, --help[=true|false]                  help for init
      --insecure-registry[=true|false]     with --delivery: the Flux OCIRepositories read the registry over plain HTTP (a local registry only)
      --max-items int                      with --cluster: the most items read per kind of object; a kind cut short reads as partial (default 10000)
      --name string                        service name (default: the workload's name, then the folder's)
      --namespace strings                  with --cluster: a namespace to read; repeat it for more (default: every namespace)
      --no-transparency-log[=true|false]   with --from: write transparencyLog: false under the golden path's publish.sign
      --out string                         with --cluster: the folder the drafts go in, one <namespace>/<name> folder each
      --owner string                       the team that owns the service, as a bare name such as billing (default: the workload's team label)
      --plan[=true|false]                  show what would be added and change nothing
      --registry string                    where to publish, as host/path (default: read from the workload's image)
      --registry-secret string             with --delivery: the docker-registry Secret, in each environment's namespace, that Flux and the Pacto resource log in to a private registry with
      --run-plugins strings                run these plugins the golden path names, by name (see the plan's plugin steps); each step prints the binary it runs
      --set stringArray                    set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --trust string                       the trust config the golden path's signature is verified with: a PEM public key or a trust config file (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
  -f, --values stringArray                 values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

In an empty folder it scaffolds three files: a valid pacto.yaml, a placeholder OpenAPI spec at interfaces/openapi.yaml and a configuration JSON Schema at configuration/schema.json.

The folder's last part becomes service.name, which must match ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$, so pacto init fleet/checkout-web writes a contract for checkout-web in fleet/checkout-web. Pass --name to choose another name.

--owner becomes service.owner.team; without it the owner is a commented placeholder and Unknown names it. --domain becomes service.domain. The contract gets no publish section and no service.version: pacto ci --publish derives both and publishes to the registry its own --registry names.

All three files are required by the scaffolded contract, because its interfaces: and configurations: sections point at the other two files. If you delete a directory, also delete the section that references it, or validation fails with FILE_NOT_FOUND. A contract that declares neither section needs only pacto.yaml, so drop the section and the directory together.

--from creates one service from a golden path, in a folder that holds no pacto.yaml yet, so it refuses --cluster and several folders. --values, --set, --trust and --run-plugins go with --from. --values files apply first, then --set; a null removes a field. --trust takes a trust config file or a bare PEM public key, which then verifies golden paths in every repository; a bare key in $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST verifies records only. Only role: template keys verify a golden path; see Trust. The path's pacto.lock is not copied: run pacto lock in the new folder to pin its references. --delivery, with --env, --registry-secret and --insecure-registry, plans the cluster pieces from the new contract when the path publishes manifests under publish.deploy; otherwise the delivery step says why none were planned.

docs.title: pacto lock
docs.text:
Resolves the full transitive dependency and reference closure and writes a committed pacto.lock pinning each to its OCI digest. With --check, verifies the existing lock without writing.

pacto lock [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto lock
  pacto lock --update
  pacto lock --update-name auth
  pacto lock --check

Flags:

      --check[=true|false]        verify pacto.lock is up to date without writing (non-zero exit on drift)
  -h, --help[=true|false]         help for lock
      --set stringArray           set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --update[=true|false]       re-resolve dependencies to the newest version within their constraint
      --update-name stringArray   re-resolve only the named dependency, preserving all other pins (repeatable)
  -f, --values stringArray        values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

See Lockfile for the lock model and how .pactoignore keeps a pacto.lock out of a pushed bundle.

docs.title: pacto login
docs.text:
Stores credentials for an OCI registry in ~/.config/pacto/config.json.

pacto login <registry> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto login ghcr.io -u my-username

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for login
  -p, --password string     registry password
  -u, --username string     registry username

Credentials are stored in ~/.config/pacto/config.json (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pacto/config.json), keeping them separate from Docker's configuration.

docs.title: GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
docs.text:
For GitHub registries (ghcr.io and docker.pkg.github.com), pacto can reuse credentials from the GitHub CLI, so you can skip pacto login.

If you already have gh installed and authenticated, pacto will use gh auth token to obtain a token transparently. To verify your setup:

# Check if gh is authenticated
gh auth status

# Verify the token is available
gh auth token

To push container images or packages, your token needs the write:packages scope. If you authenticated gh without it, refresh your scopes:

gh auth refresh --scopes write:packages

After this, pacto push oci://ghcr.io/... will work without any additional login step.

If gh is missing or unauthenticated, pacto moves on to the next credential source in the chain.

docs.title: pacto logout
docs.text:
Removes credentials for an OCI registry from ~/.config/pacto/config.json.

pacto logout <registry> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto logout ghcr.io

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for logout

docs.title: pacto mcp
docs.text:
Starts a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing Pacto tools for AI agents. Supports stdio (default) and HTTP transports.

When a bundle reference (local directory or oci:// ref) is given, the server also exposes one executable tool per OpenAPI operation in the bundle's openapi interfaces, plus a pacto_skill tool for any skills/*.md domain knowledge. Read-only (GET/HEAD) operations are exposed by default; pass --allow-writes to expose mutating operations.

With --root, the server exposes a read-only contract catalog: the given roots plus their dependency closure, resolved once at startup and then frozen, so the session keeps its startup view even when a registry tag moves. Roots that fail to resolve stay visible as partial knowledge. The catalog grants no authorization and executes nothing.

With --fleet, the server exposes the read-only operational-graph query tools over a fleet snapshot, rebuilt when a call arrives 30 seconds or more after the last rebuild attempt. With --dashboard-url their answers link each entity to its page on that dashboard. The shared fleet source flags (--local, --target-state, --evidence-url, --traces, --mira-source, --oci, --cache, --k8s, --namespace and --freshness) compose that snapshot and are read in --fleet mode only.

With --delivery, the server exposes the Pacto delivery tools (pacto_delivery_*) over the ambient cluster: operation types, plan, get, explain, history, blame, undo plans and record checks, the dashboard's delivery views (caller, inbox, environments, autonomy, published and refusals, scoped by --namespace like the dashboard's), plus propose and cancel only when the apiserver says the caller is an agent (a service account, or an agent by the identity policy Pacto delivery publishes). It has no approve tool.

Over HTTP on loopback without --auth-issuer, the server prints a bearer at launch (pmcp_..., this launch only) and every request must carry it, so other local processes cannot call the server.

Over HTTP, --auth-issuer and --resource make every request carry a bearer token the server verifies (issuer, audience, expiry) and publish protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728); a bind beyond loopback needs them and refuses --auth and --allow-writes, which would lend this process's service credential to every caller. With --delivery the server then exchanges each caller's token for one the apiserver accepts (RFC 8693, --exchange-client-id) and builds the tools for that caller on every request, so an agent proposes as itself and a person gets the read-only tools. With --fleet the server exchanges each caller's token the same way, asks the apiserver who the caller is (a SelfSubjectReview) and asks Kubernetes RBAC what that user may read.

With --publish, the authoring server also exposes pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish, which publish a contract's version exactly as pacto publish does, with this process's registry credentials.

Over HTTP the contract tools are pacto_schema and pacto_declare: pacto_create, pacto_edit and pacto_check read and write the server's folders and follow refs with its credentials, so they run beside the agent over stdio. pacto_declare plans declaring a running workload; over stdio it writes a draft-<n> tag a person accepts with pacto declare --from-draft, and over HTTP (with --auth-issuer and token exchange) it plans with the caller's own cluster credentials, only in the registries --oci names, and writes nothing.

A bundle reference, --fleet and --delivery combine in one server; --root and --publish select servers of their own. Call pacto_capabilities to learn what a server serves.

pacto mcp [bundle-ref] [flags]

Examples:

  # Start MCP server over stdio (default)
  pacto mcp

  # Start MCP server over HTTP
  pacto mcp -t http

  # Expose a bundle's OpenAPI operations as agent tools
  pacto mcp ./my-service --base-url https://api.example.com

  # Include mutating operations and an auth credential
  pacto mcp oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc:1.0.0 --base-url https://api.example.com \
    --auth bearerAuth=$TOKEN --allow-writes

  # Expose a contract catalog discovered from explicit roots
  pacto mcp --root oci://ghcr.io/acme/platform:1.4.0 --root ./experimental-platform

Flags:

      --allow-writes[=true|false]     expose mutating operations (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) as tools
      --audience string               with --auth-issuer: the audience incoming tokens must carry (default --resource)
      --auth stringArray              credential for a security scheme as name=value (repeatable)
      --auth-issuer string            OpenID issuer whose bearer tokens every HTTP request must carry
      --base-url string               base URL for live invocation (overrides the OpenAPI servers[] URL)
      --cache[=true|false]            include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray           kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --dashboard-url string          with --fleet: base URL of a Pacto dashboard; fleet answers then carry an href to each entity's page there
      --delivery[=true|false]         expose the Pacto delivery tools over the ambient cluster
      --delivery-namespace string     in --delivery mode: namespace Pacto delivery runs in, whose published identity policy (agent, break-glass and human groups, team prefix) says who is an agent and who may answer (default "pacto-delivery")
      --delivery-trust string         the trust config delivery records (in --delivery mode), the golden paths pacto_create creates from and the target snapshots (the owner policy pacto_declare reads included) pacto_impact and --target-snapshot read are verified with (a PEM public key or a YAML trust config: the recorder's key for records, the operator's advertised installation key for a target snapshot, which verifies only under a key scoped to its cluster: streams ["<uid>/*/*"]; default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string               add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray      base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --exchange-audience string      with --fleet or --delivery over HTTP with --auth-issuer: the audience to exchange for, one the apiserver accepts (default "pacto-cli")
      --exchange-client-id string     with --fleet or --delivery over HTTP with --auth-issuer: the server's own OAuth client, which exchanges each caller's token for the cluster (RFC 8693); its secret comes from PACTO_MCP_EXCHANGE_CLIENT_SECRET
      --external-catalog string       organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string           a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --fleet[=true|false]            expose read-only operational-graph (fleet) query tools
      --freshness duration            mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]             help for mcp
      --host string                   bind address for HTTP transport; beyond loopback it needs --auth-issuer, and on loopback without it every request carries the bearer printed at launch (default "127.0.0.1")
      --index string                  organization index pacto impact and pacto ci read consumers from, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the provider reference; none reads none; skipped when --root names the consumers; pacto ci --publish also writes its entries there; other fleet commands ignore it)
      --k8s[=true|false]              include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray             local bundle root(s) to scan in --fleet mode (repeatable); over HTTP none unless set (default [.])
      --mira-source stringArray       base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable)
      --namespace string              namespaces to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces)
      --oci stringArray               registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --oidc-groups-claim string      ID token claim the API server takes the groups from; must match its claim mapping (default groups)
      --oidc-groups-prefix string     prefix the API server puts before every group; must match its claim mapping
      --oidc-username-claim string    ID token claim the API server takes the username from; must match its claim mapping (default sub)
      --oidc-username-prefix string   prefix the API server puts before the username; must match its claim mapping (default the issuer URL and #, none for the email claim; - for none)
      --owner-policy string           over HTTP: the mounted owner policy (the chart's declare block as policy.json) that names who may set a service owner in pacto_declare plans; refused over stdio, which reads it from the signed target snapshots
      --port int                      port for HTTP transport (default 8585)
      --publish[=true|false]          expose pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish beside the authoring tools
      --resource string               with --auth-issuer: this endpoint's URL as clients reach it, served as protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728)
      --review string                 with --fleet over HTTP with --auth-issuer: how people are reviewed: cluster asks once about every namespace and needs a ClusterRole; local asks in each --namespace only, which a namespaced Role grants, and then services without a namespace show to nobody (default "cluster")
      --root stringArray              contract root to discover a read-only catalog from: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --stats-read-registry string    with --fleet: the stats repository pacto_stats reads; it reads and never records. Over stdio the default is $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY; over HTTP only this flag enables pacto_stats
      --target-snapshot stringArray   signed target snapshot(s) to read targets from: an oci:// pacto-targets repository, or :cluster-<uid> tags or digests to pin the clusters CI expects (repeatable); pacto impact, pacto ci and pacto_impact on a stdio pacto mcp also take auto (the default: derived from the provider ref) and off
      --target-state stringArray      offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray            OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)
  -t, --transport string              transport type: stdio or http (default "stdio")

The default server exposes the four authoring tools below and pacto_capabilities, which reports what the server serves. A bundle reference and four flags add tools or select a different server. See Server modes after this table:

Tool Description pacto_create Create a new contract from intent-level inputs (name, description, interfaces, runtime semantics), or with from from a golden path (stdio only). Supports dry run. pacto_edit Edit an existing contract: add or remove interfaces, dependencies and configuration references, add environments and set their values, set the service lifecycle or the golden path template, change runtime, update metadata. Checks values against a referenced contract's schema before writing. Supports dry run. pacto_check Validate a contract and return errors, warnings and actionable improvement suggestions. pacto_schema Return the Pacto format explanation and full JSON Schema reference.

These four authoring tools operate on local contract directories (they read and write pacto.yaml on disk) and accept no oci:// refs. Over HTTP the server serves only pacto_schema of the four.

docs.title: Server modes
docs.text:
The default server exposes the authoring tools above. A bundle reference, --fleet and --delivery add their tools and combine in one server. --root and --publish each select a server of their own, and passing either with another mode is an error:

Invocation Server pacto mcp Authoring tools. pacto mcp <bundle-ref> Authoring tools plus the bundle's OpenAPI operations as executable agent tools, alongside a pacto_skill tool for any bundled skills. pacto mcp --fleet Authoring tools plus read-only operational-graph query tools. pacto mcp --publish Authoring tools plus pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish, which publish a version to your registry, and pacto_capabilities. Stdio only. pacto mcp --delivery Authoring tools plus the delivery tools over the cluster your kubeconfig points at: read delivery state and the dashboard's delivery views and, for an agent, ask for or cancel a change. There is no approve tool. pacto mcp --fleet --delivery [<bundle-ref>] Authoring tools plus the tools of every mode named, in one session. pacto mcp --root <ref> [--root <ref>] A read-only contract catalog discovered from the named roots. Catalog mode registers only catalog tools, and none of them writes to disk.

--root is repeatable and takes a local bundle directory or an oci:// reference. The roots and their dependency closure are resolved once, at startup, through the same reference parsing, credentials and cache the rest of the CLI uses; after that the session is frozen, so every answer reflects startup state even if a registry tag moves. A root that fails to resolve stays visible with a classified reason, and the catalog reports itself as partial. The catalog reads only the named roots and their closure, never refreshes and persists nothing.

docs.title: Fleet tool arguments
docs.text:
The arguments each fleet query tool takes. Arguments are optional unless marked:

Tool Arguments pacto_fleet_search text, owner, business_domain, offering, status, compliance, workload, scope, source, ready, not_ready, has_capability, has_dependency, template (only keeps golden paths, exclude leaves them out), label (target labels as key=value), limit, offset pacto_fleet_get service (a logical service) or target (an operational target by key or name) pacto_fleet_graph service, revision or target to root the traversal, then direction, transitive and max_depth (0 = unlimited) pacto_fleet_status needs_attention for every category, or any of invalid, non_compliant, unknown, stale, unresolved_deps, unsatisfied_ranges, missing_readiness, unowned, undeclared, golden_path_deployed; plus limit. No category, including empty input, reports every category pacto_fleet_explain subject (required): a service name or a target key or name pacto_fleet_entities text, kind (any entity kind; empty lists services, owners, domains and offerings, or the one kind a readiness, scope, source_kind or source_health filter applies to), owner, owner_key, business_domain, offering, consumes (services that depend on or reference a provider of this offering), phase, environment, template (only lists golden paths, exclude leaves them out), created_from (the services created from this golden path, by service key), ownership, status, has_non_compliant, capability, domain, service, source, scope, readiness, source_kind, source_health, sort, limit, offset pacto_fleet_entity kind and key (both required): a service, revision, target, owner, source, business domain or offering pacto_fleet_attention category, severity, owner, owner_key, business_domain, service, kind, key, source, status, stale_only, limit, offset pacto_fleet_neighborhood service (required): a service name or key, then direction (dependencies, dependents or both, the default), depth, views (comma-separated expected, observed and differences; empty means expected,observed), max_nodes and max_edges pacto_fleet_versions offering (required), then provider (a key, or a name only one domain uses) and range (a semver range; each version then carries rangeStatus and each provider its latestCompatible version) pacto_fleet_revision_document key and path (both required): a revision key and a document path its docs list pacto_impact old_ref and new_ref, plus include_observed and traces; or running with new_ref alone; or event (unavailable, removed or regressed) with service, plus revision for regressed pacto_stats registry (stdio only), since and until (30d, 12h, a date or RFC 3339; default the last 30 days), by (service, owner, domain, repository or environment), service and kinds (comma-separated run-record kinds, for example diff,impact). It appears with --fleet over stdio, and over HTTP only when the server was started with --stats-read-registry

Argument names differ from flag names: the substring filter is text. Every tool above closes its schema, so an unknown argument is an error.

With --fleet, the server rebuilds its snapshot when a call arrives 30 seconds or more after the last rebuild attempt, and pacto_impact analyses over the same snapshot as the other tools. Add --dashboard-url <url> to make search, graph, status, entities, entity, attention, neighborhood and versions answers carry an href to each entity's page on that Pacto dashboard, and each contracted consumer in a pacto_impact answer an href to its service page.

See MCP Integration for setup and the MCP reference for serving a bundle's operations as tools and the catalog surface.

docs.title: pacto migrate
docs.text:
Walks the given directories (the current one by default) with the rules of the local fleet source and raises the pactoVersion of every pacto.yaml it finds. Hidden folders, node_modules and vendor are skipped; folders past depth 8 and folders a root .pactoignore names are skipped and printed as skipped.

A file is raised only when validation finds nothing new at the new version. Its version token changes, and two removals can apply even to a file already at the version: a leftover delivery section, and any publish.artifacts[].build block that pacto ci --publish detection reproduces. Every other byte stays as written, and each line names what changed. A raise that would change what the contract means keeps the file and says why. 1.x files are left to MIGRATION.md.

Exits 1 only when a file cannot be read or written, or --to names an unsupported version.

pacto migrate [dir...] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto migrate
  pacto migrate --dry-run
  pacto migrate services/payments
  pacto migrate --to 2.4

Flags:

      --dry-run[=true|false]   print what would change and write nothing
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for migrate
      --to string              pactoVersion to raise to (default: the newest this Pacto supports)

docs.title: pacto otel
docs.text:
Observe runtime dependencies from OpenTelemetry traces

pacto otel [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for otel

docs.title: pacto otel observe
docs.text:
Reads an OTLP/JSON trace export and derives the service dependency edges its outbound spans prove. By default it prints the observed edges as text; add --output-format json for machine-readable output. With --evidence it emits one EvidenceSet per calling service as a JSON array. Each set's ContractRef is empty because traces carry no contract revision. pacto evidence sign reads one EvidenceSet from a file, so write the array out, split it and set each ContractRef to the revision it describes before signing (pacto evidence sign) and reporting (pacto evidence send).

pacto otel observe <traces.json> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto otel observe traces.json
  pacto otel observe traces.json --evidence --output-format json > sets.json

Flags:

      --evidence[=true|false]   emit signable EvidenceSets instead of raw edges
  -h, --help[=true|false]       help for observe
      --source string           collector/source name recorded as provenance (default "otel")

docs.title: pacto pack
docs.text:
Validates the contract in the given directory and creates a tar.gz archive of the bundle, ready for distribution.

pacto pack [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto pack my-service

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for pack
  -o, --output string        output file path (default: <name>-<version>.tar.gz)
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

The contract is validated before packing. If validation fails, no archive is created.

Files matched by .pactoignore are excluded from the archive. See Packaging ignore.

docs.title: pacto publish
docs.text:
Publishes every artifact the contract's publish section declares (pactoVersion 2.1), the contract bundle and the deploy artifact Flux applies, all tagged with service.version. Docker or the declared command builds. Pacto pushes each artifact to a new tag, signs every digest with Sigstore (built in) and attaches the SBOM files the build wrote. A breaking change since the last published version is refused below a major bump (a minor before 1.0).

--plan shows what is missing and changes nothing. Running publish again from the same commit finishes what is missing and changes nothing else. --propose hands the deploy artifact to Pacto delivery as a promote on a Stage, once the Stage records it as published, meaning Flux polled the candidate OCIRepository and verified the signature. It waits up to --propose-timeout for that.

pacto publish [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  # What would be published, and what refuses it
  pacto publish --plan

  # The same, for the contract in ./payments
  pacto publish --plan ./payments

  # Publish, then propose the version on the test Stage
  pacto publish --propose test/payments

Flags:

      --correlation-id string              with --propose, an id that ties the promote to an incident or another change, such as a ticket; kept with the change and its record, filtered by pacto delivery history --correlation-id
  -h, --help[=true|false]                  help for publish
      --image string                       with no publish section: the image to deploy, pinned by digest (repo@sha256:...); Pacto builds, signs and copies none
      --index string                       organization index repository for this version's entry, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the contract's repository; none writes no entry)
      --no-transparency-log[=true|false]   with --sign-key: keep the signatures out of the transparency log
      --on-behalf-of string                with --propose, the person an agent acts for, as the Kubernetes username the cluster authenticates them as (what kubectl auth whoami prints for them, any OIDC prefix included); asserted, not verified; required when an agent proposes, never a service account or other system user, and that person may not approve the change
  -p, --path string                        path to contract directory, the same as [dir] (default: current directory)
      --plan[=true|false]                  show what is missing and what refuses it; change nothing
      --propose string                     after publishing, propose the deploy artifact on <namespace>/<stage> (needs delivery.enabled on the pacto-operator chart)
      --propose-timeout duration           how long --propose waits for the Stage to record the version as published (default 10m0s)
      --registry string                    with no publish section: the registry to publish to (default: what the CI context or the workload image names)
      --revision string                    source revision stamped on every artifact (default: the git commit of the contract directory, which must have no uncommitted changes)
      --set stringArray                    set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --sign-key string                    with no publish section: sign with this cosign key file instead of keyless
      --stats-context string               comma-separated context to include in the run record: repository, run-url, environment=<name>; nothing is included unless named
      --stats-file string                  write the run record to this file for pacto stats publish, replacing the record it holds, so give each command its own file; default $PACTO_STATS_FILE
      --stats-registry string              publish an unsigned run record (statistics, never evidence) to this repository, for example ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats; default $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY
      --values stringArray                 values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

docs.title: pacto pull
docs.text:
Pulls a contract bundle from the specified OCI reference and extracts it to a local directory.

pacto pull <ref> [flags]

Examples:

  # Pull a specific version
  pacto pull oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:1.0.0

  # Pull the latest available version
  pacto pull oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for pull
  -o, --output string            output directory (default: service name)
      --trusted-root string      Sigstore trusted root JSON --verify-identity checks against (default: public-good Sigstore)
      --verify-identity string   pull only a bundle signed keyless by this certificate identity, such as an email (needs --verify-issuer)
      --verify-issuer string     the OIDC issuer of --verify-identity
      --verify-key string        pull only a bundle signed by the key of this PEM public key file

docs.title: pacto push
docs.text:
Validates the contract (including remote policy and config refs), builds an OCI artifact and pushes it to the specified registry reference. Pushing the same content again succeeds without writing anything; different content under an existing reference is refused unless --force.

pacto push <ref> [flags]

Examples:

  # Push with auto-tag (uses contract version)
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto -p my-service

  # Push with explicit tag
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:latest -p my-service

  # Force overwrite an existing artifact
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto -p my-service --force

Flags:

  -f, --force[=true|false]   overwrite existing artifact in registry
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for push
      --index string         organization index repository for this version's entry, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the contract's repository; none writes no entry)
  -p, --path string          path to contract directory (default: current directory)
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

If the tag already holds the same content, pacto push succeeds and writes nothing. If it holds different content, pacto push refuses with a non-zero exit and writes nothing. Use --force to overwrite.

--values has no -f shorthand on push

On every other override-taking command -f is the shorthand for --values. On pacto push, -f is --force, so --values must be spelled out in full here.

docs.title: pacto run
docs.text:
Starts the command and watches the TCP sockets of its whole process tree: the interfaces bound with --bind must be listened on, the dependencies bound with --dep reached. Every --interval it prints the contract's compliance and findings in --output-format; once the command exits it prints a final round from the last view taken while the command ran, and exits with the command's exit code. With --fail-on it exits 1 instead of 0 when the final verdict is that bad or worse.

The command runs in a process group of its own, so a Ctrl-C reaches it once. When pacto run owns the terminal, the command's group takes it over: it reads the terminal and gets Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z straight from it, and pacto run takes the terminal back once it exits. Otherwise SIGINT and SIGTERM sent to pacto run are passed on to the command's whole group.

Pacto leaves the command's stdin, stdout and stderr untouched. Rounds go to stderr, each in a single write, or with --report to a file: the file is truncated when the run starts and every round is appended to it in a single write, so a reader following it sees whole rounds (with json, one object per line).

With root (or BPF, PERFMON, SYS_PTRACE and write access to its own cgroup) on Linux 5.11 or later with BTF and cgroup v2 (or 5.8 or later with BTF and root or CAP_SYS_RESOURCE), the command starts inside a new cgroup pacto-run-<pid> and an eBPF program sees every listener and every connection outcome of the tree, failures included (collector pacto-run+ebpf). Otherwise it falls back to polling /proc every second and says so (collector pacto-run): listeners are seen in full, so a missing one is still confirmed, but a connection is seen only while it is open at a poll and a failed connection never, so a dependency is reported reachable or unknown, never unreachable. If the program attached but the command cannot start inside the new cgroup, the run falls back to polling too and says so. Elsewhere than Linux the command runs unobserved and every runtime assertion is unsupported.

A negative is reported once it persists for --stabilization-window. Health and metrics capabilities are probed on --host at their bound interface's port. With --evidence-url every round is also signed and sent to an Evidence Server, which needs the contract pinned as oci://...@sha256:<digest>.

pacto run --contract <dir|oci ref> [flags] -- command [args...]

Examples:

  pacto run --contract ./payments --bind api=8080 --dep postgres=127.0.0.1:5432 -- ./payments-server
  pacto run --contract oci://ghcr.io/acme/payments:1.4.0 --bind api=8080 --fail-on noncompliant \
    --stabilization-window 30s --output-format json --report rounds.jsonl -- java -jar payments.jar

Flags:

      --bind stringArray                interface=port the command serves the interface on (repeatable)
      --cgroup-root string              cgroup v2 directory the session cgroup is created in (default: the caller's own cgroup under /sys/fs/cgroup)
      --contract string                 contract bundle directory or oci:// reference (required)
      --dep stringArray                 dependency=host:port the command reaches the dependency at (repeatable)
      --enable-probing[=true|false]     also probe the wire protocol of every interface found listening
      --evidence-key string             private key file envelopes are signed with
      --evidence-key-id string          key id (must match the server's trust entry)
      --evidence-producer string        producer id
      --evidence-url string             Evidence Server base URL
      --fail-on string                  exit 1 when the command exits 0 but the final verdict is this bad or worse: one of [none noncompliant unknown] (default "none")
  -h, --help[=true|false]               help for run
      --host string                     address capability and protocol probes dial (default "127.0.0.1")
      --interval duration               how often a round is evaluated and printed (whole seconds) (default 10s)
      --proc-root string                where /proc is mounted (default "/proc")
      --report string                   file every round is appended to instead of stderr (truncated when the run starts)
      --ringbuf-size uint32             kernel ring buffer size in bytes; a power of two and a multiple of the page size (default 262144)
      --stabilization-window duration   how long a negative must persist before it is reported (default 2m0s)

docs.title: pacto stats
docs.text:
Pacto can record what it catches as unsigned statistics in a registry you name; pacto stats and the dashboard Metrics page total them, and nothing leaves your registry. Total the run records in a stats repository for a time window, as text or JSON. Run records are unsigned statistics about Pacto runs: nothing that decides ever reads them, and this command only reads. Every answer says how many records were read, how many could not be read and which bound cut the read; a rate with nothing to take it over is marked unknown. With --by owner or --by domain, owner and domain are inferred from the fleet snapshot the fleet source flags build. See https://pacto.run/latest/measure-what-pacto-does/.

pacto stats [flags]

Examples:

  pacto stats --registry ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats
  pacto stats --since 7d --by environment --output-format json
  pacto stats --by owner --kind impact --kind publish

Flags:

      --by string                     group the numbers by service, owner, domain, repository, environment
      --cache[=true|false]            include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray           kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --delivery-trust string         the trust config target snapshots are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string               add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray      base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --external-catalog string       organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string           a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --freshness duration            mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]             help for stats
      --index string                  organization index pacto impact and pacto ci read consumers from, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the provider reference; none reads none; skipped when --root names the consumers; pacto ci --publish also writes its entries there; other fleet commands ignore it)
      --k8s[=true|false]              include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --kind stringArray              total only run records of this kind: diff, impact, publish, operation, coverage (repeatable)
      --local stringArray             local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --mira-source stringArray       base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable)
      --namespace string              namespaces to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces)
      --oci stringArray               registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --registry string               stats repository to read or publish to, for example ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats (default $PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY)
      --root stringArray              contract root whose whole dependency closure joins the snapshot: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --service string                total only the run records of this service: the contract's service.name
      --since string                  start of the window: 30d, 12h, a date or RFC 3339 (default 30d)
      --target-snapshot stringArray   signed target snapshot(s) to read targets from: an oci:// pacto-targets repository, or :cluster-<uid> tags or digests to pin the clusters CI expects (repeatable); pacto impact, pacto ci and pacto_impact on a stdio pacto mcp also take auto (the default: derived from the provider ref) and off
      --target-state stringArray      offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray            OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)
      --until string                  end of the window, exclusive: 30d, 12h, a date or RFC 3339 (default now)

docs.title: pacto stats publish
docs.text:
Publish run record files, written by --stats-file, to a stats repository as unsigned statistics. Operation records are written only by the delivery promoter and are refused. Every file is tried; the command fails when any of them could not be read, parsed or published. The publishing job vouches for the files with its own credentials: never publish files from untrusted (fork) jobs into a repository others read.

pacto stats publish <file...> [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for publish

docs.title: pacto tui
docs.text:
Opens a full-screen terminal UI over the same fleet snapshot pacto fleet queries. Navigate services, revisions, targets, owners and sources, then run pacto's verbs against the selection, which becomes the command's argument.

Read verbs run in-process against the loaded snapshot. Write verbs shell out to this same binary so they own the terminal, and every one of them asks for confirmation first. Pass --read-only to hide the write verbs entirely.

Requires an interactive terminal. In a pipeline or CI, use the plain commands.

pacto tui [flags]

Examples:

  # Browse the local fleet
  pacto tui --local .

  # Browse a live cluster plus the local bundles, without write verbs
  pacto tui --local . --k8s --read-only

Flags:

      --cache[=true|false]            include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --context stringArray           kubeconfig context to read live Pacto CRs from, like --k8s for the current one; repeatable, each cluster read once
      --delivery-trust string         the trust config target snapshots are verified with: a YAML file with a key scoped to each cluster (default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --detected string               add what the operator detected as inferred rows: k8s:<namespace>/<name> of its <release>-detected ConfigMap, or a file holding the same JSON
      --evidence-url stringArray      base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --external-catalog string       organization external catalog to merge over the default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST, else PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG; a tag is refused
      --fingerprints string           a file (YAML or JSON) of the workload managers and promoters this installation runs, as the chart's fingerprints value: each promoter found reads promotion owned by <product> in the detected providers
      --freshness duration            mark target evidence older than this as stale (the dashboard's window; 0 skips the check and every answer says so) (default 24h0m0s)
  -h, --help[=true|false]             help for tui
      --index string                  organization index pacto impact and pacto ci read consumers from, as <registry>/pacto-index with no tag or digest (default <registry>/pacto-index from the provider reference; none reads none; skipped when --root names the consumers; pacto ci --publish also writes its entries there; other fleet commands ignore it)
      --k8s[=true|false]              include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray             local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --mira-source stringArray       base URL of a Mira node whose service map supplies observed calls between services (repeatable)
      --namespace string              namespaces to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s, comma-separated (empty = all namespaces)
      --oci stringArray               registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --read-only[=true|false]        hide every write verb
      --root stringArray              contract root whose whole dependency closure joins the snapshot: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --target-snapshot stringArray   signed target snapshot(s) to read targets from: an oci:// pacto-targets repository, or :cluster-<uid> tags or digests to pin the clusters CI expects (repeatable); pacto impact, pacto ci and pacto_impact on a stdio pacto mcp also take auto (the default: derived from the provider ref) and off
      --target-state stringArray      offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray            OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)

docs.title: pacto update
docs.text:
Downloads and installs the specified version of pacto. If no version is given, updates to the latest release.

pacto update [version] [flags]

Examples:

  # Update to the latest release
  pacto update

  # Update to a specific version
  pacto update v1.1.0

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for update

Note

pacto update works only on release builds. If you built from source without version injection, install a release build first.

docs.title: Update notifications
docs.text:
When a newer version is available, pacto displays a notification after any command:

A new version of pacto is available: v1.0.0 -> v1.2.0
Run 'pacto update' to update.

The check runs asynchronously and adds no latency. Results are cached for 24 hours in ~/.config/pacto/update-check.json.

Notifications are suppressed when:

  • Running a dev build
  • Using --output-format json or --output-format markdown (the notice shows only for text output)
  • The PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 environment variable is set

docs.title: pacto validate
docs.text:
Validates a pacto.yaml in the given directory (or oci:// reference) against the specification, running the three validation layers: structural, cross-field and policy.

The output has one PASS, FAIL or SKIP line per stage, in order: load, lock, structural, cross-field, policy, configuration-refs, environments, guarantees, readiness and closure. The configuration-refs stage fetches the contract each configuration ref names and checks the values against its configuration schema; a ref that cannot be fetched fails it when values depend on it. The environments stage checks each environment's file against the schema of every configuration it names. Each error sits under its stage with its file:line:column when Pacto can locate it. A failed load or lock stage skips every stage after it, and a failed structural, cross-field or policy stage skips the stages after it up to environments. A failed configuration-refs stage skips nothing. The guarantees, readiness and closure stages run even when an earlier stage fails. The last line, Next:, names the one command to run now. With --output-format json the same comes as stages and next.

pacto validate [dir | oci://ref] [flags]

Examples:

  # Validate a local contract
  pacto validate my-service

  # Validate from current directory
  pacto validate

  # Validate from an OCI registry
  pacto validate oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:1.0.0

  # JSON output
  pacto validate --output-format json my-service

  # Also check the readiness gate (fail if score < minScore)
  pacto validate --readiness my-service

  # Also check every dependency against this contract's policies
  pacto validate --closure my-service

Flags:

      --closure[=true|false]     also check every contract in the dependency closure against the policies this contract resolves. Fails when a dependency cannot be resolved and warns about deprecated interfaces of direct dependencies. Fetches each dependency once
  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for validate
      --readiness[=true|false]   also check the readiness gate: fail if the derived readiness score is below the declared (or default 100) minScore. Opt-in because gate evaluation is time-dependent (check expiry is compared against the run time), which would otherwise make plain validation non-deterministic
      --set stringArray          set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray       values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

The --readiness gate is opt-in because it is time-dependent: it compares the assessment's single readiness.expires date against the run time, which would make plain validate non-deterministic. Expiry is declared once for the whole assessment. Individual claims carry no expires field, and adding one fails to load with PARSE_ERROR. Without the flag, validation checks the contract's structure and rules. It still checks the shape of readiness claims and skips the freshness gate. See the readiness reference for the score and gate semantics.

A contract with a mistyped value fails like this:

svc is invalid
PASS load
SKIP lock               no pacto.lock
FAIL structural
  svc/pacto.yaml:6:1: ERROR [SCHEMA_VIOLATION] workload: at '/workload': value must be one of 'service', 'job', 'scheduled' (did you mean "service"?)
SKIP cross-field        structural failed
SKIP policy             structural failed
SKIP configuration-refs structural failed
SKIP environments       structural failed
SKIP guarantees         no dependency declares requires
SKIP readiness          not requested (--readiness)
SKIP closure            not requested (--closure)
Next: fix workload at svc/pacto.yaml:6:1 [SCHEMA_VIOLATION], then run pacto validate svc

Errors within a stage are listed in file order. An unknown field or an enum value close to a known one carries a did you mean hint. A failed lock stage names the pacto lock command that repairs it. When every stage passes, Next is pacto impact PUBLISHED_REF <dir>, which shows the services the change breaks; replace PUBLISHED_REF with the oci:// reference of the version you run today. In JSON, stages lists each stage with its status, reason and errors, each error carries line and column when known, file is the file they point into, and next holds the command. errors and warnings still list every stage's findings. With --set or -f an error in pacto.yaml carries no line or column, because those flags validate a merged document whose lines differ from the file. An error in an environment's file keeps them.

Exit code: Non-zero if validation fails.

docs.title: pacto version
docs.text:
Prints the current pacto version.

pacto version [flags]

Examples:

  pacto version

Flags:

  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for version

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Boolean variables are parsed the way Go parses a boolean: 1, t, T, true, TRUE and True enable them and 0, f, F, false, FALSE and False disable them. Any other value, including yes and on, reads as off with no warning. The two opt-outs PACTO_NO_ANIM and PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK are the exception: for them any other non-empty value reads as on.

Variable Description PACTO_CACHE_DIR Cache directory for the pacto dashboard bundle scan. The core CLI cache location is controlled by XDG_CACHE_HOME (see below). PACTO_NO_CACHE Boolean. Disable OCI bundle caching (equivalent to --no-cache) PACTO_NO_ANIM Boolean. Disables spinners and animations (equivalent to --no-anim). PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Boolean. Disables automatic update checks. PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME Registry username for authentication PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD Registry password for authentication PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN Registry token for authentication PACTO_INSECURE_REGISTRIES Comma-separated registry hosts that Pacto reaches over plain HTTP. It applies to every registry access: pacto push, pacto pull, dependency and policy resolution and the Evidence Server. Scoped per host, so HTTPS registries are unaffected. Loopback hosts use plain HTTP without being listed. Use it only for a controlled in-cluster registry: it disables transport encryption, so credentials and payloads travel in the clear. PACTO_EVIDENCE_SOURCE_URL Base URL of an Evidence Server whose read-only operational-graph contribution pacto dashboard should consume. The operator sets it when it wires a managed Evidence Server. Unset means no evidence source configured, which the dashboard reports separately from an unavailable source. XDG_CONFIG_HOME Override config directory (default: ~/.config). Affects pacto login credentials and update check cache XDG_CACHE_HOME Override cache directory (default: ~/.cache). Affects OCI bundle cache location

docs.title: Dashboard environment variables
docs.text:
The following variables configure the dashboard when set (see also Dashboard Container). Each mirrors the flag named beside it: an explicitly passed flag wins, and otherwise the variable overrides that flag's default.

Variable Flag Description PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO (positional args) Comma-separated OCI repositories, used only when no positional oci:// argument is given PACTO_DASHBOARD_HOST --host Bind address (default: 127.0.0.1) PACTO_DASHBOARD_PORT --port HTTP port (default: 3000) PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE --namespace Kubernetes namespaces to read, comma-separated (empty = all) PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN --cors-origin One explicit origin allowed to call the API. Unset means same-origin only. PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES --traces OTLP/JSON trace files to fold observed dependencies from PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES --mira-source Space-separated Mira base URLs whose service map supplies observed calls PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES --trace-source Named offline trace sources as NAME=PATH, where NAME is the source's identity (what the fleet, the API and the dashboard's Data Source list call it) and PATH is the trace file location. Identity and location are separate, so reordering the configuration or moving the file keeps the source's name. Two sources whose files share a basename stay two sources. A name must be unique across every Data Source the dashboard assembles.

The three list variables split on whitespace

PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES, PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES and PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES go through the same generic flag binding as every other dashboard variable, which splits a multi-valued string on spaces. PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES="a.json b.json" supplies two files; PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES=a.json,b.json supplies one, named a.json,b.json. PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is read directly and splits on commas.

The dashboard starts either way: it skips a trace file it cannot read, so the symptom is missing observed dependencies with no error. Check the snapshot's reported limitations if the operational graph looks emptier than you expect.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Pacto follows this credential resolution chain:

  1. Environment variables (PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, or PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME + PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD)
  2. Pacto config (~/.config/pacto/config.json, written by pacto login, which persists --username and --password)
  3. GitHub CLI (gh auth token, for ghcr.io and docker.pkg.github.com only)
  4. Docker config (~/.docker/config.json) and credential helpers (including cloud-registry helpers for ECR, GCR and ACR)
  5. Anonymous fallback

For GitHub registries, step 3 means you can skip pacto login entirely if you have gh authenticated with the write:packages scope (see pacto login above).

Pacto stores no credentials in contract files.

docs.title: How Pacto relates to other tools
docs.text:
Pacto composes the interface tools it sits between, such as OpenAPI and config schemas, and complements the deploy tools, such as Helm and Terraform. Its core makes no deployment decisions. The opt-in delivery component decides which version runs where and leaves applying it to Flux or Argo CD.

This page grades Pacto and several nearby projects on the same criteria. Reviewed on 2026-11-16. Maintainers review this page at every minor release. These projects move fast, so check the source page before you rely on a cell.

docs.title: Criteria
docs.text:
Each column asks one question:

  • Versioned artifact: the tool publishes the service description as an immutable, versioned artifact that others pull, such as an OCI image. Versioned snapshots that stay inside the tool are Partial.
  • Semantic diff: the tool classifies a change by its compatibility impact. A line-based text diff is Partial.
  • Dependency graph: the tool records which services depend on which. Dependencies between platform packages, or inside one application, are Partial.
  • Transitive policy: the platform's rules follow every policy reference, fail closed and are evaluated across the dependency closure. Following the references without evaluating the closure is Partial.
  • Runtime verify: the tool checks running workloads against an independently declared contract. Reconciling toward the tool's own desired state is Partial.
  • Deploys?: the tool applies workloads itself.

A cell holds ✅ for first-class, Partial for adjacent or limited and a dash (—) when the source page covers the area and describes no such feature. A cell holds "not verified" when the source page alone does not settle it.

docs.title: The table
docs.text:
Versioned artifact Semantic diff Dependency graph Transitive policy Runtime verify Deploys? Source Score not verified not verified Partial not verified not verified No Score specification Crossplane Configuration ✅ not verified Partial not verified Partial Yes Configurations KubeVela Partial Partial not verified not verified not verified Yes Version control Kratix Partial not verified Partial not verified not verified Yes Promise reference Kargo Partial not verified not verified not verified not verified No Core concepts Argo CD not verified Partial not verified not verified Partial Yes Argo CD overview Flux not verified not verified Partial not verified Partial Yes Kustomization Backstage not verified not verified ✅ not verified not verified not verified Descriptor format Port not verified not verified not verified not verified not verified not verified Relate blueprints Pact not verified Partial ✅ not verified Partial No Pact Broker introduction oasdiff not verified ✅ not verified not verified not verified No oasdiff README buf not verified ✅ Partial not verified not verified No buf README Pacto ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ (opt-in) ✅ No (delivery promotes, alpha) This site

What each source page shows:

  • Score: a Score file describes one workload. Its resources are evaluated as an acyclic graph at deploy time, and a Score implementation turns the file into platform configuration.
  • Crossplane: a Configuration is a versioned OCI package that lists the packages it depends on with version constraints. Crossplane installs and reconciles its contents and reports them Healthy.
  • KubeVela: an ApplicationRevision keeps a snapshot of each published version, vela live-diff prints a line diff between the edited application and its current revision and KubeVela rolls back to a past revision.
  • Kratix: Kratix keeps each Promise version as a Promise Revision, a Promise lists the Promises it requires and Kratix schedules resources to matching Destinations.
  • Kargo: Freight is a Kargo resource that references specific revisions of images, charts and commits. Stages form a promotion pipeline, and a GitOps agent such as Argo CD does the deploying.
  • Argo CD: Argo CD compares the live state of each application with the target state in Git, reports the differences and marks a drifted application OutOfSync. It syncs the manifests to the target clusters and analyses the health of their resources.
  • Flux: a Kustomization applies the manifests from a source artifact and corrects drift on every interval. Its dependsOn list waits for other Kustomizations to be ready, and its health checks report the rollout status.
  • Backstage: a Component descriptor lists the components and resources it depends on and the APIs it provides and consumes. The catalog turns these fields into two-way relations such as dependsOn and dependencyOf.
  • Port: a relation connects two blueprints and the entities built from them. Dependencies between services are one of its common uses, and several sources can add targets to the same relation.
  • Pact: consumer tests write the expected requests and responses to a pact file, and the Pact Broker shares it and draws the network of services. The provider build replays the pact against the provider, and can-i-deploy reads the results before a deployment proceeds.
  • oasdiff: oasdiff compares two OpenAPI specs and lists the changes that break existing clients, from the command line or in CI. Its rules classify each change as breaking or non-breaking.
  • buf: buf breaking compares a Protobuf schema with a past version and flags source, JSON or wire-format incompatibilities. A buf.yaml declares the schema modules it depends on, and buf.lock pins them.

docs.title: Where each tool wins
docs.text:
Each tool below wins at the job its source page describes. Pacto adds the check named after it.

  • Score wins at describing one workload in a file that each Score implementation turns into platform configuration, Score specification. When you run the workload under pacto run or pacto agent on Linux, or under the operator with its node agent turned on (nodeAgent.enabled), Pacto checks that it serves the ports its contract declares and, with eBPF, that it reaches the declared dependencies. What it cannot see it reports as unknown (runtime conformance).
  • Crossplane wins at shipping Compositions and the packages they depend on as one portable OCI package, Configurations. Given two versions of a contract, Pacto classifies each change as breaking, potentially breaking or non-breaking (diff).
  • KubeVela wins at keeping a revision of each published application and rolling back to a past one, Version control. Given the old contract, the new one and the consumer contracts it can see, Pacto lists the consumers the new version would break (impact).
  • Kratix wins at packaging a platform service as a Promise with its API and the Promises it requires, Promise reference. From the sources you connect, such as your registry or a cluster, Pacto shows which services depend on a service and which revision runs where (operational graph).
  • Kargo wins at promoting Freight through a pipeline of Stages and leaves the deploying to a GitOps agent, Core concepts. In a pull request, Pacto lists which consumers would reject the new version, from the target snapshot your clusters publish or the contracts you name with --root (who breaks).
  • Argo CD wins at syncing Git state to target clusters and showing where the live state differs, Argo CD overview. With the health check from GitOps gates in argocd-cm, an Application goes Degraded when its Pacto is NonCompliant or Invalid and stays Progressing while the verdict is Unknown.
  • Flux wins at applying manifests from a source artifact and correcting drift on every interval, Kustomization. With the health check expression from GitOps gates, a Kustomization that holds a NonCompliant or Invalid Pacto turns unready and the Kustomizations that depend on it wait.
  • Backstage wins at a catalog where each component lists what it depends on and the APIs it provides and consumes, Descriptor format. A Pacto contract also records which versions of each dependency it accepts, so pacto impact names the consumers a new version breaks among the contracts it is given (impact).
  • Port wins at a data model where relations connect blueprints and their entities and several sources add targets to the same relation, Relate blueprints. From the sources you connect, Pacto keeps relationships declared in contracts apart from those observed in traffic and says how complete each answer is (operational graph).
  • Pact wins at testing the requests each consumer expects against the provider before it deploys, Pact Broker introduction. From the consumer contracts you name with --root or a fleet source, Pacto lists which would reject the new version and reports a breaking change it cannot fully check as unverified (impact).
  • oasdiff wins at listing the changes between two OpenAPI specs that break existing clients, from the command line or in CI, oasdiff README. From the consumers your clusters' target snapshots name, or the contracts you name with --root, Pacto lists those whose accepted range rejects the new version (who breaks).
  • buf wins at checking a Protobuf schema against a past version for source, JSON or wire-format breaks, buf README. Pacto classifies a change to the whole contract, including its configuration and dependencies, as breaking, potentially breaking or non-breaking (diff).

docs.title: Pacto's own row
docs.text:
We graded our own row on the same criteria:

  • Transitive policy is ✅ and opt-in. Pacto follows policy references from one policy contract to the next and fails closed when one cannot be resolved. By default it checks the policies against the root contract only. pacto validate --closure also checks every contract in the dependency closure against them, and fails when a dependency cannot be resolved. The flag is on pacto validate only. See Dependency closure.
  • Semantic diff classifies each change as non-breaking, potentially breaking or breaking (diff).
  • Runtime verify compares running workloads with the contract (runtime conformance).
  • Deploys? Pacto's core deploys nothing. Delivery, which is alpha, moves the version digest on a Flux or Argo CD source, and Flux or Argo CD applies it (delivery).

Radius was in an earlier version of this table. Its row returns when a source page settles its cells.

docs.title: Dashboard Container
docs.text: Run the Pacto dashboard, a web UI for your services, their contracts, dependencies and compliance, as a container. It is the same server as pacto dashboard in the CLI, packaged for Docker and Kubernetes.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:<version>

The tag matches the Pacto release version, without a v prefix. The image has no latest tag, so swap the pinned version below for the release you want. The image is signed keylessly; verify it with the command in Supply chain.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Every docker run here publishes to 127.0.0.1 on purpose: the image sets --host 0.0.0.0, and without sign-in the dashboard refuses to serve beyond loopback unless PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true allows it.

# Run with OCI registry sources
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO=ghcr.io/org/svc-a,ghcr.io/org/svc-b \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1

# Run with registry authentication
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO=ghcr.io/org/svc-a \
  -e PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=ghp_xxx \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1

To build the image from a checkout instead, make docker-build and make docker-run tag it with the version derived from your git state.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Variable Description Default PACTO_DASHBOARD_HOST Bind address for the server 0.0.0.0 (in image), 127.0.0.1 (CLI) PACTO_DASHBOARD_PORT HTTP server port 3000 PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE Kubernetes namespaces to read, comma-separated (empty = all) "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO Comma-separated OCI repositories to scan "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN Trusted cross-origin allowed to call the API "" (same-origin only) PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES Offline OTLP/JSON trace exports to fold observed dependencies from. Space-separated list of paths "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER_URL Identity provider people sign in with before the dashboard shows anything; every view then follows their Kubernetes RBAC (also _CLIENT_ID, _CLIENT_SECRET, _REDIRECT_URL, _EXTRA_SCOPES, _DISPLAY_NAME for the provider's name on the sign-in button and the claim mapping, see dashboard authentication) "" (no sign-in) PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS true serves beyond loopback without sign-in, to everyone who reaches the address; without it such a dashboard refuses to start false PACTO_DASHBOARD_REVIEW local reviews signed-in people with a LocalSubjectAccessReview in each PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE only, which a namespaced Role grants; services without a namespace then show to nobody. cluster asks once about every namespace and needs a ClusterRole cluster PACTO_DASHBOARD_TOKEN_LOGIN true lets people sign in by pasting a Kubernetes bearer token false PACTO_DASHBOARD_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT, PACTO_DASHBOARD_SESSION_MAX_AGE How long a session lasts idle and in all 1h, 12h PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES Mira base URLs whose service map supplies observed calls. Space-separated list "" PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY Stats repository the Metrics page reads; read anonymously when public, otherwise with the registry credentials. Delivery-derived metrics need sign-in "" (Metrics explains how to turn recording on) PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES The same input with a stable identity per file: space-separated NAME=PATH entries, where NAME is the Data Source name the API and UI show "" PACTO_CACHE_DIR Directory the dashboard scans for cached OCI bundles (read side) /home/pacto/.cache/pacto/oci PACTO_NO_CACHE Disable OCI bundle caching (1) 0 PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Disable update checks (1) 1 (set in image) PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME Registry authentication username "" PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD Registry authentication password "" PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN Registry authentication token ""

Most PACTO_DASHBOARD_* variables map to the CLI flag of the same name. Three are different: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is the repository positional argument, PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES maps to --trace-source and PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES maps to --mira-source, both singular.

The two trace variables let the dashboard learn which services really call each other, from trace files. Pacto has no OpenTelemetry (OTLP) receiver, so you export traces to files and mount them in. Each file becomes a named observation source. Under Kubernetes the operator-managed dashboard sets PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES for you from dashboard.observation.sources. See offline trace sources.

PACTO_CACHE_DIR sets only where the dashboard reads cached bundles. It writes them under XDG_CACHE_HOME. To keep the cache, mount a volume at ~/.cache/pacto/oci. The defaults line up because the image sets HOME=/home/pacto. The Kubernetes example below mounts an emptyDir there instead, so its cache is rebuilt on every restart. The CLI reference lists every variable.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
The dashboard auto-detects its sources at startup. The container-specific bindings are:

  • oci: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is set, or repositories are discovered from Kubernetes resolvedRef fields. Supplies bundles, version history, interfaces and diffs.
  • cache: the on-disk OCI cache, surfaced as its own source only as an offline baseline when no registry is configured.
  • k8s: a kubeconfig is mounted, or the container runs in-cluster. Supplies runtime state from the Pacto operator.
  • local: a pacto.yaml is found in the working directory (mount via volume).

docs.title: Kubernetes + OCI hybrid mode
docs.text: When the Kubernetes source is on and the operator fills status.contract.resolvedRef, the dashboard finds the contract repositories by itself. You get what is running from the operator and the contracts from the registry. If a registry is unreachable, or private and not logged in, the dashboard quietly falls back to Kubernetes only: no version history, interfaces, schemas or diffs.

docs.title: Mounting the k8s and local sources
docs.text:
Both arrive as volumes; inside a cluster the in-cluster config is used automatically, with no kubeconfig mount:

# k8s: a kubeconfig, scoped to one namespace
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true \
  -v ~/.kube/config:/home/pacto/.kube/config:ro \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE=production \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1

# local: a contract directory
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true \
  -v /path/to/contracts:/data:ro \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1 dashboard /data

docs.title: Operational Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Description GET /health Returns {"status": "ok", "version": "..."}. Use for liveness and readiness probes. GET /metrics Returns {"serviceCount": N, "sourceCount": N}: counters of the running process. GET /api/stats Pacto outcomes over a window, from the run records in PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY: the numbers the Metrics page draws, labelled unsigned statistics. GET /openapi.json OpenAPI 3.1 specification (includes a server URL matching the bind address). Also served as /openapi.yaml, and downgraded to OpenAPI 3.0.3 at /openapi-3.0.json. GET /docs Interactive API documentation.

/openapi on its own is a prefix and returns 404. The image also carries a Docker HEALTHCHECK polling /health every 10 seconds.

The status filters of /api/fleet/services, /api/fleet/entities and /api/fleet/attention and the comma-separated kinds filter of /api/fleet/entities are enums checked item by item: an unknown value or an empty item such as a trailing comma gets a 422 that names the parameter, for example query.kinds[1].

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Keep the dashboard private unless sign-in protects it

Without sign-in the dashboard refuses to serve beyond loopback unless PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true allows it. Then it has no login, API key or authorization: anyone who can reach the port reads every contract, dependency and compliance result, and can make the container pull from your registries. Publish it to 127.0.0.1 (-p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000), put an authenticating proxy in front of it, or configure sign-in with PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER_URL. The protections below defend against CSRF and resource exhaustion. They give no access control against a client that reaches the port.

A few endpoints mutate local state (POST /api/resolve, POST /api/versions and POST /api/refresh pull and cache OCI artifacts). Against those:

  • Same-origin only by default. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is emitted and cross-origin mutating requests get a 403, so a malicious page in your browser cannot drive the dashboard. The bundled UI is unaffected.
  • Explicit cross-origin opt-in. --cors-origin https://your-app (or PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN) allows one trusted cross-origin client.
  • HTTP timeouts guard against slow-client (Slowloris) exhaustion.

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
