  name: pacto-dashboard
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: pacto-dashboard
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: pacto-dashboard
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: dashboard
          image: ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          env:
            # No sign-in here: put an authenticating proxy in front of it.
            - name: PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS
              value: "true"
            - name: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO
              value: "ghcr.io/org/svc-a,ghcr.io/org/svc-b"
            - name: PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: pacto-registry
                  key: token
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 3
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 128Mi
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          volumeMounts:
            - name: cache
              mountPath: /home/pacto/.cache
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: cache
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: pacto-dashboard
spec:
  selector:
    app: pacto-dashboard
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 3000

docs.title: The service page
docs.text: Open a service in the dashboard to see everything Pacto knows about it on one page: who owns it, which contract it runs, what it depends on and where it runs. An empty area always says why it is empty.

docs.title: What the page answers
docs.text: The facts at the top name the service's domain, its owner, the contract it runs, its capabilities and the sources that saw it. The operational summary shows compliance, how certainly each target is matched to a revision, how recently it was observed and how the declared dependencies compare with observed traffic. The sections below list findings, observed traffic, resources, operational targets, environments, delivery, revisions, expected dependencies, dependents, signatures, policies, configuration, recent evidence and the limitations that make any of it uncertain.

docs.title: Owner and contract
docs.text:
The Owner fact reads No declared owner when a readable contract revision exists and none of them names an owner. It reads Owner unknown when Pacto could not read any of the service's contracts and no operational target reports the contract it runs, so Pacto cannot tell whether an owner is declared. The fleet counts both cases as unowned, and both link to this service's unowned attention item. For an unknown owner that item asks you to make one of the service's contracts readable. A declared owner links to the revision that declares it, under Declared in, where the owner's contacts are listed. The Contract fact links the newest revision in use, or the newest known revision when nothing runs the service.

A mark after an owner no revision Pacto read declares, including a resource's provider owner, says in its tooltip where it comes from.

  • Where the values come from, a fold closed by default, lists each field of the current revision with one mark whose tooltip says declared, accepted (and by whom), attested or inferred, with its source and when it was read. It shows for a service whose current revision carries a declaration or that replaced an inferred service through one. Inferred values are muted, and clearing Show inferred values hides them; the fold is then their one list on the page, in place of Inferred by Pacto. Below them, the inferred services the service replaced through a declaration and what the newest one's workload showed, or a count of those whose workload you cannot see.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Expected dependencies lists every dependency the contract declares. A dependency on a fleet service links to that service. An external dependency is delivered outside Pacto and shows the version the contract declares. An unresolved dependency matches nothing Pacto knows. Dependencies hidden by your Kubernetes permissions are counted and never named. The section count is the Declared dependencies count in the dependency drift row, which also counts the dependencies declared and observed, declared and never observed, observed and never declared, and unresolved. Outside accepted range counts dependencies whose provider version falls outside the range the contract accepts. Cannot be observed counts dependencies Pacto has no observation data for, so it cannot tell whether the service talks to them.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Each card is one resource the service consumes.

Part Shows Heading The provider, linked, its offering or no offering, the kind of use, the accepted range and the provider's lifecycle. A use of a provider with no offering appears once an adapter reports on it Provider owner The provider's owner and whether the provider answers where it runs, apart from this resource's phase Requested (declared) On the configuration row only: the provider revision, the configuration entry and the values the contract asks for Provisioning (observed) The phase per environment with the adapter, signed or unsigned and the external reference. Select a phase to see the request as a drawing. A phase is never the service's health; see Resources a service consumes Usage Not reported with the reason, and a link to the service in Mira when Mira is configured Below the cards At least N resources from providers you may not see, counted from this service's own contract and reports, then the sentence: Resize or delete runs in the provider's tools. pacto_edit refuses a request the provider's schema rejects, and pacto validate and push fail on it

docs.title: Targets and delivery
docs.text: Each operational target shows its environment, or Environment unknown when no source reported one. The Delivery section lists the service's Stages: the version each environment runs and whether it is verified, failed, frozen or waiting. A Stage belongs to the service when its spec.service.name equals the service name exactly, so orders never shows the Stages of orders-api. A Stage that names a registry domain in spec.service.domain shows only on the page of the service in that domain. A Stage that names no domain shows on the page of every service with that name. When the service has a domain, such a row reads Stage names no domain: the match is by service name only. When no Stage matches, the section says so: delivery is opt-in per service. When the dashboard does not serve delivery, the section says why, and when Pacto cannot reach the cluster it shows the error with a retry. When Pacto could not list every namespace, the section reads No Stages of this service that you can see and names what it could not list.

docs.title: Stages, actions and why
docs.text:
Each Stage row shows its state, the version it runs linked to its revision, the contract behind it and the source revision pacto publish stamped (an annotation, not signed). A Stage that cannot promote says why and how to fix it. The row shows the newest re-check, marked stale when it is about an earlier version, and the newest change. A change read from an Operation's status is marked from status, not signed.

The buttons under a row are the actions you may take: promote, unfreeze, freeze and undo. An action you may not take stays disabled, with the reason beside it. Every action proposes with your identity. Why asks the cluster, as you, what holds the Stage back, with each fix as a command when you may run it.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
The Environments section lists each environment the current revision declares or a target you can see reports, alphabetically. It never shows a promotion order: the Delivery section does. Each fact says whether it is declared, observed or inferred.

Cell Shows Declared Whether the environment's values pass, its lifetime (Lifetime not declared when absent, never persistent), its expiry, or Expired (inferred, as of ...) once expires has passed, and its owner: declared, service owner, inferred or Owner unknown. An environment only targets report reads Not declared by the current revision Observed The targets you can see labelled with the environment, linked to that target list, with (incomplete) and the reason when you may not see every target, and the revisions they run Provisioning The phases of the resources in the Resources section there (including those whose provider declares no offering), Unknown until a provider reports or why provisioning is not tracked there. A provider you may not see makes the cell Unknown Stage On a dashboard that serves delivery, the Stages whose spec.environment equals the name exactly, with their state. Stages unknown: partial listing when Pacto could not list every Stage. A Stage environment that matches no row is listed as Stage only

Below the rows:

  • Targets with no environment label, or whose sources disagree, form one Unknown row.
  • Differences between environments lists each value the declared environments disagree on, one row per environment, with not set for a value an environment leaves out.
  • Environment changes opens the What changed in this service? section filtered to environment changes; see a service's changes.
  • An expired environment is never deleted; see temporary environments.

docs.title: Delivery links
docs.text: The Delivery history and Open in Delivery links open the delivery history and the environments board narrowed to the same Stages. Both pages name the service they show and link back to every service. The dashboard API filters Stages the same way with the service and domain parameters of /api/delivery/environments and /api/delivery/history.

docs.title: Golden paths and created services
docs.text:
The page of a golden path adds a Golden path section:

  • Create a service from it holds a copyable CLI command and MCP call that name the path's newest revision by digest when a registry served it, or its folder when it was read from local files, or says why no command is available;
  • Signature shows the path's signature check: who signed it and whether a publisher rule, pin or policy accepts that signer;
  • Plugins lists the generate plugins the path names;
  • Requirements lists the offerings and references the path asks for, each reference that does not resolve and how many are on services you may not see;
  • Services created from it lists the services whose declared origin matches the path by content digest, and counts those you may not see.

A service created from a golden path shows a Created from fact labelled declared: its contract records the origin, and Pacto did not observe the creation. It links to the golden path and its revision, or shows the recorded ref with the reason it matches no golden path. The Creation status section lists the creation checklist, derived from what Pacto observes now.

docs.title: Readiness, policies and configuration
docs.text: The readiness bar tallies every known revision as passing, below its own threshold, assessment expired or not assessed, and each bucket opens those revisions. Policies and Configuration show what the current revision declares. For a schema inside the bundle, the page shows its title, description and properties, read from the bundle when the page is requested. A policy that references another contract links to that contract, which holds its content. A configuration that references another contract links to it and, once the reference resolves, shows the provider, its version, the selected configuration and that schema's content inline. An unresolved reference shows why. A schema Pacto cannot read shows why too.

docs.title: Bundle signatures and referrers
docs.text:
Only a registry source checks signatures. When the dashboard reads a revision from a registry, it lists the OCI referrers attached to the revision's digest, reads who signed each Sigstore signature and checks that signer against a publisher rule, a person's pin or a signed delivery policy (which publishers Pacto accepts). publish.sign never decides. Revisions read from a local directory, the cache or a catalog read Not checked.

Status When verified A signature verifies and its signer is accepted by the installation's rule, a pin, a verified policy or, for an external system, its release signer unverified A signature verifies, and no rule, pin or policy accepts its signer. The page names who signed in the reason and the rule's identity as the Expected signer unsigned No Sigstore bundle is attached to the digest, or the attached bundles hold no signature unknown Pacto could not decide: the registry could not list the referrers or returned only their first page, the revision has no digest, the trusted root could not be fetched, the checks ran out of time or the rule was inferred. The reason is shown
  • source says what decided: rule, pin, policy, release, inferred or none, shown as a mark on the revision page's Checked against row.
  • When the dashboard reads the installation's publishers.json and pins from the cluster, it judges as the promoter does. Without them it infers a rule from where the revision lives, such as ghcr.io/acme, and an accepted signer reads unknown with source inferred: that rule matches any organization's CI on its own artifacts, so it never makes a signature verified.

A key or KMS signer reads unknown because the bundle carries no public key and the dashboard never calls a contract's KMS. Legacy cosign .sig tags are not read. On GHCR it reads pacto publish's pacto-sig- tags, never the sha256-<hex> index.

Each result is cached for 5 minutes, and a failed check for 1 minute. The checks of one refresh share a 20 second budget. pacto fleet runs the same check on each registry reference given with --oci. The result is the provenance field of each revision in pacto_fleet_get and in /api/fleet/entities/revision?key=<key>.

docs.title: Pacto for Developers
docs.text:
You own the service, so you own its contract. This guide shows how to write one next to your code: a pacto.yaml file that says what your service exposes, what it needs and how it behaves. Platform engineers, CI and other teams then read the same file instead of asking you.

New to Pacto? Start with the five-minute Quickstart. The CLI reference lists every command and contract sections lists every field.

docs.title: Your workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Write code] --> B[Infer schemas]
    B --> C[Define pacto.yaml]
    C --> D[pacto validate]
    D --> F[pacto ci]
    F --> G[CI / Platform picks it up]

docs.title: 1. Initialize your contract
docs.text:
pacto init my-service

This creates a my-service/ directory (a bundle) with a valid starter contract. Edit pacto.yaml to match your service.

docs.title: 2. Infer schemas from your code (optional)
docs.text: If your config already ships a JSON Schema, such as your Helm chart's values.schema.json, vendor that file into your bundle and point configurations[].schema at it. Otherwise the schema-infer plugin generates one from a config file.

docs.title: Generating a configuration schema
docs.text:
Pacto resolves the --option file= path relative to the bundle directory, so keep the config file inside the bundle. With config.yaml in my-service/:

pacto generate schema-infer my-service --option file=config.yaml -o my-service

This generates my-service/config.schema.json. Reference it in your contract:

configurations:
  - name: default
    required: true
    schema: config.schema.json

Secret leak trap

The plugin leaves your config.yaml sitting in the bundle, and a bundle directory is published whole. pacto pack and pacto push upload every file under it, so pacto pull hands your config values, secrets included, to anyone who can read the artifact. The contract needs only the inferred schema. Delete the input once the schema exists, or list it in .pactoignore if you want to keep it beside the contract.

docs.title: Generating an OpenAPI spec
docs.text:
If your service exposes an HTTP API using FastAPI or Huma, use the openapi-infer plugin to extract an OpenAPI 3.1 spec from your source code:

# Auto-detect the framework: FastAPI or Huma (generates interfaces/openapi.yaml)
pacto generate openapi-infer my-service -o my-service

# Override framework detection
pacto generate openapi-infer my-service -o my-service --option framework=fastapi

Both plugins need the pacto.yaml that step 1 wrote. The starter contract already points its api interface at interfaces/openapi.yaml. A contract that pacto init read from a Dockerfile and manifests has an interface only when it found an OpenAPI file, so add the interfaces entry yourself.

Both plugins live in a separate repository and ship as separate binaries. The installer script fetches them alongside the CLI; go install and make build build only pacto. See Official plugins for how to get them.

docs.title: 3. Define the contract
docs.text: See Contract sections for interfaces, workload, state and capabilities; Dependencies and state for dependencies; and Configuration and policy for configurations and policies.

docs.title: 4. Validate and publish
docs.text:
pacto ci              # on a pull request: validate and plan every service
pacto ci --publish    # on the merged commit: publish every changed service

See Validation layers for the rules and error codes. In CI, pacto ci init writes the one step that runs both; see Put it in your repository. A published version is signed and never overwritten.

On Kubernetes, the operator checks what your service does on the network against this contract. See runtime conformance.

docs.title: Offerings and infrastructure
docs.text: Your platform team may publish contracts for the infrastructure it offers, such as a PostgreSQL database. Find them on the dashboard's Offerings page or with pacto fleet search --offering <slug>, pick a version with pacto fleet versions <slug>, then reference the contract from yours and write the values its schema lets you control. pacto validate checks those values against the provider's schema, and the Offerings page shows what the platform reports about your resource. See Provision infrastructure through contracts.

docs.title: Golden paths
docs.text: Your platform team may publish golden paths: contracts a new service starts from. List them with pacto fleet entities --template or on the dashboard's Golden paths page, then create your service with pacto init <dir> --from <path> --owner <team>. See Create a service from a golden path.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Contract reference: every field, precisely
  • Composition patterns: the compositions these primitives are usually assembled into
  • CLI reference: every command and flag
  • For platform engineers: the other side of the same contract

docs.title: External evidence
docs.text:
Some environments cannot be watched from your platform: edge sites, air-gapped estates, customer tenants and short-lived CI runners. The external evidence protocol lets them report on themselves. The remote side signs a report and pushes it to you, and Pacto checks it against the contract.

Evidence is what a tool saw in a running system. Pacto carries it in an EvidenceSet: a list of observations about one service. In Kubernetes the operator gathers evidence itself, and the optional node agent adds what the kernel saw on the network (see runtime conformance). This page covers evidence that arrives from outside.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
The producer (the remote environment) makes a key, signs a report and sends it. The platform runs the receiving server.

# Producer: create a signing key bound to the producer "edge-eu-west".
pacto evidence keygen --producer edge-eu-west --key-id edge-eu-west-2026

# Producer: sign an EvidenceSet and send it.
pacto evidence sign evidence.json --key edge-eu-west-2026.key \
  --key-id edge-eu-west-2026 --producer edge-eu-west --sequence 1 > envelope.json
pacto evidence send envelope.json --url https://pacto.example.com/api/evidence/v1/envelopes

# Platform: accept reports about one exact contract revision.
pacto evidence serve --trust ./trust \
  --subject oci://registry.example.com/acme/payments-api@sha256:<digest>

Hand the edge-eu-west__edge-eu-west-2026.pub file to the platform and put it in ./trust.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Traffic goes one way: Pacto never connects to a remote environment, which starts every request. Accepted evidence is stored in your contract registry as an OCI 1.1 referrer: an artifact attached to the contract revision it is about. The registry is the only store, so the Evidence Server needs no bucket, volume or database. When the dashboard reads a contract revision from a registry, accepted evidence records appear in the referrers list on that revision's page; see Bundle signatures and referrers.

GHCR cannot host Pacto evidence

GitHub Container Registry does not serve the native OCI Referrers API, which the Evidence Server requires. Publish contracts you want to carry evidence to a conformant registry (zot, Docker Hub, Harbor, ECR, ACR, Artifactory).

The protocol signs evidence envelopes: the wrapper around one report. Every envelope is Ed25519-signed and checked against a trust store (the list of public keys you accept) before it is stored.

docs.title: Wire format
docs.text:
An envelope carries exactly one EvidenceSet plus the identity, ordering and freshness metadata the platform needs to trust and place it.

Field Type Meaning apiVersion string Protocol version. Must be pacto.dev/evidence/v1. kind string Must be EvidenceEnvelope. id string Unique envelope id. The CLI defaults it to a sha256: hash over apiVersion, producer.id, sequence and the evidence, so two producers reporting identical evidence get different ids. producer.id string The environment that produced the envelope. Becomes the target's scope. producer.version string Optional producer or collector version. producer.keyId string Trust-store key id that signed this envelope. sequence uint64 Monotonic per-producer counter for replay and ordering. issuedAt RFC3339 When the envelope was signed. expiresAt RFC3339 End of the validity window. Zero disables expiry. evidenceSet object The Pacto EvidenceSet being reported. Top-level keys: Subject, ContractRef, Source, ObservedAt, Observations. signature object { "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "<base64>" } over the canonical bytes.

A full envelope on the wire:

{
  "apiVersion": "pacto.dev/evidence/v1",
  "kind": "EvidenceEnvelope",
  "id": "sha256:8f3c…",
  "producer": { "id": "edge-eu-west", "version": "1.4.2", "keyId": "edge-eu-west-2026" },
  "sequence": 42,
  "issuedAt": "2026-07-29T10:00:00Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-07-30T10:00:00Z",
  "evidenceSet": {
    "Subject": { "kind": "service", "name": "payments-api" },
    "ContractRef": "oci://registry.example.com/acme/payments-api@sha256:1a2b…",
    "Source": "edge-collector",
    "ObservedAt": "2026-07-29T09:59:00Z",
    "Observations": [ … ]
  },
  "signature": { "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "2Q6d…gyZhDw==" }
}

Canonical bytes. The signature covers envelope JSON with the signature field omitted, re-encoded so map keys are sorted and whitespace is normalized. Transport formatting has no effect on verification.

Immutable contract references. A reported ContractRef must be an immutable oci://…@sha256:… digest reference. Local paths, bare refs and mutable tags are rejected.

Bounds. An envelope is capped at 1 MiB and may carry at most 10,000 observations. Oversized payloads are refused before parsing. Decoding rejects unknown fields and requires apiVersion, kind, id, producer.id and producer.keyId.

Complete observation payloads. An Observed observation must carry every verdict-bearing key for its kind, even when false: present (capability), type (workload), type and present (interface), reachable (dependency), durable (persistence) and present (configuration, plus conformant when present is true). Pacto rejects a missing or null key, so a gap never reads as a confirmed negative. Other keys, such as protocol, are optional.

Freshness and replay. issuedAt and expiresAt bound the validity window. Verification rejects expired or not-yet-valid envelopes. A zero expiresAt disables the expiry check. Each producer stamps a strictly increasing sequence. Ingestion rejects a repeated id or a non-increasing sequence. Replay protection runs inside the serialized commit, over a duplicate-id set and a per-producer sequence maximum. Both are re-derived from the registry on every commit, so they survive process restarts.

docs.title: Producers that ship with Pacto
docs.text:
Two Pacto commands observe a running service and send signed envelopes with the same --evidence-url, --evidence-key, --evidence-key-id and --evidence-producer flags, so you can use the protocol without building an EvidenceSet yourself:

  • pacto agent --sink evidence watches every bound workload on a host and sends one envelope per workload each round.
  • pacto run --evidence-url ... sends one envelope per round about the command it wraps.

Both sign with a 24-hour expiry and sequences that start at the wall clock in nanoseconds, so they keep increasing across restarts. Both need the contract pinned as oci://...@sha256:<digest>, which must also be one of the server's --subject values.

docs.title: Clusters
docs.text:
The operator sets --cluster-id, the UID of the kube-system namespace, and a name when it has one. Each accepted record carries the id of the cluster that accepted it, which may differ from where the subject runs. One subject has exactly one accepting server, the single-writer rule behind replay protection. Two sources that report one record with two clusters raise CLUSTER_CONFLICT.

The targets endpoint answers pacto.dev/evidence-source/v5 when it carries a cluster, and older readers accept only v2 to v4: upgrade them before you set --cluster-id. See Clusters and target keys.

With the operator chart's registry set, accepted targets reach CI through the operator's signed target snapshot. The server still needs evidence.enabled, its subjects and its trust config.

docs.title: Provider reports
docs.text: A provider adapter reports the phase of a resource a consumer asked for with ResourceProvisioned, and its usage and cost with ResourceUsage. Both kinds need a key granted them by name. See Provider reports.

docs.title: CLI commands
docs.text: Command Side Purpose pacto evidence keygen producer Mint an Ed25519 signing keypair. Writes <keyId>.key (secret, 0600) and the public key. --producer is optional: with it the public key is <producer>__<keyId>.pub, binding the key to that producer; without it, a bare <keyId>.pub binds it to a producer named after the key id. pacto evidence sign producer Wrap an EvidenceSet in a signed envelope. Reads the EvidenceSet JSON, validates it, wraps it and signs with --key, --key-id, --producer, --sequence. Default --ttl 24h; --ttl 0 disables expiry. pacto evidence send producer Report a signed envelope outbound to an ingestion endpoint. POSTs to POST /api/evidence/v1/envelopes. pacto evidence verify either Verify a signed envelope against a trust store. Checks signature, freshness, producer authorization and trust. Exits non-zero on failure. pacto evidence provisioned producer Write an EvidenceSet with one ResourceProvisioned observation about a consumer revision (--contract), its --configuration or --dependency, --environment, --provider, --phase and --external-ref. See Provisioning reports. pacto evidence usage producer Write an EvidenceSet with one ResourceUsage observation: the --metric figures and --cost of the resource a consumer revision asked for. See Usage reports. pacto evidence serve platform Run the ingestion endpoint. Loads trust store from --trust, resolves every --subject (at least one required), verifies and evaluates envelopes and publishes results to the registry as OCI 1.1 referrers. Listens on 127.0.0.1:8686 or --listen-address. --cluster-id, with an optional --cluster-name and --cluster-name-source, names the cluster that accepts the records.

docs.title: Ingestion HTTP API
docs.text:
The ingestion host mounts five endpoints under /api/evidence/v1.

Method + path Purpose Success POST /api/evidence/v1/envelopes Accept, verify, de-duplicate, evaluate and store one envelope. 202 Accepted with { id, compliance, findings, acceptedAt } GET /api/evidence/v1/health Liveness. Independent of the registry. 200 OK with { "status": "ok" } GET /api/evidence/v1/ready Readiness. 503 until every configured subject resolves and answers native Referrers discovery. 200 OK with { "status": "ready" } GET /api/evidence/v1/producers List the trusted producer ids the host advertises. 200 OK with { "producers": [ … ] } GET /api/evidence/v1/targets The latest accepted report per target for a read-only HTTP evidence source, plus the latest provisioning reports. 200 OK with the versioned targets DTO: schema pacto.dev/evidence-source/v5 when it carries a cluster, pacto.dev/evidence-source/v4 when it carries usage records, pacto.dev/evidence-source/v3 when it carries provisioning records, pacto.dev/evidence-source/v2 otherwise

The targets endpoint takes no authentication and lists contract references, producers and the external references of provisioned resources. Keep it behind the same network and auth boundary as the dashboard. Targets and provisioning records share one bound, and a response cut by it sets truncated.

POST status codes. A non-2xx response is a JSON object { "code": <stable-code>, "message": <generic> }. The code is stable and the message is generic; neither contains the underlying error text, keys or signature bytes. The server logs verification failures and server-side errors and keeps them from the caller. TLS termination is the host's responsibility. Signature verification is always on and cannot be disabled.

Status Code When 202 Accepted — Verified, evaluated and stored. 400 Bad Request invalid_envelope The body could not be read or the envelope could not be decoded. 401 Unauthorized unauthorized_producer Signature, trust, freshness failure or the key is not authorized for this producer or subject. 409 Conflict replay A duplicate id or an out-of-sequence sequence. 422 Unprocessable Entity contract_ref_rejected The contract ref is not an approved immutable digest reference. 422 Unprocessable Entity invalid_evidence The EvidenceSet is invalid. 502 Bad Gateway contract_resolution_failed The referenced contract could not be resolved. 503 Service Unavailable store_not_ready The server has not yet resolved and enumerated its configured subjects. 503 Service Unavailable registry_unavailable, registry_incomplete The accepted history could not be read or could not be read completely, so the replay check could not run. 503 Service Unavailable store_degraded The record could not be published to the registry. 500 Internal Server Error internal_error An unexpected failure.

docs.title: Registry conformance
docs.text:
Native Referrers API is mandatory. Verify before configuring:

oras discover --distribution-spec v1.1-referrers-api <repo>@sha256:<digest>

A conformant registry answers GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest> with HTTP 200 and an OCI image index. A non-conformant one answers 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN.

Registry Referrers API zot, Docker Hub, Harbor, ECR, ACR, Artifactory Yes GHCR, CNCF distribution (registry:2, registry:3) No Operation Requirement Permissions Pull (resolve contract, enumerate referrers, read payloads) and push (publish accepted record) on every configured subject's repository. Never deletes, never writes tags, never touches unconfigured repositories. Authentication Pacto OCI credential policy: explicit credential, pacto login, GITHUB_TOKEN for GHCR or Docker config. In Kubernetes: evidence.registry.credentialsSecret names an existing kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret. Subjects Explicit allow-list of exact immutable contract revisions: --subject oci://registry.example.com/acme/checkout@sha256:<64 hex>. Mutable tags, local paths, non-oci:// refs and catalog-wide discovery rejected. At least one required. Artifact format One untagged OCI manifest per accepted report. subject: contract digest from ContractRef. artifactType: application/vnd.pacto.evidence.record.v1+json. One layer carrying pacto.dev/evidence-record/v1. Deterministic build. Writer concurrency Single active writer: one replica, Recreate rollout strategy. Registry offers no compare-and-set. Commit: verify, mutex, enumerate all referrers, rebuild replay state, check replay globally, publish, confirm discoverable, return 202. State re-derived from registry. Retention and GC Pacto never deletes evidence. Retention, backup and GC are registry responsibilities. Exclude referrers of contract manifests from GC policies that prune untagged manifests. Deleting a subject deletes its evidence.

Registry write access is evidence write access. The signature is checked once at ingestion; the read path does not re-verify it.

Readiness and partial state. Writes fail closed when reads are incomplete.

State Meaning /ready /targets ready Every subject resolved, every referrer valid. 200 200, authoritative partial (bad artifact) Every subject resolved, some referrer unreadable. 200 200 with health.status: partial partial (bad subject) Some subject failed, others read. 503 200 with health.status: partial unavailable No subject readable. 503 503 registry_unavailable

Beside status, the health block carries the counts that say which half of a partial you have: subjects, failedSubjects and invalidArtifacts.

docs.title: Trust store and trust config
docs.text:
A trust store is a single .pub file or a directory of .pub files (base64 Ed25519 public keys). The filename binds the producer: <producerId>__<keyId>.pub authorizes key keyId for producer producerId, while a bare <keyId>.pub binds the producer whose id equals the key id.

Authentication and authorization are separate. An envelope whose keyId is not in the trust store is rejected as an unknown key. An unsigned envelope, an unsupported algorithm or a bad signature is rejected. The envelope's producer.id must then match the key's bound producer, so a trusted key cannot sign as another producer.

Rotation. Add a new <producerId>__<newKeyId>.pub, sign with the new keyId and remove the old entry. The producer identity survives the key change.

Structured trust configuration for per-key allowlists:

apiVersion: pacto.dev/evidence-trust/v1
keys:
  - keyId: edge-eu-west-2026
    producerId: edge-eu-west
    publicKeyFile: edge-eu-west__edge-eu-west-2026.pub
    allowedSubjects: [payments-*]                  # path.Match globs; empty = any
    allowedContractRepos: [registry.example.com/acme/contracts]  # prefixes; empty = any
    allowedObservationKinds: [ResourceProvisioned]  # empty = every runtime kind
    allowedProviderRepos: [ghcr.io/acme/platform/postgresql]  # prefixes of provider repositories; empty = any provider

An empty allowedObservationKinds withholds ResourceProvisioned and ResourceUsage, so a team's runtime key cannot mark its own resources Ready. Give a provider adapter its own key that lists them. A key that lists only ResourceProvisioned cannot send an empty EvidenceSet.

allowedProviderRepos scopes a provisioning or usage key to its providers (Pacto core 4.5.0 or later):

  • The Evidence Server accepts a report only when the consumer's declared configuration or dependency ref is an oci:// ref to a repository under one of the prefixes, and refuses any other, a local path or a dependency with no ref included, with HTTP 403 and the code provider_not_allowed.
  • A scope requires ResourceProvisioned or ResourceUsage in allowedObservationKinds.
  • No key, scoped or not, accepts a report whose ref names a pacto-inferred repository, and loading refuses a prefix under one: an inferred contract never anchors provisioning or usage evidence.
  • The server logs a warning at startup for every provisioning or usage key with no scope.
  • The scope applies to reports accepted after the change. Reports already accepted stay until a newer report replaces them or they pass the provisioning window, so after narrowing a key have the right adapter report again.
  • pacto evidence verify holds no consumer contract, so it checks the signature, producer, subject and kind only.

Loading validates the schema version, identifier grammar, duplicate key ids, contradictory producer bindings, missing or traversing key files and malformed patterns.

Distributing the trust store is an out-of-band operator responsibility. The protocol verifies against whatever keys the host trusts and never fetches them. In Kubernetes the trust store is a Secret mounted read-only (evidence.trust.existingSecret).

For Kubernetes deployment (trust store, trust config, subjects, registry credentials), see The Evidence Server.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Operational graph: where ingested targets appear and how freshness and completeness work
  • Collectors and the evidence boundary: how an EvidenceSet is produced and evaluated
  • CLI reference: the full command surface

docs.title: External catalog reference
docs.text:
This page describes how the operational graph names the systems outside your Pacto system that contracts depend on: vendor APIs, managed cloud services and legacy hosts. Each one is a single graph node of kind external, so "who depends on Stripe?" has an answer without anyone writing a contract for Stripe. The operational graph reference covers how queries return them.

An external system never clears a gate. Pacto delivers none, never checks a version range against one and reports its status as Unknown.

docs.title: Identities
docs.text:
An identity is a path of lower-case segments. The same string is the graph key and the CLI and MCP subject external:<identity>.

Form Example Used for <vendor> stripe A vendor API, one global segment <provider>/<service>/<account-or-project>/<region>/<id> aws/rds/123456789012/eu-west-1/orders-db A managed cloud resource host/<registrable-domain> host/corp-legacy.example A host no catalog entry classifies

Rules:

  • at most five segments and 253 bytes;
  • each segment is 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits, ., _ or -, starts and ends with a letter or digit and never contains ..;
  • a host identity has exactly two segments;
  • other-egress is reserved for the cap node.

An identity carries no cluster: a vendor is the same system whichever cluster calls it. The operator reports a host that an ExternalName Service, a selectorless Service or a ServiceEntry names, and no catalog entry classifies, as legacy.

docs.title: How a declared external joins
docs.text:
A dependency with external: true and no ref joins the first identity that applies, in this order:

Order Match Rule 1 identity The dependency's identity field (pactoVersion: "2.5") 2 catalog-alias A catalog alias equal to the dependency name, or to its normalized form (Stripe API is stripe-api), ignoring case; organization entries first 3 host The registrable domain of a name that is a hostname with a public suffix: api.corp-legacy.example joins host/corp-legacy.example 4 normalized-name The name lower-cased, a numeric :port dropped, with spaces, _ and / turned into - and other characters dropped: Legacy MQ and legacy-mq join legacy-mq

A dependency with a ref resolves through its provider contract and never joins. A name that normalizes to nothing, or to other-egress, stays an unresolved external dependency. Consumers write nothing new: two contracts that declare Stripe and stripe-api join one stripe node through the default catalog. Two unrelated systems that share a generic name, such as model, also join by name; set identity or add an organization alias to tell them apart. A managed resource such as aws/rds/123456789012/eu-west-1/orders-db takes the class of its provider and service entry (aws/rds) and keeps its own name. The external page says how its consumers join it: by a declared identity, by a registrable domain or by name only.

docs.title: Catalog format
docs.text:
A catalog is one YAML file. Pacto decodes it strictly and rejects unknown keys.

apiVersion: catalog.pacto.trianalab.io/v1
entries:
  - identity: stripe
    class: vendor-api
    label: Stripe
    aliases: [stripe, stripe-api]
    hosts: [api.stripe.com, "*.stripe.com"]
    sdkModules: [github.com/stripe/stripe-go, npm:stripe, pypi:stripe, "maven:com.stripe:stripe-java"]
    keyPatterns: ["STRIPE_*"]
  - identity: aws/rds
    class: managed-cloud
    hosts: ["*.rds.amazonaws.com"]
    terraform: ["aws_db_instance:identifier"]
    crossplane: [rds.aws.upbound.io/Instance]
Field Required Rule apiVersion Yes Exactly catalog.pacto.trianalab.io/v1 entries[].identity Yes A valid identity, unique in the file; a managed-cloud entry names exactly <provider>/<service> entries[].class Yes vendor-api, managed-cloud, legacy or unclassified entries[].label No The name the dashboard shows entries[].aliases No Dependency names that join this entry; non-empty entries[].hosts No Lower-case DNS names with an optional leading *. entries[].sdkModules No Client libraries: a bare Go module path without its /vN suffix, npm:<package>, pypi:<normalized name> (lower case, runs of -, _ and . as one -) or maven:<groupId>:<artifactId> entries[].terraform No managed-cloud only. A lower-case resource type, optionally with the attribute that holds the resource id: aws_sqs_queue or aws_db_instance:identifier. An id attribute named like a password, secret, token, key, credential, private key or DSN is refused entries[].crossplane No managed-cloud only. <api group>/<Kind> of a managed resource, or of a claim or composite resource of your own XRD entries[].keyPatterns No Environment and secret key names: A-Z, 0-9 and _, with at most one trailing * entries[].otel No dbSystem, messagingSystem and rpcSystem lists of OpenTelemetry system values

An alias, host, key pattern, SDK module, Terraform resource type or Crossplane kind claimed by two entries of one file is an error, and the error names the entry. A file holds at most 2000 entries and 1 MiB. Pacto joins declared dependencies by aliases. hosts, keyPatterns, sdkModules, terraform, crossplane and otel classify what pacto init, the operator and trace sources recognize, as Matching describes.

docs.title: Matching
docs.text:
pacto init, the operator and the fleet all classify through the same matcher.

Input Rule Confidence A host The longest catalog host rule wins, an exact host over a *. wildcard of the same length. An exact rule matches only that name, and *.example.com matches its subdomains and never example.com itself likely A host no rule names Three or more labels and a public registrable domain give host/<registrable-domain>. A two-label name matches only a catalog rule, because a namespace short form such as orders.shop reads like a vendor's domain likely A configuration key name Compared without case against the entries' key patterns, with - and . read as _, so the Secret name stripe-credentials reads like STRIPE_CREDENTIALS possible An SDK a folder's manifest or lockfile lists The package name in its ecosystem. A Go module matches with its /vN suffix dropped, and so does any package under a listed module possible A Terraform resource or a Crossplane object in the folder Its resource type, or its <group>/<Kind>, equals an entry's row possible; likely for a Crossplane object whose connection Secret the workload reads An OpenTelemetry db.system, messaging.system or rpc.system value Compared exactly, without case, against the entries' values. A protocol no entry claims, such as grpc, gives no match. The default catalog claims only values that name one managed service, such as aws_sqs or dynamodb, so a generic postgresql or kafka callee stays unresolved likely

A configuration value is a host candidate only when it has a scheme (https://), a port or a key named like a host: one that contains url, uri, host, endpoint, addr, address, server or broker. A value that names no host can still match by its key name. likely means a host or a system value matched. possible means only a key name did, and nothing else confirms it.

docs.title: Redaction
docs.text:
The matcher reads a host and a port and nothing else:

  • A URL keeps only its host and port. The user name, password, path, query and fragment are never read, so postgres://user:pass@db.xyz.rds.amazonaws.com:5432/app?password=x shows as db.xyz.rds.amazonaws.com:5432.
  • A value under a key that names a password, secret, token, key, credential, private key or DSN is never parsed. Only its key name is matched. The rule reads parts of a name, so a DATABASE_DSN or KEYCLOAK_URL value gives no host either.
  • A Secret contributes its name and key names, never a value.
  • A comma-separated seed list, such as Kafka brokers, gives one host per entry, and a jdbc: prefix is dropped.

docs.title: Names that never match
docs.text: An IP address, a single label, localhost, a name with a svc label (such as orders.shop.svc.corp.local), a *.cluster.local name and a name with a label outside RFC 1123 give no match. In-cluster names stay dependencies on services. A value that does not parse gives no match, never part of the string.

docs.title: Managed resource identities
docs.text:
• A Terraform resource or Crossplane object gets the identity <provider>/<service>/<account>/<region>/<id> only when the provider, account, region and id are all literals in the folder.
  • The id is the entry's id attribute (Terraform) or the crossplane.io/external-name annotation, else the object's metadata.name (Crossplane). A Terraform resource whose id attribute is not a literal is named by its label, and the id is listed as missing.
  • When a part is missing, Pacto never invents it: the dependency keeps the entry's identity and the inferred record names the resource and the parts it misses, as below.
  • A five-segment identity takes the class, label and aliases of its <provider>/<service> entry.
external:
  identity: aws/sqs
  resource: {type: aws_sqs_queue, name: newsletter-signups, missing: [account, region]}

docs.title: The default catalog
docs.text:
Every Pacto binary embeds a default catalog of well-known vendors (Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog, Auth0, Algolia and Mailgun) and the AWS, Google Cloud and Azure managed services. Each host, SDK module, Terraform resource type and Crossplane kind cites the vendor documentation it comes from.

Each core release publishes the same bytes as an OCI artifact at ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/external-catalog:<core version> and signs it with Cosign keyless signing, as Installation lists. The digest is the sha256 of a manifest that depends only on the catalog bytes, so the embedded copy and the published artifact have one digest. Every answer records that digest in externalCatalogs, whichever copy was used.

Pacto checks the default catalog's signature only when a configured source already reads ghcr.io, so a private-registry or air-gapped installation never calls it. The check runs in the background and never delays a build: the first answer reports signature: unknown with a reason saying the check is running, and a later refresh reports the result. A one-shot command such as pacto fleet never starts the check; the dashboard, pacto mcp and the TUI report the result. When the signature verifies, copy reads registry: the embedded copy matches the signed artifact. Otherwise copy reads embedded: Pacto classifies with the copy compiled into the binary and reason says why the signature was not checked. A release run from a branch other than main signs with another identity, so that version's default catalog reads unverified and the embedded copy still classifies.

docs.title: Organization catalogs
docs.text:
An organization catalog adds entries and overrides default ones. An entry with the identity of a default entry replaces it, and an alias, host, key pattern, SDK module, Terraform resource type or Crossplane kind the organization claims is taken from any default entry that also claims it.

Give it by digest:

Surface Setting pacto fleet, pacto impact, pacto mcp, pacto stats, pacto tui --external-catalog oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST pacto init --external-catalog or PACTO_EXTERNAL_CATALOG, which pacto pack, pacto push and pacto explain also read pacto dashboard --external-catalog or PACTO_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_CATALOG The operator-managed dashboard Chart value dashboard.externalCatalog

A tag is refused, because a tag can move. The digest pin is what Pacto trusts the catalog by: its signature is reported as unknown with the reason and never decides whether it loads. A catalog Pacto cannot pull or parse is skipped, the default catalog alone classifies and the answer is partial with EXTERNAL_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE.

Publish one with ORAS and pin the digest it prints:

oras push registry.example.com/platform/external-catalog:2026-11 \
  --artifact-type application/vnd.pacto.external-catalog.v1 \
  catalog.yaml:application/vnd.pacto.external-catalog.v1+yaml

Pacto reads any manifest with that artifactType, the OCI empty config descriptor (ORAS writes it when no --config is given) and one layer of the media type application/vnd.pacto.external-catalog.v1+yaml. From a Pacto checkout, go run ./cmd/genexternalcatalog check -f catalog.yaml validates the file merged over the default and prints the entry count. The digest it prints belongs to Pacto's own minimal manifest; ORAS adds annotations, so pin the digest the registry returns.

docs.title: The cap
docs.text: One answer names at most 200 external systems. Beyond that, the least-consumed fold into one other-egress node of class other-egress, whose folded counts them; a relationship to a folded system keeps its real toExternal and gains foldedInto: other-egress. The answer is partial with EXTERNAL_CAP. The snapshot itself keeps every identity. A list answer shows at most 50 consumers of one external system, with consumersTotal and sourcesTotal counting them all.

docs.title: Restricted views
docs.text: A caller who cannot see a consumer never learns its name. An external system lists only visible consumers and counts the rest in hiddenConsumers, and its totals count visible data only. An external system that only hidden services declare, call or use is left out and counted in the Overview's hiddenExternals. An observed or inferred edge follows its caller, and evidence read on a hidden target is dropped even when its service stays visible. The cap ranks on visible consumers, so two callers with the same view get the same answer.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Raised when EXTERNAL_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE The organization catalog could not be pulled or is not a valid catalog EXTERNAL_CAP An answer folds external systems into other-egress EXTERNAL_USE_UNATTRIBUTED A source reported external uses of a service the snapshot does not hold, or with an invalid identity; they are dropped EXTERNAL_CATALOG_MISMATCH A source classified external uses with a catalog other than the one the snapshot classifies with EXTERNALS_UNREPORTED A target's source cannot say which external systems it uses (an older operator, partial coverage or a stale status)

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Pactify a service: the externals pacto init finds in a folder
  • Operational graph: how observed and inferred edges to external systems join the graph

docs.title: Fleet views
docs.text: Three ways to see all your services at once: the dashboard in a browser, pacto fleet in a terminal or CI job and pacto tui in an interactive terminal. All three read the same operational graph, the joined view of your contracts, their versions and where they run. An AI agent asks the same questions through the pacto_fleet_* tools of pacto mcp --fleet. The contract-to-infrastructure side is in For platform engineers.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
pacto dashboard opens a web dashboard over the same contracts the CLI manages and the operator checks. It has four views: what needs attention now, the service list, the Operational Graph and change analysis. It finds its sources at startup and merges them per service. Next to the Kubernetes operator it needs no OCI arguments: it reads the registry addresses from the resolvedRef field in each Pacto resource's status, then shows version history, interfaces, configuration schemas and diffs. See the pacto dashboard reference for its flags and environment variables. The service page describes what a service's page shows and how it says what Pacto does not know. The Overview counts inferred services apart and the Services list filters them.

Its HTTP API is described at /openapi.json; see Dashboard container.

docs.title: Fleet queries without a browser
docs.text:
pacto fleet answers the same questions from a terminal or a CI job: it builds one snapshot from the sources you name, then queries it with search, get, graph, status and explain. entities, entity and attention list owners, business domains and offerings, inspect one of them and list what needs attention, most severe first. Ask questions about your organization maps common questions to these commands. pacto fleet neighborhood <service> lists who a service depends on and who depends on it, with their owners, and --mira-source <url> adds the calls a Mira node saw as observed edges. pacto fleet versions <offering> lists each provider's versions of a platform offering and, with --range, which satisfy it, and pacto fleet entities --consumes <offering> lists the services that consume it. pacto fleet entity offering <slug> shows each consumer's provisioning status. pacto fleet entities --kind external lists the external systems contracts name, and get, graph and explain take external:<identity>, such as external:stripe.

For inferred services:

  • pacto fleet entities --declaration inferred --k8s lists them, as below, each with the group the cluster puts it in, and --group takes a group key (workload.group.key) to list one group;
  • pacto fleet graph lists the calls with no contract on one end as inferred edges, with the sources that saw them;
  • get or graph on the key of an inferred service a contract took over first says which service replaced it.
2 of 2 entit(ies):
  inferred    k8s:shop/Deployment/billing  k8s:shop%2FDeployment%2Fbilling  -
              namespace shop  kind Deployment  image registry.example/billing:1.4.2  group Argo CD Application shop
  inferred    k8s:shop/Deployment/cart     k8s:shop%2FDeployment%2Fcart     -
              namespace shop  kind Deployment  image registry.example/cart:2.0.1  group Helm release shop/cart

Golden paths have their own filters:

  • pacto fleet entities --template lists golden paths, and --template=exclude leaves them out;
  • pacto fleet entities --created-from <key> lists the services created from one golden path, (none) those that declare no origin and (unresolved) those whose origin resolves to no golden path; --sort created ranks golden paths by the services created from them;
  • pacto fleet search --template filters a search the same way;
  • the MCP tools take template and created_from, and the dashboard lists golden paths on its Golden paths page.

Platform offerings answer the same questions on every surface:

  • pacto fleet entities --kind offering --lifecycle deprecated (or sunset) lists offerings by the worst provider version in use, so the demo lists postgresql, and services by their newest revision; --failed keeps offerings with a failed provisioning request. The pacto_fleet_entities tool takes lifecycle and failed, and the dashboard API takes the same query parameters;
  • pacto fleet entity offering <slug> and pacto_fleet_entity add each provider's availability, successor and latestSupported, the offering's availability roll-up and its observedConsumers;
  • pacto fleet versions <offering> and pacto_fleet_versions add each provider's successor and, with a range, whether the range accepts it in successorRange;
  • pacto fleet status --lifecycle and the lifecycle argument of pacto_fleet_status report services that use a deprecated or past-sunset provider.
$ pacto fleet search --local ./contracts --oci ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0
1 of 1 service(s):
  payments-api                 NotEvaluated owner=acme/payments  domain=-            offering=-            revs=1 targets=0
warning: answer is partial (as of 2026-08-23T01:30:40+02:00)
  - [SOURCE_PARTIAL] source oci returned a partial result
  - [SOURCE_RECORD_INVALID] ref ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0 could not be resolved: artifact not found: ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0

Read the completeness before you read the rows. Pacto reports an unreachable registry, so a service missing from a partial answer may be one the missing source knew about. Likewise 1 of 1 is this page of total matches. --output-format json carries the same facts in a meta envelope for a CI job to branch on, and query semantics has the five operations and the knowledge vocabulary behind completeness.

docs.title: Detected providers
docs.text: pacto fleet providers --k8s lists the providers Pacto detected in each cluster. --detected k8s:<namespace>/<release>-detected adds the rows the operator detected, marked (inferred), here and in pacto fleet status.

docs.title: Namespace scope
docs.text: A Kubernetes source that reads a list of namespaces (--namespace payments,ledger, or an operator with controller.watchNamespaces) is always partial. It names its scope in a K8S_NAMESPACE_SCOPED limitation, such as source kind-demo watches 2 namespaces (ledger and payments); services in any other namespace are unknown, and in its namespaces list. A listed namespace it could not read is left out of namespaces and named in a K8S_NAMESPACE_UNREADABLE limitation.

docs.title: A service's changes
docs.text: A service's detail carries its changes: each declared change between the revisions Pacto holds, in version order, with provenance and source. pacto fleet entity service <key> --reached and reached on a stdio pacto_fleet_entity add when each change's revision reached a Stage, from delivery records read with your credentials; see a service's changes.

docs.title: The organization in one answer
docs.text:
pacto fleet overview prints the answer the dashboard overview draws: target compliance with its stale Compliant subset, operational health, knowledge gaps, ownership, evaluation coverage, the business domains and where to look next. The MCP tool pacto_fleet_overview returns the same answer. Run on the demo fixture, abridged:

$ pacto fleet overview --local examples/demo/bundles --target-state examples/demo/fleet-targets.yaml
asOf 2026-11-15T04:41:58+01:00  completeness complete
Targets 9: compliant 5 (5 stale) · not compliant 1 · unknown 3
Health: healthy 0 · failing 1 · unknown 2 · not observed 6
Owners: 34 declared · 3 disputed · 0 none declared · 0 unknown
Next: pacto fleet attention --category health  (Operational targets failing their health check: 1)

Failing means a target's own health check reports it is not healthy, and unknown means Pacto cannot tell. Organizational health and knowledge explains each count, and the tallies reference lists every field. The CLI lists each incomplete source by name in the answer, and the dashboard's Incomplete sources entry point opens the same sources.

pacto fleet, pacto mcp --fleet and pacto tui mark target evidence older than 24 hours as stale by default, the window the dashboard uses. --freshness 0 skips the check; the answer then carries the FRESHNESS_NOT_EVALUATED limitation and the CLI prints it as a note.

docs.title: One question, three surfaces
docs.text:
A person and an agent ask the same question in the same words. Each row names the command, the MCP tool and the dashboard API route that answer it; a flag, a tool argument and a route parameter with one meaning carry one name. A dash marks a surface that does not answer the question, and the note says where that answer lives instead.

Question CLI MCP tool Dashboard route Note Which owners, domains, offerings or services match? pacto fleet entities pacto_fleet_entities GET /api/fleet/entities What is this service, revision, owner, domain, offering or external system? pacto fleet entity pacto_fleet_entity GET /api/fleet/entities/{kind} What changed in this service, and when did it reach each Stage? pacto fleet entity service <key> --reached pacto_fleet_entity with reached GET /api/fleet/entities/{kind}?reached=true Times only from delivery records read as you; an HTTP MCP server answers times: not-read What needs attention? pacto fleet attention pacto_fleet_attention GET /api/fleet/attention Who depends on this service, and on whom does it depend? pacto fleet neighborhood pacto_fleet_neighborhood GET /api/fleet/neighborhood Which services match this text or filter? pacto fleet search pacto_fleet_search GET /api/fleet/services How is the fleet doing? pacto fleet status pacto_fleet_status GET /api/fleet/status How healthy is the organization and how much do we know? pacto fleet overview pacto_fleet_overview GET /api/fleet/overview What did Pacto detect in my cluster, and what does it use each for? pacto fleet providers pacto_fleet_status (providers) GET /api/fleet/providers No separate tool; the status answer carries the rows What is this service or target? pacto fleet get pacto_fleet_get GET /api/fleet/service, GET /api/fleet/target What is this service's dependency tree? pacto fleet graph pacto_fleet_graph GET /api/fleet/services/{name}/graph Why does Pacto say this? pacto fleet explain pacto_fleet_explain - The dashboard explains on its entity pages Which versions of this offering exist? pacto fleet versions pacto_fleet_versions GET /api/fleet/versions What does a document in this revision say? pacto doc pacto_fleet_revision_document GET /api/fleet/revisions/document The CLI reads the bundle itself What is the whole read model? pacto fleet snapshot - GET /api/fleet/snapshot MCP answers through the fleet tools Which services should Backstage show? pacto export backstage - GET /api/backstage/entities YAML for a Backstage catalog location, outside the OpenAPI document; agents read the same services through the fleet tools Which consumers does this change affect? pacto impact pacto_impact GET /api/fleet/impact, POST /api/fleet/impact Over HTTP and on a shared dashboard, only revisions in your view What did Pacto catch and deliver? pacto stats pacto_stats GET /api/stats Unsigned statistics; the dashboard reads the repository pacto dashboard --stats-registry names Which run records are behind this number? - - GET /api/stats/records The Metrics page lists them; the CLI and MCP answer totals What does this server serve? - pacto_capabilities GET /api/capabilities The CLI runs every command as the local user Who am I to delivery? pacto delivery caller pacto_delivery_caller GET /api/delivery/caller What waits on me? pacto delivery inbox pacto_delivery_inbox GET /api/delivery/inbox Which environments run which version? pacto delivery environments pacto_delivery_environments GET /api/delivery/environments How far is each Stage from autonomy? pacto delivery autonomy pacto_delivery_autonomy GET /api/delivery/autonomy Which versions do the Stages know, and are they signed? pacto delivery published pacto_delivery_published GET /api/delivery/published Which publishes did Pacto refuse? pacto delivery refusals pacto_delivery_refusals GET /api/delivery/refusals Which publishers does each service accept? pacto delivery trust pacto_delivery_trust GET /api/delivery/trust Where is this service in delivery? pacto delivery status pacto_delivery_status GET /api/delivery/progress Progress is status with --why (why in MCP) What happened on this Stage? pacto delivery history pacto_delivery_history GET /api/delivery/history What did each Stage run at a past time? pacto delivery history --at pacto_delivery_history with at GET /api/delivery/history?at= From signed records; the CLI and MCP revision is derived, the dashboard's is the fleet's Who put this digest there? pacto delivery blame pacto_delivery_blame GET /api/delivery/blame Which versions may this Stage take? pacto delivery candidates pacto_delivery_candidates - The dashboard lists them in its propose panel What does this delivery record say? pacto delivery record get pacto_delivery_record_get GET /api/delivery/record Does this delivery record verify? pacto delivery record verify pacto_delivery_record_verify - The dashboard verifies on its record page Where is this operation? pacto delivery get pacto_delivery_get GET /api/delivery/operations/{namespace}/{name} Why is this operation where it is? pacto delivery explain pacto_delivery_explain - The dashboard explains on its operation page How would I undo this operation? pacto delivery undo pacto_delivery_undo_plan GET /api/delivery/undo Where is this service in its lifecycle? pacto delivery lifecycle pacto_delivery_lifecycle GET /api/delivery/lifecycle Which operation types exist? pacto delivery describe pacto_delivery_operation_types - The dashboard's propose panel lists them What would this operation do? pacto delivery plan pacto_delivery_operation_plan POST /api/delivery/plan Propose this operation pacto delivery propose pacto_delivery_operation_propose POST /api/delivery/operations Cancel this operation pacto delivery cancel pacto_delivery_cancel DELETE /api/delivery/operations/{namespace}/{name} Answer this operation pacto delivery approve - POST /api/delivery/operations/{namespace}/{name}/decision People answer; MCP has no approve tool Create a contract pacto init pacto_create - The dashboard writes no contract files Edit a contract - pacto_edit - People edit pacto.yaml and run pacto validate Is this contract valid? pacto validate pacto_check - The dashboard validates nothing What may a contract say? - pacto_schema - The JSON Schema is published with the docs Declare a running service pacto declare pacto_declare - An agent writes a draft a person accepts with pacto declare --from-draft; over HTTP the tool only plans Accept proposed ranges or a break pacto accept pacto_accept POST /api/fleet/accept An agent writes an acceptance draft a person signs with pacto accept --draft; the tool is served over stdio only; the dashboard shows the plan and the pacto accept command and never signs or writes

For one fleet, the three surfaces return the same asOf, completeness, limitations and unknown counts. The dashboard, and MCP with --dashboard-url, also add href links to dashboard pages.

docs.title: The terminal UI
docs.text:
pacto tui is the dashboard's terminal equivalent, built over the snapshot pacto fleet builds and taking the same source flags. It loads that snapshot once and opens on the Services tab. From there you move through services, revisions, targets, owners and sources, with whatever row is highlighted standing in as the argument, so you never type a path. It needs an interactive terminal; in a pipeline, use the plain commands.

One difference from the dashboard matters more than the rest: the dashboard only reads and the TUI also writes. Read verbs run in-process against the loaded snapshot. Write verbs shell out to this same binary so they own the terminal. Each one names what it is about to change before it waits for a y: the directory a pull will overwrite, the resolved plugin binary, the output directory a generate will write. Pass --read-only to remove the four write verbs from the in-TUI help screen.

# whatever bundles are under the current directory
pacto tui

# a populated screen from the committed demo fixture
pacto tui --local examples/demo/bundles \
  --target-state examples/demo/fleet-targets.yaml \
  --traces examples/demo/traces.json

# the same demo with no clone at all, straight out of the registry
pacto tui --root oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/pacto-demo:1.0.0 --local ""

The second command needs a clone and a paste from the repository root; it opens on 38 services, a golden path and 4 operational targets. The third needs nothing on disk: --root follows the published contract's dependency declarations and pulls 12 of the demo's 39 services out of ghcr.io, and --local "" switches off the default directory scan. A registry has no record of where anything runs, so every service reads NotEvaluated until you add the --target-state fixture.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Action tab / shift+tab cycle the tabs: kinds on the list, categories under a, direction on a graph / filter; enter applies it, esc discards what you typed enter open the highlighted row a what needs attention + / - graph depth ? toggle the key table for the current screen r reload the snapshot q back, or quit from the root screen esc clear an applied filter, otherwise the same as q y copy the equivalent pacto command v validate the selected bundle E / e explain the bundle, or explain it from the fleet's point of view l check the lock file d / i diff or impact between two selections, pressed twice g the selection's neighborhood graph p / P push, or pull (writes; asks first) L rewrite the lock file (writes; asks first) G run a generate plugin (writes; asks first)

y copies the command you would have typed to the clipboard, so you can run anything the TUI has no key for. The line is shell-quoted, so a value carrying a space or a semicolon still pastes as one argument. With no clipboard, for example over ssh or on a headless box, the TUI prints the line and the reason it could not copy it. See the pacto tui reference for every flag.

docs.title: GitHub Actions Integration
docs.text: pacto-actions runs Pacto in GitHub Actions. Its reusable workflow plans every service of a repository on pull requests and publishes the changed ones on merges to the default branch, with pacto ci as its only step. Its composite action runs single Pacto commands in jobs you write.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pacto ci init writes this caller to .github/workflows/pacto.yml:

on: [pull_request, push]
permissions: {contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, pull-requests: write}
jobs:
  pacto:
    uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions/.github/workflows/ci.yml@8b64cfe46f01f82a1b990afc5b64a01a73d0f4d0 # v2.0.0

The uses: line pins a pacto-actions commit, with the release in the comment, the form Dependabot rewrites when it bumps the pin. The caller runs once per workflow run: it plans every service under path, and a second call in the same run, such as a matrix over folders, collides on its artifact names. See Put it in your repository for what the plan shows.

docs.title: Jobs and permissions
docs.text:
Job Runs when Runs Permissions plan a pull request pacto ci, then the job summary and one annotation per service that does not read as unchanged contents: read, packages: read publish a push to the default branch, with publish on pacto ci --publish, one run per repository at a time contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write comment a pull request from the same repository, with comment on posts or updates one plan comment pull-requests: write

GitHub checks every job's permissions against the caller's before it starts the workflow, skipped jobs included, so a caller grants the whole map in the quick start. Each job then takes only its own. A push to any other branch runs no job.

Only publish holds id-token: write. GitHub mints the OIDC token for that job, and the Pacto CLI in it exchanges the token with Sigstore for a short-lived certificate; the token never leaves the job, and the Pacto installation never holds it.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Meaning path . root pacto ci walks for pacto.yaml files registry empty registry the services publish to, such as ghcr.io/acme; empty resolves it from the platform pacto-version empty Pacto release to run; empty runs the release this pacto-actions release pins and checks by sha256; latest runs the newest release unpinned; a release without pacto ci stops the job with an error naming this input pacto-artifact empty name of an artifact of the same run holding a static linux pacto, used instead of the download publish true publish on a push to the default branch comment false post the plan as one sticky comment on pull requests from the same repository fail-on blocked blocked fails the plan job on exit 1; unverified also fails it on exit 2 transparency-log true with sign-key, record the signatures in the transparency log; keyless signing always records them

docs.title: Secrets and outputs
docs.text:
Secret Use registry-username, registry-password registry login for a registry other than GHCR; GHCR uses the workflow's token sign-key, sign-key-password a cosign key publish signs with instead of keyless; written to the runner's temporary directory only

Keyless signing records the repository, workflow and commit in the public Rekor log. A private repository that must not appear there sets the sign-key secret, or declares publish.sign with a private log.

The workflow outputs gate (clear, blocked or unverified) and exit-code (0, 1 or 2) from the plan job.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: The plan job annotates each service that does not read as unchanged on its pacto.yaml: an error when it is blocked, a warning when it is unverified and a notice when it is clear. A service Pacto could not compare, such as one with no registry to read, is annotated too. GitHub shows at most 10 annotations of each level per step; the job summary lists every service.

docs.title: Commands for your own jobs
docs.text:
The composite action TrianaLab/pacto-actions@<sha> takes a command:

Command Runs setup installs pacto, pinned by version and sha256; its version input names another release ci pacto ci, with gate and exit-code outputs and the fail-on input; gate is empty when Pacto could not plan publish pacto ci --publish, keyless (the job needs id-token: write) or as publish.sign declares impact, validate, diff, doc the Pacto command of that name

A service that builds with ko, Jib or buildpacks runs command: setup, its build and command: publish in a job of its own.

docs.title: Moving from v1
docs.text: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1 keeps working and stays at v1. v2 removes the push command: replace it, and the jobs that ran validate, diff and pacto publish, with the caller above; From an imperative pipeline to one step maps each one.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
This page defines every word these docs use with a special meaning, in alphabetical order. Each word is defined here once, and the link after it leads to the page that explains it in full. Other pages link here instead of explaining the word again. The dashboard and the command line use the same words. Where the dashboard shows a different label, the last column gives it.

Word Meaning In the dashboard Acceptance record A signed statement, attached to a service's published version, that its owner accepts proposed ranges or a break a provider announces in breaks. Written with pacto accept; only one signed by the service's declared owner counts, and pacto ci --publish carries it into the next version. See Accept proposed ranges — Accept the unknown A person lets a change with an Unknown check go ahead. It is recorded as accepted, never as a pass. See What Unknown means Accept the unknown Adapter The program that reports what it provisioned for the requests of a platform offering, as ResourceProvisioned evidence. Its slug is free text it picks; scope its key with allowedProviderRepos. See Adapters Adapters reporting Admission policies Rules the Kubernetes cluster runs on every request before it accepts it. Pacto's check who may ask for and approve a change, and records say whether they were on (guarded). See Install — Agent An AI agent, such as Claude, that calls Pacto's tools over MCP. It can plan and ask for changes, and only a person approves one. See Who may approve. An agent you build is a service like any other: see an agent is a service. The pacto agent command is the runtime watcher; see Node agent Agent Anchor One fixed digest per Stage in the streams repository. Every record of that Stage hangs on it as a referrer, so the anchor is where the Stage's whole history is read. See Where records live — Approval A person's answer on one held change: approve, accept the unknown or reject. See Look, then decide Approve Argo CD A GitOps tool that applies Kubernetes files to a cluster. Pacto works with an OCI-sourced Argo CD Application, one that reads its files from an artifact in a registry, and moves a version by writing its digest onto it. See Apply through Argo CD — Auto-hold Set when someone rolls a Stage back by hand, or promotes it back to a version it already verified. Automation stops promoting there until a person unfreezes it or promotes a version it has not verified yet. See Roll back by hand — Availability Whether a platform offering serves in an environment: available, degraded, unavailable or unknown. Pacto derives it from the provider's fresh targets and the reports of consumers that cannot reach it, never from compliance, and reads unknown when it cannot see every target. It is separate from resource health. See Is an offering available? Availability Break-glass A group, pacto:break-glass by default, allowed to force a version past every check. A forced version freezes the Stage. See Force a version — Breaking change A change that removes or changes something consumers may use. Pacto classifies every change as breaking, possibly breaking or non-breaking. See Change classification — Bundle A contract together with the files it points to (OpenAPI documents, schemas), as one folder or one published artifact. See Bundle structure — Change One requested move of a Stage to another version, from request to outcome. In Kubernetes it is an object of kind Operation. See What happens to a change Change Check A test Pacto runs on a version before or after it moves: was it published and signed, does it break a consumer, does the running service do what its contract says. Each answers Pass, Fail or Unknown. See What happens to a change Checks Check suite A test or eval file a version ships in its checks list. A Stage runs it, and only a verdict about that exact file counts. See Checks — Clear The contracts clear a change when every consumer accepts the new version. See Who is asked and why — Cold start A new Stage begins on observe and earns more freedom from there. See Cold start — Collector What gathers evidence, such as the Kubernetes observer or the eBPF node agent. See Collectors — Compliant The compliance state of a contract whose evidence covers it and raises no error or warning. Compliant Consumer A service that calls another one. Checkout is a consumer of payments. See Impact analysis Consumers Consumer range Which versions of another service a contract accepts, such as ^2.0.0 (any 2.x), set in compatibility. Pacto judges each change per consumer by these ranges, never per field or endpoint. Also called version range. See Who is asked and why — Consumption What a consumed resource uses and costs. Pacto shows it only when a provider reports it; until then it reads not-reported, and live utilization comes from Mira. The word never names Pacto's own metrics.
