    ObservedAt:  time.Unix(0, 0),
    Observations: []evidence.Observation{
        evidence.NewInterfaceObserved(evidence.SubjectRef{Kind: "interface", Name: "public-api"}, "openapi", true, prov),
    },
}

// 3. The pure engine evaluates Contract x Evidence.
findings, coverage := validation.Evaluate(c, ev)

Across a trust boundary a remote environment reports a signed EvidenceSet over the evidence protocol instead.

docs.title: Distinctions the model keeps
docs.text:
The model keeps each of these pairs apart. Merging a pair turns an uncertain answer into a wrong one.

  • A requested reference and a resolved identity. payments-api:latest is a question; payments-api@sha256:… is an answer. A tag is mutable, so resolve the reference before you treat it as exact content.
  • The same name in two domains. Identity is domain-qualified, so two organizations that both run a payments-api stay two services. A repository basename or a path leaf is a label.
  • An exact revision match and retrievable content. A target can pin a digest that names a revision unambiguously while that content sits in a registry Pacto cannot read. A feature that needs the content reports it as missing; a feature that needs only the identity works as usual.
  • Declared ownership and a canonical owner identity. An owner identity carries both its kind and its value, so a team and a person who share a string stay separate. An email address is a contact for an owner.
  • Readiness and compliance. Readiness is a team's own scored self-assessment of a revision. Compliance comes from evidence. A revision that passes every readiness check can run on a target that is non-compliant.
  • No evidence and evidence of absence. Pacto records each observation as observed, unsupported, failed, stale or insufficient. "We could not look" and "we looked and it was missing" are different records.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Pacto records what a service revision guarantees, so that people and tools can compute against it. These limits hold for the contract engine and the operator. The opt-in delivery component changes two of them, as noted.

  • Pacto complements your developer portal and service catalog. A portal decides what people see and a catalog lists services to browse. Pacto keeps the contracts and their golden paths: contracts a platform team publishes and pacto init --from copies into a new service. See Create a service from a golden path.
  • Pacto publishes to the OCI registries you already run.
  • Pacto models one service's operational intent. Your databases, queues and networks stay in the tools that manage them.
  • Permissions stay with your runtime controls. Pacto validates a contract against policy schemas. OPA, Kyverno, admission and IAM decide whether an action is permitted. Delivery adds its own admission policies, which decide who may move or approve a change to a Stage.
  • The engine reasons; collectors observe; actors act. The engine reads only Contract and EvidenceSet. Delivery is one such actor: it picks the version a Stage runs, rolls back and freezes, and Flux or Argo CD applies it.
  • Reading a contract grants no permission. Finding and reading a contract changes nothing and performs no action.

docs.title: The operational control loop
docs.text:
These roles compose into a loop a platform or an agent can drive. Steps 1, 2, 5 and 6 are implemented here: the CLI, the dashboard, the collector and Evaluate. Steps 3 and 4 belong to systems you already run.

  1. Declare. A contract states the service's identity, interfaces, capabilities, configuration, dependencies and policies.
  2. Read. A platform, a controller or an agent inspects the contract (pacto explain, the dashboard API or generated tools over MCP).
  3. Constrain. (External.) Policies, permissions, admission and IAM decide which actions are allowed.
  4. Act. (External.) Controllers, deploy systems, plugins or agents act through existing infrastructure.
  5. Observe. Collectors obtain runtime evidence from the real system and produce an EvidenceSet.
  6. Evaluate. Evaluate(contract, evidence) reports whether observed reality is consistent with the declared contract.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• The Pacto Operational Graph: the read model over many such evaluations, and the vocabulary for how much of the world an answer saw
  • Validation layers: whether a contract is valid, a separate question from whether it matches reality
  • Evidence protocol: reporting a signed EvidenceSet across a trust boundary
  • Impact analysis: the confidence model over a change

docs.title: Multi-cluster
docs.text: This page describes how one Pacto reads the Pacto resources of several clusters and how each signed-in person sees only what each cluster's own RBAC lets them read. Keys and cluster names are covered in Clusters and target keys.

docs.title: Read several clusters (ad hoc, read-only)
docs.text:
Name each cluster by its kubeconfig context with --context, once per cluster:

pacto dashboard --context eu-prod --context us-prod
pacto fleet status --context eu-prod --context us-prod
pacto mcp --fleet --context eu-prod --context us-prod

pacto fleet, pacto tui, pacto impact, pacto stats and pacto mcp take --context beside --k8s. --k8s keeps reading the current context, and --k8s --context us-prod reads both. On pacto dashboard, outside a pod, the named contexts replace the current context: the dashboard neither reads it nor signs people in against it. Each context is read with its own credentials, even when Pacto runs in a pod with a kubeconfig it mounts itself.

These reads are ad hoc and read-only. Pacto reads Pacto resources only, never delivery objects or an internal developer platform, and writes nothing in any cluster.

docs.title: Each cluster is read once
docs.text:
Pacto identifies a cluster by the UID of its kube-system namespace. Two contexts that reach the same UID on the same server and certificate authority are one cluster, read once through the first context. One UID on two servers, which happens when a cluster is restored from another cluster's etcd snapshot, is a CLUSTER_CONFLICT: Pacto reads only the first context and marks the answer partial.

A context whose cluster identity Pacto cannot read is refused when other clusters are read beside it, with a CLUSTER_UNKNOWN limitation that names the context, so same-named targets of two clusters never merge. A single context keeps working without an identity.

docs.title: The sign-in cluster
docs.text: The dashboard signs people in against one cluster, the sign-in cluster: the in-cluster configuration when the dashboard runs in a pod, else the first --context, else the current context. The dashboard prints it at start-up as Sign-in cluster:.

docs.title: What each person sees
docs.text:
Pacto asks each cluster's API server, with that context's credentials, a SubjectAccessReview about the signed-in person. A grant on prod in eu-prod shows prod in eu-prod only, never prod in us-prod. Each context's credentials need create subjectaccessreviews in their cluster. Answers are kept for a minute per cluster, person, resource and namespace, so a removed RoleBinding hides its namespace within that time. A failed review is never kept.

Every cluster reviews the same person the sign-in cluster signed in. This is right when every cluster maps people the same way: one OIDC issuer with the same claim mapping. Clusters with different issuers are not supported yet.

ServiceAccount and node identities exist in one cluster only, so Pacto reviews a person whose user starts with system:serviceaccount: or system:node:, or who is in the system:serviceaccounts or system:nodes group, in the sign-in cluster only. Every other cluster is hidden from them as not reviewable.

The HTTP MCP fleet tools and the MCP delivery reads review callers in each cluster the same way. Their sign-in cluster is always the current context, or the in-cluster configuration in a pod, since --context adds clusters there. pacto mcp prints it at start-up and warns when the fleet does not read it; add --k8s so that ServiceAccount callers see their own cluster.

docs.title: Hidden clusters
docs.text:
A cluster a person sees nothing of is named, never silently left out. Each one adds a CLUSTER_HIDDEN limitation and marks the answer partial; the other clusters' answers stay whole and the request never fails.

Word Meaning no access You may read no namespace in that cluster. review failed The review failed or took longer than 5 seconds; the cluster shows again when a review answers. not reviewable Pacto has no way to review you there: no context reaches it, its identity conflicts or you signed in with a ServiceAccount or node identity of another cluster.

A cluster that stops answering is never read as empty. The dashboard and an MCP server keep the last good read and show it as stale, with its targets. A one-shot command has no earlier read, so the cluster is unreachable and the answer partial.

docs.title: Cluster status and filter
docs.text:
Every fleet answer lists each cluster in meta.clusters, with its status, its access word and how many targets it shows. pacto fleet status prints a Clusters: line with each cluster's UID, such as Clusters: eu-prod (5b0c...) complete, us-prod (9f1c...) no access. A context Pacto refused to read shows why: conflicting id or unidentified.

List one cluster's targets, and the services and revisions that run there, with its UID. Inferred services of that cluster are listed too. An id that no cluster has, such as a cluster's name, answers an empty list with a CLUSTER_FILTER_UNKNOWN limitation:

pacto fleet entities --kind target --cluster 9f1c4e2a-... --context eu-prod --context us-prod

The MCP tool pacto_fleet_entities takes the same cluster argument and the dashboard API takes ?cluster=. On the dashboard, the Services and Targets lists show a Cluster filter with a line such as Showing 1 of 2 clusters (us-prod: no access), and Data sources shows each cluster's status, both only when two or more clusters are known.

docs.title: Operation records
docs.text: Delivery runs in one cluster. The Metrics page leaves out the operation records of a service you may read whose Stage is in another cluster, and counts them: 12 operation records from other clusters are not shown. The statistics answer carries the count as hidden.otherClusters. When the dashboard cannot read the sign-in cluster's identity, every record that names a cluster is hidden, with a HOME_CLUSTER_UNKNOWN limitation that counts them.

docs.title: Offering availability and lifecycle
docs.text: This page describes the answers the operational graph gives about a platform offering as a whole: whether it serves, whether its providers are deprecated and what replaces them, who calls it without declaring it and what happens if it goes down.

docs.title: Is an offering available?
docs.text:
Each provider and each offering carries availability: a state per environment in byEnvironment, a roll-up state and the asOf time it is judged against. Pacto derives it from what it observes. It never reads the compliance verdict and the contract declares nothing about it. Availability answers whether the capability serves, a separate question from the provisioning status of the resources consumers asked for: a database server can serve while one consumer's database failed.

Per provider and environment, a target is fresh when it is neither stale nor quarantined and its evidence is less than 24 hours older than asOf. A fresh target serves when no interface it declares reports INTERFACE_ABSENT or an inconclusive finding such as EVIDENCE_MISSING; it serves nothing when every interface its contract declares reports INTERFACE_ABSENT:

What Pacto sees state provenance A provider target is hidden from the viewer or a target source is partial, stale or unavailable unknown unknown Every fresh target serves and no consumer reports it unreachable available observed Fresh targets, some reporting INTERFACE_ABSENT degraded observed Fresh targets, every one serving none of its interfaces unavailable observed Fresh serving targets and a consumer target that reports DEPENDENCY_UNREACHABLE for it degraded inferred No fresh provider target, and every consumer target that declares it reports it unreachable unavailable inferred No fresh provider target, and some of those consumer targets report it unreachable degraded inferred Fresh targets whose interfaces were never seen answering unknown unknown Targets with no fresh evidence unknown unknown No target and no report unknown unknown

Each environment gives its reason, the reporting and targets counts and at most five consumer targets in unreachable. Pacto reads no replica count, so reporting counts targets with fresh evidence, whatever their readiness. A managed provider outside the observed clusters has no target, so one consumer that cannot reach it among others that do reads degraded, never unavailable. When no target or report places a provider in any environment, one entry with an empty environment keeps the reason, and the CLI and the dashboard call it nowhere observed, or no target you may see when targetsHidden says every target is hidden from the viewer.

docs.title: How states roll up
docs.text:
A provider's state is available when every environment is available and unavailable when every one is. It is degraded when an environment is degraded, or one is unavailable and another available, and unknown otherwise, so an unknown environment never reads as trouble. An offering takes the best provider per environment, in the order available, degraded, unknown and unavailable: a provider that may serve keeps the offering from reading unavailable. A provider seen in no environment, or with targets hidden from the viewer, keeps every environment from reading unavailable and marks it partial; its nowhere-observed entry is left out once another provider places the offering.

The offering page shows availability first, per environment.

docs.title: Deprecated providers and successors
docs.text:
A consumer that reaches a deprecated or past-sunset provider through a dependency or a configuration reference gets one item in the lifecycle attention category, and the Overview tile Services using a deprecated provider opens them:

Code Severity When DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_DEPRECATED warning The provider revision the consumer reaches is deprecated. DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_SUNSET error That revision's sunset date has passed. SUCCESSOR_OUT_OF_RANGE error The consumer's range excludes the provider's resolved successor.

The lifecycle a consumer sees belongs to the newest provider revision its range reaches, or the one pacto.lock pins, so a successor released under the same service never hides the deprecation of the version a consumer still uses. pacto fleet status --lifecycle and the lifecycle argument of pacto_fleet_status report the same items. A provider's own lifecycle, successor and an offering row's lifecycle come from its current revision: the newest one a target runs, else the newest readable one, as on a service page. The demo's postgresql targets still run 16.1.0, so its row reads deprecated after 17.0.0 ships.

docs.title: Successors
docs.text: A provider whose current revision declares a successor carries it in successor. The last path segment of the oci:// reference names a service in the provider's registry domain, and its tag or digest names one revision. A resolved successor is inferred, as a resolved dependency is. A successor that names no revision in the fleet is unknown, gives its reason and raises a SUCCESSOR_UNRESOLVED limitation, and no range is graded against it. Each consumer use carries successorRange against the resolved successor and supportedRange against latestSupported, the provider's newest readable revision that declares no lifecycle and is newer than every revision that declares one. A successor that is another service says so in its reason, and no range for the old provider is graded against it: the next step is to change the dependency. In a restricted view an unresolved successor's reason says "you may see". The dashboard shows the latest supported verdict when the successor cannot be graded. With a range, pacto fleet versions and the offering page's range check name the successor of the newest revision the range reaches, so ^16.0.0 still asks about 16.x once 17.0.0 ships.

docs.title: Who else calls it
docs.text: observedConsumers lists the services seen calling a provider at runtime that declare no use of any provider of the offering, with provenance observed, lastSeen and stale once the call is more than 24 hours older than asOf or carries no time, at most 200 with the true total. A caller with no contract is listed by name with uncontracted: true and no time, so its last sighting is unknown. Observed callers are never counted in consumers. The offering page lists them under Also calling a provider.

docs.title: What if an offering goes down
docs.text: pacto impact --unavailable offering:<name> and --removed offering:<name> ask what happens to the consumers of every provider of the offering at once. The offering page links to the same question with What if it becomes unavailable?. See Ask about an offering.

docs.title: Under a restricted view
docs.text: Availability is partial in every environment where the provider has dependents or consumers the viewer cannot see, and its reason says so. A provider the viewer cannot see is counted in hiddenProviders, and in each environment it turns an offering's unavailable into unknown. Observed callers the viewer cannot see are counted in hiddenObservedConsumers.

docs.title: Clusters and target keys
docs.text: This page describes how the operational graph keys targets when it reads more than one cluster, how old keys keep resolving and where each cluster name comes from. The live Kubernetes source, a target-state file with a cluster block and an Evidence Server each report a cluster. Multi-cluster covers reading several clusters and what each signed-in person sees in each.

docs.title: Key forms
docs.text:
A target key names one target as <scope>/<kind>/<name>. The cluster component appears only when the snapshot holds more than one cluster: then each target with a known cluster gains a leading component, the UID of that cluster's kube-system namespace. Every component is escaped the same way. A snapshot that reads a cluster lists it in clusters, with the sources that reported it.

Snapshot Key of the payments Deployment Zero or one cluster payments/kubernetes/payments Two or more clusters 9f1c4e2a-…/payments/kubernetes/payments Two or more clusters, target with no known cluster _/payments/kubernetes/payments

The _ component never names a real cluster, so a target with no known cluster keeps a key of its own.

docs.title: Resolving a key
docs.text:
You ask for Answer A 3-part key with zero or one cluster That target A 3-part key that one cluster matches That target, under its 4-part key A 3-part key that one cluster matches while a source is unavailable or partial That one candidate to choose; the missing source may hold another A 3-part key that several clusters match The candidates; nothing is guessed A 4-part key with zero or one cluster The 3-part target in that cluster A 4-part key whose target has no known cluster That target as the one candidate, with the reason A _ key with zero or one cluster The 3-part target with no known cluster

On an ambiguous key the dashboard API answers 409 Conflict with one candidates detail per target (the key as value, its label as message), and the dashboard page lets you choose. Name ambiguity keeps 422. The CLI and MCP print the candidates; the CLI exits 1:

ambiguous target key: this target key names targets in more than one cluster; choose one; candidates:
  us-prod / payments / payments   77ad01b3-…/payments/kubernetes/payments
  eu-prod / payments / payments   9f1c4e2a-…/payments/kubernetes/payments

A candidate list holds only targets your view may see, and every candidate key opens its own target.

docs.title: Cluster names
docs.text:
A target with a cluster component is shown as eu-prod / payments / payments. The name is display only, and clusterNameSource says where it came from:

clusterNameSource Name node-label A node label that holds the cluster name, such as alpha.eksctl.io/cluster-name context The kubeconfig context name file The cluster.name of a target-state file uid The first 8 characters of the UID

A name the live source read always wins over a name another source reported, and a reported name carries clusterNameReportedBy. A reported name is at most 63 bytes; a name the live source read is at most 253, so an EKS ARN context name fits. When two clusters resolve to the same name, each name gains the first 8 characters of its UID, such as eu-prod (9f1c4e2a). Renaming a cluster keeps its UID; a rebuilt cluster has a new UID and so new keys.

docs.title: Targets with no cluster
docs.text: CLUSTER_UNKNOWN names a source whose targets carry no cluster id. With several clusters it makes that source partial. With one cluster it does so only when such a target merged into a clustered one; otherwise it is informational. With no known cluster it never appears.

docs.title: Migrating stored keys
docs.text: A stored 3-part key keeps working while one cluster matches it, and an old dashboard link redirects to the canonical one. Store the key an answer returns. A 4-part key never becomes ambiguous.

docs.title: Inferred services
docs.text: This page describes how the operational graph shows the workloads a cluster runs before anyone writes a contract for them, what Pacto reads from each one and what an inferred service never does. The other sources are in the operational graph reference.

docs.title: The workload source
docs.text:
With --k8s, and in the dashboard next to the operator, a second source reads every Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet and CronJob of the cluster, or of the namespaces you name. Its id is the Kubernetes source id followed by -workloads, k8s-workloads without one, and its kind is kubernetes-workloads. Each workload no Pacto resource targets joins the graph as an inferred service with its image, its container ports and its readiness, liveness and startup probes, each with the object path Pacto read it from.

The source needs list on deployments, statefulsets and daemonsets in the apps group and on cronjobs in the batch group, plus the grouping kinds. Listing a workload also returns every inline env[].value of its pod template, kube-system included. Pacto reads no environment variable, Secret, ConfigMap, command, argument or header, and no annotation other than the grouping ones, and drops those values before anything is stored or served. It cuts a probe path at the first ? or #, because probes often carry tokens there, and drops an image or a probe path that holds a control character or runs past 512 or 256 characters. The workload lists each such field in dropped, and one SOURCE_RECORD_INVALID limitation per source counts those workloads.

Limitation Meaning PACTO_CRD_NOT_INSTALLED The cluster serves no Pacto CRD. The Kubernetes source reads no target and is partial; the workloads still show as inferred services INFERRED_SERVICES_CAPPED A source reported more than 5000 workloads. The rest are left out and the source is partial DECLARATION_UNVERIFIED Pacto could not read the Pacto resources of the inferred service's namespace, so a contract may describe it. The service carries declarationUnverified, one limitation per source counts them and the Overview counts them as inferredUnverified INFERRED_REPLACEMENT_AMBIGUOUS More than one declared service targets the workload or names it in its declaration, a target of unknown cluster names it in a snapshot of several clusters, or a declaration names it with no cluster in a fleet of several clusters. The workload stays an inferred service; see When a contract takes over INFERRED_LINK_IGNORED A declaration names the workload but hands nothing over: no accepted person signed it or the source checks no signatures, a Pacto target runs as the workload, the workload is in a namespace where the service has no target, its cluster contradicts the fleet's, or a newer revision ships an inferred record Pacto cannot read. The workload stays an inferred service; see When a declaration replaces an inferred service SUBJECT_REPLACED pacto impact --event was asked about the key of an inferred service a declared service replaced, and answers for the declared service SERVICE_INFERRED The answer is about an inferred service. pacto fleet graph and pacto impact --event answer partial, since no contract can depend on it; pacto fleet explain lists it as a reason SERVICE_GROUP_AMBIGUOUS Two groups of one rule claim the workload, so it stays ungrouped; see Groups and repositories

The check is conservative. A Kubernetes source that reads every namespace verifies its workloads only when it is available, so one invalid Pacto resource leaves every inferred service of that cluster unverified. A source scoped to a namespace list verifies the namespaces it read.

docs.title: Declared and inferred services
docs.text:
Every service record carries declaration: declared when a contract revision or a Pacto target describes it, inferred when Pacto only sees a workload. An inferred service's name is the workload's k8s:<namespace>/<kind>/<name>, such as k8s:shop/Deployment/billing; with more than one cluster the cluster id comes first, as in k8s:<cluster>/shop/Deployment/billing. Its domain and summary read unknown and its status is empty.

  • --declaration inferred on pacto fleet entities and pacto fleet search, and declaration on pacto_fleet_entities and pacto_fleet_search, keep only inferred services; declared leaves them out. With no filter the listing marks them. Entity and search rows carry declaration and inferred rows carry image.
  • An inferred service never satisfies a dependency, never counts as a consumer in impact and never clears a gate or a promotion. A dependency named exactly like one stays unresolved.
  • A workload source reports no consumer, so when it is unavailable or capped the snapshot reads partial but impact and promotion answers do not; its limitation still shows.
  • An inferred caller of a declared service stays an uncontracted caller, so BlockerMissingContract still fires. The caller carries the inferred service's key in entity and its UNCONTRACTED_CALLER attention item in caller.
  • services on the Overview and every tally count declared services only; inferredServices counts the rest.
  • The detail lists the declared services the workload was seen calling. callsObserved is false when no source that reports calls covers its cluster, and an empty list then means unknown.
  • A restricted view shows an inferred service only to a viewer whom Kubernetes lets list both Pactos and that workload kind in its namespace. Hidden ones are counted and never named. An uncontracted caller whose inferred service is hidden is left out too, and the declared service it calls counts it in hiddenDependents, even when you may list Pactos in the caller's namespace.

docs.title: Groups and repositories
docs.text:
Every inferred service carries workload.group, the group the cluster already puts its workload in. Pacto reads it from the workload's own labels, annotations and field managers, and the first rule with a claim wins:

Rule Read from Label argocd The argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id annotation or the argocd.argoproj.io/instance label; with neither, app.kubernetes.io/instance written by an argocd field manager Argo CD Application argocd/cart flux-kustomization The kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name and /namespace labels Flux Kustomization flux-system/apps flux-helmrelease The helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name and /namespace labels Flux HelmRelease observability/log-shipper helm The meta.helm.sh/release-name and /release-namespace annotations, unless a Flux HelmRelease claims the workload Helm release shop/exporter part-of The app.kubernetes.io/part-of label, in the workload's namespace part-of checkout in shop instance The app.kubernetes.io/instance label, in the workload's namespace instance cart in shop workload None of the above This workload only

The group carries rule, namespace, name, from (what Pacto read), label and key, rule/namespace/name, with the cluster first in a snapshot of several clusters. pacto fleet entities --group, group on pacto_fleet_entities and GET /api/fleet/entities?group take the key, which pacto fleet entity prints on its group key line. The dashboard shows the group and repository in the Workload section of the inferred service page, and the Services list shows the group under the image.

docs.title: Ambiguous groups
docs.text: When two claims of one rule name different owners, such as a tracking id and an instance label naming two Applications, Pacto merges nothing. The workload keeps its own workload group, reads Ungrouped and says in ambiguous which claims disagree. A lower rule never decides instead. The service carries SERVICE_GROUP_AMBIGUOUS, and one limitation per source counts those workloads. An Argo CD instance with no namespace that matches several Applications stays ungrouped the same way, and the reason says neither how many match nor where.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
workload.repositories lists at most five source repositories, each with url, path, from, namespace and kind; dropped names each one past five. An Argo CD Application gives spec.source.repoURL and each spec.sources[].repoURL, read as in Application argocd/cart spec.source.repoURL. A Flux Kustomization or HelmRelease gives the spec.url of the GitRepository it deploys from. Every grouping label is metadata the workload's writer controls, so a repository attaches only when the object's own status lists the workload: the Application's status.resources, the Kustomization's inventory or a HelmRelease that installs into the workload's namespace. Helm releases and label groups name no repository. Pacto drops the credentials, query and fragment of every URL and never writes to Git.

When a group names a repository Pacto cannot show, repositoryUnknown says why, for example:

  • Application payments/payments-api does not list this workload;
  • the source is Helm chart redis, not a Git repository;
  • the source is OCIRepository manifests, not a GitRepository;
  • no Application named cart was read;
  • Applications outside the namespaces this source reads;
  • the cluster does not serve Applications;
  • Pacto read only the first 10000 entries Kustomization flux-system/apps lists;
  • Pacto could not discover the Argo CD and Flux APIs.

A restricted view shows a repository only to a viewer whom Kubernetes lets list its kind, such as applications.argoproj.io or gitrepositories.source.toolkit.fluxcd.io, in its namespace, whether or not they can read Pactos there. Anyone else reads hidden by your permissions. A repositoryUnknown reason read from a GitOps object follows the same rule; one that names no object, such as the cluster does not serve Applications, shows to everyone. The group of a workload you can see always shows.

docs.title: What Pacto reads to group
docs.text: To group, Pacto reads only the labels and annotations in the table and the names of the workload's field managers. From Applications, Kustomizations, HelmReleases and GitRepositories it decodes only names, source fields, Argo CD status.resources and Flux inventory entries, never inline Helm values or substitutions. The source needs list on those four kinds and reports Argo CD, Flux and Helm as detected providers.

docs.title: Calls with no contract on one end
docs.text:
A runtime call between two workloads, from a source that reports calls, joins the graph as an inferred edge when at least one of its ends is an inferred service. The other end can be a declared service, another inferred service or an external system. The edge carries the call count, the first and last time it was seen and each source that saw it.

  • Inferred edges live in the snapshot's inferredRelationships, apart from relationships. They never satisfy a dependency, never count as a consumer in impact and never clear a gate or a promotion.
  • An inferred caller of a declared service is both an inferred edge and an uncontracted caller, so BlockerMissingContract still fires.
  • An end Pacto cannot resolve still raises OBSERVED_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED, and a call from a workload to itself is dropped. In a snapshot of several clusters, both k8s: ends of a call gain the cluster of the source that saw it.
  • When impact reads trace edges, an inferred caller of the changed service is never a consumer: the answer names it in an OBSERVED_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED limitation and stays partial.
  • pacto fleet graph and pacto_fleet_graph list these edges with their sources, and the dashboard graph draws them in the inferred style. The neighborhood shows them in the default expected and observed views.
  • A restricted view drops an edge whose inferred end it hides and counts that end once in hiddenDependents or hiddenDependencies, even when the same workload is also an uncontracted caller.

docs.title: When a contract takes over
docs.text:
When a Pacto resource's target runs as a workload Pacto showed as an inferred service, that workload stops being one. Its observed calls resolve to the declared service from then on, even when no source lists the workload. When the workload's creationTimestamp is more than 10 minutes earlier than that of every Pacto of the service that targets it, the cluster shows the workload ran with no contract first, and the snapshot records a replacement in replacements: from the inferred key, to the declared service, link: pacto-target, the target and at, when the Pacto was created. A Pacto created before its workload, or within 10 minutes after it as an install that applies the Pacto last does, or a missing creation time, records nothing. Pacto keeps no snapshot history, so a Pacto deleted and created again records a fresh replacement.

  • The service answer and page list replaces, the newest first. For 24 hours after at, an INFERRED_REPLACED attention item in the knowledge category names the replacement, and the Overview knowledge tile counts it.
  • pacto fleet get, pacto fleet graph, their MCP tools and the dashboard entity page answer an old inferred key with the declared service and replacedFrom. pacto impact --event and pacto_impact answer for the declared service and add SUBJECT_REPLACED. Other queries, the dashboard's impact event among them, answer not found for it.
  • When two declared services target the workload (counting a target of unknown cluster that names it), or a target's cluster is unknown in a snapshot of several clusters, nothing is merged: the workload stays inferred and the answer carries INFERRED_REPLACEMENT_AMBIGUOUS.
  • A restricted view shows a replacement only when it shows both services.
$ pacto fleet graph k8s:shop/Deployment/cart --k8s
k8s:shop/Deployment/cart was replaced by shop/cart 3m ago (linked by Pacto shop/cart target)
dependencies of shop/cart (1 node(s)):
    k8s:shop/StatefulSet/ledger (depth 1, inferred)
  cart -> k8s:shop/StatefulSet/ledger  inferred (observed by kernel, mesh)

docs.title: When a declaration replaces an inferred service
docs.text:
When a person declares a service from its inferred twin with pacto declare, the declared bundle's pacto.inferred.yaml names that twin in declaration.inferredFrom. The fleet then shows one service: the inferred service stops being listed, its observed calls as caller and as callee resolve to the declared service, and replacements records link: inferred-from with the revision, by (the person who signed it) and workload (what the twin showed, when a source reported it).

  • Signer rule. A hand-over needs a signature the fleet verified whose subject and issuer are those of the declaration's asker signing as a person. The installation signer rule must also allow that person (delivery.identities.signers). Only a registry read checks signatures, so a hand-over never happens in a --local fleet or from the Kubernetes source alone. Otherwise the twin stays inferred and INFERRED_LINK_IGNORED says why and names the fix.
  • A Pacto target wins. When a Pacto target runs as the workload, or may run as it (two targets name it, or its cluster is unknown), the Pacto target link decides and the declaration hands nothing over.
  • Ambiguity. When the declarations of two services name one workload, nothing merges: the workload stays inferred with INFERRED_REPLACEMENT_AMBIGUOUS. In a fleet of several clusters, a claim with no cluster merges nothing either.
  • One claim per service. Only the newest declared revision of a service counts. A newer declaration that names no workload retracts the claim; a CI publish without a declaration keeps it. A newer revision whose inferred record Pacto cannot read may have retracted it, so the claim hands nothing over. A service with Kubernetes targets claims a workload only in a namespace where one of its targets runs.
  • Attention. Each hand-over raises an INFERRED_REPLACED item in the knowledge category that asks you to confirm the workload is the service. It carries no time and stays while the declaration holds.
  • Fields. pacto fleet get, pacto fleet explain, their MCP tools, the TUI and the dashboard read fields for a service whose current revision carries a declaration or that replaced an inferred service through one: each field of the current revision as declared, accepted (with by, who signed the accepted declaration), attested or inferred, with its source and asOf. A proposed range stays unknown beside proposed. Inferred fields never clear a gate.
  • Restricted viewers. A viewer sees the replacement only when they may see both the declared service and the workload. Otherwise replacesHidden counts it and no workload key, image, port, probe or cluster source reaches them.
  • Dashboard. The service page keeps the Replaces line and adds one closed fold, Where the values come from; see The service page.
$ pacto fleet get invoices
Service: invoices
Declared by ana@acme.com from inferred k8s:billing/Deployment/invoices (revision invoices@sha256:...)
Owner: billing
Fields:
  owner         billing    declared
  ledger range  ^2.3.0     accepted by ana@acme.com
  audit range   unknown    proposed ^1.4.0 (fleet, partial)

docs.title: Detected providers
docs.text: This page describes the providers Pacto detected: the systems each source read evidence from, what Pacto uses each one for and how sure it is.

docs.title: The rows
docs.text:
pacto fleet providers, GET /api/fleet/providers, the providers field of pacto_fleet_status and the Detected providers block on Data sources show the same rows. Each row carries id, source, cluster, name, evidence, usedFor, status and limitations, plus objects and objectsTotal when the evidence names objects. The evidence never names a namespace.

Each cluster reports at least two rows, from two sources: the Kubernetes source (such as prod) and its workload source (prod-workloads).

  • Pacto CRD: served (pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1) or not installed. Pacto uses it for declared targets.
  • Kubernetes workloads: how many Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets and CronJobs the workload source listed. A kind it could not list is unreadable, never 0, and one it listed in only some namespaces reads at least 12 Deployments (some unreadable). Pacto uses it for inferred services.
  • Argo CD and Flux: when the cluster serves their APIs, how many Applications (Argo CD) or Kustomizations, HelmReleases and GitRepositories (Flux) the workload source listed, such as 1 GitRepository, 1 HelmRelease or no Applications found. A kind it could not list is unreadable and the row partial. Pacto uses them for service grouping and repository provenance; see Groups and repositories. A cluster that serves neither shows no row.
  • Helm: how many Helm releases group at least one workload. Pacto reads no release Secret, so it uses them for service grouping only. When the workload read was cut short or a workload kind was unreadable, the row is partial.
  • Promotion: one row per promoter the installation names in its fingerprints and the cluster shows, by the API group of a CRD it serves or a label or annotation on a workload, such as promotion owned by Kargo (API group kargo.akuity.io served). Delivery reads promotion owned by <product> to know another tool promotes. When discovery fails, a promoter named only by its CRD shows a partial row that says Pacto could not check. A restricted view lists only the workloads you may list.
  • Reporting adapters: one row per adapter, signed or unsigned, that reports provisioning in the target-state file or signed envelopes, and one per producer the Evidence Server's trust config allows to report ResourceProvisioned or ResourceUsage, from the additive adapters list of its GET /api/evidence/v1/producers. Trust config rows show to every viewer, since that endpoint lists them to anyone.
$ pacto fleet providers --k8s
PROVIDER              EVIDENCE                                             USED FOR
Pacto CRD             served (pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1)                 declared targets
Kubernetes workloads  412 Deployments, DaemonSets unreadable, 31 CronJobs  inferred services (partial: source prod-workloads could not list DaemonSets in any namespace: forbidden)

With two or more clusters the table gains a leading CLUSTER column. With no row and no Kubernetes source it prints No providers detected: this view reads no Kubernetes cluster (add --k8s). When no source reported a service or a target, the answer's completeness is empty, so the CLI also prints warning: answer is empty on stderr while it still lists the rows.

A row can carry offers: Pacto integrations that fit the detected provider, each with an id, a one-sentence text and a setup guide in doc. Pacto installs nothing. The Argo CD row offers "Gate every Argo CD sync with one repo-server plugin" (setup), which the CLI prints as an offer: line under the row and the dashboard as a Set up link.

docs.title: Fingerprints
docs.text:
--fingerprints <file> on pacto fleet, pacto dashboard, pacto mcp and the other fleet commands, and the chart's fingerprints value, name the workload managers and promoters an installation runs. Each entry names a product and exactly one matcher: a fieldManager, label or annotation for a manager, and a crd (<plural>.<group>), label or annotation for a promoter. A file holds at most 64 entries. Pacto names no product in code: the chart's three defaults are entries of an open list, and a private IDP is one more. A promoter entry can also carry an offer (an id, a text that starts with "Gate every " and an https doc), which its row lists under offers; the Kargo entries offer "Gate every Kargo promotion with one shared AnalysisTemplate" (setup).

managers:
  - product: Internal Deployer
    fieldManager: acme-deployer
promoters:
  - product: Kargo
    crd: stages.kargo.akuity.io
    offer:
      id: kargo-analysis-template
      text: Gate every Kargo promotion with one shared AnalysisTemplate
      doc: https://pacto.run/latest/integrations/kubernetes/gitops-kargo/#kargo
  - product: Kargo
    crd: warehouses.kargo.akuity.io
    offer:
      id: kargo-analysis-template
      text: Gate every Kargo promotion with one shared AnalysisTemplate
      doc: https://pacto.run/latest/integrations/kubernetes/gitops-kargo/#kargo
  - product: Argo CD Image Updater
    annotation: argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/image-list
  - product: Flux ImageUpdateAutomation
    crd: imageupdateautomations.image.toolkit.fluxcd.io
  - product: Acme Release Train
    annotation: release-train.acme.example/stage

A workload one of the managers applies reads external: <product> in the Stage applier verdict.

docs.title: Registry rows
docs.text:
An OCI source adds one Registry <host> row per registry host it read a contract from. Pacto probes each host once per process, with the first contract it resolved there, and keeps the answer until the process restarts.

  • Evidence: what the probe saw, such as no Referrers, no _catalog or Referrers, _catalog.
  • Used for: native-referrers or write-once-tags, then index-listed-by-catalog or index-listed-by-tag. The CLI prints them with spaces.
  • Details: mode: referrers=<mode> listing=<mode>, the auth scheme of the /v2/ challenge, artifactType: not checked (read-only probe) and cosign signatures: not checked. Every detail says what was checked or that it was not. asOf is when the probe ran.
$ pacto fleet providers --oci oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/postgresql:17.0.0
PROVIDER          EVIDENCE                   USED FOR
Registry ghcr.io  no Referrers, no _catalog  write once tags, index listed by tag

The _catalog answer depends on the credentials the probe sends. The output above is anonymous. With a GHCR token, which Pacto finds through gh auth, GHCR serves _catalog with every public repository on ghcr.io, and the row reads no Referrers, _catalog and write once tags, index listed by catalog.

A probe that cannot tell (a network error, a server error, an answer that is not an OCI index) is never a mode. The row then reads capabilities unknown, is partial and carries REGISTRY_PROBE_FAILED. A host whose contracts all failed to resolve has no row. A registry row never changes the answer's completeness. A restricted view drops a registry row when it hides every service read from that host. The delivery records reference explains what each mode means for records.

docs.title: Detected rows
docs.text:
With --detected, the rows the operator detected in a cluster join from a source of kind detection: Registry, Cloud, Sign-in, Exposure, Metrics and Nodes. Each carries five more fields:

Field Meaning provenance Always inferred asOf When the operator read it; older than 15 minutes is stale hint A command to review, set only when one candidate holds most namespaces. MCP omits it details Other candidates or facts, at most 5 scope cluster for a row read cluster-wide

Detected rows list after the rows a source reported. A detected row never clears a gate and never changes the answer's completeness. An entry the operator could not read is unavailable with a DETECTION_<KIND>_UNKNOWN limitation, and a partial one carries DETECTION_<KIND>_PARTIAL. A row naming a cluster no Kubernetes source of the snapshot reads carries DETECTION_CLUSTER_MISMATCH, and its source reads stale. A restricted view clears the evidence, hint and details of a row that names a namespace you cannot read, or of a cluster-wide row when you cannot read the cluster scope.

docs.title: Not read and not installed
docs.text:
A cluster Pacto could not reach contributes no row. Every surface names its source as not read with the error, such as prod not read (connection refused). Only a cluster that answered without the Pacto CRD says not installed.

A row is never healthier than its source. A row that is not available always carries a limitation that says why. PROVIDER_SOURCE_DEGRADED says so when the source itself is partial or stale, when the source marked the row partial without a reason or when a restricted view hid every other reason.

docs.title: Restricted views
docs.text: A restricted view keeps every row except a registry row whose every service it hides. Objects in namespaces you cannot read and cluster-scoped objects are hidden, as are limitations that name them, and so is the name of a cluster where you can see no target. A count stays only where you can read the namespace and list its kind there; a Helm release needs every workload kind. The rest becomes one hidden total, such as 12 Deployments (+30 hidden by your permissions). Hiding objects or counts never makes the answer partial.

docs.title: Operational graph reference
docs.text: This page describes the sources of the operational graph, the target-state file format, what each query returns, how owners are keyed and how services are grouped by domain.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
The graph is assembled from sources, each contributing the revisions and targets it can observe right now. The dashboard lists them as Data sources. A source is where the graph reads records from. A collector produces the compliance evidence that a source carries.

  • Local bundles (--local): the revision a developer is editing. The scan defaults to the working directory, descends 8 levels and skips hidden directories, node_modules and vendor. A directory the operating system refuses is reported as a gap and stepped over.
  • A contract root and its closure (--root <path|oci://ref>): the root you name plus every revision it declares, followed transitively. It is the same discovery pacto mcp --root freezes into a catalog, through the same resolver. Roots and dependencies that fail to resolve stay visible as limitations.
  • Contracts in OCI (--oci <ref>): the published revision catalogue, resolved cache-first so a pulled ref works offline.
  • Local OCI cache (--cache): every bundle already pulled to disk. Opt-in, because on a machine that has pulled contracts for months the cache holds everything anyone ever fetched. That is a useful offline baseline but a poor picture of the running fleet.
  • Live Kubernetes (--k8s [--namespace]): Pacto CRs read from a running cluster: which revision runs in which target, and its operator-computed compliance, findings, coverage and observed runtime. The operator also reports runtime calls no contract declares and callers with no contract, which join the graph as observed. It reports only undeclared calls, so this observation alone leaves every declared edge insufficient. The source id is the cluster UID when the source can read the kube-system namespace, otherwise the context name. With more than one cluster, target keys gain a cluster component; see Clusters and target keys. The externals the operator reads from a workload's pod spec (status.externals) join as inferred edges to external systems. A Pacto whose status predates them, reports incomplete coverage or is stale adds EXTERNALS_UNREPORTED to its target, and the external answers that consume it read partial.
  • Kubernetes workloads (--k8s): workloads no Pacto resource targets join as inferred services, declaration: inferred. A runtime call with an inferred service on one end joins as an inferred edge in inferredRelationships, and a Pacto target that takes over one records a replacement in replacements. Both report detected providers.
  • Operator detection (--detected k8s:<namespace>/<name> or a file, PACTO_DASHBOARD_DETECTED for pacto dashboard): what the operator detected in a cluster, read from its <release>-detected ConfigMap as source kind detection. It adds only provider rows, each with provenance: inferred. The source is advisory: a missing, unreadable, foreign or future-dated ConfigMap leaves it unavailable with the reason and one older than 15 minutes leaves it stale. Neither makes the answer partial.
  • Ingested external evidence (--evidence-url <url>): a running Evidence Server's read-only contribution over HTTP, exposing a remote environment's signed EvidenceSet reports as operational targets.
  • Target snapshots (--target-snapshot <oci://ref>, repeatable): the signed snapshot each cluster's operator publishes to <registry>/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid>, read with registry access and no kubeconfig. A repository reads every cluster-* tag (at most 32); a tag or digest pins one cluster. Each snapshot becomes up to three sources with the same cluster: targets-<uid> of kind target-snapshot (its Pacto resources), targets-<uid>-workloads of kind kubernetes-workloads (its inferred services) and targets-<uid>-evidence of kind evidence-http (its Evidence Server's targets). pacto impact and pacto ci derive the repository from the change's oci:// ref; see Where consumers come from and Target snapshots.
  • Offline target-state fixtures (--target-state): an unsigned demo and test adapter for supplying targets without a cluster.
  • Offline trace exports (--traces, or --trace-source NAME=PATH on pacto dashboard only): observed dependency edges. Pacto reads trace files only and ships no live OTLP receiver on ports 4317 or 4318. Run a Collector you own and point a source at the file it exports.
  • Mira (--mira-source <url>, or PACTO_DASHBOARD_MIRA_SOURCES for pacto dashboard): the calls between services that a Mira node saw in its last 15 minutes of traces, read from its service map as observed edges of source kind mira. Like the operator, Mira sees only part of the traffic, so a declared edge it did not see stays insufficient. A failed read leaves the source unavailable; a truncated or empty map, or calls Pacto cannot attribute to a named service, leave it partial.

pacto fleet and pacto impact read every source flag above. pacto mcp --fleet reads all but --root, which on pacto mcp selects a frozen catalog server and takes no other mode. Two are narrower: impact takes a single --traces file, and --trace-source is pacto dashboard only.

docs.title: Target snapshots
docs.text:
Snapshot sources carry:

Field or code Meaning ref The snapshot read, pinned as <repository>@<digest> signer The trust entry that verified it: its name, or key:<fingerprint>; empty when unverified. Never the publisher the payload claims publisher Who the payload says published it, such as the operator's ServiceAccount; a claim, with control characters dropped like the publisher's limitations cluster The cluster the snapshot describes, its id the kube-system UID lastSuccessfulSync The snapshot's asOf TARGET_SNAPSHOT_UNVERIFIED Read with no delivery trust config (--delivery-trust or $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST); the source is partial TARGET_SNAPSHOT_UNSCOPED Verified only by a key whose streams do not name the cluster's UID (a bare PEM included); partial TARGET_SNAPSHOT_STALE Its asOf is more than 15 minutes old; stale TARGET_SNAPSHOT_INVALID Missing (a pinned tag), a bad signature, a cluster other than its tag, an unknown predicate or an asOf in the future; not used, unavailable TARGET_SNAPSHOT_BOUND More than 32 cluster tags, a snapshot over 8 MiB or the 20 second read timeout; partial or unavailable TARGET_SNAPSHOT_SCOPED The publishing operator watches only the namespaces the message names (controller.watchNamespaces), so any other namespace is unknown; partial Text line pacto fleet status and pacto fleet snapshot print one per source, such as Source targets-<uid> (target-snapshot): available, ref <repository>@<digest>, signed by <signer>, asOf <time>; unverified replaces the signer when no trust entry verified it, and a source that is not available ends with its reason

docs.title: Observed calls under a restricted view
docs.text:
A declared edge any source saw is matched. A restricted view hides each caller with no namespace, from any source, and each unresolved observed name, counting them in hiddenDependents and one OBSERVED_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED limitation per source.

  • A declared external dependency is matched when an observed call maps to the same identity through the external catalog.
  • Only a name that matches more than one service, or that is neither a service nor an external system, is unresolved.
  • An observed or inferred edge to an external system follows its caller: when the caller is hidden, the edge is dropped and counted among the external system's hidden consumers.
  • An inferred edge whose inferred end is hidden is dropped and that end counted once, and a replacement shows only when both of its services do.

docs.title: Clusters under a restricted view
docs.text: Limitation Raised when CLUSTER_HIDDEN The view hides one cluster: you may read no namespace there, its review failed or Pacto cannot review you there (Multi-cluster). Its source is the cluster id; the answer is partial CLUSTER_FILTER_UNKNOWN A list filtered by a cluster id that no cluster of the answer has, such as a display name or a retired cluster, so its empty list says nothing about it. Completeness is unchanged

docs.title: What a target-state fixture looks like
docs.text:
--target-state is the only source you author yourself: a single YAML or JSON document with schemaVersion: pacto.dev/fleet-targets/v1, or pacto.dev/fleet-targets/v2 when it also carries provisioning reports. Pacto rejects a second --- document, an unknown field, provisioning in a v1 file or any other schemaVersion.

schemaVersion: pacto.dev/fleet-targets/v1
cluster:                             # optional: the cluster of every target
  id: 9f1c4e2a-5b7d-4c1e-8a3f-2d6b0e9c7a41   # required in the block: kube-system UID
  name: eu-prod                      # a display name
targets:
  - service: orders-service          # required: the service this target runs
    name: commerce/orders-service    # required: unique within the scope
    scope: production-eu             # the environment, for example a cluster
    kind: kubernetes-workload        # what sort of target it is
    labels: { env: production, region: eu }
    requestedRef: oci://ghcr.io/acme/orders-service:1.2.0
    resolvedRef: oci://ghcr.io/acme/orders-service:1.2.0
    digest: sha256:…
    compliance: NonCompliant
    coverage: { evaluated: 5, required: 5 }
    evidenceAt: 2026-07-29T09:40:00Z     # when the evidence was gathered
    reconciledAt: 2026-07-29T09:41:00Z   # when the target was last reconciled
    observedRuntime: { replicas: 3 }     # free-form; surfaced as a bounded preview
    findings:
      - code: STATELESS_PERSISTENT_CONFLICT   # required within a finding
        severity: error
        category: RuntimeDrift
        subjectKind: state
        subjectName: orders-db
        message: declared stateless but the observed workload mounts a volume
state:                               # optional: the source's own health
  status: available
  message: ""

Only service and name are required. Omit evidenceAt to model a target the collector could not observe. A file may declare at most 5000 targets. An entry that fails validation is skipped with a SOURCE_RECORD_INVALID limitation and the rest is kept. A failure of the file drops the whole source with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and marks the snapshot partial. Three fields are closed sets:

  • compliance: Compliant, NonCompliant, Unknown, Invalid, Reference, NotEvaluated, Warning or empty
  • findings[].severity: error, warning, info, unknown or empty
  • state.status: available, stale, partial or unavailable. A value outside this set is silently coerced to available, so a typo here reads as a healthy source

A malformed fixture is reported the same way as a missing one

Both produce exactly SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the output omits the parse error, even with -v. If the source drops and the path is right, suspect the file: check schemaVersion first, then field spelling and the closed sets above.

A v2 file adds provisioning, one entry per report about a resource a consumer revision asked for:

schemaVersion: pacto.dev/fleet-targets/v2
provisioning:
  - service: catalog-service       # required: the consumer
    digest: sha256:32b570087a9cd70b16772e9cb5d3cbc1a6aea6fc31b1c021d9d848c10424b518  # required
    kind: configuration            # required: configuration or dependency
    name: database                 # required: the consumer's entry
    environment: production
    provider: platform-db          # a lowercase slug
    externalRef: databases/catalog-production
    phase: Ready                   # Requested, Provisioning, Ready, Failed or Deleting
    outcome: Observed              # the default; any other outcome carries no phase
    producer: platform-adapter
    observedAt: 2026-11-06T09:00:00Z

The file is unsigned, so every surface shows its reports as unverified. See Provisioning status for how reports join the graph.

examples/demo/fleet-targets.yaml is the complete fixture the live demo runs on.

docs.title: Query semantics
docs.text:
The read model answers five kinds of question, each a pure operation with no I/O. A single snapshot serves concurrent queries.

Query Answers search Which logical services match this filter (owner, label, status, compliance, capability, dependency, readiness). Bounded and deterministically ordered. get Everything about one service (its owner, revisions, targets, declared dependencies, dependents, tools and skills, and the inferred services it replaces) or one target. The key of a replaced inferred service answers with the service that replaced it and replacedFrom, as does graph. graph Traverse dependencies or dependents from a service, direct or transitive, cycle-safe, with unresolved edges surfaced. Resolved configuration references count as dependencies. The CLI and MCP graph also follow observed-only edges, and each node's provenance (declared, observed, declared+observed or inferred) says how the edge that first reached it was known. inferred has two producers: an external system read from configuration, and a runtime call one of whose ends is an inferred service. Inferred edges are listed in edges and never count as dependencies or consumers. Rooted at a revision or target, a dependencies traversal takes its first step over that revision's declared edges only; deeper steps are service-level and include observed edges. status What needs attention, in the attention categories. With no category selected it reports every category. total counts every match and truncated says the limit cut the list. explain Deterministic, structured reasons for a subject's state. An agent can turn them into prose; Pacto itself embeds no model.

Two more operations sit beside the queries: snapshot emits the whole read model and reconcile compares declared dependencies with observed ones. Every answer carries a meta envelope, here from pacto fleet search --output-format json with an unreachable OCI source:

{
  "meta": {
    "schemaVersion": "pacto.dev/fleet/v1",
    "snapshotId": "sha256:c81df8fd572ecaa7c884968e728daff5b47c40b8e8c5cbcf1926c19740db95a9",
    "asOf": "2026-07-29T10:00:00Z",
    "completeness": "partial",
    "limitations": [
      { "code": "SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE", "source": "oci",
        "message": "source oci is unavailable; its records are missing from this snapshot" }
    ],
    "sources": [
      { "id": "local", "kind": "local", "status": "available",
        "lastSuccessfulSync": "2026-07-29T10:00:00Z",
        "revisionCount": 25, "targetCount": 0 },
      { "id": "oci", "kind": "oci", "status": "unavailable",
        "error": { "code": "UNAVAILABLE", "message": "the source is unavailable" },
        "revisionCount": 0, "targetCount": 0 }
    ]
  },
  "total": 1,
  "count": 1,
  "services": [
    { "key": "payments-service", "name": "payments-service",
      "owner": { "team": "payments" }, "status": "NotEvaluated",
      "revisionCount": 6, "targetCount": 0, "sources": ["local"] }
  ]
}

schemaVersion is the compatibility contract to branch on and snapshotId the content digest that proves two answers share one system view. count is the rows on this page and total the whole matched population. Match on key, because name can repeat across domains. A bounded preview nested in a get answer omits total when its walk was bounded: an absent total means "we stopped counting".

Beside the rows, answers carry tallies over the complete matched population, computed before paging. The tallies reference lists them, the knowledge-gap filters and the attention categories.

get, graph and explain name a single subject and carry no envelope, so no completeness: a missing subject is a failure. pacto fleet get ghost exits 1 with service "ghost" not found in the fleet snapshot on stderr. Read completeness from search before you treat a miss as an absence.

docs.title: Where a service runs
docs.text: placement Detail Read from A service's detail: pacto fleet entity service <key>, pacto_fleet_entity and the dashboard's service page. Targets cover services delivered without Pacto delivery too Groups The union of the environments the current revision (currentRevision) declares and the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/environment labels the targets report; no label or conflicting labels form one unlabelled group Order Alphabetical (natural order), unlabelled last; never a promotion order, which delivery status gives Declaration declaration: the current revision's entry with its values check, lifetime (not-declared when absent), expires, owner and expired, inferred against asOf. Absent for an environment only targets report Owner owner with provenance: declared on the environment, inferred from the service owner, or unknown with a reason Counts targets (observed), then declared, notDeclared and unknown: whether the revision each target runs declares that environment. targetsComplete is false, with targetsReason, when you may not see every target Provisioning provisioning, a tally by phase of the statuses of the service's uses there (consumedOfferings, including reported uses of providers with no offering); provisioningTracked is false, with provisioningReason, when no provider is asked about it there, so the tally is never a zero. When a provider you may not see may provision there, the reason says its status is unknown Revisions The newest 8 distinct revisions, with revisionsTotal and revisionsTruncated Differences differences: each value the declared environments disagree on, by configuration and path, with differencesTotal, or differencesError saying why they are unknown. pacto explain --environments computes the same list Restricted Only targets, revisions and provisioning your view may see count; on a partial answer the CLI heading reads "Environments (targets Pacto can see)" changes Detail Items Every declared change across the revisions the answer holds, newest first in version order. kind is owner, domain, offering, dependency, lifecycle, environment or finding (a validation finding that appeared or resolved); subject names the dependency, environment or finding; change is present, added, removed or changed, with fields, from and to. revision is the first held revision that shows the change and previous the one it was compared with; provenance is declared and source is contract or validation Times A change carries a time only in reached: per Stage you may read, when its revision first arrived there (at), with the record, verified, fromStatus and the recorded impact verdict. It is read from delivery records as you when asked (--reached, reached, ?reached=true); times says whether they were read: not-read, read, partial (with timesUnreadable) or hidden, with timesReason Gaps gaps counts revisions whose contract could not be read; no change is reported across them Completeness partial when your view or a source holds only some of the service's revisions, or when two versions are compared: no source lists every version, so a change is placed between the versions held

docs.title: Configuration-reference consumers
docs.text:
A service that takes a configuration schema from another contract by ref consumes that contract. Once the reference resolves to a revision in the snapshot, by digest or through the consumer's pacto.lock, the edge counts like a declared dependency: graph traversal, dependents, the neighborhood and hidden counts include it, and impact judges the consumer. A neighborhood edge carries the relation configuration_reference and no declared-against-observed comparison, because a reference never produces runtime calls. Policy references stay out: a policy checks the consumer's own contract.

The fleet validates configuration references against the revisions it holds. A reference it cannot place reads CONFIG_REF_UNVERIFIED, so a missing provider never makes a revision invalid and never passes its values. A relationship carries the provider's service lifecycle as providerLifecycle.

docs.title: Resolved dependencies and accepted ranges
docs.text:
A declared dependency has two separate answers. resolved: true means a service with that name exists in the fleet. rangeStatus says whether the version the fleet holds satisfies the consumer's compatibility range:

rangeStatus Meaning satisfied Every revision of the provider in the fleet (or the one pacto.lock pins) is inside the range. unsatisfied None is. status reports it as DEPENDENCY_RANGE_UNSATISFIED in the out-of-range category. unknown The range or a version cannot be read as semver, the provider has no revision in the fleet, or its revisions disagree. With rangeReason: INFERRED_PROVIDER the provider is an inferred contract or a revision only the operator signed, which no range is checked against and fleet versions never names latestCompatible; a view that hides the provider blanks both fields. absent The dependency declares no range, is unresolved or joins an external system without a ref, which is never ranged.

A consumer that asks for ledger ^2.0.0 while the fleet holds ledger 1.6.2 is resolved and unsatisfied.

A dependency that declares requires also carries guaranteeStatus, checked against every provider revision it can reach: the one pacto.lock pins, or else every revision inside its range.

guaranteeStatus Meaning met Every revision it can reach offers what it requires. unmet None does. unmet lists what the newest one refuses. unknown The provider is not in the fleet, no revision is in range, its revisions disagree or the caller cannot see it. guaranteeReason says which. absent The dependency requires nothing.

deprecatedInterfaces lists each deprecated interface of the newest provider revision the dependency reaches, with its deprecated, sunset and successor. The dashboard shows both on the dependency, on the consumer's page and on the provider's.

docs.title: Ownership and the canonical owner key
docs.text:
The graph aggregates and navigates by a canonical owner key namespaced by which field named the owner, written kind:name:

  1. If owner has team → team:<team>
  2. If owner has dri (no team) → dri:<dri>
  3. If owner has only contacts → no canonical key. The service still counts as owned, but has no owner to rank or link to.

The namespace is part of the identity, so team:payments and dri:payments are different owners, and only the name is shown on screen, with a Team / DRI badge where two owners would otherwise be indistinguishable. The free-text owner filter searches team, DRI and contacts and can match several owners.

search and get return owner in one shape, the contract's own {team, dri, contacts}, and leave it out when no contract declares one. The owner comes from the newest revision that declares one. A service known only from Kubernetes takes the owner the operator read from the running contract (status.contract.owner). A service counts as unowned, in the ownership tally and in attention, only when no revision declares an owner and no source reports one. A service with no owner claim whose contract Pacto cannot read counts as unknown instead: the dashboard labels it Owner unknown and never No declared owner.

get also returns where the owner comes from; see Who may set a service owner:

Field or code Meaning ownerProvenance declared (a revision's pacto.yaml), attested, declared-via-target (the running contract the operator read) or inferred, in that precedence ownerSource For attested only: the file and line, the commit and the CI identity that signed it, such as CODEOWNERS:7 at a1b2c3, signed by github.com/acme/invoices/.github/workflows/ci.yml provenance.signature.signerRepository, signerCommit On a revision, the repository and commit an accepted CI signer's certificate names provenance.ownerRight On a revision, the owner rule's verdict on the owner it sets: allowed, code and message OWNER_CONFLICT Also raised when attested revisions of the service were signed from different repositories; no attested owner is set OWNER_DECLARATION_REFUSED A registry revision sets an owner its signer may not set, so its owner is not used OWNER_DECLARATION_UNVERIFIED A registry revision sets an owner the rule could not check (no verified signer or policy, or no earlier owner read), so its owner is not used and the answer is partial

docs.title: Business domains
docs.text:
A service's business domain is the service.domain of its newest revision by semver that is valid. An older revision that declares another domain is a move. When no revision declares a domain, the service takes the domain the operator read from the contract each target runs (status.contract.domain), as it does for owners. A value that is not a lowercase slug is never a domain.

Each service is in exactly one group:

  • a named domain;
  • No domain, when a valid revision or the operator says the contract declares none;
  • Domain unknown, when Pacto cannot tell. Pacto has no valid revision of the service and no source that reports the domain, such as an operator that writes a status.statusFormat below 2, or the operators observing its targets report different domains. A disagreement also raises a DOMAIN_CONFLICT limitation.

No domain and Domain unknown are listed and counted like any other domain and never read as healthy. The API filters them with businessDomain=(none) and businessDomain=(unknown), and marks an unknown domain with businessDomainUnknown. A contract revision's own row shows the domain that revision declares, while the filter groups it by its service's domain. Domains are returned only to a query that asks for the domain kind.

The registry path in the service key, such as ghcr.io/acme, is a different value: domain in the API and Registry on the dashboard.

docs.title: Golden paths
docs.text: See the golden paths reference.

docs.title: Platform offerings
docs.text:
See the platform offerings reference and offering availability and lifecycle.

AvailabilityState Meaning available Fresh provider targets serve and no consumer reports the provider unreachable. degraded Some provider targets report INTERFACE_ABSENT, or some consumer targets cannot reach it. unavailable Every fresh provider target serves none of its interfaces, or with no fresh provider target every consumer target that declares it cannot reach it. unknown Targets are hidden, a target source is incomplete, no fresh evidence exists or no interface was seen answering. Limitation Raised when SUCCESSOR_UNRESOLVED A provider's declared successor names no revision in the fleet. HIDDEN_PROVIDERS An offering event has providers the viewer cannot see. OFFERING_NOT_IN_FLEET No visible service provides the offering an event names. A service's consumedOfferings item Detail Rule Every declared dependency or configuration reference on a provider with an offering, plus one on a provider with no offering once a provider reports on it (offering empty) providerOwner Who owns the provider, as its offering page names it providerAvailability Whether the provider answers where it runs; separate from the resource's phase requested On the configuration_reference row only: each entry, configuration, provider revision and values the current revision declares, with provenance: declared; requestedTruncated when the configuration preview was cut consumption On every use that provisions: one entry, state: not-reported, provenance: observed and a reason. A policy reference carries none hiddenProviders On the service detail: at least this many resources come from providers you may not see, counted from the service's own contract and reports and never named; omitted at zero

The capability filter and facet count each declared capability by its key: health, metrics or, for an extension, its ref, such as acme.io/cost.

docs.title: External systems
docs.text:
A ref-less external: true dependency joins an entity of kind external, one per canonical identity. The external catalog reference covers identities, the join order and catalogs.

Surface Behaviour Relationship toExternal names the identity and resolved stays false, because no fleet service delivers it. It never gets resolvedRevision and never counts in impact, dependents or delivery. Only a dependency whose ref names pacto-inferred/<identity> gets rangeStatus: unknown with rangeReason: INFERRED_PROVIDER Provider provider on the record holds the system's inferred contract: repository, revisions (operator-signed first, each group newest first, each with version, digest, ref, surface and signature), revisionsTotal, and rangeStatus: unknown with rangeReason: INFERRED_PROVIDER. A restricted view that hides any source or consumer drops every surface. A contract under pacto-inferred whose service.external disagrees with its path is attached nowhere and raises INFERRED_IDENTITY_MISMATCH Attention One INFERRED_PROVIDER item in the knowledge category per inferred contract that ranges check against, counting only visible consumers Snapshot externals, one record per identity, and externalCatalogs, the catalogs used with digest, origin, copy, signature and reason; every answer's meta repeats externalCatalogs Record key, label, class, aliases, sources (one per consumer and dependency position, each with provenance, match and superseded when a newer consumer revision no longer declares it), sourcesTotal, catalog (origin, digest and entry; absent when no entry classifies it), joinedBy (identity, catalog-alias, host or normalized-name), consumers, consumersTotal, hiddenConsumers Entities --kind external (MCP kind: external) lists them, --class keeps one class; the default listing leaves them out Get pacto fleet get external:<identity> and pacto_fleet_get with service: external:<identity> Search A search on text alone, first page, adds up to 20 matching externals, by identity, label or alias, with externalsTotal; any other filter or a later page lists none Explain EXTERNAL_DECLARED per source, then EXTERNAL_CATALOG_MATCH, EXTERNAL_UNCLASSIFIED (joined by identity or host) or EXTERNAL_NAME_ONLY, EXTERNAL_SOURCES_TRUNCATED when consumers are cut or hidden, and EXTERNAL_CAP when folded; status is always Unknown Graph Rooted at external:<identity>, it walks the consumers and their dependents (an unset direction means dependents); an explicit direction: dependencies is an invalid query Neighborhood External systems are leaves beside the services that declare them; focusing one shows its consumers Overview externals and hiddenExternals Repository An external system a revision's inferred record names joins as an inferred edge whose sources have kind repository and name that revision, never as a service dependency, impact or gate input Cap An answer that names more than 200 external systems folds the rest into other-egress and is partial with EXTERNAL_CAP; see the cap

docs.title: Operational graph tallies
docs.text: This page lists the counts the operational graph returns beside its rows: the overview summary, the entity list aggregate, the owner and domain summaries and the attention categories. Organizational health and knowledge explains what they mean. Every tally is a partition with its own unknown bucket, and Pacto computes no score from them. Under a restricted view each tally counts only what your view sees.

docs.title: Entity list aggregate
docs.text:
The dashboard's entity list and the TUI carry an aggregate over the complete matched population, computed before paging:
