A Helm chart's values.schema.json may be reused as a configurations[].schema only when the named scope has the same semantic shape as those values, or when an explicit mapping exists between them. Composition patterns explains whether the service or the platform owns that schema.

docs.title: What the Kubernetes collector validates
docs.text: The Kubernetes integration binds a configurations[] scope to a runtime object only when the Pacto CR sets spec.target.configBindings. When it does, it validates the decoded content of the bound ConfigMap key against the declared schema, or against the referenced schema for a configuration that takes its schema by ref. It validates the whole decoded JSON or YAML value at that key. For a Secret it verifies only that the object exists and never reads Secret values. A required scope whose bound object or key is confirmed absent is a violation (NonCompliant), and so is a schema mismatch on observed content. A binding that the operator cannot observe is insufficient evidence (Unknown).

docs.title: policies
docs.text:
Defines or references policy constraints for the contract. Optional: a service with no policy can omit this section. A policy is a JSON Schema that validates the contract itself, so an organization can state its standards as rules. Examples: require a health capability, require a declared owner, restrict interface visibility or require a readiness gate.

When present, each entry must have a name and either schema or ref specified.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Non-empty identifier for the policy entry schema string Conditional Non-empty. Path to a JSON Schema file in the bundle (convention: policy/schema.json). Required if ref is not set ref string Conditional Non-empty. OCI or local reference to another Pacto contract. If the referenced contract declares policies[], those schemas are used directly; otherwise Pacto uses the fixed path policy/schema.json. Required if schema is not set target string No What the policy is evaluated against. contract is the only accepted value and the default. The field exists so a later release can add a second target without a breaking change. Any other value fails Layer 1 with SCHEMA_VIOLATION

schema and ref are mutually exclusive. An entry defines its policy inline or references an external one.

docs.title: Policy as a contract author
docs.text:
To define a policy, create a JSON Schema that describes constraints on pacto.yaml contracts and place it at policy/schema.json in the bundle:

# pacto.yaml: a policy contract
pactoVersion: "2.0"
service:
  name: platform-policy
  version: 1.0.0
  owner:
    team: platform
policies:
  - name: platform-policy
    schema: policy/schema.json

Example policy schema (policy/schema.json) requiring every contract to declare an owner:

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["service"],
  "properties": {
    "service": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["owner"]
    }
  }
}

A policy schema validates the contract itself, so it can require any contract field, for example a health capability through a capabilities contains rule or a readiness gate. A contract is always checked against its own inline schema policies, so this policy contract satisfies the rule above by declaring service.owner.

docs.title: Policy as a contract consumer
docs.text:
To adopt a policy, reference the policy contract via OCI:

policies:
  - name: platform-policy
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/platform-policy-pacto:1.0.0

The ref row above lists the schemas a referenced contract contributes. Layer 3 lists the commands that walk that chain and what happens when a link in it fails to fetch.

The policies apply to the contract that references them. pacto validate --closure also checks every contract in its dependency closure against them; see Dependency closure.

Tip

Like configurations[].ref, policy references create reference edges in the dependency graph (pacto graph --with-references) and are pinned in pacto.lock alongside dependencies.

Warning

pacto push rejects local policies[].ref values (file:// and bare paths). Use them for development and switch every ref to oci:// before you publish.

Info

pacto push resolves every remote policies[].ref before publishing and rejects the push if the contract violates one of those schemas.

A policy author's own bundle carries the schema at policy/schema.json, the fixed path a policies[].ref resolves against; see bundle structure for where that sits among the other optional directories.

docs.title: Dependencies and state
docs.text: Four fields: dependencies lists the other services this one calls, breaks announces deliberate breaking changes to its consumers, workload says how it runs (a long-running service, a job or a scheduled job) and state says what data it keeps. Impact analysis, the lockfile and the Kubernetes operator all read them. The other sections are in Contract sections, Configuration and policy and Readiness.

docs.title: dependencies
docs.text:
Declares dependencies on other services via their Pacto contracts.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes, unless ref Non-empty identifier for the dependency. In 2.5, derived from ref when absent. See Name from ref ref string Yes, unless external or, in 2.5, a dependency by name Non-empty. OCI reference (oci://...) or local path (file://... or bare path) required boolean Yes (2.0 to 2.4) Whether the dependency is mandatory. In 2.5 an absent required is true compatibility string With ref; optional by name Non-empty. Valid semver constraint, or unknown in 2.5. See Unknown compatibility external boolean No true when something outside this Pacto system delivers the dependency. Needs pactoVersion: "2.1" version string Only for external without ref The version it runs against, as free text identity string No Only for external without ref. The canonical identity of the external system. See Name an external system. Needs pactoVersion: "2.5" requires list No Guarantees this service relies on from the provider. See Required guarantees. Needs pactoVersion: "2.2"

Note

true means the service cannot function without the dependency. false means it degrades gracefully when the dependency is unavailable. The field is declared intent: consumers read it and the dashboard uses it to work out the affected consumers. Pacto checks nothing about it at deployment time.

docs.title: Name from ref
docs.text:
In a "2.5" contract a dependency may leave out name. Pacto takes the last path segment of the repository in ref, so ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/payments:1.4.0 is named payments. A dependency with neither name nor ref fails with DEPENDENCY_NAME_REQUIRED.

A derived name is a guess from a path. The operational graph resolves it only against a provider published at that same repository, never against another service that happens to share the name, and a local ref never resolves by a derived name. The dashboard and the fleet tools mark it as a name from ref. An unresolved derived name that matches a changed service keeps its impact partial (DERIVED_NAME_CONSUMERS_UNRESOLVED).

docs.title: Depend on a service by name
docs.text:
In a "2.5" contract a dependency on a service of your own may leave out ref. Pacto resolves it by name in your domain, and pacto ci proposes the ref from the organization index:

pactoVersion: "2.5"
dependencies:
  - name: ledger                 # resolved in this service's domain
  - name: fraud
    compatibility: "^2.0.0"      # optional; without it the range reads unknown
  • A dependency by name gives no version: Pacto reads it from the fleet, and version beside it fails with VERSION_WITHOUT_REF.
  • Without compatibility the range is unknown, so impact cannot tell whether a change breaks this service. pacto ci proposes a range, which the owner accepts with pacto accept.
  • pacto graph shows the dependency as resolved by name, and a catalog closure that meets it reads partial (DEPENDENCY_BY_NAME).
  • pacto lock and pacto validate --closure cannot follow it: they fail naming the dependency (LOCK_UNRESOLVED, CLOSURE_DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED) until you declare its ref.
  • An older contract fails with NEEDS_PACTO_2_5.

docs.title: Unknown compatibility
docs.text:
compatibility: unknown says that a range has not been decided yet. It needs pactoVersion: "2.5". Everything that reads a range reads it as unknown, never as compatible: impact analysis gives the consumer the verdict unknown and keeps a breaking change unverified, delivery holds a promotion that depends on it and the operator reports the dependency as unverified. An oci:// reference without a tag cannot be resolved, since there is no range to pick a tag with: pin a tag or declare a range. pacto diff reports unknown to a range as non-breaking and a range to unknown as potentially breaking.

pactoVersion: "2.5"
service: {name: reports, version: 1.0.0}
dependencies:
  - ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/payments:1.4.0
    compatibility: unknown

docs.title: Required guarantees
docs.text:
Each requires entry names a provider interface and the guarantees this service relies on. The provider must declare each one at least as strong as written.

dependencies:
  - name: orders
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/orders
    compatibility: "^2.0.0"
    required: true
    requires:
      - interface: order-events
        delivery: at-least-once
        dedupeWindow: 5m
  • pacto validate reads the provider contract and reports every unmet guarantee in one run as GUARANTEE_UNMET, naming both services, the guarantee and both values: an error on a required dependency, a warning on an optional one.
  • When Pacto cannot read the provider contract, validation warns with GUARANTEE_UNVERIFIED and reports the guarantees stage as SKIP, naming the dependency.
  • pacto publish and pacto push run the same check and refuse an unmet guarantee of a required dependency. pacto pack works offline and fetches no providers. pacto graph marks each refused edge.
  • pacto impact lists the consumers whose requirement a change breaks and blocks the release when one of them runs.
  • Delivery holds a promote that leaves a consumer's required guarantee unmet, wherever the consumer runs. A status an older operator wrote records no guarantees, so delivery reads it as unknown until the new operator reconciles it: a breaking or possibly breaking change to such a provider waits for a person to accept the unknown.

docs.title: External dependencies
docs.text:
external: true marks a dependency that something outside this Pacto installation delivers. Your company may still run it. Pacto expects no running instance of it, never proposes moving it first and leaves it out of the unresolved list. It takes one of two forms:

dependencies:
  - name: ledger                 # someone wrote a contract for it
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/ledger
    compatibility: "^4.0.0"      # compared like any other dependency
    required: true
    external: true
  - name: model                  # no contract: name the version instead
    external: true
    version: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5
    required: true

With ref, versions are compared as usual. Without it, version is required: it shows in the graph and in pacto diff, where any change is potentially breaking. Pacto has no contract to compare it with, so anything that relies on it is Unknown and never passes. Before "2.5", a dependency with no ref and no external: true fails validation with DEPENDENCY_REF_REQUIRED (NEEDS_PACTO_2_5 when it gives no version). An external dependency with no ref and no version fails with EXTERNAL_VERSION_REQUIRED.

docs.title: Name an external system
docs.text:
Each ref-less external dependency joins one graph node per external system. A catalog alias joins its entry (stripe-api joins stripe); any other name gets a node of its own. When the name says what the dependency does, set identity to the system it calls:

pactoVersion: "2.5"
dependencies:
  - name: payments-provider
    external: true
    version: "2024-06-20"
    required: true
    identity: stripe             # or host/corp-legacy.example
  • An identity is lower-case path segments: a vendor (stripe), host/<registrable-domain> or <provider>/<service>/<account>/<region>/<id> (aws/rds/123456789012/eu-west-1/orders-db).
  • It needs external: true and no ref (IDENTITY_WITHOUT_EXTERNAL). An unparseable identity or the reserved other-egress fails with INVALID_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY. Changing it is never breaking. See the external catalog reference.
  • pacto init records the external systems a folder names in the inferred record, never here, and the fleet shows them as inferred edges of source kind repository until you declare them.

docs.title: A dependency whose contract is not published yet
docs.text:
For a service your Pacto system delivers whose contract nobody has published yet, leave external out. Set ref to the repository its contract will be published at and compatibility to the versions you accept:

dependencies:
  - name: ledger
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/contracts/ledger   # published later
    compatibility: "^1.0.0"
    required: true

The contract validates. Until ledger publishes, Pacto lists it as unresolved, so the gap stays visible. With external: true and a version instead, compatibility stays Unknown for good.

docs.title: Dependency reference schemes
docs.text:
Scheme Example Description oci:// oci://ghcr.io/acme/auth-pacto:1.0.0 OCI registry reference (required for pacto push) oci:// (no tag) oci://ghcr.io/acme/auth-pacto Resolved to the highest semver tag satisfying compatibility file:// file://../shared-db Local filesystem path (bare path) ../shared-db Local filesystem path (shorthand for file://)

When an oci:// reference omits the tag, Pacto picks the highest semver tag that satisfies compatibility: with ^2.0.0 and tags 1.0.0, 2.0.0, 2.3.0 and 3.0.0 it resolves to 2.3.0. Tag listings are cached for the duration of the command, so dependencies on the same repository share one registry query.

compatibility applies only to untagged references

Pacto reads the constraint only when the reference omits its tag. A ref that names a tag or a digest resolves to exactly that version, and validation skips the compatibility check. This example validates with no warning:

dependencies:
  - name: auth
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/auth-pacto:1.0.0   # resolves to 1.0.0 …
    required: true
    compatibility: "^2.0.0"                    # … which this does not satisfy

If you pin, the pin wins. Keep compatibility accurate anyway: consumers and the lockfile read it as your declared range.

At runtime the Kubernetes operator does check the range: when the provider runs under its own Pacto resource, the contract version it reports outside compatibility is DEPENDENCY_VERSION_MISMATCH, an error for a required dependency and a warning for an optional one. An unknown version stays unverified.

Note

Validation rejects OCI references whose tag or digest is malformed. Tags must follow the OCI tag grammar ([A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}), and digests must be well-formed (sha256:<64 hex> or sha512:<128 hex>). The same check applies to config and policy refs.

docs.title: Compatibility constraint examples
docs.text:
Pacto uses Masterminds/semver constraint syntax:

Constraint Matches Use case ^2.0.0 >= 2.0.0, < 3.0.0 Accept patches and minors within a major version ~2.1.0 >= 2.1.0, < 2.2.0 Accept only patches within a minor version >= 2.0.0 2.0.0 and above (including 3.x, 4.x, …) Track the latest version above a floor >= 2.0.0, < 4.0.0 2.x and 3.x only Constrain to a range of major versions * Any version Always resolve to the absolute latest

Warning

Use local dependency references (file:// and bare paths) during development. pacto push rejects contracts with local dependencies, so switch every ref to oci:// before you publish.

Practices:

  • Pin by digest in production. Use oci://...@sha256:.... A tag-based reference produces a validation warning.
  • Give cloud-managed resources a contract when you can. A lightweight Pacto contract for GCP Cloud SQL, AWS SNS or Azure Service Bus, referenced as an external dependency, makes it version-tracked alongside your own. When nobody writes one, name its version with version.
  • Pin the whole closure with pacto lock. When a pacto.lock file is present, every resolved dependency must match the pinned digest or the command fails. See Lockfile.

docs.title: breaks
docs.text:
Announces a deliberate breaking change to the consumers it affects. Needs pactoVersion: "2.5". An announcement changes no interface: pacto diff reports every change to breaks as non-breaking.

Each consumer owner accepts the break with pacto accept --break. Without expires, pacto ci records the commit time plus 30 days, and an expired announcement blocks again.

breaks:
  - consumers: [reports]
    reason: Amounts move from cents to euros; read amount_eur.
    expires: "2026-12-14"
Field Type Required Constraints consumers list Yes Non-empty, unique service names. A consumer appears in one entry at most (DUPLICATE_BREAK_CONSUMER) and the service never names itself (BREAK_NAMES_SELF) reason string Yes Non-empty. Why the break is needed and what the consumers change expires string No YYYY-MM-DD date the announcement stops applying (INVALID_BREAK_EXPIRES otherwise)

docs.title: workload
docs.text:
Top-level string describing the execution pattern of the workload. Optional. Enum: service, job, scheduled.

Value Description service A long-running process that serves requests continuously job A one-shot task that runs to completion and then exits scheduled A task that runs on a recurring schedule (for example cron) 
workload: service

docs.title: state
docs.text:
Top-level section declaring how the service manages state. Optional: a minimal contract can omit it. The contract tells the platform whether the service needs persistent storage or a stable network identity.

Field Type Required Enum values type string Yes stateless, stateful, hybrid persistence Persistence Yes dataCriticality string Yes low, medium, high

State types:

Value What it means Example services stateless No data retained between requests. Any instance can handle any request. Instances are interchangeable. REST APIs, reverse proxies, API gateways stateful Retains data between requests. Requires stable storage or instance affinity. Databases, message brokers, distributed caches hybrid Handles requests statelessly but keeps selective in-memory or local state that enriches behavior. Losing that state degrades the service but leaves it running. APIs with local caches, services with in-memory session stores

How platforms interpret state:

The combination of state.type, persistence.scope and persistence.durability tells a platform what infrastructure a service needs. These signals are platform-agnostic. See Platform engineers for the full contract-field → platform-decision mapping (Deployment, StatefulSet, PVC and the equivalents on Nomad, ECS or a custom platform).

Data criticality:

Value What it means low Loss of data has minimal impact. Can be regenerated or is non-essential. medium Loss has moderate impact. May require manual recovery. high Loss has severe business impact. Must be prevented. Implies backups, replication, stricter disruption budgets.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
Field Type Required Enum values scope string Yes local, shared durability string Yes ephemeral, persistent
  • local: data stays on a single instance. Each replica has its own.
  • shared: all instances share data through a common store.
  • ephemeral: data can be lost on restart without impact. Caches, temp files and reconstructible state.
  • persistent: data must survive restarts. Requires durable storage.

At runtime the Kubernetes operator reads scope from the workload: one PersistentVolumeClaim in the pod template of a workload with more than one replica is shared, so local scope with such a claim is PERSISTENCE_MISMATCH. shared scope with per-replica storage stays unverified, because the shared store may live outside the cluster.

docs.title: State invariants
docs.text:
Condition Constraint type: stateless durability must be ephemeral

The JSON Schema rejects a stateless service with persistent storage.

state:
  type: stateful
  persistence:
    scope: shared
    durability: persistent
  dataCriticality: high

docs.title: pacto diff and change classification: what counts as a breaking change
docs.text:
pacto diff compares two versions of a contract and tells you which changes can break the services that depend on it. Run it in CI to catch a breaking change before it merges:

pacto diff oci://ghcr.io/acme/payments-api:1.4.0 ./payments-api

Every change goes through a fixed rule table, so the same two contracts always give the same answer. The tables below list every field Pacto compares and its verdict.

Each change is classified as:

  • BREAKING: a change that breaks consumers or platforms relying on the previous contract
  • POTENTIAL_BREAKING: a change that may break consumers, depending on how they use the field
  • NON_BREAKING: a safe change that keeps compatibility

A change that matches no specific rule below defaults to POTENTIAL_BREAKING. Inside an interface schema the default is BREAKING; see Schema position.

docs.title: Service identity
docs.text:
Field Change Classification service.name Modified BREAKING service.version Modified NON_BREAKING service.owner.team Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.owner.dri Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.owner.contacts[] Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.domain Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.offering Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.summary Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.lifecycle Added / Removed NON_BREAKING service.lifecycle.deprecated Modified NON_BREAKING service.lifecycle.sunset Added / Removed NON_BREAKING service.lifecycle.sunset Modified, earlier POTENTIAL_BREAKING service.lifecycle.sunset Modified, later NON_BREAKING service.lifecycle.successor Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING service.template Added NON_BREAKING service.template Removed NON_BREAKING service.template.plugins Modified NON_BREAKING service.origin Added NON_BREAKING service.origin Modified NON_BREAKING service.origin Removed NON_BREAKING service.external Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

The owner block is compared field by field, so changing a dri or adding a contact while the team is unchanged reports that specific change. Contacts are keyed by type:value, and a purpose change on an existing contact is a modification. service carries identity only, so the contract has no image or chart field to diff. A pactoVersion change, such as "2.0" to "2.1", is NON_BREAKING.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
Field Change Classification interfaces Added NON_BREAKING interfaces Removed BREAKING interfaces.type Modified BREAKING interfaces.ref Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING interfaces.visibility Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle Added / Removed NON_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle.deprecated Modified NON_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle.sunset Added / Removed NON_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle.sunset Modified, earlier POTENTIAL_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle.sunset Modified, later NON_BREAKING interfaces.lifecycle.successor Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING interfaces.guarantees Added NON_BREAKING interfaces.guarantees Removed BREAKING interfaces.guarantees.weakened Modified BREAKING interfaces.guarantees.strengthened Modified NON_BREAKING interfaces.compatibilityEpoch Modified (raised or lowered) BREAKING interfaces.port Added / Removed NON_BREAKING interfaces.port Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING

Interfaces are keyed by name. The type enum is openapi/asyncapi/grpc/mcp, and the spec pointer is ref. Deprecating an interface changes nothing a consumer calls, so it is a notice. An earlier sunset shortens the time consumers have to migrate. Removing an interface before its sunset is still BREAKING, and the reason says that the sunset has not been reached.

Each guarantee is compared on its own: a longer dedupeWindow or retention, a shorter timeout, global ordering in place of per-key and a new idempotent: true are stronger. A delivery change is weaker in both directions, because a consumer relying on the old value breaks.

A compatibilityEpoch change marks a behavior change that no spec diff can see.

docs.title: Configurations
docs.text:
Field Change Classification configurations[] Added NON_BREAKING configurations[] Removed BREAKING configurations[] One becomes several, so a selector-less ref turns ambiguous BREAKING configurations[].schema Added POTENTIAL_BREAKING configurations[].schema Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING configurations[].schema Removed BREAKING configurations[].ref Added NON_BREAKING configurations[].ref Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING configurations[].ref Removed BREAKING configurations[].configuration Added NON_BREAKING configurations[].configuration Modified / Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING configurations[].values.* Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

Dropping a schema is BREAKING: the configuration a consumer supplies stops being validated. Introducing a schema where there was none is POTENTIAL_BREAKING, because a configuration that was unchecked before can now fail validation.

Inline configuration values and environment values are the provider's own inputs. Pacto diffs them key by key (for example configurations[app].values.replicas) and classifies each change NON_BREAKING. Values beside a ref are a request the provider's schema checks. Removing the configuration selector can leave the ref ambiguous.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Field Change Classification environments[] Added NON_BREAKING environments[] Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING environments[].*, a value in the environment's file, for example environments[production].chart.ingress.host Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
Field Change Classification policies[] Added NON_BREAKING policies[] Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING policies[].schema Added / Modified / Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING policies[].ref Added NON_BREAKING policies[].ref Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING policies[].ref Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING

Introducing a policy schema where there was none is POTENTIAL_BREAKING for the same reason it is on a configuration: a contract that no policy checked before can now fail against it.

docs.title: Workload and state
docs.text:
Field Change Classification workload Modified BREAKING workload Added / Removed NON_BREAKING state.type Modified BREAKING state.persistence.scope Modified BREAKING state.persistence.durability Modified BREAKING state.dataCriticality Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING state.dataCriticality Added / Removed NON_BREAKING

workload and state are top-level sections. Scheduling and scaling are delivery concerns, so the contract has no runtime, lifecycle or scaling section to diff.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
Field Change Classification capabilities Added NON_BREAKING capabilities Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING

Capabilities (health, metrics, extension) are compared as a set, keyed by type, plus ref for an extension. Adding a capability is a new signal (NON_BREAKING). Removing one loses an observability guarantee (POTENTIAL_BREAKING). The diff ignores binding, so re-pointing a capability's binding.interface or binding.path produces no change.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Field Change Classification dependencies Added NON_BREAKING dependencies Removed BREAKING dependencies.ref Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING dependencies.compatibility Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING dependencies.compatibility.declared Modified (from unknown to a range) NON_BREAKING dependencies.compatibility.unknown Modified (from a range to unknown) POTENTIAL_BREAKING dependencies.required Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING dependencies.requires Added / Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING dependencies.requires Removed NON_BREAKING dependencies.identity Added / Removed / Modified NON_BREAKING

docs.title: Breaks
docs.text: Field Change Classification breaks Added / Removed NON_BREAKING breaks.reason Modified NON_BREAKING breaks.expires Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text: pacto diff performs deep comparison of referenced OpenAPI specs, detecting changes at the path, method, parameter, request body and response level.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text: Field Change Classification openapi.paths Added NON_BREAKING openapi.paths Removed BREAKING

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Field Change Classification openapi.methods Added NON_BREAKING openapi.methods Removed BREAKING

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Field Change Classification openapi.parameters Added (optional) POTENTIAL_BREAKING openapi.parameters Added (required: true) BREAKING openapi.parameters Removed BREAKING openapi.parameters Modified (optional → required) BREAKING openapi.parameters Modified (schema narrowed) BREAKING openapi.parameters Modified (any other) POTENTIAL_BREAKING

Introducing a new required parameter, or flipping an existing one from optional to required, is BREAKING because existing clients omit it. A parameter's schema sits in request position, so narrowing it, for example dropping an enum value or lowering a maxLength, is BREAKING too. Relaxing required to optional is POTENTIAL_BREAKING.

Parameters are identified by name + in (location: query, path, header, cookie). A parameter renamed or moved to a different location counts as a removal plus an addition.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text: Field Change Classification openapi.request-body Added POTENTIAL_BREAKING openapi.request-body Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Field Change Classification openapi.responses Added NON_BREAKING openapi.responses Removed BREAKING

Neither table has a Modified row. A request body or a status code present on both sides is deep-diffed field by field. A request body schema sits in request position and a response schema in response position, and the schema position rules classify each inner difference. A documentation edit, such as a response description or an example, is NON_BREAKING. Any other change around the schema, such as a media type or a header, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING, except that removing a response's whole content, one of its media types or its schema is BREAKING.

Change paths pinpoint the exact location, for example:

openapi.paths[/users].methods[GET].parameters[filter:query]
openapi.paths[/users].methods[POST].request-body.content.application/json.schema.required[email]
openapi.paths[/users].methods[GET].responses[200].content.application/json.schema.properties.email

docs.title: AsyncAPI
docs.text: pacto diff compares referenced AsyncAPI documents at the channel and operation level. Both AsyncAPI 2.x and 3.x are supported, in YAML or JSON.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Field Change Classification asyncapi.channels Added NON_BREAKING asyncapi.channels Removed BREAKING asyncapi.channels.publish, subscribe (a 2.x flip removes one) Removed BREAKING

A channel present on both sides is compared field by field, so each payload difference surfaces as its own change. Old and new publishers and subscribers run side by side, so a message's payload and headers schemas sit in record position: a new optional property is NON_BREAKING and every other schema difference is BREAKING. Documentation, tags included, and a new 2.x publish or subscribe operation are NON_BREAKING. Any other difference, such as a binding or a message name, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING. For that reason the table has no asyncapi.channels Modified row.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Field Change Classification asyncapi.operations Added NON_BREAKING asyncapi.operations Removed BREAKING asyncapi.operations.action, channel.$ref Modified BREAKING

An operation present on both sides is deep-diffed exactly like a channel, so flipping action from send to receive surfaces as asyncapi.operations[sendOrder].action (BREAKING).

Top-level operations are an AsyncAPI 3.x concept. A 2.x document has no operations map, so only its channels are compared.

The diff ignores info, servers and defaultContentType, which change on most releases and leave what a consumer can publish or subscribe to unchanged. Components are compared where they are used.

Change paths pinpoint the exact location, for example:

asyncapi.channels[payment.completed]
asyncapi.channels[payment.refunded].publish.message.payload.required[charge_id]
asyncapi.operations[sendOrder].action

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
pacto diff compares referenced .proto files at the service, rpc, message, field and enum level.

Field Change Classification grpc.services Added NON_BREAKING grpc.services Removed BREAKING grpc.rpcs Added NON_BREAKING grpc.rpcs Removed BREAKING grpc.rpcs Modified BREAKING grpc.messages Added NON_BREAKING grpc.messages Removed BREAKING grpc.messages.fields Added NON_BREAKING grpc.messages.fields Removed BREAKING grpc.messages.fields Modified BREAKING grpc.enums Added NON_BREAKING grpc.enums Removed BREAKING grpc.enums.values Added POTENTIAL_BREAKING grpc.enums.values Removed / Modified BREAKING

proto3 has no required, so an added rpc, message or field is always wire-compatible with existing clients. An added enum value is POTENTIAL_BREAKING: the scan cannot tell whether the enum reaches a reader that switches over every value. A removed or renumbered value is BREAKING. Everything else here is BREAKING. Removing a service, rpc, message or field breaks every caller. A changed rpc signature (including a switch between unary and streaming), or a field whose type or number changed, breaks the wire format for clients built against the old descriptor. For that reason a modified field is BREAKING.

Change paths pinpoint the exact location, for example:

grpc.services[FraudService]
grpc.rpcs[FraudService.EvaluateTransaction]
grpc.messages[EvaluateTransactionRequest].fields[metadata]

docs.title: Limits of the proto comparison
docs.text:
The comparison scans proto3 source as text. It runs no protobuf compiler, which has these effects:

  • imports stay unresolved. Pacto compares only the declarations in the referenced file. A message that moves into an imported file reads as a removal.
  • Nested messages, nested enums and oneof bodies are skipped. Their fields are left out of the enclosing message, so a change inside one produces no change entry.
  • Identity is the declared name. A renamed field or rpc reads as a removal plus an addition even when the field number is unchanged.
  • Type identity is textual. The scanner compares names as written, without package or import resolution, so fully qualifying a type (Inner → pkg.v1.Inner) reads as a modified field even though the descriptor is unchanged.
  • Inline field options are ignored. Adding or removing [deprecated = true] produces no change entry, while a retype behind one still does. A field whose option block contains braces (a nested text-format value such as [(validate.rules).string = {min_len: 1}]) is dropped from the revision that carries it, and only from that one. Adding such an option to an existing field therefore reads as a removal and is classified BREAKING.
  • Comments and string literals are inert. A //, a } or a /* inside a string literal, such as a URL in an option line, is read as part of the string.

docs.title: JSON Schema (configuration & policy schemas)
docs.text:
Schema files referenced by configurations[].schema, policies[].schema or the auto-detected policy/schema.json are compared recursively. Pacto detects and classifies every structural difference, including properties, types, constraints, defaults and enums.

Field Change Classification schema.properties.* Added POTENTIAL_BREAKING schema.properties.* Removed POTENTIAL_BREAKING schema.properties.* Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING schema.required Added / Removed BREAKING schema.description, title, examples and other documentation Added / Removed / Modified NON_BREAKING schema.* (any other path) Added / Removed / Modified POTENTIAL_BREAKING

A configuration or policy schema carries no position. A configuration schema constrains a value the platform supplies, so both required transitions take the conservative answer and stay BREAKING.

docs.title: Schema position
docs.text:
An interface schema is judged by the position it sits in, because the same edit helps one side of an exchange and hurts the other.

Position Where Who reads it Widening Narrowing request OpenAPI request bodies and parameters, MCP inputSchema the new provider, from an old caller NON_BREAKING BREAKING response OpenAPI responses, MCP outputSchema an old consumer, which may switch over every enum value BREAKING NON_BREAKING record AsyncAPI message payload and headers schemas old and new code at once, in both directions BREAKING BREAKING Edit Effect enum value added, oneOf or anyOf variant added or type member added widens type changed from integer to number, or nullable: true set widens maxLength, maximum, maxItems or maxProperties raised, or a min* bound lowered widens a bound, pattern, format, const, enum, allOf or items removed widens additionalProperties: false relaxed to a schema or removed widens required entry or the whole required list removed, or allOf member removed widens the mirror of each row above narrows enum or required entries reordered no change pattern, format, const or multipleOf rewritten, or type changed to an unrelated type breaks in every position anything inside not or if, a default, readOnly or discriminator changed, any other keyword breaks in every position a $ref Pacto cannot resolve POTENTIAL_BREAKING in every position an x- extension keyword added, removed or changed POTENTIAL_BREAKING in every position description, title, summary, example, examples, $comment, externalDocs, deprecated or tags NON_BREAKING in every position

Properties have their own rules:

  • Adding an optional property is NON_BREAKING in every position, because a reader tolerates a field it does not know.
  • Removing an optional property is BREAKING from a response or a record whether or not required listed it. Most payload schemas list nothing, and the field is data a reader may use.
  • Removing one from a request is POTENTIAL_BREAKING: the provider drops the caller's field unread.
  • An object with additionalProperties: false accepts no undeclared field, so adding a property widens it and removing one narrows it.
  • Inside a response's headers map every grade stops at POTENTIAL_BREAKING, because removing the whole header is POTENTIAL_BREAKING.

docs.title: References and components
docs.text:
Each $ref is resolved first, so a component is judged where it is used:

  • A component used in more than one position, such as a schema in a request body and in a response, is judged in each one. Pacto reports one change with the worst grade, at the usage path where that grade applies. The reason names the component and its usages.
  • Pacto compares what a ref resolves to. Renaming a component with identical content is no change, and a ref pointed at a different schema is graded by the structural difference.
  • Local refs (#/components/..., #/definitions/..., #/$defs/...) and relative file refs inside the bundle resolve, and a ref inside another file resolves against that file. Request bodies, responses, parameters and headers resolve the same way as schemas.
  • A remote (http or https) ref, or one whose target is missing, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING, and the reason says Pacto could not resolve it. The same unresolved ref in both revisions reports no change, because Pacto sees nothing change. A ref whose text stays the same while its target goes away, such as a renamed component or a file dropped from the bundle, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING at the usage path.
  • A ref to another ref resolves through the chain. A chain that loops never resolves.
  • A path item written as a $ref, local or to a file, is followed to the operations it holds.
  • A recursive schema is compared once per position, so cycles terminate.
  • A component that no path, channel or operation reaches through a $ref is reported as one NON_BREAKING change, because no consumer reads it. Security schemes are named without a $ref, so that report leaves them out.
  • In AsyncAPI 3 a ref from an operation to its channel or message is compared as text, because the channel is compared on its own.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Field Change Classification readiness Added / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.expires Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.minScore Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.partialCredit Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.claims[] Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

All readiness changes are NON_BREAKING, because readiness tracks operational maturity and leaves runtime compatibility unchanged. Adding or removing the whole readiness block surfaces as a single readiness change; otherwise the gate fields (expires, minScore, partialCredit) are compared individually. Claims are keyed by id, and a claim whose status, weight, evidence or any other field changed is reported as a modification of that claim (for example readiness.claims[dashboard]). The diff skips the readiness.history revision log, an append-only changelog that changes on every release.

docs.title: Inferred record
docs.text:
Field Change Classification inferred.<field> Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING
  • A field of the bundle's inferred record is something Pacto read from the folder, outside the declared contract, so a change to it never asks for more than a patch.
  • pacto diff leaves out changes to the record's inputs.

docs.title: Fields the diff skips
docs.text:
Section Behavior metadata Skipped. Free-form metadata keys appear in documentation and the dashboard. capabilities[].binding Skipped. Capabilities are keyed by type (and ref), so pacto diff reports no change for a new binding.interface or binding.path on an otherwise unchanged capability. readiness.history[] Skipped. An append-only changelog that changes on every release; see Readiness.

To flag changes to these fields in CI, gate on them separately, for example with a policy or a custom check.

docs.title: SBOM
docs.text:
SBOM changes are reported separately from contract changes. They are informational and leave the overall diff classification unchanged.

Change Description Package added A new package appears in the SBOM Package removed A package left the SBOM Package version modified A package's version changed Package license modified A package's license changed Package supplier modified A package's supplier changed

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: environments lists the environments a service runs in and the configuration values each one uses. pacto validate checks those values against the schema of every configuration they name, on every change. Pacto applies nothing and deploys nothing. The other sections are in Contract sections and Configuration and policy.

docs.title: environments
docs.text:
Optional. Needs pactoVersion: "2.3": an older contract with it fails validation with NEEDS_PACTO_2_3. 2.3 needs Pacto core 4.4.0 or later and operator 6.4.0 or later; see Versions.

pactoVersion: "2.3"
service:
  name: web
  version: 1.4.0
configurations:
  - name: app
    schema: configuration/schema.json
    required: true
    values:
      LOG_LEVEL: info
  - name: chart
    schema: chart/values.schema.json
    required: true
environments:
  - name: staging
    file: environments/staging.yaml
  - name: production
    file: environments/production.yaml
Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, at most 63 characters. Unique in the contract (DUPLICATE_ENVIRONMENT_NAME otherwise) file string Yes Path to a YAML or JSON file, from the bundle root, with no leading / or ./ and no .. (FILE_NOT_FOUND otherwise, or when the file is missing) lifetime string No temporary or persistent. Needs pactoVersion: "2.4". Absent reads "not declared", never persistent expires string No An RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z, and only with lifetime: temporary (INVALID_ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRES, ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRES_NOT_TEMPORARY otherwise). Needs pactoVersion: "2.4" owner object No Who owns this environment when it is not the service owner, in the shape of service.owner (team, dri, contacts). Needs pactoVersion: "2.4"

A contract older than 2.4 that sets lifetime, expires or owner fails with NEEDS_PACTO_2_4 at that field.

The file maps each configuration name to the values that environment uses for it:

# environments/production.yaml
app:
  LOG_LEVEL: warn
chart:
  replicaCount: 5
  ingress:
    host: shop.example.com

The -f/--values and --set flags change the contract itself; an environment's values live in its file.

The file is part of the bundle, so pacto pack and pacto push ship it with the contract. A .pactoignore entry that hides it makes validation report FILE_NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: Temporary environments
docs.text:
A preview or pull-request environment lives hours or days. Declare it temporary, give it an expires time and, when another team runs it, an owner:

pactoVersion: "2.4"
environments:
  - name: production
    file: environments/production.yaml
    lifetime: persistent
  - name: pr-482
    file: environments/pr-482.yaml
    lifetime: temporary
    expires: "2026-11-20T00:00:00Z"
    owner: {team: storefront-qa}

Once expires is at or before the clock of the run, pacto validate and pacto_check add an ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRED warning to the environments stage:

WARN  [ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRED] environments[1].expires: environment pr-482 expired at 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z; nothing was deleted: remove it with pacto_edit remove_environments or move expires

The verdict stays the same. Pacto deletes nothing for an expired environment: no contract entry, file, Stage or resource. The fleet and the dashboard's service page show it as expired (inferred), as of the time of their answer. An environment with no owner shows the service owner, labelled inferred.

docs.title: Create, list, compare and retire
docs.text:
Task Command Create a service with environments pacto init --delivery --env test,pr-482 declares each environment with an empty values file and writes a Stage for each Add environments to a contract pacto_edit with add_environments, such as [{"name":"pr-482","lifetime":"temporary","expires":"2026-11-20T00:00:00Z"}] Retire an environment pacto_edit with remove_environments, such as ["pr-482"]. A file no other environment names is deleted. Nothing in a cluster changes List a service's environments pacto fleet entity service <name>, pacto_fleet_entity or the service page Compare two environments pacto explain <bundle> --environments production,pr-482 or pacto_check with environments See the Stages that deliver it pacto delivery status --service <name>

Adding an environment declares it: nothing in a cluster changes until a Stage exists for it. pacto_edit returns the steps that get there in chain: publish the contract, then plan a promote on the environment's Stage. Its executor names who acts on the published revision, an adapter or a GitOps tool, and impact says who the edit affects when the session has a fleet snapshot.

pacto explain --environments lists only the values the environments disagree on:

Differences between production, pr-482 (1):
  chart.replicaCount
    production  6
    pr-482      1

When a Stage is created or deleted, the delivery promoter emits a Kubernetes Event (EnvironmentCreated, EnvironmentDeleted) and the recorder posts a CDEvent (environment.created, environment.deleted); see delivery setup and delivery records. Each names one Stage; other Stages for the same environment are unaffected.

docs.title: How values are checked
docs.text:
For each environment, and for each configuration its file names, Pacto merges the environment's values over the configuration's default values and checks the result against the configuration's schema. Objects merge key by key, and the environment's value wins. A null removes its key from the merged values, at any depth, so an environment can drop a default:

# environments/staging.yaml
chart:
  ingress:
    className: null  # staging uses the cluster's default ingress class

A configuration named with no values, such as app:, keeps its defaults. A required: true configuration that the file leaves out must pass its schema with its defaults alone. A configuration that is optional and left out is not checked.

Condition Code The file names a configuration the contract does not declare ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION The merged values fail the configuration's schema, or the file does not parse, is not a mapping of configuration names or has a key that is not a string ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID A required configuration has no values in the file and its defaults fail its schema ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_MISSING The configuration names its schema by ref and the referenced contract cannot be resolved, or there are no bundle files to read. A resolved ref has its values checked against the referenced contract's configuration schema like a local one ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED (warning)

Each error names the environment, the configuration and the JSON Pointer of the value, and points at its line in the environment's file. A key that holds a dot or a slash, such as prometheus.io/scrape, is one step of the pointer, with / written as ~1 and ~ as ~0. The checks run in the environments stage of pacto validate.

Values hold references to secrets, such as a Secret or ExternalSecret name. Keep secret material out of the environment files, as you keep it out of the contract; see Secret references.

docs.title: Catch a chart change that breaks an environment
docs.text:
A Helm chart's values.schema.json is a JSON Schema, so you can reference it as a configuration and keep one file per environment. Version 1.4.0 of the web service ships this chart schema:

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "replicaCount": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
    "ingress": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"host": {"type": "string"}}
    }
  }
}

The contract references it and lists two environments:

pactoVersion: "2.3"
service:
  name: web
  version: 1.4.0
  owner: {team: storefront}
configurations:
  - name: chart
    schema: chart/values.schema.json
    required: true
environments:
  - name: staging
    file: environments/staging.yaml
  - name: production
    file: environments/production.yaml

Staging sets an ingress host. Production sets only a class name:

# environments/staging.yaml
chart:
  replicaCount: 1
  ingress:
    host: staging.example.com

# environments/production.yaml
chart:
  replicaCount: 5
  ingress:
    className: nginx

Version 1.5.0 updates the chart, and its schema makes ingress.host required. pacto validate reports the environment it breaks before you deploy it:

$ pacto validate web-1.5.0
web-1.5.0 is invalid
PASS load
SKIP lock               no pacto.lock
PASS structural
  INFO  [CONTRACT_BEHIND] pactoVersion: pactoVersion "2.3" is behind "2.5"; fix the errors this run reports before Pacto can tell whether raising pactoVersion keeps its meaning
PASS cross-field
PASS policy
SKIP configuration-refs no configuration references
FAIL environments
  web-1.5.0/environments/production.yaml:3:3: ERROR [ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID] environments[1].file: environment production: configuration chart at /chart/ingress: missing property 'host'
SKIP guarantees         no dependency declares requires
SKIP readiness          not requested (--readiness)
SKIP closure            not requested (--closure)
Next: fix environments[1].file at web-1.5.0/environments/production.yaml:3:3 [ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID], then run pacto validate web-1.5.0
validation failed with 1 error(s)

The command exits 1. Add the host to the production file and run pacto validate again. pacto diff then lists the schema change and the new value:

$ pacto diff web-1.4.0 web-1.5.0
Classification: BREAKING
Required bump: major
Changes (4):
  [NON_BREAKING] service.version (modified): service.version modified [1.4.0 -> 1.5.0]
  [POTENTIAL_BREAKING] schema.properties.ingress.properties.className (added): schema.properties.ingress.properties.className added [+ map[type:string]]
  [BREAKING] schema.properties.ingress.required (added): schema.properties.ingress.required added [+ [host]]
  [NON_BREAKING] environments[production].chart.ingress.host (added): environments[production].chart.ingress.host added [+ shop.example.com]
breaking changes detected

docs.title: What a change needs
docs.text:
pacto diff compares environments by name:

Change Classification An environment added Non-breaking: it only adds values to check An environment removed Potentially breaking: the environment may still run the service An environment's file, lifetime, expires or owner added, removed or changed, at environments[<name>].<field> Non-breaking: they describe this service's own environment, and no consumer reads them A value in an environment's file added, removed or changed, at environments[<name>].<configuration>.<path> Non-breaking: the values are this service's own inputs, and only the service reads them

docs.title: Environments and Stages
docs.text:
When delivery promotes a version, it matches the Stage's spec.environment against the environment names the version's contract declares. The pacto.environment check runs the same environments stage as pacto validate, on the version's own bundle:

The version's contract The promote Declares no environments Goes on. The check says it does not apply Declares environments, but none named like the Stage's spec.environment Waits for the service's team to approve it Declares that environment, and its values fail with an error from the table above Waits for the service's team to approve it, with each error located in the file Declares that environment, and its values are ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED Waits for a person to accept the unknown Declares that environment, and its values pass Goes on

Name each environment after the spec.environment of the Stages that deliver the service there, such as staging and production. pacto init --delivery --env and pacto_create with delivery declare each environment in the contract, with an empty values file, beside the Stage they write for it, so the names match from the start.

docs.title: Inferred record
docs.text:
pacto.inferred.yaml holds what Pacto completes for a service from its folder, apart from what pacto.yaml declares. Pacto writes it into the bundle of a pactoVersion: "2.5" contract when it packs, pushes or publishes, and never into pacto.yaml. Only a --cluster draft gets a copy in its folder. Each value names the file and line it was read from, how sure Pacto is and the YAML that would declare it.

A declared value always wins: Pacto never records a field that pacto.yaml already declares, and it never changes pacto.yaml. The other sections are in Contract sections and Dependencies and state.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
format: pacto.inferred/v1
inputs:
  commit: 4e1a9c0d...          # left out when the folder is not a git checkout
  pacto: 4.6.0                 # the Pacto that completed it
  discovery: "5"               # raised when what Pacto reads from a folder changes
  sources:                     # every file a field cites, sorted by path
    - {path: deploy/app.yaml, digest: "sha256:..."}
    - {path: openapi/v1.yaml, digest: "sha256:..."}
    - {path: "repository:.github/CODEOWNERS", digest: "sha256:..."}
  chartDependencies:           # each chart dependency Chart.lock pins
    - {chart: chart, name: redis, version: 19.0.1, repository: "https://charts.example", digest: "sha256:..."}
fields:                        # sorted by field, then source
  - field: capabilities[health]
    value: GET /healthz (readinessProbe)
    source: deploy/app.yaml:31
    confidence: likely
    declare: |
      capabilities:
        - type: health
  - field: configuration.DB_PASSWORD
    value: string, writeOnly
    source: deploy/app.yaml:24
    confidence: likely
    declare: '"DB_PASSWORD": {"type":"string","writeOnly":true,"description":"..."}'
  - field: ports[8080]
    value: 8080/tcp
    source: Dockerfile:12
    confidence: likely
    outranks: [deploy/app.yaml:18]
  - field: service.owner
    value: payments
    source: catalog-info.yaml:7
    confidence: likely
    declare: |
      service:
        owner:
          team: payments
    class: ownerFile
    outranks: ["repository:.github/CODEOWNERS:4"]
findings:                      # what Pacto recognized and could not read
  - code: DISCOVERY_CHART_DEPENDENCY_UNLOCKED
    source: chart/Chart.yaml:9
    message: chart dependency 'redis' has no Chart.lock digest, not read
  • value is a short summary for people. A configuration key carries its type only, never its value, and a dependency carries the host name only, never the URL.
  • source is path:line, or the path alone when the whole file counts, such as an OpenAPI document. A file at the repository root outside the folder, only CODEOWNERS, is repository:<path>:<line>, relative to the repository root. It is not in the bundle, so inputs.sources cites it with its digest and a change to it changes the record. A version derived by pacto ci --publish cites registry:<repo>@sha256:<digest>, the verified baseline it was raised from, or registry:<repo> when the repository held no version. An image passed on the command line cites flag:--image.
  • class: ownerFile marks a service.owner read from CODEOWNERS or catalog-info.yaml, the only value and the only field it goes on. pacto init shows it as "attested". The marker alone raises no trust: the owner stays inferred unless a CI identity the publisher rule accepts signed the bundle at the commit inputs.commit names, which makes it attested. Neither ever clears a gate.
  • outranks lists, sorted, the other sources that gave the same field. The ranks are in What Pacto reads from your folder.
  • findings lists each file Pacto recognized and could not read, with a code, a path:line and a fixed message that never quotes a value. DISCOVERY_TRUNCATED comes first, then the rest by code and source. At most 100 are kept; findingsDropped counts the rest.
  • inputs.chartDependencies lists each chart dependency Chart.lock pins, with the repository URL stripped of credentials. Pacto never downloads one.
  • inputs.acceptances lists each signed acceptance pacto ci --publish carried from the previous version: the record as <repository>@sha256:<hex>, its signer and the fields it pinned into the published pacto.yaml (or the break it accepts). The next run reads them again and drops one that no longer verifies.
  • confidence is likely (read from a file in the repository) or possible.
  • declare is the YAML to add to pacto.yaml. For a configuration key it is the property to add to the configuration's JSON Schema.
  • A record completed from a folder has no timestamp: the same folder at the same commit gives the same bytes. Only a --cluster draft's record carries read times (Cluster facts).
Field Read from Recorded unless pacto.yaml workload The Kubernetes workload kind declares workload service.owner catalog-info.yaml, CODEOWNERS or the workload's team label declares service.owner service.summary The Dockerfile's org.opencontainers.image.description label declares service.summary service.domain spec.system in catalog-info.yaml declares service.domain interfaces[api], interfaces[events], interfaces[grpc] An OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or gRPC file at any path declares an interface of that name or whose ref is that file ports[<n>] EXPOSE, a containerPort, Helm values or Compose ports declares an interface on that port; a port reaches interfaces[].port only when a person declares it image Helm values, Kustomize images, Compose or a manifest is never compared environments[<env>].file environments/<env>.yaml, a Helm values file or a Kustomize overlay, confirmed by an Argo CD or Flux object declares an environment of that name capabilities[health] A readiness, liveness or startup probe, else the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK declares a health capability configuration.<KEY> Each environment key, ConfigMaps included declares the key in a configuration's values or schema properties, or declares a configuration whose keys Pacto cannot list (a ref, or a schema it cannot read or that uses allOf, anyOf, oneOf, $ref or patternProperties) dependencies[<name>] A service name inside the cluster in an environment value, or spec.dependsOn in catalog-info.yaml declares a dependency of that name or ref service.version The verified baseline and the change since it, when pacto ci --publish or pacto publish derives it, such as 1.4.3 (1.4.2 + patch, NON_BREAKING) or 1.0.0 (no versions in <repo>). The bundle's pacto.yaml carries the same version declares service.version publish.build The build tool the folder shows, or image supplied, not built by Pacto: <ref> for --image or a workload image pinned by digest declares publish publish.deploy The folder's Kustomization, Helm chart or manifests, and the image pinned by digest declares publish

docs.title: External dependencies
docs.text:
A vendor API, managed cloud service or legacy host the folder names is a dependencies[<name>] field with an external member, one per identity, or per identity and resource name for a managed resource whose account, region or id the folder does not show. The field's value is the identity, its source the first place that names it and its confidence the strongest source's. inputs.catalog lists the digest of each catalog that classified, default first:

inputs:
  catalog:
    - default sha256:62a3fd52...
fields:
  - field: dependencies[stripe]
    value: stripe
    source: chart/values.yaml:9
    confidence: likely
    external:
      identity: stripe
      catalog: default              # the catalog that classified it: default or organization
      sources:                      # sorted; every file is also in inputs.sources
        - {kind: helmValues, path: chart/values.yaml, line: 9, key: STRIPE_API_BASE, host: api.stripe.com}
        - {kind: sdk, path: requirements.txt, line: 1}
      client: {sdk: stripe, major: 11}   # major left out when no lockfile or exact range gives it
  - field: dependencies[newsletter-signups]
    value: aws/sqs
    source: infra/main.tf:1
    confidence: possible
    external:
      identity: aws/sqs
      catalog: default
      sources:
        - {kind: terraform, path: infra/main.tf, line: 1, key: aws_sqs_queue.signups}
      resource: {type: aws_sqs_queue, name: newsletter-signups, missing: [account, region]}
  • kind is env, configMap, secretKeyRef, secretRef, helmValues, compose, kustomize, sdk, terraform or crossplane.
  • host is a host and an optional port, key a configuration key name and path a relative path inside the folder. Pacto refuses a record that holds a user name, a password, a query or a path outside the folder in any of them.
  • missing names only account, region and id; the external catalog reference says when a managed resource gets its full identity.
  • How pacto init finds them is in External dependencies.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
When pacto ci raises an older pactoVersion in memory, the bundle's record says so. A record can hold migrations and an empty fields:

format: pacto.inferred/v1
inputs:
  commit: 4e1a9c0d...
  pacto: 4.6.0
  discovery: "1"
  sources: []
fields: []
migrations:
  - from: "2.4"                # the version pacto.yaml declares in your folder
    to: "2.5"                  # the version the bundled copy declares
    source: pacto.yaml
    by: pacto ci 4.6.0
  • Entries are sorted by source, then from. Each needs all four keys, a from and to this Pacto knows with from older than to, and a source no other entry names.
  • Every entry must match the bundle it sits in: source is a file in the bundle and the pactoVersion it declares equals to. A stale or edited entry makes the record INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID, and the fleet then shows no migration.
  • source is not listed in inputs.sources: its bytes are the raised ones.

docs.title: Cluster facts
docs.text:
A --cluster draft writes its record into the draft folder, completed from the folder and then from what the cluster showed. A cluster entry is added only for a field the folder did not give.

inputs:
  cluster:
    asOf: 2026-11-14T10:02:00Z     # when the cluster was read
    object: shop/Deployment/invoices
    callWindow: 24h
    maxItems: 10000
fields:
  - field: dependencies[ledger].compatibility
    value: compatibility unknown
    proposed: ^2.3.0
    source: cluster:fleet reported versions 2.3.1
    confidence: likely
    asOf: 2026-11-14T09:58:12Z
    completeness: partial
    declare: 'compatibility: "^2.3.0"'
coverage:                          # always in this source order
  - {source: workloads, state: complete}
  - {source: endpointslices, state: complete}
  - {source: runtime-calls, state: partial, reason: 2 of 3 nodes observed}
hidden: {services: 1, callers: 2}
Field Read from Source Recorded unless pacto.yaml A field of the table above The draft's manifests.yaml cluster:manifest <object> <file>:<n> (or <file> alone when the line was not found), or cluster:label <object> <label key> for the team label declares it, as for a folder image.digest[<container>] The running pods' image digests, sorted and joined cluster:runtime pods of <object> is never compared: a digest is never declared dependencies[<name>] A Service the pods were seen calling cluster:runtime calls from <object> declares a dependency of that name or ref dependencies[<name>].compatibility The versions the Pactos describing the called Service report cluster:fleet reported versions <v>[, <v>...] declares that dependency with a range
  • <object> is always inputs.cluster.object, the drafted workload, as <namespace>/<Kind>/<name>. A source never names another object, a value, an argument or a URL, and Pacto refuses a record whose source does.
  • asOf is required on every cluster entry, in UTC to the second. Entries from manifests.yaml and image digests carry the read time. runtime and fleet entries carry the oldest node observation they rest on.
  • completeness is complete or partial, on runtime and fleet entries only. It is partial when a node the workload ran on was not observed, when a source they rest on was cut short or failed, or when a called Service is hidden. An image digest is partial when the pods, ReplicaSets or Jobs list was cut short.
  • proposed is a range, on a dependencies[<name>].compatibility entry with a cluster:fleet source only. The dependency keeps compatibility: unknown until a person declares one.
  • coverage lists the sources workloads, pods, replicasets, jobs, services, endpointslices, pactos and runtime-calls, each complete, partial or failed. A source that is not complete has a fixed reason that names no namespace and no object: stopped at the item bound (<n>), forbidden, not found, timed out, the continue token expired, listing failed (<HTTP status>), listing failed (no response) when the API server never answered, listing failed (malformed observation), <k> of <m> nodes observed, no node runtime observations, <x> called services you may not read, the pods were not all read or no running pods observed when no pod of the workload ran on a node.
  • hidden counts the Services the workload called and the callers of its own Services that a read on behalf of a viewer drops. It never names them.
  • Bundle verification accepts these keys only beside a declaration: a bundle whose record holds a cluster source, inputs.cluster, coverage or hidden without one is INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID.

docs.title: Declaration
docs.text:
pacto declare adds a declaration block after fields. It says who declared the service, which workload it came from and which proposed ranges the signer accepted.

declaration:
  state: declared
  asker: {subject: ana@acme.com, issuer: https://accounts.google.com, class: human}
  inferredFrom: k8s:billing/Deployment/invoices
  cluster: 3f1c0b6e-...
  baseline:
    version: 1.4.0
    bundle: ghcr.io/acme/invoices@sha256:...
    deploy: ghcr.io/acme/invoices-deploy@sha256:...
  accepted:
    - {field: dependencies[ledger].compatibility, range: ^2.3.0}
  draft: {tag: draft-3, digest: sha256:..., asker: {subject: "", issuer: none, class: agent}, onBehalfOf: ana}
Key Meaning state declared, signed through a person's Sigstore login, or draft, written by anyone else asker The identity that signed: subject, issuer and class (human, agent or ci). A declared record needs human, a draft never has it. An unsigned draft has exactly {subject: "", issuer: none, class: agent}, a draft signed with a key {subject: "", issuer: key, class: agent}, and a draft whose token names no readable identity has issuer unknown onBehalfOf On a draft only: the person an agent asserts it acts for, never verified inferredFrom The inferred service it came from, k8s:<namespace>/<Kind>/<name> cluster The uid of the cluster's kube-system namespace, left out when it could not be read baseline The published version it starts from, its bundle and its deploy artifact, each pinned by digest accepted On a declared record only: each proposed range the signer accepted, which pacto.yaml declares requested On a draft only: each proposed range the agent asks a person to accept draft On a declared record that accepted a draft: the draft's tag, digest, signer and onBehalfOf
  • Validation checks the block against pacto.yaml: each accepted or requested range is the declared compatibility (DECLARATION_ACCEPTED_MISMATCH), and each other proposed range stays unknown (DECLARATION_RANGE_NOT_ACCEPTED). A draft's pacto.yaml declares the ranges it requests; accepting it sets them back to unknown unless the person accepts them again.
  • A reader shows the cluster facts of a declared record only when the bundle carries a signature it verified naming exactly asker and its installation signer policy allows that person. Otherwise the cluster facts, coverage and hidden are dropped with DECLARATION_SIGNER_UNVERIFIED or DECLARATION_SIGNER_NOT_ALLOWED, and the answer is partial.
  • A draft is never a version: the fleet leaves it out with DECLARATION_DRAFT_IGNORED.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text:
The inferred contract of an external system holds a surface block: the hosts, ports and client majors the fleet sees of it. The bundle shows an example.

Key Meaning identity The external identity; it equals the contract's service.external (INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID otherwise) class The external class, required asOf, completeness When the surface was computed and whether the fleet snapshot was complete catalog The catalog entry that classified it: origin, digest and entry, all required when present hosts, ports, clients Each value once, with the sources that saw it, the catalog digest and firstSeen and lastSeen, both set or both left out
  • A client is <name>/<major>, such as stripe-go/76 or npm:@stripe/stripe-js/4: up to 500 letters, digits and @._~:/-, then a major of up to 9 digits.
  • A source is 1 to 253 characters with no whitespace or control character.
  • A value listed twice is INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID.

docs.title: When Pacto writes it
docs.text:
• pacto init and the MCP tool pacto_create (with pactify: true) on a folder that holds a pactoVersion: "2.5" pacto.yaml say how many values it declares and how many Pacto completed. They write no file: the record is generated, so a committed copy would go stale on the next commit.
  • An older pactoVersion is never completed, so its bundle keeps the same bytes. init says to set pactoVersion: "2.5". pacto ci completes a contract it raised in memory and adds a migrations entry.
  • A --cluster draft completes its contract and writes pacto.inferred.yaml into the draft folder, because its cluster facts cannot be read from the folder again. It keeps a record already there.
  • pacto validate, pacto diff, pacto explain, pacto impact and pacto fleet --local compute the record in memory for a local folder.
  • pacto pack, pacto push and pacto publish put a fresh record into the bundle and replace any copy in the folder. With nothing inferred, the bundle holds no record.
  • Validation refuses a record beside an older pactoVersion (NEEDS_PACTO_2_5), and one that is malformed or cites a file the bundle lacks or holds with another digest (INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID).

docs.title: Publishing again
docs.text:
When a published tag differs from the new bundle only in its inferred record, and both records cite the same files with the same digests, pacto publish reports the bundle as adopted (only the inferred record differs ... not republished). Pacto first checks that the tag is signed by the identity in publish.sign, or the CI token's identity when it declares none. An unsigned tag, or one signed by someone else, is a conflict that needs the next version.

The cited files are part of the bundle, so editing one changes the bundle and needs a new version. When the declared files match but the record cites a different set of files, for example after a newer Pacto reads more of the folder, the plan asks for a patch version. A record whose digests do not match its own bundle never counts as a record-only change. A contract with publish.artifacts takes a patch on every new commit, because each artifact is built from that commit.

docs.title: Reading it
docs.text:
• pacto explain lists each inferred field with its source under Inferred (not part of the contract), then the YAML to copy into pacto.yaml to declare them.
  • pacto diff classifies every change in the record as NON_BREAKING, so it never asks for more than a patch.
  • The operational graph reads a dependency in the record as an inferred relationship with compatibility: unknown. Impact counts its consumer with confidence inferred, so a breaking change reads unverified and never clear. Dependents and the dashboard's expected dependencies list declared ones only.
  • The dashboard shows inferred values in a collapsed Inferred by Pacto block on the service page, or in its Where the values come from fold when the revision carries a declaration, and in the Inferred block of a revision. A mark beside each value gives its source and confidence.
  • A record Pacto cannot read or verify shows as "Pacto could not read the inferred record", never as an empty list, and the fleet answer is partial.

docs.title: Contract overrides
docs.text:
Overrides change contract values at the command line without editing pacto.yaml, the same way Helm values work:

pacto validate . --set service.version=2.0.0 -f values-prod.yaml

Overrides are available on all commands that take a contract reference: validate, explain, doc, generate, graph, pack, push and lock. The two commands that take a pair of contracts (diff, impact) use the prefixed flags in Diff overrides. See the CLI reference for the complete command and flag listing.

docs.title: Override flags
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --values <file> -f Merge a YAML values file into the contract --set <key=value> Set an individual value using dot-notation

Note

On pacto push, -f is the shorthand for --force, so spell out --values.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Overrides follow the same precedence logic as Helm (lowest to highest):

  1. Base pacto.yaml
  2. Values files (-f), in the order they are specified
  3. --set values

Later sources override earlier ones. Multiple -f flags apply in order, and the last file wins for any conflicting key.

docs.title: --set type inference
docs.text:
--set key=value infers the value's type from the string, trying in order: integer (int64) → float (float64) → boolean → string. The first parse that succeeds wins, and a value that matches none stays a string. For example:

  • --set readiness.minScore=80 → integer 80; --set ratio=1.5 → float 1.5.
  • --set flag=true → boolean true (but --set flag=1 → integer 1).
  • A multi-dot semver like --set service.version=1.0.0 has two dots, so it matches none of the numeric or boolean types and stays a string. A two-segment value like 1.0 parses as the float 1.0. Set values that must stay strings in a -f values file with explicit YAML typing.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Override the service version
pacto validate my-service --set service.version=2.0.0

# Use a values file for environment-specific overrides
pacto validate my-service -f staging-values.yaml

# Combine both (--set takes precedence over -f)
pacto validate my-service -f staging-values.yaml --set service.version=3.0.0

# Set configuration values validated against the config schema
pacto validate my-service --set configurations[0].values.DB_HOST=localhost

# Set array elements using bracket notation
pacto validate my-service --set interfaces[0].visibility=internal

Configurations as composable claims shows a worked per-environment layout: one values file per environment, the array-replacement caveat and this precedence rule applied end to end.

docs.title: Diff overrides
docs.text:
diff and impact each take two contract references, an old one and a new one. To override each side independently, use these prefixed flags:

Flag Description --old-values <file> Values file for the old (first) contract --old-set <key=value> Set value for the old contract --new-values <file> Values file for the new (second) contract --new-set <key=value> Set value for the new contract 
# Override only the new contract
pacto diff oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc-pacto:1.0.0 my-service --new-set service.version=2.0.0

# Override both contracts
pacto diff old-service new-service \
  --old-values old-env.yaml \
  --new-values new-env.yaml \
  --new-set service.version=3.0.0

# The same four flags work on impact
pacto impact old-service new-service --new-set service.version=2.0.0

docs.title: Schema validation
docs.text:
Every command validates the contract against the Pacto JSON Schema after it applies overrides, so every command rejects invalid enum values, unknown fields and type mismatches.

# Rejected: "invalid" is not a valid enum value for state.type
pacto explain my-service --set state.type=invalid

# Rejected: "unknownField" is not defined in the schema
pacto doc my-service --set service.unknownField=value

docs.title: Publish
docs.text: publish says what a service publishes, where each artifact goes and how it is built. Only pacto publish and pacto ci --publish read it. Leave it out and pacto ci --publish derives one from the folder. The other sections are in Contract sections, Configuration and policy, Dependencies and state and Readiness.

docs.title: publish
docs.text:
Optional. Needs pactoVersion: "2.1": a 2.0 contract with a publish section fails validation with NEEDS_PACTO_2_1. Every other 2.0 contract keeps working unchanged. Pacto core older than 4.1.0 and operator older than 6.1.0 reject a 2.1 contract, and that includes your consumers. Once you publish a 2.1 bundle, a consumer on an older Pacto or operator fails to resolve it as a dependency. Have your consumers upgrade first.

pactoVersion: "2.1"
service: {name: payments, version: 2.4.0}  # every tag is this version
publish:
  bundle: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/payments  # the contract bundle
  deploy: manifests                          # the artifact an applier deploys
  artifacts:
    - name: api
      type: image
      ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/payments       # no tag
      build:
        command: [./hack/build-image.sh]     # an OCI layout to $PACTO_OUT, and the SBOM
