      sbom: sbom/api.spdx.json               # sbom/ is listed in .pactoignore
    - name: manifests
      type: manifests
      ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/deploy/payments
      build:
        command: [./hack/render.sh]          # writes a directory to $PACTO_OUT
  sign: {key: cosign.key}
Field Meaning bundle Required. The repository the contract bundle goes to, as oci://host/path with no tag deploy The name of the manifests or chart artifact any applier deploys. Pacto adds the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/contract annotation to it and tags it last artifacts[].name Unique. Later builds see the digest as PACTO_DIGEST_<NAME> (upper case, - becomes _) artifacts[].type image, chart or manifests artifacts[].ref The repository, as oci://host/path with no tag artifacts[].build Deprecated in pactoVersion: "2.5", where it is optional: leave it out and pacto ci --publish detects the build, the folder's build tool for an image and Pacto's own assembly for manifests or a chart. A 2.5 contract that declares it gets a PUBLISH_BUILD_DEPRECATED warning; an older contract without it fails with NEEDS_PACTO_2_5 artifacts[].build.dockerfile context, optional file and platforms. Runs docker buildx into an OCI image layout. Images only. Deprecated in 2.5 artifacts[].build.command A command run in the contract directory that writes the artifact to $PACTO_OUT: an OCI image layout for an image, one .tgz for a chart, files for manifests artifacts[].sbom The SPDX (.spdx.json) or CycloneDX (.cdx.json) JSON file the build writes, relative to the contract directory. Pacto attaches it to the image and signs it. The image's build command must write it, for example with syft dir:. -o spdx-json=sbom/api.spdx.json inside the command. Pacto refuses a file older than the build, and refuses sbom on a dockerfile build because that build writes no SBOM. A path inside the contract directory must be in .pactoignore (publish --plan names the line). Images only sign Exactly one of keyless: true, key (a PEM key file, such as a cosign key) or kms (a KMS key URI, which needs a pacto built with -tags kms). transparencyLog: false keeps signatures out of the public log (pacto init --from <golden path> --no-transparency-log writes it); keyless signing refuses it. Optional: without sign, Pacto signs keyless as the identity the CI's OIDC token names (Signing) sign.identity, sign.issuer Required with keyless: true: the certificate identity the signature carries and its OIDC issuer. Pacto keeps or adopts only what this identity signed

Builders write to $PACTO_OUT and Pacto does all the pushing. It pushes every artifact to a new tag, signs each digest with Sigstore and stamps org.opencontainers.image.version and org.opencontainers.image.revision on each manifest it pushes. deploy names a manifests or chart artifact, never an image.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text: readiness is a checklist a team fills in about its own service, such as "we have a runbook" or "we load-tested it". Pacto turns it into a score and flags it when the score is too low or the assessment has expired. The other sections are in Contract sections, Configuration and policy and Dependencies and state.

docs.title: readiness
docs.text:
Optional. A pactoVersion: "2.0" feature. Declares operational readiness state for the service in a provider-neutral way. Each claim has a completion status, optional category and weight. The assessment includes an expiry date and scoring configuration. Pacto computes a readiness score from claim statuses and weights.

Readiness is a declared self-assessment: it records what the service's authors say they have done. Pacto checks the arithmetic and the expiry. The underlying work stays the authors' claim. Compliance is a separate verdict, decided from observed evidence about a running workload. The dashboard shows readiness on a revision and as a Needs attention category, and keeps it out of compliance verdicts.

readiness:
  expires: "2027-06-30"  # assessment-level expiry (YYYY-MM-DD)
  minScore: 80           # gate: the derived score must be >= this (omitted ⇒ 100)
  partialCredit: 0.5     # weight multiplier for partial claims (omitted ⇒ 0.5)

  claims:
    - id: dashboard
      type: url
      status: done
      category: observability
      weight: 20
      evidence: https://grafana.example.com/d/service-dashboard
      description: Main production dashboard

    - id: runbook
      type: document
      status: partial
      category: documentation
      weight: 15
      evidence: docs/runbook.md
      description: Incident runbook exists but missing escalation procedures

    - id: security-review
      type: ticket
      status: not-done
      category: security
      weight: 25
      evidence: JIRA-1234
      description: Security assessment pending

    - id: legacy-cleanup
      type: ticket
      status: deferred
      category: code-quality
      weight: 10
      evidence: TECH-5678
      description: Post-launch cleanup task

  history:
    - date: "2026-12-15"
      version: 1.0.0
      author: alice
      description: Initial readiness assessment

readiness.expires, readiness.claims[] and per-claim status are required when readiness is present. readiness.minScore, readiness.partialCredit and readiness.history[] are optional.

readiness fields:

Field Type Required Constraints expires string Yes Assessment-level expiry as a strict YYYY-MM-DD date. If the current date is past this date, ALL claims earn 0 weight regardless of status. Parsing is exact round-trip: zero-padded fields required and the value must re-serialize unchanged, so 2026-1-1, RFC 3339 timestamps and impossible dates (for example 2026-02-30) are rejected. minScore integer No Gate threshold on the same 0–100 scale as the score. Omitted ⇒ 100 (every claim must be complete). Checked by pacto validate --readiness and the operator. partialCredit number No Multiplier for partial status claims (0.0–1.0). Omitted ⇒ 0.5 (half credit). claims Claim[] Yes At least one claim. history HistoryEntry[] No Audit trail of readiness assessment changes.

docs.title: Claim fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Constraints id string Yes Stable readiness requirement id. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?$. Unique within the contract. Policies usually target this field. type string Yes Enum: url, document, ticket, report, artifact, identifier, other. Evidence type. status string Yes Enum: done, partial, not-done, deferred. Completion state for the claim. category string No Enum: architecture, testing, code-quality, observability, security, documentation, infrastructure, ci-cd, deployment, resilience, backup-recovery, incident-response, compliance, other. Categorizes the requirement type. weight integer Yes Contribution to the readiness score. Range 0–100. evidence string Yes Where the evidence lives: a URL, a bundle-relative file path, a ticket ID or any other string. Pacto checks only that it is non-empty. It never fetches the value, resolves a path or verifies that the target exists, so the evidence is your claim. interfaces[].ref and configurations[].schema, by contrast, must exist in the bundle. description string No Optional human-readable explanation (non-blank when present).

docs.title: History entry
docs.text:
Field Type Required Constraints date string Yes Date of the change as YYYY-MM-DD. version string Yes Contract version at the time of the change. Non-blank. author string Yes Person or system that made the change. Non-blank. description string Yes Description of what changed.

The service owner is declared at the contract level, so readiness claims carry no per-claim owner. Tooling computes the readiness score (pacto explain, the dashboard and the operator) from claim statuses, weights, the assessment expiry and the current time. The contract stores no score.

docs.title: Readiness score and gate
docs.text:
If assessment is expired (today > readiness.expires):
  score = 0

Otherwise:
  earnedWeight = sum of earned weights for all in-scope claims
    - deferred claims: excluded from both numerator and denominator
    - done: full weight
    - partial: round(weight × partialCredit)
    - not-done: 0

  totalWeight = sum of weights for all in-scope claims (excluding deferred)
  score = round(earnedWeight / totalWeight × 100)

passing = score >= minScore          # minScore defaults to 100

Worked example. Using the four claims from the example above (weights 20, 15, 25, 10):

  • legacy-cleanup has status: deferred → excluded from both numerator and denominator
  • In-scope weights: 20 + 15 + 25 = 60 (total)
  • dashboard (done, weight 20) → earns 20
  • runbook (partial, weight 15) → earns round(15 × 0.5) = 8
  • security-review (not-done, weight 25) → earns 0
  • Earned weight: 20 + 8 + 0 = 28
  • Score: round(28 / 60 × 100) = round(46.7) = 47

Weights are relative. The score normalizes by totalWeight, so only the ratio of weights matters. A weight of 20 reads as "20%" only when the weights sum to 100. Weights can sum to any value. When they sum to 100, each one reads as a percentage. pacto explain and the dashboard show each claim's normalized contribution.

The gate (minScore) is a readiness threshold. With minScore: 80 you require 80% weighted completion, and a lower score fails the gate. Tooling evaluates the gate separately from contract validity:

  • pacto explain shows Gate: PASS/FAIL (score N / minScore M).
  • pacto validate --readiness (off by default) fails when score < minScore. It is opt-in because it depends on the current time, which would make plain validate non-deterministic.
  • The operator sets status.readiness.passing and the ReadinessSatisfied condition from the same rule.

Because minScore is an authored literal, a policy can require it org-wide, for example readiness.minScore >= 80. Presence rules live in policies and the threshold lives here.

docs.title: Requiring claims with policies
docs.text:
The base schema requires no specific claim. You express organizational standards as policies using standard JSON Schema. For example, to require a dashboard claim with status: done, category: observability and weight >= 20:

{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["readiness"],
  "properties": {
    "readiness": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["claims"],
      "properties": {
        "claims": {
          "type": "array",
          "contains": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": ["id", "status", "category", "weight"],
            "properties": {
              "id": { "const": "dashboard" },
              "status": { "const": "done" },
              "category": { "const": "observability" },
              "weight": { "minimum": 20 }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Combine multiple contains under allOf to require several claims (for example dashboard, runbook and security-review). JSON Schema cannot express some constraints, such as "total weight must equal 100", and Pacto has no other policy engine for them yet.

docs.title: Contract sections
docs.text: The fields that name a service, say who owns it and list what it exposes: pactoVersion, service, interfaces, capabilities, metadata and extensions. Configuration and policy are in Configuration and policy; dependencies and state are in Dependencies and state; readiness is in Readiness.

docs.title: pactoVersion
docs.text:
The contract specification version: "2.0", "2.1", "2.2", "2.3", "2.4" or "2.5".

  • 2.1 adds publish, checks, external dependencies and the mcp interface type.
  • 2.2 adds the interface lifecycle, an interface's compatibilityEpoch, its guarantees and dependencies[].requires.
  • 2.3 adds environments.
  • 2.4 adds service.domain, service.offering, service.summary, the service lifecycle, service.template and service.origin, and values and a configuration selector beside a configuration ref.
  • 2.5 makes pactoVersion, service, service.name and service.version optional (see the smallest contract), derives a dependency name from its ref, defaults required to true, accepts compatibility: unknown and adds an interface port and breaks.

Each version accepts every contract of the version before it. Versions lists the Pacto core and operator releases each version needs.

pactoVersion: "2.0"

The version picks the JSON Schema the contract is validated against: pacto-v2.0.schema.json, pacto-v2.1.schema.json, pacto-v2.2.schema.json, pacto-v2.3.schema.json, pacto-v2.4.schema.json or pacto-v2.5.schema.json. Any other value fails to load with PARSE_ERROR (unsupported pactoVersion "3.0"; supported: 2.0, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5). See Validation layers.

docs.title: service
docs.text:
Identifies the service. A "2.5" contract may leave out service, name and version; see the smallest contract.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes (2.0 to 2.4) Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$ version string Yes (2.0 to 2.4) Parses as semver (for example 2.1.0). See the note below owner OwnerInfo No Object only (string form removed) domain string No Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$, at most 63 characters. pactoVersion 2.4 offering string No Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$, at most 63 characters. pactoVersion 2.4 summary string No 1 to 200 characters on one line with no control characters. pactoVersion 2.4 lifecycle object No pactoVersion 2.4. See service lifecycle template object No pactoVersion 2.4. See golden path template origin object No pactoVersion 2.4. See service origin external string No The canonical identity of the external system the contract describes, for example stripe or host/corp-legacy.example; the dependencies[].identity pattern, at most 253 characters. pactoVersion 2.5

service carries identity only. The contract has no image or chart field: how you build and deploy a service is a delivery concern that lives outside the contract.

version is parsed leniently, so write it strictly

Pacto accepts any version that Masterminds/semver can parse. That parser fills in the parts you leave out and accepts a leading v, so 1, 0.1 and v0.1 all validate and all mean 0.1.0-style coerced versions. 1.2.3.4, abc, a capital V1.0.0 and anything with surrounding whitespace are rejected with INVALID_SEMVER.

Later steps keep the coerced string as written, so that string is what gets published. pacto push tags the artifact with the literal string, and two contracts written 1 and 1.0.0 become two different tags of the same version. Write the full MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and skip the v.

docs.title: Business domain
docs.text:
service.domain names the business domain the service belongs to, such as payments. The operational graph groups services by it. Use the same value in every contract of the domain. The value is a lowercase slug, so Payments and payments can never become two domains.

pactoVersion: "2.4"
service:
  name: payments-service
  version: 2.1.2
  domain: payments

The business domain differs from the registry path in a service's key, such as ghcr.io/acme, which the dashboard shows as Registry. A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets domain reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4.

docs.title: Platform offering
docs.text: service.offering names the kind of offering a service provides to other teams, such as postgresql or shared-config. The operational graph lists providers of the same offering together. The value is an open lowercase slug: a new kind of offering needs no change to Pacto. The offering is unrelated to capabilities, which are assertions the service makes about itself.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
service.summary is a one-line purpose that the graph shows next to the service, such as on an offering's provider list.

pactoVersion: "2.4"
service:
  name: postgresql
  version: 16.0.1
  offering: postgresql
  summary: Primary relational database for transactional data

A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets offering or summary reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4.

docs.title: Service lifecycle
docs.text:
service.lifecycle retires a whole service on a schedule its consumers can see, with the fields of the interface lifecycle:

pactoVersion: "2.4"
service:
  name: postgresql
  version: 16.1.0
  offering: postgresql
  lifecycle:
    deprecated: "2026-11-01"
    sunset: "2027-06-30"
    successor: oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/postgresql:17.0.0
Field Type Required Constraints deprecated string Yes YYYY-MM-DD. The date the service was deprecated sunset string No YYYY-MM-DD, not before deprecated. The date from which the service may be retired successor string No An absolute URL, such as the oci:// reference of the service that replaces this one

Consumers that reach the service through a dependency or a configuration reference are warned with DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_DEPRECATED, then DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_SUNSET from the sunset date; see Validation layers. pacto diff reports the schedule (change classification). A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets lifecycle reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4.

docs.title: Golden path template
docs.text:
service.template marks the contract as a golden path, which pacto init --from copies into a new service:

pactoVersion: "2.4"
service:
  name: http-service
  version: 1.0.0
  owner: {team: platform}
  summary: An HTTP API on the platform runtime with a PostgreSQL database and the HTTP baseline policy
  template:
    plugins:
      - name: dockerfile
        description: A Dockerfile for a Go HTTP service
      - name: github-actions
        description: A CI workflow that validates and publishes the contract
        options: {go-version: "1.27"}
Field Type Required Constraints plugins array No 1 to 32 generate plugins a person may run when they create a service. template may be {} plugins[].name string Yes Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$, at most 63 characters. Pacto runs the pacto-plugin-<name> binary it finds. Listed once: a repeat reports DUPLICATE_TEMPLATE_PLUGIN plugins[].description string No 1 to 200 characters on one line with no control characters plugins[].options map of string No At most 32 entries, each value at most 1024 characters. Passed to the plugin
  • service.summary describes the golden path.
  • Creation removes the path's service.offering, and the operational graph gives a golden path no offering membership.

docs.title: Service origin
docs.text:
service.origin records the golden path a service was created from:

pactoVersion: "2.4"
service:
  name: gift-cards
  version: 0.1.0
  owner: {team: checkout}
  domain: commerce
  origin:
    ref: oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/http-service:1.0.0
    digest: sha256:077937b6249c6a7e1e47d7affdc54e6d4c57c14f3e339e0092d43a12b2659649
Field Type Required Constraints ref string Yes 1 to 512 characters with no control characters. An oci:// reference or a directory path: any other scheme or an oci:// reference that does not parse reports INVALID_ORIGIN_REF digest string Yes Pattern: ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$. The content digest of the golden path bundle, as pacto.lock records it
  • pacto init --from and pacto_create write it, and the graph shows it labelled declared.
  • A golden path derived from another golden path sets both fields.
  • Changes to either field are non-breaking (change classification).
  • A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets template or origin reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4.

docs.title: OwnerInfo
docs.text:
Structured ownership metadata. All fields are optional but at least one must be present. The field you set decides the canonical owner key that the graph groups by. See Ownership and the canonical owner key.

Field Type Required Constraints team string No The team's bare name, such as billing: usually the team label on its workloads. pacto init and pacto_check flag a team/ prefix dri string No Directly Responsible Individual contacts OwnerContact[] No Contact points

docs.title: OwnerContact
docs.text:
Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes One of: email, url, group, oncall, chat, other value string Yes Non-empty purpose string No One of: ownership, support, escalation, oncall, notifications

Examples:

# Structured form (the owner is always an object)
service:
  owner:
    team: foundations
    dri: eduardo.diaz
    contacts:
      - type: email
        value: foundations@acme.com
        purpose: ownership
      - type: chat
        value: "#foundations"

# Minimal object form (at least one field required)
service:
  owner:
    team: payments

docs.title: interfaces
docs.text:
Declares the service's communication boundaries. Optional: a service with no network interfaces, such as a batch job or shared library, can omit this section. The ref field points at the spec you already publish: an OpenAPI document, an AsyncAPI document, a gRPC service descriptor or the MCP tools a service exposes. Pacto reads that spec in place.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Non-empty. Must be unique across interfaces type string Yes Enum: openapi, asyncapi, grpc, mcp (2.1) ref string Yes Non-empty. Path to the spec file within the bundle visibility string No Enum: public, internal. Default: internal lifecycle object No 2.2. See interface lifecycle guarantees object No 2.2. Behavior consumers may rely on. See Guarantees compatibilityEpoch integer No 2.2. Minimum 0. Default: 0. See Compatibility epoch port integer No 2.5. 1 to 65535. The port the interface listens on. Several interfaces may share one port

docs.title: Interface types
docs.text:
Value Spec kind openapi OpenAPI document for HTTP/REST traffic asyncapi AsyncAPI document for event-driven communication grpc gRPC service descriptor mcp The tools a service such as an AI agent exposes, as an MCP tools/list result. See an agent is a service

Note

Interface names must be unique within a contract. Every interface requires a non-empty ref (SCHEMA_VIOLATION otherwise), and the referenced file must exist in the bundle (FILE_NOT_FOUND otherwise). A .json, .yaml or .yml ref must also parse (INVALID_INTERFACE_SPEC otherwise). For any other extension, such as a gRPC .proto, Pacto checks only that the file exists. pacto diff reports a declared or dropped port as non-breaking and a moved one as potentially breaking. Declare health and metrics endpoints as capabilities.

docs.title: Interface lifecycle
docs.text:
A provider retires an interface on a schedule its consumers can see. A lifecycle marks the interface deprecated:

interfaces:
  - name: orders-v1
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/orders-v1.yaml
    lifecycle:
      deprecated: "2026-10-01"
      sunset: "2027-04-01"
      successor: orders-v2
  - name: orders-v2
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/orders-v2.yaml
Field Type Required Constraints deprecated string Yes YYYY-MM-DD. The date the interface was deprecated sunset string No YYYY-MM-DD, not before deprecated. The date from which the interface may be removed successor string No Another interface of this service, or an absolute URL such as an oci:// reference to another service

pacto validate --closure warns a consumer about each deprecated interface of the services it depends on; see Dependency closure. A dependency names a service and not an interface, so the consumer is warned about every deprecated interface of that service. pacto diff reports the schedule; see change classification.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
guarantees declares the behavior a consumer may rely on, in a closed vocabulary: an unknown key fails to load.

Guarantee Value For Stronger value delivery at-most-once or at-least-once events Neither: they trade loss for duplicates ordering per-key or global events global, which also orders every key dedupeWindow duration events Longer retention duration events Longer idempotent boolean calls true timeout duration calls Shorter profile "1" both The vocabulary version. Omitted means 1

A duration is written like 500ms, 5m or 168h.

interfaces:
  - name: order-events
    type: asyncapi
    ref: interfaces/events.yaml
    guarantees:
      delivery: at-least-once
      ordering: per-key
      dedupeWindow: 10m
      retention: 168h

A consumer lists what it relies on in dependencies[].requires. pacto diff classifies a removed or weakened guarantee as breaking.

docs.title: Compatibility epoch
docs.text:
Raise compatibilityEpoch when an interface's behavior changes incompatibly while its spec stays the same, for example when an amount field switches from cents to euros. pacto diff reports the change as BREAKING with the interface's name in the reason, so pacto impact lists the consumers to review.

interfaces:
  - name: payments-api
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/openapi.yaml
    compatibilityEpoch: 2

An epoch only goes up. Lowering it is also BREAKING, because consumers that adapted to the higher epoch break in turn. A "2.0" or "2.1" contract that sets it reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_2.

docs.title: Interfaces at runtime
docs.text:
The Kubernetes operator checks two fields of a running interface: type and visibility.

  • type. The operator sends a probe to the port and looks at the protocol that answers. openapi accepts HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 and grpc accepts HTTP/2. Anything else is INTERFACE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH. A TLS port, no answer and asyncapi stay unverified.
  • visibility (internal when omitted). It is contradicted only when the operator sees an address outside private networks: a public externalIPs entry, or a LoadBalancer Service (without an internal load balancer annotation) or an Ingress whose status carries a public IP or hostname. That is INTERFACE_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH. A NodePort Service, an internal or address-less load balancer and an HTTPRoute leave exposure unknown, so the field stays unverified. A public interface seen only in-cluster also stays unverified, because a gateway the operator cannot see may expose it.

A field the operator cannot check leaves the contract status unchanged. See Runtime conformance.

docs.title: capabilities
docs.text:
Optional. Declares standard observability capabilities (health, metrics) or custom extension capabilities. Use this section to tell the platform that a service exposes health and metrics endpoints.

Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes Enum: health, metrics, extension ref string Conditional Required for extension only. A namespaced identifier (e.g. example.com/custom). Not allowed for health/metrics binding Binding No Standard types only (health/metrics). Binds the endpoint to a declared interface. Not allowed for extension

docs.title: Capability binding
docs.text:
Binds a standard capability endpoint (health/metrics) to a declared interface so a collector can probe it. binding.type is a closed set and http is the only supported transport in this release. Any other transport fails structural validation.

A binding resolves as follows:

  • binding.type: http means the capability is probed over HTTP.
  • binding.interface names the declared interface that provides the address and port for the probe. It is the platform-neutral counterpart of the Kubernetes CR's spec.target.interfaceBindings[].interface, which resolves to a concrete Kubernetes Service port. The capability path is independent of that interface's OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or gRPC specification.
  • binding.path is relative to the resolved endpoint.
Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes Enum: http (only supported transport; any other value fails validation) interface string Yes Must match a declared interfaces[].name: the interface whose platform binding provides the address and port (CAPABILITY_INTERFACE_UNKNOWN otherwise) path string No Application path relative to the resolved endpoint. Must start with a single / and carry no scheme/host/fragment (CAPABILITY_PATH_INVALID otherwise) 
capabilities:
  - type: health
    binding:
      type: http
      interface: rest-api
      path: /health
  - type: metrics
    binding:
      type: http
      interface: rest-api
      path: /metrics
  - type: extension
    ref: example.com/tracing

You can declare a health or metrics capability with no binding. Another collector can verify that declaration. The Kubernetes integration reports an unbound capability as Unsupported/Unknown because it has no endpoint to probe. An extension capability requires a namespaced ref and cannot declare a binding. Pacto has no evaluator for extensions, so it lists each one in coverage.unverified as capabilities[ref=<ref>] and excludes it from required assertions. A contract that declares one can still reach Compliant, and that verdict covers none of its extensions.

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
Optional. Free-form key-value pairs for organizational use. Pacto validates only the type.

metadata:
  team: payments
  tier: critical
  on-call: "#payments-oncall"

The schema sets additionalProperties: false at every level except inside metadata, so an unknown field fails validation.

Tip

metadata is a deliberate extension point for tooling. Platform teams use it to attach signals that their CI or deployment systems read from a contract. Provisioning adapters map a provider's service.offering to their implementation, so infrastructure contracts need no provider labels. See Infrastructure contracts.

docs.title: extensions
docs.text:
Optional. A free-form object for forward-compatible, namespaced extension data outside the core contract model. Use metadata for organizational key-value pairs and extensions for structured data that future Pacto features or third-party tools interpret. Namespace each key, for example with a domain, to avoid collisions. In this release Pacto validates only the type.

extensions:
  example.com/custom-tool:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Validation layers
docs.text:
pacto validate tells you whether a contract is well-formed before anyone relies on it. Run it in the bundle directory:

pacto validate .

It runs three checks in order and then the configuration-refs stage and the environments stage, and so does anything else that has to trust a contract. pack, push and publish refuse before they write or transmit a byte, and the operator revalidates every bundle it loads. Each layer short-circuits: if it fails, the layers after it are skipped, so one broken field can hide the rest. A failed configuration-refs stage skips nothing.

docs.title: Layer 1: Structural (JSON Schema)
docs.text:
Validates against the embedded schema of the contract's version, pacto-v2.0.schema.json, pacto-v2.1.schema.json, pacto-v2.2.schema.json, pacto-v2.3.schema.json, pacto-v2.4.schema.json or pacto-v2.5.schema.json:

  • Field types match
  • Required fields are present (including the mandatory required on configurations[] and dependencies[])
  • Enum values are valid (for example interface type is openapi/asyncapi/grpc/mcp, capabilities[].type is health/metrics/extension, policies[].target is contract)
  • Fields that must carry a value are non-empty (for example interfaces[].ref and checks[].file)
  • Discriminated shapes hold: a configurations[] entry has exactly one of schema or ref, a capabilities[] extension requires a namespaced ref and health or metrics sets no ref
  • State invariants hold (stateless requires ephemeral durability)
  • A pacto.inferred.yaml in the bundle parses, and every file it cites is in the bundle with the digest it records, and a surface section names the identity service.external names (INFERRED_RECORD_INVALID)
  • A declaration in that record agrees with pacto.yaml: each range it accepts or requests is the declared compatibility (DECLARATION_ACCEPTED_MISMATCH), and each other proposed range stays unknown (DECLARATION_RANGE_NOT_ACCEPTED)

Structural failures report SCHEMA_VIOLATION. A field a later version adds, in an older contract, reports that version's code for each use instead: set pactoVersion to that version, which keeps every older field.

Field Version Code publish, checks, an external dependency, an mcp interface "2.1" NEEDS_PACTO_2_1 An interface lifecycle, compatibilityEpoch or guarantees, a dependency requires "2.2" NEEDS_PACTO_2_2 environments "2.3" NEEDS_PACTO_2_3 service.domain, service.offering, service.summary, service.lifecycle, service.template, service.origin, values or a configuration selector beside a configuration ref "2.4" NEEDS_PACTO_2_4 service.external, a dependency compatibility: unknown or identity, an interface port, breaks, a pacto.inferred.yaml in the bundle "2.5" NEEDS_PACTO_2_5 No field: the contract declares a pactoVersion older than the CLI's newest any older 2.x CONTRACT_BEHIND (info, never fails pacto validate)
  • pacto validate and pacto_check report CONTRACT_BEHIND on the structural stage, in warnings, with valid and the exit code unchanged.
  • Its message says what raising pactoVersion does. Validation checks the pacto.yaml you wrote, without -f or --set values, again at the newest version. The message says the raise keeps what the contract means, or names the finding it would add (usually ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_MISSING, because from "2.4" a required configuration taken by ref has its defaults checked) or says to fix the errors the run reports before Pacto can tell.
  • When raising a contract older than "2.4" that takes a configuration by ref adds no finding, the message says the operator then also accepts ContractOverrides values for those configurations.
  • The fleet revision detail (pacto fleet entity, pacto_fleet_entity, the TUI and the dashboard revision page) shows the declared pactoVersion as 2.3 (behind 2.5). In JSON, pactoVersionCurrent is the newest version the Pacto that answered knows, and pactoVersionUnknown marks a version it does not know. A revision pacto ci raised in memory reads 2.5 (migrated from 2.4, inferred), or 2.5 (behind <newer>; migrated from 2.4, inferred) for a newer Pacto. In JSON, migratedFrom holds the version the authored pacto.yaml declared. It is inferred, read only from a verified pacto.inferred.yaml.
  • When the message says the raise keeps what the contract means, it ends with "run pacto migrate to rewrite the file". pacto migrate rewrites every behind pacto.yaml in a repository, and only in that case.
  • A 1.x contract follows MIGRATION.md and is never raised automatically.

A contract that fails to load, because of malformed YAML, an unknown field or a pactoVersion other than "2.0", "2.1", "2.2", "2.3", "2.4" or "2.5", fails before any layer runs and reports PARSE_ERROR. Loading is the parse step that turns pacto.yaml into a contract. Validation starts once it succeeds.

An absent pactoVersion reads as the newest version the CLI supports. In a "2.5" contract service, service.name and service.version may be absent too, so an empty pacto.yaml is valid. pack, push and publish write the version into the bundled pacto.yaml and refuse a contract that does not declare service.version (PUBLISH_NEEDS_SERVICE_VERSION) or service.name (PUBLISH_NEEDS_SERVICE_NAME). A bundle read from a registry, and an inline contract in a Pacto resource, must declare all three.

The operational graph drops an inferred name another service also claims (SERVICE_NAME_COLLISION). pacto impact keeps a breaking change to a contract with an inferred name unverified (SERVICE_NAME_INFERRED).

docs.title: Layer 2: Cross-field
docs.text:
Validates semantic references and consistency:

Rule Code service.version parses as semver, leniently: 1, 0.1 and v0.1 all pass INVALID_SEMVER Interface names are unique DUPLICATE_INTERFACE_NAME interfaces[].lifecycle dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD and sunset is not before deprecated INVALID_INTERFACE_LIFECYCLE interfaces[].lifecycle.successor names another interface or is an absolute URL INTERFACE_SUCCESSOR_UNKNOWN service.lifecycle dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD and sunset is not before deprecated INVALID_SERVICE_LIFECYCLE service.lifecycle.successor is an absolute URL SERVICE_SUCCESSOR_INVALID service.template.plugins[].name values are unique DUPLICATE_TEMPLATE_PLUGIN service.origin.ref is a valid oci:// reference or a directory path INVALID_ORIGIN_REF Configuration names are unique DUPLICATE_CONFIGURATION_NAME Policy names are unique DUPLICATE_POLICY_NAME Dependency names are unique DUPLICATE_DEPENDENCY_NAME Interface spec file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND Interface spec file parses, if the ref ends .json, .yaml or .yml (for any other extension, only existence is checked) INVALID_INTERFACE_SPEC An mcp interface file lists tools, each with a name used once INVALID_MCP_TOOLS Check names are unique DUPLICATE_CHECK_NAME checks[].file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND extension capability ref is well-formed CAPABILITY_REF_INVALID Each standard capability type is declared once DUPLICATE_CAPABILITY capabilities[].binding.interface matches a declared interface CAPABILITY_INTERFACE_UNKNOWN capabilities[].binding.path is a safe application path CAPABILITY_PATH_INVALID OCI dependency refs (oci://) are valid OCI references INVALID_OCI_REF A dependency has a name, or a ref its name is derived from DEPENDENCY_NAME_REQUIRED A dependency without ref is external, or from 2.5 a dependency by name DEPENDENCY_REF_REQUIRED, NEEDS_PACTO_2_5 A dependency by name gives no version VERSION_WITHOUT_REF An external dependency without ref has a version EXTERNAL_VERSION_REQUIRED compatibility appears only with ref, and version only without it COMPATIBILITY_WITHOUT_REF, VERSION_WITH_REF identity appears only on an external dependency without ref IDENTITY_WITHOUT_EXTERNAL identity and service.external are canonical external identities, other than other-egress INVALID_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY A dependency with ref has a compatibility range EMPTY_COMPATIBILITY Compatibility ranges are valid semver constraints INVALID_COMPATIBILITY OCI dependency pins a digest TAG_NOT_DIGEST (warning) configurations[].ref is a valid OCI reference INVALID_CONFIG_REF configurations[].schema file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND configurations[].schema file is valid JSON INVALID_CONFIG_JSON configurations[].schema file is valid JSON Schema INVALID_CONFIG_SCHEMA configurations[].values match the local schema (values beside a ref are checked by the configuration-refs stage) CONFIG_VALUES_VALIDATION_FAILED policies[].schema file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND policies[].schema file is valid JSON INVALID_POLICY_JSON policies[].schema file is valid JSON Schema INVALID_POLICY_SCHEMA policies[].ref is a valid OCI reference INVALID_POLICY_REF Environment names are unique DUPLICATE_ENVIRONMENT_NAME environments[].file is a path in the bundle and the file exists FILE_NOT_FOUND environments[].expires appears only with lifetime: temporary ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRES_NOT_TEMPORARY environments[].expires is an RFC 3339 time such as 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z INVALID_ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRES readiness.claims[].id are unique within the contract DUPLICATE_READINESS_ID readiness.claims[].evidence has non-whitespace content EMPTY_READINESS_EVIDENCE readiness.claims[].description (when present) has non-whitespace content EMPTY_READINESS_DESCRIPTION readiness.expires is a strict YYYY-MM-DD date INVALID_READINESS_EXPIRES readiness.history[].{date,version,author,description} are valid/non-blank INVALID_READINESS_REVISION A consumer appears in one breaks[] entry at most DUPLICATE_BREAK_CONSUMER breaks[].consumers never names the service itself BREAK_NAMES_SELF breaks[].expires is a strict YYYY-MM-DD date INVALID_BREAK_EXPIRES

This table lists the codes you can see. Layer 1 rejects the contract first and reports SCHEMA_VIOLATION wherever the JSON Schema already constrains a field. That covers the interface and capability type enums, a non-empty interfaces[].ref or dependencies[].compatibility, the configurations[] schema/ref choice, policies[].target and the stateless/ephemeral invariant. Layer 2 has its own check for each of those, but a contract that breaks them never gets past Layer 1. Build CI rules only on codes in this table.

docs.title: Layer 3: Policy checks
docs.text:
Resolves every declared policy and checks the contract against it. Policies apply with strict AND semantics: the contract must satisfy all of them. Policies have no precedence or override logic, so contradictory policies fail.

Condition Code policies[].ref cannot be resolved (resolver unavailable, network error, bundle not found) POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED Cycle detected in recursive policy resolution chain POLICY_REF_CYCLE Contract violates a policy constraint POLICY_VIOLATION policies[].ref was skipped because no resolver was configured POLICY_REF_NOT_ENFORCED (warning)

POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED is a hard error. Validation fails closed when a referenced policy cannot be resolved.

When ref-based policies are resolved. Recursive resolution of policies[].ref happens only when a resolver is configured. pacto validate and pacto push both supply one, since they can reach OCI/file refs. A ref policy that cannot be fetched then fails closed with POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED, which is how pacto push checks remote policies before publishing. pacto pack and the operator pass no resolver. They check only the locally compiled schema-based policies and skip ref policies, so they never report the unresolved error. Cycle detection is per chain: a ref is a cycle only when it reappears in its own resolution chain (A → B → A); two sibling policies pointing at the same ref resolve independently.

docs.title: Dependency closure
docs.text:
By default Layer 3 checks the root contract only. pacto validate --closure also checks every contract in the dependency closure against the policies the root resolves. Each dependency's own policies[] is left to its owner's validation. The closure resolves the same way pacto graph does, with one fetch per dependency. External dependencies carry no contract and are skipped.

Condition Code A dependency violates a policy the root resolves CLOSURE_POLICY_VIOLATION A dependency cannot be resolved, sits in a dependency cycle or has an unreadable contract CLOSURE_DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED A direct dependency declares a deprecated interface DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_DEPRECATED (warning) That interface has reached its sunset DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_SUNSET (warning) A direct dependency declares a service lifecycle DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_DEPRECATED (warning) That service has reached its sunset DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_SUNSET (warning)

A policy finding names the dependency in its path, for example dependencies[ledger@1.0.0]. A dependency that cannot be resolved is named in the message. When a dependency declared it, the path names that dependency. An unresolvable dependency fails the run, so the check fails closed.

A deprecated interface is a warning that names the interface, its sunset and its successor, with the path of the dependency that resolved to it, for example dependencies[1]. Both codes stay warnings so the verdict does not change with the date the check runs. To fail a pipeline after the sunset, gate on DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_SUNSET in --output-format json. When pacto.lock is present, the lock is verified first and a drifted closure fails with the lock error before the closure is checked.

docs.title: Configuration-references stage
docs.text:
After the policy layer, the configuration-refs stage resolves each configuration that takes its schema by ref. It fetches the referenced contract, selects one of its configurations and checks the inline values against that configuration's schema. A selected configuration that is itself a ref is followed to the end of the chain. The stage reports SKIP no configuration references for a contract without one.

Selecting a configuration describes how the stage picks a configuration from the referenced contract.

Condition Code The ref cannot be fetched, read or compiled, or its chain runs past eight refs, and something depends on it (see below) CONFIG_REF_UNRESOLVED The ref cannot be resolved and nothing depends on it, or the caller is a gate CONFIG_REF_UNVERIFIED (warning) Values for the ref were not checked because the caller has no resolver CONFIG_REF_NOT_ENFORCED (warning) The referenced contract declares several configurations and no configuration names one CONFIG_REF_AMBIGUOUS configuration names no configuration of the referenced contract, or it declares none CONFIG_REF_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION The chain of refs comes back to a ref it already followed CONFIG_REF_CYCLE A dependency on the same repository has a compatibility the resolved version is outside of CONFIG_REF_VERSION_OUTSIDE_RANGE The inline values fail the selected schema CONFIG_VALUES_VALIDATION_FAILED The referenced contract declares a service lifecycle DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_DEPRECATED (warning) That service has reached its sunset DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_SUNSET (warning)

In a "2.0" to "2.3" contract, CONFIG_REF_AMBIGUOUS and CONFIG_REF_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION are warnings, because an older contract can carry no selector, and values for that configuration stay unchecked.

Who resolves refs. pacto validate, pacto push, pacto publish and pacto_check fail closed: a ref reports CONFIG_REF_UNRESOLVED when its resolution protects a check. That is the case when the contract is 2.4, when an environment gives values for the configuration or when the contract also declares a ranged dependency on the same repository. A "2.0" to "2.3" ref with nothing to check reports CONFIG_REF_UNVERIFIED and the stage reports SKIP could not verify:. The fleet, the delivery gate and pacto doc report every unresolved ref as CONFIG_REF_UNVERIFIED and skip the stage, so a missing provider never makes a contract invalid there and never passes its values. pacto pack resolves nothing and warns CONFIG_REF_NOT_ENFORCED for each ref with values to check. The operator pulls referenced contracts itself.

Values the resolved schema rejects and selection errors in a 2.4 contract are errors for every caller: two declarations contradict each other.

docs.title: Environments stage
docs.text:
After the policy layer, the environments stage checks each environment's file against the schema of every configuration it names. It runs when the structural, cross-field and policy layers passed, whatever the configuration-refs stage reported, and reports SKIP no environments declared for a contract without environments. Environments lists the rules and the codes it reports: ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION, ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID, ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_MISSING and the ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED warning.

An error in an environment's file carries that file in file, with line and column pointing into it, also when --set or -f is given. The stage passes only when Pacto checked every value set and found no error. A configuration whose schema is behind a ref is checked against the schema the configuration-refs stage resolved. A ref that stage could not resolve leaves its values unchecked, and so does a run with no bundle files to read, such as the operator loading an inline contract. A stage with no error and an unchecked value set reports SKIP could not verify: and names each environment and configuration.

pacto validate and pacto_check also add an ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRED warning to this stage for each temporary environment whose expires is at or before the clock of the run. The stage keeps its status, and the verdict does not change with the date. Pacto deletes nothing for an expired environment: remove it with pacto_edit remove_environments or move expires. The fleet, the delivery gate and pacto doc never report this warning.
