docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• e250ce8: An empty pacto.yaml, or one line of it, is now a valid contract (pactoVersion 2.5). An absent pactoVersion reads as the newest version the CLI supports, and service, service.name and service.version may be left out. Pacto infers the service name from Chart.yaml, a Kustomization or a single-service Compose file, the org.opencontainers.image.title label, the app.kubernetes.io/name label or the folder name, and pacto validate, the fleet and the dashboard say where each inferred value came from. An inferred name that another service also claims is dropped from the operational graph with a SERVICE_NAME_COLLISION limitation, and an inferred name never clears an impact gate (SERVICE_NAME_INFERRED).

pacto pack, pacto push and pacto publish refuse a contract that does not declare service.name (PUBLISH_NEEDS_SERVICE_NAME) or service.version (PUBLISH_NEEDS_SERVICE_VERSION) and write pactoVersion into the bundled pacto.yaml. A bundle pulled from a registry, or an inline contract in a Pacto resource, that does not declare all three is rejected; the operator reports ContractUndeclared.

A dependency may leave out name, which is derived from its ref and resolves only against a provider published at that repository, and required, which defaults to true. compatibility: unknown records a range nobody decided yet: it is never read as compatible and never clears a gate or a promotion. An interface can declare its port, and breaks[] announces a deliberate breaking change to the consumers it names. Validation, pacto diff, the fleet, the dashboard, MCP and the operator status (status.interfaces[].port) read the new fields. - ca50460: Every workload a cluster runs shows up in the fleet as an inferred service, with its image, ports and probes; inferred services never satisfy a dependency or clear a gate. A new kubernetes-workloads source lists Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets and CronJobs (list only) and reads no environment variable, Secret or ConfigMap. Service records carry declaration (declared or inferred); pacto fleet entities and pacto fleet search take --declaration, the fleet MCP tools take declaration, the Overview counts inferredServices apart and the Services list shows inferred services muted with a filter. An inferred caller of a declared service stays an uncontracted caller and links to its entity. The dashboard ClusterRole and the namespace watch Role gain list on the four workload kinds, and the operator ClusterRole gains daemonsets. - bd0bdc4: Group inferred services the way the cluster already does: by Argo CD Application, Flux Kustomization or HelmRelease, Helm release or app.kubernetes.io labels, with the source repository URL and where Pacto read it. pacto fleet entities --group, pacto_fleet_entities.group and GET /api/fleet/entities?group filter by group; Data sources lists Argo CD, Flux and Helm. The dashboard role lists Argo CD Applications and Flux Kustomizations, HelmReleases and GitRepositories. Data sources also lists who promotes and who reports, from an optional fingerprints chart value and --fingerprints flag that name an installation's own workload managers and promoters; a workload one of those managers applies reads external: <product> in the Stage applier verdict, and the promoter writes no pointer for it. - bd0bdc4: Probe each registry once and record the mode Pacto uses. Delivery records now work on registries without the OCI Referrers API, such as GHCR and CNCF distribution, as one write-once, content-addressed tag per record in the streams repository; every reader reads both forms. Stages gain status.stream.registryMode and the RecordStoreReady reason WriteOnceTags; the ReferrersUnsupported reason is removed, and a Stage that recorded native is never moved to write-once tags on its own. pacto fleet providers shows a Registry <host> row for every registry an OCI source reads. - bd0bdc4: pacto impact and pacto ci find the consumers that run without cluster credentials. From the change's oci:// ref they try <host>/<first path segment>/pacto-targets, then <host>/pacto-targets, read every cluster-<uid> snapshot of the first that exists and print a Registry: line and one Targets: line per snapshot, pinned by digest. --target-snapshot (repeatable) names a repository or pins cluster tags or digests, and off reads none; --delivery-trust or $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST names the trust config. A snapshot counts only when a key whose streams name its cluster's UID verified it and its asOf is less than 15 minutes old; otherwise its source reads partial, stale or unavailable with one of TARGET_SNAPSHOT_UNVERIFIED, TARGET_SNAPSHOT_UNSCOPED, TARGET_SNAPSHOT_STALE, TARGET_SNAPSHOT_INVALID or TARGET_SNAPSHOT_BOUND, and a BREAKING change with consumers never clears. No pacto-targets repository leaves today's answer and exit code. --root in the CI recipe is now optional, for consumers that run nowhere yet.

A snapshot becomes up to three fleet sources per cluster: target-snapshot for its Pacto resources, kubernetes-workloads for its inferred services, which never count as consumers, and evidence-http for the targets its Evidence Server accepted. Source states gain ref, signer, publisher and cluster, and impact answers gain registry and targetSnapshots, also on the pacto_impact MCP tool over stdio. pacto mcp over HTTP refuses --target-snapshot. pacto delivery targets publish signs and pushes a snapshot document with a PEM key or a pacto evidence keygen seed.

The operator publishes the cluster's signed snapshot to <registry>/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid> every 5 minutes when the chart's new top-level registry value is set: the cluster's Pactos, the workloads no Pacto targets (without env values or probes) and, with evidence.enabled, the Evidence Server's targets, each with its own asOf and completeness. Give pacto-targets its own read ACL: pull on it reads every namespace's Pacto status and workload shape.

The Compose demo runs a targets service that publishes a signed snapshot of the demo cluster to registry:5000/demo/pacto-targets every 5 minutes. - e250ce8: Probing and metrics observation take auto, on or off and default to auto, which turns each one on only in namespaces whose owner labels them pacto.trianalab.io/observe with probing, metrics or probing.metrics. A namespace owner opts in with kubectl label ns payments pacto.trianalab.io/observe=probing, with no chart change, and every other namespace stays passive. The chart values are controller.probing and controller.metricsObservation; controller.enableProbing and controller.enableMetricsObservation are deprecated and still honoured, so an upgrade that reuses the earlier release's values renders the same arguments. An explicit auto overrides a deprecated true. ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor read access still comes with metricsObservation: on only.

controller.interfaceNameMatchDiscovery and nodeAgent.image are new, so every operator flag has a chart value or a documented reason, and a test keeps it that way. controller.kernelEvidence.enabled takes auto, on or "off"; false keeps following nodeAgent.enabled.

The default install gains a namespaces get grant for the label read (in each watched namespace's Role under controller.watchNamespaces). The health probe no longer follows ExternalName or selector-less Services. The RuntimeObserved message names where each setting came from, and a transient namespace read failure marks it False. - e250ce8: The operator reads no Secret across the cluster. Its ClusterRole drops secrets, and it reads pull secrets and the Secrets behind contract configurations only in the release namespace, in each watched namespace and where the new controller.secretGrants names them as namespace/name (one Role limited to each named Secret). A Secret-backed configuration it may not read reads OBSERVATION_UNSUPPORTED, and the finding names the grant to add; the collection does not fail. A pull secret outside every grant sets ContractValid=Unknown with reason PullSecretNotGranted. The operator no longer watches Secrets and reads a rotated pull secret within one check interval.

controller.watchNamespaces takes a list of namespaces and the operator takes --watch-namespaces. With a list, the chart renders Roles and RoleBindings in each namespace and no ClusterRole, unless the node agent or the dashboard's delivery views need one. controller.watchNamespace and --watch-namespace still work as deprecated aliases that join the list, also in an upgrade that reuses the earlier release's values. Moving a cluster-wide install to a list leaves the pacto-dashboard ClusterRole and binding behind: the upgrade notes and a StaleClusterRBAC Warning event name the kubectl delete command. The chart refuses an ed25519.secretName recorder key without allowOperatorReadableKey whenever a grant reaches the delivery namespace.

--namespace on pacto fleet, pacto dashboard and pacto mcp and PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE accept a comma-separated list; one value keeps working. A source that reads a list is always partial, names its scope in a K8S_NAMESPACE_SCOPED limitation and in namespaces on its source state, and names a namespace it could not read in K8S_NAMESPACE_UNREADABLE. A restricted view never names a watched namespace the reader may not read. The dashboard Overview says which namespaces the fleet watches. --review=local (or PACTO_DASHBOARD_REVIEW=local) reviews people with LocalSubjectAccessReviews in the watched namespaces only; the managed dashboard of a namespace-list install without delivery uses it.

Upgrade: list each pull secret outside the release namespace in controller.secretGrants, or add its namespace to controller.watchNamespaces, before upgrading. - e250ce8: Delivery tells people from agents by how they sign in and lets whoever may update a Stage's workload decide its held changes, with no identity values.

Upgrade effect first. An upgrade that takes the new chart's defaults turns owner-team narrowing and the ownerless protection off unless the install set delivery.identities.teamGroupPrefix explicitly: a values file through Argo CD, a Flux HelmRelease or helm upgrade -f, and the documented helm upgrade --reset-then-reuse-values. To keep the old behaviour, set delivery.identities.teamGroupPrefix: "" and delivery.identities.requireOwnerTeam: true. Plain --reuse-values keeps the old defaults ("" and true) and so keeps narrowing. The promoter emits a TeamNarrowingOff Event on each Operation it holds while narrowing is off, so the effect shows on the first held change.

  • A ServiceAccount, any other system: user and an unauthenticated request are agents; every other signed-in identity is a person. agentGroups marks automation that signs in through OIDC. The chart no longer refuses delivery with humanGroups empty: allowEmptyHumanGroups is ignored (the schema still accepts it) and humanGroups is a deprecated override.
  • Approvers need update on the Stage's workload, asked as a SubjectAccessReview by the promoter (it gains create subjectaccessreviews) and as a SelfSubjectAccessReview by the dashboard and pacto delivery approve. The same rule decides a person's unfreeze and acknowledge. Refusals read CannotUpdateWorkload and ApproverUnverified; a failed review never allows. With delivery on, the chart aggregates delivery reads into the built-in view, edit and admin roles and creating Approvals and Operations into edit and admin, so people with edit or admin in a namespace may decide there without an -approver binding.
  • teamGroupPrefix defaults to null: set, even to "", it narrows who may answer to the owner teams. requireOwnerTeam defaults to false.
  • Operation and Approval records, pacto delivery blame and history, the dashboard and MCP delivery answers carry how each actor was classified (classifiedBy) and, on each approval, the access phrase, its source and when it was answered (access, accessSource, accessAt). Records stay operation/v1, but signed records are parsed strictly: upgrade a promoter that follows another cluster's records (upstreamTrust), and the CLI, no later than the recording cluster.
  • Go API: delivery.ApprovalRefusal takes a last WorkloadAccess argument, so no caller can skip the rule; delivery.ApprovalRefusalAsking asks it only for an approval every other check lets through. delivery.ApprovalEligible is removed: use ApprovalRefusal, whose empty reason means the approval counts.
  • ca50460: The dashboard asks people to sign in by default, and the install notes print a short-lived sign-in link.

Upgrade effect first. After any upgrade, one that reuses the earlier release's values included, the dashboard asks people to sign in. To keep serving without sign-in, set dashboard.auth.tokenSignIn.enabled=false and dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous=true; the install notes say so when the previous release served without sign-in.

  • The new chart value dashboard.auth.tokenSignIn.enabled defaults to true. dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous defaults to false and passes --dashboard-allow-anonymous only when set to true. dashboard.auth.tokenLogin.enabled is deprecated and ignored; the schema still accepts it.
  • The install notes print a port-forward and a sign-in link carrying a 10-minute token for the chart's read-only pacto-viewer ServiceAccount, minted with --audience pacto-dashboard and passed after #, so the browser sends it to no server in the URL and it reaches no access log or proxy. An expired link says "link expired, run the command again".
  • A ServiceAccount token signs in only when a TokenReview proves it was minted for the pacto-dashboard audience, and its session reads the fleet only: the Delivery tab is hidden and delivery reads answer SignInLinkReadsFleet. A ServiceAccount token without the audience is refused with TokenAudienceRequired, and a sign-in link with any other token with SignInLinkNeedsDashboardToken.
  • A person's own token (an OIDC ID token, an EKS or static token) signs in as them, and their token session may now approve held changes under the approver rule. ServiceAccount tokens never approve. TokenCannotDecide is gone.
  • The dashboard's ServiceAccount gains create on tokenreviews through the ClusterRole <fullname>-<namespace>-dashboard-tokenreview, also with controller.watchNamespaces. pacto-viewer gets get, list and watch on Pactos and PactoRevisions through the ClusterRole <fullname>-viewer, or a Role in each watched namespace.
  • 73ce984: One chart value, registry, turns on the registry-backed features. The operator publishes the cluster's signed target snapshot with its installation key, advertises the registry, snapshot, index and inferred refs, and pushes only under them. Delivery stays opt-in. Pacto reaches GAR, GCR, ECR and ACR with cloud workload identity, and uses a pull Secret only once registryPullSecret names it.
  • e250ce8: Pacto detects the manager that owns each Stage's workloads and never promotes through another one. Stages can apply through a Flux HelmRelease.

Upgrade effect first. delivery.argocd.enabled and delivery.flux.enabled default to auto. An upgrade that takes the new chart's defaults on a cluster that serves Argo CD Applications grants the promoter patch on Applications, limited by admission to spec.source.targetRevision of labelled Applications; set delivery.argocd.enabled=false to keep it off. Flux access renders as before, plus HelmRelease read, --flux-helm and the applier-helmrelease admission policy when the cluster serves Flux HelmReleases; the agent, approver and recorder roles gain HelmRelease get there too, which includes inline Helm values.

  • The promoter reads, and never writes, the labels, annotations, field managers and owner references of each workload a Stage's Pactos report, and records the manager in the Stage's new status.applier (observed, with evidence, asOf and completeness) and the Applier print column. A manager that contradicts spec.applyRef reads Ready False ApplierConflict; an unsupported or ambiguous manager, a workload without its applier's marks or an unreadable one reads ApplierUnknown, with the reason a Kustomization could not be read. So does a Pacto the operator has not reconciled, or one that evaluated another workload than the Stage runs. Detection reads a Kustomization outside the Stage namespace only when it applies from the Stage's OCIRepository, and gives one fixed answer for any other the workload's labels name. status.applier.staleAt is twice the promoter's resync after asOf, so a longer --resync never reads stale.
  • The new pacto.applier promote gate fails on a conflict and is Unknown when Pacto cannot tell; both refuse the promote, and nobody can accept them.
  • spec.applyRef.kind accepts HelmRelease. The promoter writes the chart digest to the OCIRepository the HelmRelease's spec.chartRef names, in the Stage's namespace, and counts a move applied once the HelmRelease is Ready at that digest. spec.chart reads ApplierNotChartRef.
  • pacto delivery status, pacto delivery plan, MCP pacto_delivery_status and the dashboard Delivery views print one applier line per service, with the reason when the Stage does not adopt it. pacto delivery plan and the candidate list read versions from an Argo CD Application's or a HelmRelease's repository, as the promoter does.
  • An Operation the promoter cannot read the applier for says reading the applier, and a deadline says the applier did not confirm, instead of naming an OCIRepository or Flux.
  • An app.kubernetes.io/instance label of <namespace>_<app> names the Application in that namespace, as the tracking id does.
  • The delivery binary gains --flux (default true) and --flux-helm (default false). Go API: the new pkg/workloadmanager package (Detect, Describe), delivery.AdoptApplier, delivery.ApplierStatus and delivery.GateApplier.
  • bd0bdc4: Keep approvals and delivery records in the registry on every registry. The recorder signs an operation-intent/v1 record for every admitted Operation and an approval/v1 record for every Approval made in the cluster, on behalf of the person admission verified. With delivery.identities.signers set, pacto delivery approve signs the decision keyless after a fresh login and pushes it to the Stage's approvals repository (delivery.recorder.approvalsRepository); it refuses while SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN or a CI token is set. With the recorder on, an approval counts only once its record is written, and a person's signed approval only once the promoter verified it. The recorder anchors the approvals repository only once a signer is set, and a failure there never stops operation records. pacto delivery record get/verify <ref> and approve --intent <ref> read records with no kubeconfig, and the stdio MCP record tools take ref; MCP still has no approve tool. On registries without the OCI Referrers API, approval and intent records use write-once tags, and publisher signatures and SBOMs also get write-once pacto-sig-<subject hex>-<12 hex> tags that Pacto reads in place of the shared sha256-<hex> index. A recorded native registry mode can no longer narrow at admission.

Upgrade order: operation records now name each approval's record, and earlier readers decode records strictly. Upgrade the CLIs and every promoter that follows these streams before the recorder. - bd0bdc4: Accept a version only from a publisher Pacto knows. A first Stage with spec.candidates.registry watches the registry, verifies each new version's Sigstore signature and accepts it only when the signer is the CI the installation's registry names (delivery.publishers.registry, a rule derived for ghcr.io and registry.gitlab.com), an identity a person confirmed for that service or a rule of a signed delivery policy (delivery.publishers.policy). It needs no Flux, so an Argo CD-only cluster promotes its first Stage. A new CI signer raises one "Confirm identity" item in the delivery inbox; confirming it writes a signed identity-pin/v1 record to the registry. An unsigned or unreadable version, or a deploy digest a person signed, never passes. Keyless signers are classified as human, agent or ci, and an approval signed by anything but a person is a proposal that never counts. pacto delivery trust, the pacto_delivery_trust MCP tool and GET /api/delivery/trust show which publishers each service accepts.

A fleet signature status is now verified only when a publisher rule, a pin or a signed policy accepts the signer, and the new source field says which. A signer the contract's own publish.sign declares is no longer verified. pacto publish stamps org.opencontainers.image.source on the artifacts it builds in CI. - 73ce984: Only a member of a service's current owner or a default approver may set, change or remove its service.owner through a declaration, on pacto declare, pacto_declare and (once it can declare) the dashboard; agents and CI signers never do, and on_behalf_of grants nothing. A refused owner change stops before anything is pushed with OWNER_SIGNER_NOT_PERSON, OWNER_SIGNER_NOT_ALLOWED, OWNER_POLICY_UNVERIFIED or OWNER_SIGNER_UNVERIFIED, and an agent's plan lists who may accept it in mayAccept. An owner read from CODEOWNERS or catalog-info.yaml is attested when a CI identity the publisher rule accepts signed the bundle at the commit it was read at: it routes reviews and never clears a gate. The fleet adds ownerSource on services, source on ownership details, signerRepository and signerCommit on bundle signatures and ownerRight on revision provenance, and ignores a refused or unchecked owner with the limitations OWNER_DECLARATION_REFUSED and OWNER_DECLARATION_UNVERIFIED. pacto fleet get and the TUI print where an attested owner was read. The operator chart gains the declare values, rendered into an immutable, content-named ConfigMap the operator mounts, passes to its dashboard and publishes in its signed target snapshot when registry is set; the operator sets the OwnerVerified condition on a running bundle that changes the owner and withholds that owner from status unless its signer is allowed. - e250ce8: Every target, caller and record names the cluster it is in. A snapshot that reads a cluster now lists it in clusters, and each target carries cluster, clusterName, clusterNameSource, clusterNameReportedBy and clusterRelation. The live Kubernetes source's id is the cluster UID (its kube-system namespace UID) when it can get namespaces/kube-system, and the context name otherwise. The display name comes from a node label that names the cluster, then the context name, then the first 8 characters of the UID, and its source is always shown.

Target keys and k8s: callers gain a leading cluster component only when the snapshot holds two or more clusters, so single-cluster keys, hrefs, callers and MCP answers keep their form. A 3-part key keeps resolving while one cluster matches it; when several do, the dashboard API answers 409 Conflict with the candidate keys, the dashboard offers a chooser and the CLI and MCP print the candidates. An old dashboard link redirects to the canonical one. Two targets in two clusters never merge. A target with no cluster id in a multi-cluster snapshot raises CLUSTER_UNKNOWN and makes its source partial.

A --target-state file takes an optional cluster block with id and name. pacto evidence serve takes --cluster-id, --cluster-name and --cluster-name-source; each accepted record carries the cluster that accepted it, and the targets endpoint answers pacto.dev/evidence-source/v5 when it carries a cluster; older readers accept only v2 to v4. Two evidence sources that report one record with two clusters raise CLUSTER_CONFLICT.

The operator reads its cluster identity at start and passes it to the Evidence Server it runs. The operator ClusterRole and the managed dashboard ClusterRole gain get on namespaces for kube-system only. - 73ce984: - pacto impact --running oci://<repo>@<digest> never judges a revision against itself: a target already running the new digest is listed in running.excluded, so a gate that runs after a deploy, such as a Kargo verification, judges the new revision against the other revisions that run. A promoter fingerprint can carry an offer (id, text, an https doc), which its Detected providers row lists under offers on pacto fleet providers, pacto_fleet_status and the dashboard's Data sources. The demo shows the Kargo row with its offer. - The chart's default Kargo fingerprints offer "Gate every Kargo promotion with one shared AnalysisTemplate", and the GitOps docs publish that ClusterAnalysisTemplate: each Stage adds one verification stanza, exit 2 (unverified) fails unless allow-unverified is "true", and the template reads the signed target snapshots by default and needs no cluster RBAC. - e250ce8: Every vendor API, managed cloud service and legacy host that a contract names is one graph node of the new kind external, keyed by a canonical identity such as stripe, aws/rds/123456789012/eu-west-1/orders-db or host/corp-legacy.example. A ref-less external: true dependency joins it through its identity, else a catalog alias, else a hostname's registrable domain, else its normalized name, so consumers write nothing new. Its relationship carries toExternal with resolved: false; an external system never gets a range status and never enters impact, dependents or delivery.

Each external record lists its sources with their own provenance and match, its consumers and the catalog entry and digest that classified it. A snapshot lists them in externals and the catalogs used in externalCatalogs, which every answer's meta repeats. One answer names at most 200 external systems and folds the rest into other-egress, partial with EXTERNAL_CAP. A restricted view counts hidden consumers and hidden external systems and never names them.

pacto fleet get, graph and explain and the matching MCP tools take external:<identity>; pacto fleet entities --kind external --class <class> lists them and a text search adds matching externals. The TUI, the dashboard Overview, a new External systems list, an external entity page with its provenance and a distinct graph node show them. The contract graph labels a broken reference "Unresolved ref" and an external system "External system".

Pacto embeds a default external catalog. --external-catalog oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST on pacto fleet, impact, mcp, stats, tui and dashboard (or PACTO_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_CATALOG) merges an organization catalog pinned by digest; a tag is refused and a catalog that cannot be read makes the answer partial with EXTERNAL_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE. The operator chart value dashboard.externalCatalog sets it on the managed dashboard through the new operator flag --dashboard-external-catalog.

pactoVersion 2.5 adds the optional dependencies[].identity, validated with INVALID_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY and IDENTITY_WITHOUT_EXTERNAL.

Each core release publishes the default catalog to ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/external-catalog:<core version> and signs it with Cosign; its digest equals the embedded copy's. - e250ce8: Pacto recognizes the vendors, managed services and legacy hosts that a service's configuration, pod spec and traces already name, with no contract edit. Every surface shows the host and port at most: a user name, password, path and query are stripped, a value under a sensitive key is never parsed and no Secret value is ever read.

  • pacto init and pacto_create with pactify list the externals that the environment, ConfigMaps, Secret and key names and every chart's values.yaml name, and write the likely ones as commented entries under dependencies for a person to uncomment. The parsed contract does not change.
  • The operator writes status.externals, status.externalsCoverage and status.externalCatalog at PactoStatusFormat 3. It reads the target workload's env names and values, Secret names, secretKeyRef key names and the ConfigMap keys the pod spec references, plus the ExternalName Services, selectorless Services and Istio ServiceEntries of its own namespace that the workload names. status.externals shows every reader of a Pacto the normalized hosts that the referenced ConfigMap keys hold.
  • The operator role gains get, list and watch on networking.istio.io serviceentries, rendered by the chart only when the cluster serves that API. Without it the coverage reads partial, reason serviceentry-reader-off.
  • The fleet joins trace callees that the external catalog recognizes to external systems as observed edges, and reads the operator's externals as inferred edges with inferredSources. Neither enters an index that impact or a gate reads. NeighborhoodEdge.provenance gains the value inferred and edges gain inferred: true. rpc.system is now the last OTel callee key.
  • New limitations: EXTERNALS_UNREPORTED (an older, partial or stale operator status), EXTERNAL_CATALOG_MISMATCH and EXTERNAL_USE_UNATTRIBUTED. OBSERVED_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED stays for names that match more than one service or that are neither a service nor an external system.
  • 73ce984: Pacto publishes an inferred contract for every external system your services call. Once registry is set the operator writes <registry>/pacto-inferred/<identity> every 5 minutes, signed with the installation key and annotated run.pacto.contract.provenance: inferred, and only when the hosts, ports or client majors it sees change; pacto fleet publish-inferred does the same where no operator runs. The 2.5 contract field service.external names the system and the pacto.inferred.yaml section surface records what Pacto saw with its sources, catalog digest and first and last seen; it never names a consumer. A range against an inferred contract reads rangeStatus: unknown with the new rangeReason: INFERRED_PROVIDER and gates as unverified. A revision only the operator signed reads unverified with the new signature source operator and an INFERRED_PROVIDER attention item suggests pacto declare. The Compose demo publishes demo/pacto-inferred/stripe.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• ca50460: Pacto keeps what it infers in pacto.inferred.yaml, a separate bundle file with each value's source, for pactoVersion 2.5 contracts. pacto init and pacto_create complete an existing pacto.yaml without changing it, pacto explain lists each inferred field and the YAML to declare it, a publish that changes only the inferred record is not republished, the diff classifies inferred-only changes as non-breaking and impact never clears a gate on an inferred consumer. The dashboard shows inferred values apart from declared ones.
  • e250ce8: pacto init and pacto_create no longer copy environment values into the inferred configuration schema as defaults; sensitive keys are marked writeOnly, cluster drafts read sensitive literals from a Secret and every schema summary (dashboard, fleet, consume snippet, operator status) shows writeOnly keys as (sensitive). Schema diffs print (sensitive) in place of a sensitive key's schema values; values declared under configurations[].values or in an environment file are shown as written. Existing configuration/schema.json files are left as they are: remove any default that holds a secret and republish.
  • bd0bdc4: pacto ci --publish publishes every changed service of a repository on the merged commit, providers first. An undeclared service.version is derived from the newest verified version in the registry and the change since it (1.0.0 for a first publish), and a contract with no publish section gets one derived in memory: the image is built with the one tool the folder shows (Skaffold, ko, Jib, buildpacks or a Dockerfile), with no shell, and Pacto assembles the deploy artifact from the folder's manifests, Kustomization or Helm chart, with Secrets left out and the image pinned by digest. Signing is keyless by default, as the identity the GitHub Actions or GitLab id_tokens token names; a declared key or KMS key and --sign-key still sign with a key. Pull request pipelines and stale checkouts are refused, every tag is read back after it is written, a version lost to a concurrent run is planned again up to 3 times and a failure blocks only the services of the run that depend on it. Each published bundle carries a signed record of the image digests its deploy pins. In pactoVersion: "2.5", publish.deploy names a manifests or chart artifact any applier deploys and publish.artifacts[].build is optional and deprecated. pacto init and MCP pacto_create no longer write the shell publish section or the service.version placeholder. pacto publish gains --image, --registry, --sign-key and --no-transparency-log, and MCP pacto_publish and pacto_publish_plan take them as image, registry, sign_key and no_transparency_log.
  • 73ce984: A dependency on a service of your own may leave out ref in a 2.5 contract: Pacto resolves it by name in its domain. pacto ci proposes its ref from the organization index and, from the target snapshot, a ^MAJOR.MINOR.0 range for a dependency whose range is unknown. Both land in pacto.inferred.yaml and publish as compatibility: unknown. pacto accept --proposed (or --field for one field) signs, after the person's interactive Sigstore login, an acceptance record attached to the service's newest published version: a referrer of type application/vnd.pacto.acceptance.v1+json, or a write-once pacto-accept-- tag on a registry without the Referrers API. Only a record signed by the service's declared owner counts; any other signer, and every agent through the new MCP tool pacto_accept, writes a pacto-accept-draft- a person accepts with --draft. pacto ci --publish carries counted ranges into the next version's pacto.yaml and cites each record in inputs.acceptances. pacto accept --break @ accepts a break announced in breaks[], also before the provider publishes (--from); the gate clears with BREAKING_ACCEPTED once every consumer accepted, and an announcement without expires expires 30 days after the commit time. pacto ci, pacto impact, pacto_impact and Change analysis print a Ranges: coverage line, and --policy unknown-range=warn|fail and uncontracted=warn|fail: hold a BREAKING change that no range covers. A changed spec file that is only inferred prints a possible break (inferred) advisory with the YAML that declares the interface: the row reads unverified (INFERRED_POSSIBLE_BREAK) and the classification and version never change. The dashboard service page shows the plan and the pacto accept command for Accept all proposed ranges; it never signs or writes.
  • 73ce984: pacto ci init writes the CI caller that runs pacto ci into a repository's working tree: five lines in .github/workflows/pacto.yml that call the pacto-actions v2 reusable workflow pinned by commit, or one include entry in .gitlab-ci.yml for its GitLab component. It never commits, pushes or needs Git write access. The plan job runs pacto ci on pull requests, annotates each service that does not read as unchanged and writes the job summary; the publish job, the only one with id-token: write, runs pacto ci --publish on the default branch, one run per repository at a time. Pacto's own CI runs the caller over a demo monorepo with empty contracts.

    • Keyless publishes through the shared reusable workflow keep verifying across pin bumps and stay trusted by the operator's derived publisher rule: Pacto matches the caller repository and branch that Fulcio certifies, never the reusable workflow's commit. A repository moving from its own keyless release workflow keeps its earlier versions verifying. The operator picks the rule up through the core module.

    The CI guide, a new guide "From an imperative pipeline to one step" and the GitHub Actions reference teach pacto ci in place of pacto push, COSIGN_KEY and hand-raised versions.

    Until the pacto-actions release that pins a Pacto with pacto ci, a caller written by pacto ci init adds with: {pacto-version: <this release>}. - e250ce8: pacto validate and pacto_check report CONTRACT_BEHIND, an info finding that never fails a run, when a contract declares an older pactoVersion. Its message says whether raising the version keeps what the contract means, names the finding the raise would add or says Pacto cannot tell until the errors are fixed. pacto_check adds it as a suggestion.

    pacto_edit raises pactoVersion only when that keeps the contract's meaning and otherwise fails with the finding the raise would add. Its change line now names the old version: set pactoVersion to "2.4" (was "2.3"), comes first and replaces the set pactoVersion "2.1" for the external dependency line. An edit that needs a raise now fails when the contract already fails validation, does not parse or declares an unknown or 1.x pactoVersion, where it used to overwrite the version.

    The fleet revision detail gains pactoVersionCurrent and pactoVersionUnknown, and pacto fleet entity revision, the TUI and the dashboard revision page show a behind or unknown version.

    The operator reads its ContractOverrides rule for ref configurations from validation, with no behaviour change, and its finding reference lists CONTRACT_BEHIND. - bd0bdc4: pacto ci publishes a contract that declares an older pactoVersion as the current version, raised in memory, when that keeps what the contract means: only the version token of the bundled pacto.yaml changes, the bundle records the raise as a migrations entry in pacto.inferred.yaml and the plan adds one line per migrated or kept contract without changing the exit code. A raise alone does not republish an unchanged service, and the file in the repository is never rewritten. The fleet revision detail reads 2.5 (migrated from 2.4, inferred), with the inferred migratedFrom JSON key read only from a verified record, in pacto fleet, the TUI, MCP pacto_fleet_get and the dashboard revision page. The CONTRACT_BEHIND message now says when pacto ci publishes the contract as the current version. - e250ce8: Release CLI binaries, checksums.txt and the dashboard, operator and delivery images now carry signed SLSA build-provenance attestations, verifiable with gh attestation verify. The images no longer carry BuildKit's unsigned per-platform provenance manifests. - e250ce8: pacto init and pacto_create propose dependency ranges and write compatibility: unknown instead of declaring a guessed range. The proposal goes in a trailing comment: ^MAJOR.MINOR.0 of the lowest version the reconciled Pactos describing the called Service report, or of the dependency's contract in --fleet, and none when nothing was read or those Pactos disagree on the contract. A draft that writes a dependency declares pactoVersion 2.5. pacto_create and pacto_edit write compatibility: unknown when an agent gives no range. The CLI, the TUI, Used by and the dashboard say "range not declared" for such a dependency.

    The delivery controller's gate reason says range not declared for a consumer with compatibility unknown. - bd0bdc4: pacto init --cluster and pacto_create with cluster complete each draft with the engine pacto ci uses and write a pacto.inferred.yaml into the draft folder. Each value names its source (manifest, label, runtime or fleet), when it was read and, for runtime and fleet facts, whether every node was observed. The running image digest is recorded and never declared, and a proposed range stays a proposal. The cluster read lists each kind of object in pages up to --max-items (max_items), takes --call-window (call_window) and resumes a read the bound stopped with --continue (continue). A kind of object you may not list reads as failed and the run goes on. A literal secret in a container's command or args moves to the draft's Secret. A published bundle whose inferred record carries cluster facts fails validation. - 73ce984: pacto declare publishes a contract for a workload the cluster already runs as a contract-only version: 0.1.0 for a first declaration, else the published baseline raised by the change, with the baseline's deploy artifact reused and nothing built. Only a person's interactive Sigstore login (a browser, or a device code with --device) publishes a declared version; a key, an ambient OIDC token or a CI identity writes a write-once draft- tag that a person accepts with --from-draft. The bundle's pacto.inferred.yaml gains a declaration block naming the signer, the inferred workload, the baseline and each proposed range accepted with --accept. pacto pull gains --verify-identity, --verify-issuer and --verify-key. The MCP tool pacto_declare is the first tool of the agent write contract (the existing pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish stay outside it): it plans by default with an intent digest, always writes a draft carrying on_behalf_of and refuses with a stable code and the command a person runs. The fleet, explain, diff and the dashboard show a declaration's cluster facts, coverage and signer only when the bundle carries a verified signature by that person and the installation signer policy allows them. - 89eedf2: The operator no longer writes a Pacto's status on every reconcile that lands in a new second. Each finding's evidence times (observedAt, detectedAt) are stamped when the evidence is read, so comparing them made almost every reconcile look like a change. They now refresh with the lastReconciledAt heartbeat, at least once every half check interval, and a status that is otherwise unchanged is not rewritten.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• da4494d: Add pactoVersion: "2.4" with service.domain, service.offering, service.summary, service.lifecycle, and values and a configuration selector beside a configuration ref. Every 2.3 contract is schema-valid under 2.4, but 2.4 checks configuration refs strictly: a ref that cannot be resolved or that matches more than one provider configuration is an error, and a required ref configuration needs values in every environment. Raising a contract to 2.4 can therefore turn those warnings into errors. A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets any of the new fields reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4.

service.domain is the business domain a service belongs to, and pacto diff reports an added, changed or removed domain as NON_BREAKING. The operator reports the domain in status.contract.domain and writes status.statusFormat 2, so a service seen only through Kubernetes is still grouped by it. A status from an older operator leaves that service's domain unknown.

The dashboard groups services by domain: domains have a list and a page with their services, owners, operational targets and attention, and the overview breaks services down by domain, with services that declare none under No domain and services whose domain Pacto cannot tell under Domain unknown. Sources that disagree on a domain raise DOMAIN_CONFLICT. The registry path that used to read "domain" now reads "Registry". Services with no owner from any source appear in attention as unowned. An operational target shows the environment it runs in when its Pacto carries the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/environment label, and whether the revision it runs declares that environment; without the label it reads Unknown. The services list filters by declared capability. pacto fleet search --business-domain, the pacto_fleet_search MCP tool and the TUI accept a domain, (none) or (unknown), and pacto_edit sets one. - a6c189d: A delivery plan or proposal can carry a correlation id, such as a ticket or incident id: pacto delivery plan|propose --correlation-id, correlation_id on pacto_delivery_operation_plan and pacto_delivery_operation_propose, and correlationID in the dashboard's plan and propose bodies, and pacto publish --propose --correlation-id. The id is at most 128 printable ASCII characters, checked by the client and by the operation admission policy. The automatic rollback, freeze and step-down the promoter raises after a change inherit its id, so pacto delivery history --correlation-id lists the changes of one incident.

The intent digest now binds the cause a proposal cites (--cause-verdict, cause_verdict), never the correlation id, and PlanStale names a changed cause. Proposals that cite a cause need the CLI, the dashboard and the operator at the same release, in both directions: across releases the client and the promoter compute different digests, and the promoter finishes the Operation Rejected with PlanStale. Proposals without a cause are unaffected.

An agent must name the person it acts for (onBehalfOf, --on-behalf-of, on_behalf_of), as the Kubernetes username the cluster authenticates them as, when it proposes a change, never itself, a service account or the promoter. The client, the promoter and the operation admission policy refuse an agent's proposal without one, with the reasons NoPrincipal, SelfPrincipal and NotAPerson; planning needs none, and changes the promoter raises itself need none. Existing agent automations that propose without naming a person must add it. The named person may not approve the change, and an approval of an agent's change that names nobody is refused. The name is asserted, never verified: it records who an agent says it acts for, and it does not stop a person who controls an agent's credentials from naming someone else and then approving the change.

The dashboard's propose panel proposes the plan it shows when a reason or an on-behalf-of person is typed, with no false "Something changed" warning. Its delivery errors carry differs, the field that made a plan stale. The propose panel asks an agent who it acts for and takes a ticket or incident id.

Fleet attention items whose fix is a contract edit carry nextAction ({"verb": "edit-contract", "tool": "pacto_edit"}), inferred from the item's code beside nextStep; it grants nothing, and unknown, stale, unresolved or non-compliant items carry none. pacto_edit returns impact (who the edit affects, from the session's fleet snapshot), chain (publish and promote, each with its tool and CLI command) and executor (who acts on the published revision), also on a dry run; pacto_create returns chain. The dashboard's target, revision and Change analysis pages offer Plan… for the operations the caller may take there, and a correlationID in the page URL fills the propose panel's ticket field. - a6c189d: The dashboard's Metrics page, under Change and delivery, draws the run records in a stats repository as daily or weekly trends: breaking changes caught, consumers protected, gates, delivery rates, lead time per environment and coverage of contracts and observations. Every number is labelled unsigned statistics and links to the records behind it. Start the dashboard with pacto dashboard --stats-registry (or PACTO_STATS_REGISTRY); without one the page explains how to turn recording on. A signed-in viewer sees only the services their Kubernetes RBAC allows: hidden services are never named or counted. pacto fleet status --stats-registry (or --stats-file) writes a coverage record of the snapshot it read. The operator chart value dashboard.stats.registry points the managed dashboard at a stats repository. - 1e7624b: An environment in environments[] can now declare its lifetime (temporary or persistent), an expires time (RFC 3339, only with temporary) and an owner in the shape of service.owner (pactoVersion 2.4). A lifetime nobody declared reads "not declared", never persistent. Once a temporary environment's expires has passed, pacto validate and pacto_check warn ENVIRONMENT_EXPIRED; Pacto deletes nothing for it. pacto diff classifies every change to these fields, and to an environment's file, as non-breaking.

pacto init --delivery --env and pacto_create with delivery also declare each environment in pacto.yaml with an empty values file. pacto_edit add_environments takes lifetime, expires and owner, and pacto_edit remove_environments retires an environment and deletes the values file no other environment names. pacto explain --environments a,b and pacto_check environments list the configuration values two or more environments disagree on.

A service's environments are one list in pacto fleet entity service, pacto_fleet_entity and the dashboard's service page: each environment the current revision declares or a visible target reports, with its declaration, its owner (declared, or the service owner labelled inferred), the targets observed there, its provisioning tally, the differences between environments and how the declarations changed between versions. On a delivery host the service page also shows the Stages for each environment. pacto fleet entities --consumes <offering> --phase <phase> --environment <env> and the matching pacto_fleet_entities arguments list the consumers in a provisioning phase in one environment.

The delivery promoter emits the Kubernetes Events EnvironmentCreated and EnvironmentDeleted when a Stage is first reconciled and when it is deleted, and the recorder posts the CDEvents environment.created and environment.deleted to its CDEvents sink. Each names one Stage. - 9cdf40f: service.template (pactoVersion 2.4) marks a contract as a golden path and names the generate plugins it offers, and service.origin (pactoVersion 2.4) records the golden path a service was created from as declared provenance (ref and the path's content digest). A "2.0" to "2.3" contract that sets either field reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_4; a repeated plugin reports DUPLICATE_TEMPLATE_PLUGIN and an origin that is neither an oci:// reference nor a directory reports INVALID_ORIGIN_REF. pacto diff classifies every change to either field as non-breaking.

pacto init <dir> --from <oci-ref|dir> --owner <team> creates a service from a golden path: it resets the identity, applies --values and --set, records service.origin, validates the result with its references resolved and only adds files. A path read from a registry is pulled by digest and, when the trust config (--trust or $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST) names a role: template key, must be signed by one; otherwise the signature step reads Unknown. --run-plugins runs only the plugins of the path you name. --delivery, with --env, --registry-secret and --insecure-registry, plans the cluster pieces from the created contract when the path publishes manifests under publish.deploy. The step list says what was checked and what Pacto cannot tell yet. The MCP pacto_create tool gains from, values, set, run_plugins and domain, and takes delivery and its options with from; from serves stdio only. pacto_edit gains template.

A blank pacto init now writes --owner, --domain and a publish section, and no placeholder readiness block. pacto_create without pactify refuses a folder that already holds pacto.yaml and keeps any interface or schema file already there.

The operational graph treats a service whose newest readable revision declares service.template and that runs nowhere as a golden path. Its dependencies and references are requirements, never consumption: impact, dependents, offering consumers, attention and the Overview population counts leave it out, and the Overview counts it in goldenPaths and invalidGoldenPaths. A running service that declares service.template stays a service and raises GOLDEN_PATH_DEPLOYED. A declared origin links to the golden path revision whose content digest matches. Entity lists take template (only or exclude) and createdFrom (MCP created_from), search takes template and marks golden path hits, and a service created from a path carries a creation checklist derived from what the fleet observes. A restricted viewer sees a golden path with no Kubernetes target, with the services created from it that they may not read counted. The CLI, MCP tools, dashboard (a Golden paths tab) and TUI show all of it. Consume snippets carry structured entries, and a values skeleton leaves out and names in missingValues every required value no candidate satisfies.

The operator chart's dashboard.repositories (operator flag --dashboard-repositories) lists oci:// references the operator-managed dashboard reads beside the contracts it discovers, so golden paths, which are never deployed, show on its Golden paths tab. - a6c189d: People and agents now see the same organization and meet the same policy on every surface.

Changes that callers notice:

  • An MCP server over HTTP serves only pacto_schema of the contract tools. pacto_create, pacto_edit and pacto_check read and write the server's folders and follow refs with its credentials, so they run beside the agent with pacto mcp over stdio.
  • A remote pacto mcp --fleet with --auth-issuer needs token exchange (--exchange-client-id): it asks the API server who each caller is, the way remote delivery does, in place of reading the token's claims.
  • pacto mcp -t http on loopback without --auth-issuer prints a bearer at launch (pmcp_...), and every request must carry it.
  • pacto dashboard bound beyond loopback without sign-in refuses to start unless --allow-anonymous (PACTO_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true) allows it. The operator passes --dashboard-allow-anonymous from the new chart value dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous, true by default with a warning in the install notes, so existing installs keep starting.
  • A bundle operation whose name starts with pacto_ is skipped, so a bundle never takes a Pacto tool's name.
  • pacto_impact over HTTP, and the impact view of a dashboard that is not on loopback, accept only refs of revisions in the caller's view and read each at its digest-pinned ref.

Additions:

  • Every MCP tool carries annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint); a generated tool takes them from its HTTP method. --allow-writes and the stdio-only rules still decide what runs.
  • A bundle, --fleet and --delivery combine in one pacto mcp process, whose instructions describe only the modes it serves. pacto_capabilities reports the modes, the contract tools, the caller and how Pacto knows them, whether writes are exposed and the transport.
  • Six delivery read tools answer what the dashboard's delivery views show, with the caller's identity: pacto_delivery_caller, pacto_delivery_inbox, pacto_delivery_environments, pacto_delivery_autonomy, pacto_delivery_published and pacto_delivery_refusals. The CLI gains pacto delivery caller, inbox, environments, autonomy, published and refusals over the same route code.
  • pacto fleet entities and pacto_fleet_entities list any entity kind and take every filter the dashboard's entity list takes; a filter of one kind, such as --source-kind, lists that kind. pacto fleet attention and pacto_fleet_attention take kind, key, source, status and stale-only, pacto_fleet_neighborhood takes max_edges and pacto_fleet_search takes label. pacto mcp --publish serves pacto_capabilities too.
  • pacto_fleet_revision_document reads one document of a revision's bundle, as the dashboard's revision page does.
  • With --verbose, every MCP tool call logs one mcp tool call line with the tool, the caller and how Pacto knows them, the outcome, the duration and a keyed digest of the arguments.
  • Generated tool calls send User-Agent: pacto-mcp/<version>.
  • Fleet views maps each question to its command, MCP tool and dashboard route.
  • af4f27d: service.lifecycle (pactoVersion 2.4) deprecates a whole service with a sunset and a successor, and a configuration ref takes values and a configuration selector beside it (pactoVersion 2.4). Consumers of a deprecated service are warned with DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_DEPRECATED or DEPENDENCY_SERVICE_SUNSET, and pacto diff classifies the schedule like an interface lifecycle.

Configuration references are now resolved and their values validated against the referenced contract's selected configuration schema in a new configuration-refs validation stage, in the fleet, the delivery gate, pacto_check, pacto_edit and the operator. pacto validate, pacto push and pacto publish fail with CONFIG_REF_UNRESOLVED on an unreachable configuration ref whose values or selection depend on it, like a policy ref; a "2.0" to "2.3" ref with no values anywhere only warns. Environment values of "2.0" to "2.3" ref configurations are now checked, and only 2.4 reports missing required values for a ref configuration. A failed configuration-refs stage does not skip environments. Impact, graph traversal and dependents count resolved configuration-reference consumers, and impact checks their values against the new provider schema. Neighborhood edges gain the configuration_reference relation.

Provider adapters report provisioning status as ResourceProvisioned evidence, written with pacto evidence provisioned. A trust entry needs allowedObservationKinds listing ResourceProvisioned to report it. The Evidence Server's targets endpoint answers pacto.dev/evidence-source/v3 with a provisioning list only when it holds provisioning reports, and v2 otherwise, and target-state files accept pacto.dev/fleet-targets/v2 with unsigned provisioning reports. Offering uses carry a provisioning status per environment that reads Unknown without a current report. pacto fleet versions, pacto_fleet_versions and the dashboard list each provider's versions with their lifecycle and range status, --consumes and consumes list an offering's consumers, and pacto_edit gains remove_configuration_refs, add_environments, set_environment_values and lifecycle. A provider with no Kubernetes target that declares its offering is visible to every signed-in viewer, with its targets hidden and its hidden consumers counted. OfferingProvider.revisions and activeRevisions become versions. pacto explain lists each configuration with its environmentValues, the effective values per environment an adapter provisions from.

The operator resolves configuration references with host-scoped credentials and validates their values, spec.overrides and bound ConfigMaps against the resolved schema. status.metadata renders non-string values as JSON. The chart's evidence.trust.configKey (operator flag --evidence-trust-config-key) names a structured trust config inside the trust Secret, so the operator's Evidence Server can grant an adapter key ResourceProvisioned. - a6c189d: A failing health check is reported as HEALTH_FAILING (category Inconclusive, severity unknown), and compliance stays Unknown: a failing endpoint does not contradict the contract. The operator reports it when the declared health endpoint answers with a 5xx other than 501, or when the readiness probe on the declared health path keeps every pod out of Ready; pacto run and pacto agent report it on a 5xx other than 501. A 501 or a 405 stays EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT, as do a workload scaled to zero and endpoints the operator cannot map to the health port. COLLECTION_FAILED now means only that a collector query errored, an EndpointSlice read included. The Evidence Server re-evaluates the same evidence and reaches the same finding. The CapabilityObserved evidence payload gains the optional healthy key, which only a present capability may carry. Strict decoders reject unknown keys, so upgrade the Evidence Server with or before the operator.

pacto fleet, pacto mcp, pacto tui and pacto impact now mark target evidence older than 24 hours as stale by default, the window the dashboard already uses. --freshness 0 still skips the check, and every answer then carries the FRESHNESS_NOT_EVALUATED limitation, so a stale count of zero is never read as "nothing is stale"; the CLI also prints it as a note on stderr. The limitation does not change completeness.

pacto fleet overview, the MCP tool pacto_fleet_overview and the dashboard overview answer "how healthy is the organization and how much do we know" in one shape. The overview summary gains operationalHealth (targets that are healthy, failing their own health check, unknown or declare no health check), knowledge with its gap kinds (noSummary, noDomain, noInterfaceDocs, noReadiness, notDeployed, unverifiedCapability) and an unknown bucket, knowledgeItems, coverage (assertions evaluated and required, and the targets that report none) and staleCompliantTargets. Every compliance tally gains staleCompliant, the Compliant targets or services that rest on stale evidence: a subset, never subtracted from compliant, drawn hatched. The entity list aggregate gains targetHealth and knowledge. The dashboard draws an Operational health band and a Knowledge band, and a target that is unknown is never counted as healthy. There is still no composite score.

Ownership splits a service whose contract Pacto cannot read from a service that declares no owner: ownership.unknown and the filter value ownership=unknown are new, labelled Owner unknown. Each business domain row gains failingHealth, ownerUnknown, notDeployed and withGaps; owner and domain pages gain operational health, knowledge, readiness, services that run nowhere, services whose placement is unknown and unresolved and undeclared dependencies; owner and domain list rows gain unknown, stale, failingHealth and withGaps counts, and sort=health ranks them by those counts. New filters and sorts: gap (--gap), sort=gaps and sourceHealth=incomplete, which the new Incomplete sources entry point opens. The attention categories health and knowledge are new, and the dashboard's Attention view lists every category with each item's reason.

Changed meanings: ownership.unowned and a domain row's unowned no longer count services whose contract Pacto cannot read; the lead "Services needing attention" tile and servicesNeedingAttention count every service with at least one attention item, and the tile's itemCount carries the item total; an unknown attention item names its cause in code (for example EVIDENCE_STALE or EVIDENCE_MISSING) and keeps UNKNOWN only when no cause is known; the CLI and MCP mark targets stale after 24 hours by default; and the evidence payload gains healthy. The dashboard's sidebar badge counts only attention items above info. - 78fd229: service.offering (pactoVersion 2.4) names the platform offering a service provides to other teams such as postgresql, and service.summary a one-line purpose; pacto diff reports an added, changed or removed offering or summary as NON_BREAKING. The operator reports both in status.contract.offering and status.contract.summary.

The dashboard gains an Offerings page. Each offering lists its providers with their versions, owners, interfaces, configuration and policies, the services that consume it and a snippet to consume it from a contract. A service page lists the platform offerings the service uses and, marked inferred, the providers its unresolved dependencies may mean. The capability filter and chips now read "Declared capability" and count each extension by its ref. pacto fleet search --offering, the offering argument of pacto_fleet_search and the TUI Offerings tab find providers, and pacto_edit gains offering, summary, add_configuration_refs and add_policy_refs. - a6c189d: The delivery promoter can publish an unsigned run record of every operation it concludes to a repository you name with delivery.stats.repository (Helm) or --stats-repository. Records hold the type, outcome, verification, gate results, how long each operation was held, the class of who asked, the Stage and the digests, never a name. Publishing is best effort: a full queue or a registry error is counted in pacto_delivery_stats_dropped_total and never changes an outcome. pkg/runrecord describes kind: operation records.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• a6c189d: Provisioning keys can be scoped to provider repositories with allowedProviderRepos in the structured trust config. The Evidence Server refuses a provisioning report whose declared configuration or dependency ref names a repository outside the scope with HTTP 403 and the code provider_not_allowed, and it logs a warning at startup for every provisioning key with no scope. Older binaries reject a trust config that uses the field.

An offering answer names who reports on it on the CLI, TUI, MCP and dashboard: adapters lists each adapter slug, producer and signature with the environments and phases it covers, conflicting counts requests whose adapters disagree and unattributed counts requests no adapter reported on. A report with no slug reads "unnamed adapter". unresolvedUses counts the declared references that may name a provider of the offering but did not resolve, and above 0 the answer carries OFFERING_USES_UNRESOLVED and is partial.

Phase tallies count an unsigned Ready apart in readyUnsigned, and the CLI prints "N ready (M unsigned)". The dashboard shows an unsigned Ready as "Ready (unsigned)" in the info tone, so only a signed Ready reads positive.

Impact's CONFIG_REF_CONSUMERS_UNRESOLVED and POLICY_REF_CONSUMERS_UNRESOLVED now count hidden consumers and count each consumer once instead of once per revision, so their numbers can change.

The demo adds a security-scanning offering, provided by platform-security, with a signed and an unsigned report from the scanner adapter. - 1e7624b: Follow a service through delivery on every surface. pacto delivery status, the pacto_delivery_status MCP tool and the dashboard show each Stage of a service in promotion order with its upstream, the one state the board counts, the version, contract and source revision it runs, its newest re-check with Watched and what you may ask for (offers: promote, unfreeze, freeze and undo, each with why or why not). --why and /api/delivery/progress say why a candidate cannot move yet, with each reason's fix and a dry-run plan that proposes nothing. Offers go unavailable when RBAC denies or cannot answer, and when the delivery identity policy cannot be read, with a --delivery-namespace hint when it is not found. A Stage whose admission policies are missing (Ready False Unguarded) and a Stage that observes (including one that reports no level) offer no promote, and none appears in actions.

pacto delivery lifecycle, pacto_delivery_lifecycle and /api/delivery/lifecycle follow one version through every Stage, and pacto delivery record get, pacto_delivery_record_get and /api/delivery/record read one signed record by its id. History takes --cause and --correlation-id (cause and correlation_id in MCP, which also accepts durations for since and until); both narrow the timeline too. The CLI history shows applied, cause and correlation columns and marks lines that are not signed. /api/delivery/plan and propose return the full plan answer (next, precedent and order). Published versions show the source revision pacto publish stamps, an annotation, not signed, and link their fleet revision; a service whose Stages name two domains is listed once per domain. Delivery service filters match the service name exactly. A Stage waiting on exactly one held change names it (heldOperation). A fleet service detail carries placement, where its targets report it runs. The CLI labels an evidence gate's Pass as Checked, pacto.contract verdicts cite each Pacto's target, status, evaluation time and findings, a held promote on a frozen Stage names the StageFrozen conflict and the CandidateUnverified fix points at spec.verify. The operator uses the shared Ready reasons and auto-promote rule, and a held shadow promote keeps the person's question. - 8517f96: Bump Go dependencies (sigstore, sigstore-go, go-jose, oras-go, prometheus, pflag, ginkgo and k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver), dashboard frontend dependencies (jsdom 31, vite, vitest, playwright, mermaid, marked, d3 and svelte-check) and the cosign-installer, docker/login-action and CodeQL GitHub Actions. - a39e7dc: Build with Go 1.27.4 (was 1.27.3) everywhere it's pinned (both modules, go.work, both Dockerfiles) for GO-2026-6859, a net/http vulnerability fixed in Go 1.27.4 and reachable from Pacto's code. No source changes. - a6c189d: The demos ship generated run records, labelled unsigned statistics: the browser demo opens Metrics with about 90 days of records that follow the payments story, the Compose demo seeds CI records into its own registry and the Kubernetes demo records its real publishes and promoter operations on top of a seeded history. The delivery tour visits Metrics before its recap. The new guide "Measure what Pacto does" explains what is recorded, where it goes, how to turn it on in CI and in delivery, who sees which records and how to prune them, and the run record reference says for every field whether it can hold personal data. - a6c189d: A service's detail now carries its changes: every declared change between the revisions Pacto holds (owner, business domain, offering, dependency, lifecycle and environment) and each validation finding that appeared or resolved, newest first in version order, each with the revision that shows it, the one it was compared with, its provenance and its source. changes replaces the unreleased environmentHistory. pacto fleet entity service <key> --reached, reached on a stdio pacto_fleet_entity and the service page add when each change's revision reached a Stage, from signed delivery records read as the caller; a change with no record reads "time not recorded", and "time hidden" when the caller may not read delivery. The TUI and the dashboard's service page show the same changes.

A sequential owner handover is now an owner change, never OWNER_CONFLICT. OWNER_CONFLICT remains for targets that run revisions declaring different owners, or for two revisions of one version that disagree, and says when the link is inferred. Rankings, owner filters and owner pages count the current owner, and a former owner's page still lists the revisions it declared.

pacto delivery history, pacto_delivery_history and Delivery history name the fleet revision of every artifact and the pacto.impact verdict each record signed, apart from a re-analysis against today's graph; blame names the revision too. pacto delivery history --at, at on pacto_delivery_history and ?at= on the dashboard answer which revision each Stage ran at a past time, from signed records, and read unknown where no record holds. - a6c189d: A service's detail lists every resource it consumes. A use of a provider that declares no offering now shows once a provider reports on it, and the service's hiddenProviders says at least how many resources come from providers the viewer may not see. Each use carries providerOwner, providerAvailability, requested (the values the contract declares, on the configuration-reference row) and consumption, which reads not-reported until a provider reports usage or cost. A new provisioning attention category raises PROVISIONING_FAILED and PROVISIONING_STALE; a resource's phase never changes the service's compliance. pacto fleet entity service and the TUI's service page print a Resources block with provenance, and the dashboard's service page gains a Resources section that joins each use with its requested configuration.

Provider adapters can report a resource's usage and cost with the new ResourceUsage observation kind, written by pacto evidence usage. Only a key that lists ResourceUsage in allowedObservationKinds may report it, scoped by allowedProviderRepos like ResourceProvisioned, and an EvidenceSet carries one provider-reported kind only. The Evidence Server's targets endpoint lists usage under schema pacto.dev/evidence-source/v4, written only when it holds usage. consumption reads reported, with the figures, only for a signed, fresh, uncontested report about the current revision; otherwise it reads unknown and keeps the raw figures apart under reported. The CLI, MCP and the dashboard's Resources section show both, and Pacto never sums or converts a cost.
