A digest joins status.published only when its signer passes one of three checks, and each verdict names the one that decided:

Source Accepts Set by rule On ghcr.io/<org>, a GitHub Actions workflow of <org>; on registry.gitlab.com/<group>, a GitLab CI pipeline of <group>, the org or group in any case. Both on the default branch, and the repository the certificate attests must match the artifact's org.opencontainers.image.source delivery.publishers.registry and defaultBranch pin One CI identity (issuer, subject and repository) a person confirmed for one service the delivery inbox policy The rules of a signed delivery policy, which replace the derived rule once verified delivery.publishers.policy and policySigners

Other registries, such as ECR, Artifact Registry, ACR, Docker Hub, Harbor or zot, name no CI provider and get no rule: a person confirms the first signer of each service. The contract never decides: publish.sign only says how pacto publish signs.

Unsigned, unreadable or unreachable is unknown and never passes, and neither does a missing trusted root or a policy that does not verify. A person's signature passes only through a policy rule that names it, never on first use. A registry-declared revision must reuse its CI-signed baseline's deploy digest: a deploy digest a person signed is refused.

pacto delivery trust <service>, the pacto_delivery_trust MCP tool and the dashboard's Published view show the rule, the pins, the signers waiting and the newest verdicts. Setup lists the values.

docs.title: Confirm a new signer
docs.text:
A CI identity no rule, pin or policy covers is a new-signer. The promoter raises one Operation of type delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/trust per service at a time, and the delivery inbox asks "payments: new signer <subject> (issuer, repository, attested). Confirm it may publish payments?".

  • Confirm identity opens the change, where a person approves or rejects it; pacto delivery approve -n <namespace> <operation> does the same. Whoever may update the workload may answer. With team narrowing, only the team that owns the running version is asked, never the team the candidate names. An agent never decides.
  • Once approved, the recorder writes a signed identity-pin/v1 record and the watch accepts that signer. Confirming a signer marks no digest verified: the version still passes every gate.
  • Other new identities wait in the trust view until the open question concludes. A signer that differs from the pinned one asks again ("signer changed from ... to ..."), and confirming it replaces the pin. A rejected signer stays out until delivery.recorder.operationTTL (168h) deletes the operation, then it is asked again; a question nobody answered in time is asked again at once.
  • Pins need the recorder (delivery.recorder.enabled) and a key to verify them: keyless recorder signing or delivery.recorder.signing.publicKey. Without them no question is raised, and status.publisher.message says why.

A pin counts only when it verifies under this cluster's recorder key or a delivery.recorder.trust key that lists an explicit pins/ stream, and only when the approval record it cites verifies and answers the trust operation for the same identity in the namespace the pin names. A Stage uses only the newest pin of its own namespace. Deleting it brings back no older one: the Stage keeps status.publisher.pinAt and judges with no pin while the newest is gone. Pins or a policy the watch could not read leave a signer they may cover unknown: nobody is asked, nothing published leaves and Ready is False.

docs.title: The signed delivery policy
docs.text:
A security owner who wants explicit rules signs a delivery policy: an in-toto statement of predicate type delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/policy/v1 in a Sigstore bundle with one DSSE signature by a role: policy key of delivery.publishers.policySigners, pushed as the one layer of an OCI artifact. delivery.publishers.policy names it by tag.

predicate:
  at: "2026-11-17T09:00:00Z"   # signed time; an older policy is refused
  publishers:
    - name: release
      issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
      subject: ^https://github\.com/acme/[^/]+/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/heads/main$
      repository: ^https://github\.com/acme/[^/]+$
      ref: refs/heads/main
      services: ["pay*"]        # empty covers every service
  signers:
    - name: release bots
      issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
      subject: ^https://github\.com/acme/bots/.+$
      class: agent              # human, agent or ci
  • Every subject and repository pattern is anchored (^...$) and matches no identity nobody has, or the policy is refused. An unknown key is refused too, so an older promoter keeps its last policy.
  • A policy key verifies only policies, never a record or a pin.
  • A tag that fails to read or verify, or that moves to a policy signed before status.publisher.policyAt, keeps the last verified policy. A configured policy that never verified accepts only pinned signers.

docs.title: Signer classes
docs.text: Every verified keyless signer carries a class and classifiedBy. The first signers rule of the policy that matches decides (policy:<name>); otherwise the default rule (default:<reason>) reads a certificate that attests a source repository, or one from a CI issuer, as ci; a SPIFFE, Kubernetes service account or Google service account subject as agent; an email from an interactive login as human; and anything else as agent. Only a human signature makes an approval a decision. A CI- or agent-signed approval record is a proposal and never counts, a trust confirmation included.

docs.title: What stays outside the policies
docs.text:
• The policies match only objects that carry the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref label. A Stage leaves observe only once its pointer carries it.
  • Fields outside the rules stay open, such as an OCIRepository's interval and verify or an Argo CD Application's syncPolicy.
  • The GitOps controllers may create and delete a labelled pointer with no digest check. When the promoter finds a digest it did not write, it records an override and freezes the Stage.
  • No policy matches workloads or the Stage spec. RBAC alone limits kubectl apply on a Deployment.
  • The -agent and -approver roles may get, though not list, a Flux HelmRelease or an Argo CD Application they can name, so a plan can find the version source. That read includes inline Helm values. Bind these roles with a RoleBinding in the Stage namespaces, and keep secrets in valuesFrom rather than inline values.

Close the rest with RBAC on workloads, Stages and pointer objects, and with your own admission on workloads.

docs.title: Signed records
docs.text: A change leaves a signed record only when the recorder is on. The recorder is off by default. Signed records and history sets it up.

docs.title: Delivery reference: setup and gates
docs.text:
Alpha

Delivery is new: its settings and commands may still change.

Reference for Pacto delivery. To pactify a service end to end, follow Pactify a service instead. The API group is delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1 (alpha). Plans, approvals and who may do what are in Delivery reference: plan, propose and approve.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
The two automatic levels need signed records, and records work on any OCI registry. The recorder probes the streams repository: where it serves the OCI Referrers API, records are referrers; where it does not, as on GHCR and CNCF distribution, they are write-once tags in the streams repository.

  • The recorder chooses the mode by itself, and a Stage that recorded native never narrows to tags.
  • With tags, records attached to versions cannot be listed, so what a plan says a version did on other Stages stays partial.
  • Without the Referrers API, pacto publish also gives each signature and SBOM a write-once pacto-sig-<subject hex>-<12 hex> tag, and Pacto reads only those, never the shared sha256-<hex> tag.
  • Only the recorder pushes to the streams repository. People who approve from the CLI need push only on the approvals repository (delivery.recorder.approvalsRepository, default <streamsRepository>-approvals). The recorder also pushes there, once delivery.identities.signers lists a signer. The promoter's delivery.promoter.registryCredentials need pull there: an approval record it cannot read does not count.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Delivery is the pacto-operator chart's delivery section, off by default. Turn it on:

helm upgrade pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.6.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system \
  --reset-then-reuse-values --set delivery.enabled=true
  • delivery.flux.enabled and delivery.argocd.enabled default to auto: the chart grants the promoter access to Flux and Argo CD when the cluster serves their APIs at install or upgrade. Install Flux or Argo CD before Pacto, or run helm upgrade after; with helm template, pass their APIs with --api-versions. true or false decide regardless of the API.
  • The promoter moves versions through the manager that already applies each workload (which manager applies a Stage). The first Stage of a service admits new versions through the promoter's registry watch (spec.candidates.registry, judged against delivery.publishers) or a Flux OCIRepository with spec.verify. A cluster that runs only Argo CD uses the registry watch and needs no Flux.

It needs no identity values: whoever may update a Stage's workload decides (who may decide).

If you set crds.install=false to manage the CRDs yourself, apply the delivery CRDs before you turn delivery on. The promoter and the recorder do not start without them:

kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts \
  -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/pacto/integrations/kubernetes/v6.6.0/integrations/kubernetes/config/crd/bases/delivery.pacto.trianalab.io_approvals.yaml
kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts \
  -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/pacto/integrations/kubernetes/v6.6.0/integrations/kubernetes/config/crd/bases/delivery.pacto.trianalab.io_operations.yaml
kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts \
  -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/pacto/integrations/kubernetes/v6.6.0/integrations/kubernetes/config/crd/bases/delivery.pacto.trianalab.io_stages.yaml

This needs Helm 3.14 or later. Delivery runs in delivery.namespace (pacto-delivery, never the release or node agent namespace), where the operator holds no role, so it cannot act as the promoter. It reads its Secrets only when watched or granted: prefer KMS or keyless recorder signing. Set delivery.createNamespace=false to create the namespace, with the recorder key, yourself. Bind pacto-operator-delivery-agent to agents. People with edit or admin in a namespace may already decide there. The image is signed.

The admission policies make the actor of an Operation and the person behind an Approval true, so the chart always installs them with delivery and refuses Kubernetes below 1.30 and a cluster without the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API. With helm template, pass --api-versions admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, or set delivery.admissionPolicies.skipCapabilityCheck=true to skip only that check. While a policy the chart rendered is missing or weakened, the promoter admits no operation, counts no approval and shows Unguarded (when a policy is missing).

To run an unreleased build, from the repository root:

docker build -f integrations/kubernetes/Dockerfile --target delivery --build-arg CMD=cmd/delivery \
  -t registry.example.com/pacto-delivery:dev .
helm upgrade --install pacto-operator integrations/kubernetes/charts/pacto-operator \
  -n pacto-operator-system --create-namespace --set delivery.enabled=true \
  --set delivery.image.registry=registry.example.com --set delivery.image.repository=pacto-delivery \
  --set delivery.image.tag=dev

The repository of delivery run records must be private.

docs.title: Metrics and Events
docs.text:
The promoter and the recorder serve Prometheus metrics over plain HTTP on port 8080. The promoter's are behind the <release>-delivery-metrics Service; set delivery.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled=true to create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor for it. delivery.recorder.monitoring.enabled=true gives the recorder's their own Service, ServiceMonitor and alerts.

Metric What it counts pacto_delivery_operations_total concluded operations by type, outcome, verification and actor_class: how much shipped with no person, and how often a person accepted an unknown pacto_delivery_verdicts_total gate verdicts of concluded operations and re-checks, by gate, phase and result pacto_delivery_stage_frozen 1 while a Stage is frozen pacto_delivery_stage_watched 0 while the newest re-check of the running version did not pass pacto_delivery_records_pending concluded operations per stream that have no record yet (recorder) pacto_delivery_unverified_approval_records approval records in an approvals repository that do not verify, each counted once; the recorder never turns them into an Approval (recorder) pacto_delivery_stats_dropped_total run records not published, by reason: queue-full, namespace-full (one namespace already holds a quarter of the queue), publish-failed (logged with the operation, and the record in flight when the promoter stops), no-stage (the operation had no Stage, so no service to file it under) or shutdown (still queued, or concluded, after the promoter began to stop). Every reason reads 0 from startup. A shutdown drop is counted by a process about to exit, so its lasting trace is the promoter's log line run records not published at shutdown

The promoter emits a Kubernetes Event on an operation when it waits on a person (Held, with TeamNarrowingOff while owner teams do not narrow who may answer) and when it concludes (its outcome). It emits one on a Stage when it raises a rollback (RollbackRaised), freezes (Frozen) or stops being watched (RecheckUnknown, RecheckFailed). It emits EnvironmentCreated on a Stage the first time it reconciles it, with the Stage's creation time, and EnvironmentDeleted when the Stage is deleted. Each names one Stage, such as "Stage test/payments-pr-482 for payments in pr-482 was deleted"; other Stages for the same environment are unaffected. A promoter restart emits neither again, a Stage whose status was reset emits EnvironmentCreated again with its original creation time, and a Stage deleted while the promoter is down emits nothing.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Upgrade the operator as usual: helm upgrade updates the delivery CRDs, and helm.sh/resource-policy: keep keeps them and their history on uninstall.

docs.title: How a change moves
docs.text:
A Stage names the applier, such as a Flux OCIRepository, and its status.pointer is the digest it moved the environment to. Only the promoter moves it, and the only field it writes on an object it does not own is that repository's spec.ref.digest. Every change is an Operation whose spec never changes:

flowchart LR
  P[Pending] -->|gates pass| L[lock]
  P -->|a person must decide| H[Held]
  H -->|approved| L
  L --> R[Running]
  R -->|Flux applied it| V[Verifying]
  V -->|Pass| S[Succeeded]
  V -->|Fail| F[Failed, rolled back]
  S -->|re-check fails| F
  • Before: pacto.published admits only a version pacto publish published, pacto.diff compares the contracts and pacto.impact checks every consumer in the environment that declares a range on the service, as Who is asked and why explains. Anything unseen (an unreadable Pacto, a registry silent for 10 seconds) is Unknown. pacto.suites holds a version that does not ship a suite one of the Stage's checks names, for a person to accept the unknown. It also holds a version that changes a suite it ships, on every level. pacto.environment holds a version whose contract declares environments but none named like the Stage's spec.environment, or values there that fail their schemas. A contract with no environments passes it. pacto.applier refuses a promote while the Stage's status.applier reads Conflict or Unknown.
  • After: the Pacto contract check counts only when status.evaluatedRevision names this version's contract digest and the current workload generation. Compliant and Warning pass, NonCompliant and Invalid fail, anything else is Unknown. Health checks can join it.
  • Rollbacks, freezes and the 50 failed versions never tried again work as What happens to a change says. A rollback that is refused or unclear also freezes the Stage, and a person's rollback puts an auto-hold on a Stage on an automatic level.

Only six built-in operation types exist: promote, rollback, override, freeze, unfreeze and autonomy, which moves the Stage up or down the autonomy ladder. Stage approval policy is approval.always, not an expression.

docs.title: What the pointer guarantees
docs.text: Pacto mediates the pointer and signed records name it. The pointer alone decides what runs only when nothing else can change it; the Stage's Mediated condition says whether that holds. It is True when exactly one Flux Kustomization applies the apply OCIRepository, both carry the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref label, the Kustomization sets a serviceAccountName and sets none of images, patches, components, postBuild, namePrefix, nameSuffix, kubeConfig, suspend or decryption, and the OCIRepository sets no spec.ignore. Without a serviceAccountName Flux applies each version as kustomize-controller, which is cluster-admin in a default install, so a version whose contract did not change could ship a ClusterRoleBinding and an automatic level would apply it: the levels judge only the contract. pacto init --delivery writes a namespaced deployer account for each environment. On Argo CD it is True when the Application carries the label, has one source and sets no Kustomize images, patches or components, Helm parameters, values or value files, or plugin. Otherwise it is False and the reason (ApplyRefUnguarded, NoApplier, SeveralAppliers, ApplierUnguarded, ApplierUnscoped, ApplierOverrides, SeveralSources) names what else decides what runs.

docs.title: What only break-glass may change
docs.text: On labelled objects, only break-glass may change: removing the label, the OCIRepository's spec.url, spec.layerSelector and spec.ignore, the rest of an Application's spec.source, its spec.sources, spec.destination and spec.project, and a Kustomization's sourceRef, path, images, patches, components, postBuild, namePrefix, nameSuffix, targetNamespace, serviceAccountName, kubeConfig, suspend and decryption. A GitOps tool that applies those objects must leave these fields alone or run as break-glass. Deleting a labelled object, or creating one with the label, is an edit too: only break-glass, system:masters, the namespace controller, the garbage collector and the users in delivery.admissionPolicies.gitopsUsers (Flux's kustomize-controller and Argo CD's application controller by default) may. On kubeadm clusters, kind included, the admin kubeconfig is in kubeadm:cluster-admins, not system:masters, so let GitOps create the pointers or add that user to gitopsUsers. If one of them is ever recreated without the label, the Stage shows Ready False with the reason ApplierUnlabelled and Mediated False with the reason ApplyRefUnguarded. kubectl set image on the workload itself is not mediated: Flux puts it back on its next reconcile, and Argo CD does with selfHeal; until then it runs beside the pointer. The security model lists what each admission policy checks and what stays open.

docs.title: Publishers
docs.text:
• A service's first Stage reads new versions from the registry by default: set spec.candidates.registry, and the promoter watches the repository the Stage's applier takes versions from, or candidates.registry.repository.
  • A Stage names at most one candidate source: registry, ociRepositoryRef, upstreamStage or upstreamRecords.
  • The promoter accepts a version only from a publisher it knows (which publishers Pacto accepts).
spec:
  service: {name: payments}
  applyRef: {name: payments}
  candidates:
    registry: {}   # or {repository: ghcr.io/acme/payments-deploy}
Value What it sets delivery.publishers.registry The host/org your services publish to. On ghcr.io and registry.gitlab.com the promoter derives a rule from it; empty, only the policy or a person's confirmation in the inbox accepts a signer delivery.publishers.defaultBranch The branch whose CI the derived rule accepts (main) delivery.publishers.policy A signed delivery policy (repository:tag) that replaces the derived rule delivery.publishers.policySigners The trust config whose role: policy keys sign that policy delivery.publishers.trustedRoot A trusted_root.json for a private Sigstore; empty uses public-good Sigstore delivery.recorder.signing.publicKey The PEM public key of an Ed25519 or KMS recorder, so the promoter verifies the pins it writes. Keyless recorder signing needs none
  • GHCR serves no Referrers API; the watch reads pacto publish's write-once pacto-sig- tags there, so GHCR works with no extra value.
  • Clients read the same configuration from publishers.json in the pacto-delivery-identities ConfigMap in delivery.namespace.
  • A Stage whose registry cannot be listed has Ready False with the reason RegistryUnreadable, and one without a trusted root PublisherUnverifiable; nothing is published meanwhile.
  • When a policy narrows, a digest among the newest 20 tags that is no longer accepted leaves status.published. One older than those 20 stays there until 50 newer versions push it out: the watch reads only the newest tags.

docs.title: Set up a Stage
docs.text:
With Flux, a first Stage can follow a candidate OCIRepository instead. It follows the deploy artifact's repository and its spec.verify names the publisher, so Flux checks every signature. The Stage lists each digest Flux verified in status.published and refuses anything else as NotPublished. Without a secretRef or matchOIDCIdentity Flux accepts a keyless signature from anyone, so such a Stage promotes nothing. Flux reads a matchOIDCIdentity issuer and subject as regular expressions, so each must be anchored (^...$) and must not match an identity nobody has: .*, or a subject left open at the end, counts as no identity at all. A Stage that cannot promote has Ready False with the reason CandidateUnverified, CandidateNotFound, NoCandidateSource or UpstreamUntrusted.

apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: OCIRepository
metadata: {name: payments-candidates, namespace: test}
spec:
  url: oci://registry/apps/payments
  ref: {semver: ">=0.0.0"}
  verify: {provider: cosign, secretRef: {name: cosign-pub}}
  # keyless: matchOIDCIdentity with the issuer and subject of publish.sign

Label the OCIRepository that applies the Stage with delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref=<stage name>, so admission keeps everyone but the promoter and break-glass off its digest, and give it the same spec.verify. The value names the one Stage that applies through it, so a second Stage cannot drive the same pointer. Without the label, or with another Stage's name in it, the promoter may not write the digest either: the Stage has Ready False with the reason ApplierUnlabelled, and a refused write shows in the operation's status.message. A downstream Stage takes only what its upstream lists in status.offered: versions that passed the published gate and were verified there, never one let through on an accepted unknown.

apiVersion: delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1
kind: Stage
metadata: {name: payments, namespace: prod}
spec:
  service: {name: payments}
  environment: prod
  applyRef: {name: payments}
  candidates:
    upstreamStage: {name: payments, namespace: test}
  startLevel: advise
  gates:
    verify: {window: 5m}

docs.title: Delivery reference: signed approvals
docs.text:
Alpha

Delivery is new: its settings and commands may still change.

With the recorder on, every decision on a held change is a signed record in your registry. CI and agents read it with no cluster credentials. Who may decide is in Delivery reference: approvals.

docs.title: Approval and intent records
docs.text:
Each Stage's stream also holds two smaller in-toto statements. Neither has a seq, and the operation chain skips both:

Predicate type Written by Says delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/operation-intent/v1 the recorder, for every admitted Operation what was asked and by whom (the admission-bound user), whether admission guarded it, and the approvals repository a person pushes a signed approval to; params, reason and cause that look like a secret are left out delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/approval/v1 the recorder for an Approval made in the cluster (dashboard, kubectl), or the person's own client (pacto delivery approve) the operation (name, uid, intent digest, Stage), the decision, the note and who signed: a person, or the recorder with onBehalfOf the person admission verified

The recorder signs an Approval on behalf of its author only while the approval admission policy guards the cluster, and only for Approvals created after it first saw that policy, so turning it on never signs past decisions. It keeps that moment in memory: an Approval made before a recorder restart, or in the second the recorder first saw the policy, gets no record and never counts. Approve again. A person's signed approval goes to the Stage's approvals repository (delivery.recorder.approvalsRepository, published on status.stream.approvals), never to the streams repository. For a held operation the recorder finds it there, verifies it against delivery.identities.signers and makes an Approval for it.

With the recorder on, the promoter counts an Approval made in the cluster once the recorder wrote its record, and an Approval made for a person's signed record only once it fetched that record and verified it. The operation record lists every counted approval with its record id. A verified approval record is a recorded decision: a gate reads the operation record's approvals[] to know whether it counted.

docs.title: Sign a decision from the terminal
docs.text:
The installation can accept approvals a person signs keyless. List the issuers that may sign in delivery.identities.signers:

delivery:
  identities:
    signers:
      - issuer: https://idp.example.com
        clientID: pacto-approve
        usernamePrefix: "https://idp.example.com#"
        subjects: '^[^@]+@example\.com$'   # required
        fulcioURL: https://fulcio.example.com
        timestampURL: https://tsa.example.com/api/v1/timestamp
        trustedRoot: |
          { ... the Sigstore trusted_root.json ... }

pacto delivery approve then logs you in again in your browser, signs the decision keyless with that login alone and pushes the signed record to the Stage's approvals repository. It refuses while SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN or a GitHub Actions token variable is set: approving needs your own fresh login. The issuer must put auth_time, email and email_verified: true in its tokens; Fulcio refuses an unverified email. trustedRoot is required and the command fetches no root: for public-good Fulcio, paste its trusted_root.json.

The approver is usernamePrefix followed by the certificate's email, with no groups, so set the prefix your apiserver puts on that user. That user still needs to be allowed to update the Stage's workload. A certificate that names a URI, an email outside subjects or a workload domain such as *.iam.gserviceaccount.com is an agent and never approves.

A certificate shows neither groups nor a login time, so the command records the Approval in the cluster instead when no signer matches, the Stage asks for a recent sign-in, humanGroups is set or owner teams narrow who may answer. --keyless=false always records it in the cluster.

With no kubeconfig, approve the operation an intent record names:

pacto delivery approve --intent registry.example/pacto/streams@sha256:... \
  --trust recorder.pub --signers identities.yaml --decision approve

Public-good Fulcio logs every certificate, the approver's email included, to Certificate Transparency. Run a private Fulcio to keep emails out of a public log.

docs.title: Read one record with no cluster
docs.text:
record get and record verify take a record reference (<repository>:<tag> or <repository>@<digest>) and read no kubeconfig:

pacto delivery record verify registry.example/pacto/streams@sha256:... \
  --trust recorder.pub --signers identities.yaml

For an approval it says decision recorded (signature verified), then counted, not counted or unknown when the stream cannot be read or holds no record of the operation yet. --signers takes a file holding the pacto-delivery-identities ConfigMap's policy.json, which verifies an approval a person signed. For an intent it prints the pacto delivery approve --intent command that approves it. A reference that finds no records is unknown, never an empty stream.

docs.title: Upgrade: approval records
docs.text: Readers decode records strictly, so an earlier CLI or promoter cannot read an operation record that names its approvals' records: it reports the record unreadable and a follower stops promoting. Upgrade the CLIs and every promoter that follows these streams before you upgrade the recorder. Operation records written with no approval records are unchanged.

docs.title: Delivery reference: status, progress and lifecycle
docs.text:
Alpha

Delivery is new: its settings and commands may still change.

How to read where a service stands in Pacto delivery: what each Stage runs, why a version cannot move yet, what you may ask for and how one version travelled. Every answer here only reads; changes still go through plan, propose and approve.

docs.title: Where each Stage stands
docs.text:
pacto delivery status --service payments
pacto delivery status --service payments --why

pacto delivery status, the MCP tool pacto_delivery_status and the dashboard's service page (/api/delivery/environments?service=payments) return one row per Stage of the service you can see. They read with your own identity. Without -n the CLI reads every namespace you can list; a namespace you cannot list makes the answer partial and appears in unreadable. A partial answer never means the service has no other Stages. The MCP tool takes service, domain, namespace and why; on a person's server, which registers no propose tool, its note says so.

Rows come in promotion order, taken from each Stage's spec.candidates, and each row names its upstream: the Stage, signed records or OCIRepository its candidates come from. Cycles and environments that services order both ways are named in the note and are never silently ordered.

Field What it says state The one state the board also counts: failed, frozen, autohold, waiting, empty, unverified or verified. Status rows add unknown when the Stage's operations could not be read (heldUnknown; the CLI prints ? held) version, contractRef The version the running artifact's contract declares and the digest-pinned contract it names (delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/contract). The dashboard links it to the fleet revision page sourceRevision The source revision pacto publish stamped on the artifact (org.opencontainers.image.revision): an annotation, not signed lastCheck The newest re-check after release: the worst result, when it ran and each verdict with its citation. current is false once the Stage moved to another version watched The Watched condition while lastCheck is about the running version, else Unknown with reason NotRechecked ready, readyFix The Ready condition and, when it is False, the change that clears it offers What you may ask for here, below

The CLI labels a Pass on pacto.diff, pacto.impact or pacto.environment as Checked, as the dashboard does: those gates pass once they ran. Read the message and the plan's floor to learn whether what they found holds the change. The signed result stays Pass.

Each status answer costs one Operation list and one history read per Stage, bounded like pacto delivery history --all (500 Stages in two minutes).

docs.title: Why a version cannot move yet
docs.text:
--why (MCP why: true, the dashboard's /api/delivery/progress) adds progress to each row: a state, a one-sentence summary, every reason with its fix and the promote planned for you. The plan is a dry run and proposes nothing. A status answer plans at most 16 Stages and names the rest in its note; name a namespace with -n to plan the others.

State Meaning up-to-date The Stage runs its newest candidate and nothing is open on it can-promote Nothing holds the candidate back, and there is a candidate to move to needs-person A held change or the plan waits for a person's decision blocked Something must change first: Ready False, no candidate, frozen, observe level, RBAC, a rejected or waiting plan unknown Pacto could not read the operations, the identity policy, the RBAC answer, the Ready condition or the plan; the status predates the Stage's spec; or a change is open on a Stage with nothing to move to

completeness is partial whenever a reason ends in Unknown or is StatusStale, whatever the state: a reason may be missing.

Reason codes: NotReady, ReadyUnknown, StatusStale, NoCandidate, Frozen, AutoHold, Held, InFlight, Level, OpsUnknown, PolicyUnknown, NotPermitted, RBACUnknown, PlanRejected, PlanHeld, PlanWaits and PlanUnknown. A fix prints a command only when you may run it: the approve command only for a person who may answer and did not ask for it, the unfreeze command only for someone admission lets unfreeze and never an approve command for an agent.

autoPromote is the promoter's own reason for not promoting on its own: the level is observe or advise, the Stage is frozen or on auto-hold, there is no candidate or an operation is already in flight. The promoter and this answer share the rule, so they cannot disagree.

Ready reason Fix Unguarded Install or repair the delivery admission policies and their bindings (delivery.enabled on the pacto-operator chart) CandidateNotFound Create the OCIRepository spec.candidates.ociRepositoryRef names CandidateUnverified Set spec.verify on the candidate OCIRepository with a secretRef or matchOIDCIdentity naming the publisher, then publish with pacto publish UpstreamUntrusted Give the promoter the upstream recorder's key (promoter.upstreamTrust) UpstreamUnreadable Make the upstream records readable: the repository, the registry credentials and the upstream trust key NoCandidateSource Set one of spec.candidates.ociRepositoryRef, upstreamStage or upstreamRecords ApplierUnreadable Create the object spec.applyRef names, or install its CRD, and let the promoter read it ApplierUnlabelled Label the applier delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref=<stage> ApplierMultiSource Give the Argo CD Application one OCI spec.source instead of spec.sources ApplierNotOCI Point the Application's spec.source.repoURL at an oci:// repository ApplierNotAutomated Set spec.syncPolicy.automated on the Application ApplierConflict Point spec.applyRef at the manager status.applier names, or move the workloads to the Stage's applier ApplierUnknown Deliver the workloads through Argo CD or Flux so they carry its labels, or let the promoter read them ApplierNotChartRef Point the HelmRelease's spec.chartRef at an OCIRepository

docs.title: What you may do
docs.text:
offers lists promote, unfreeze (while frozen or on auto-hold), freeze and undo, each available or not with a reason. actions keeps only the available promote and unfreeze, as before. Freeze and undo are offered only when the request names a service, so the many-service board costs no history read. An observe Stage and a Stage whose admission policies are missing (Ready False Unguarded) never offer a promote.

An undo offer is labelled undo, never rollback: when the shipping Operation is gone, undo becomes a promote back that runs every gate. pacto delivery undo or /api/delivery/undo gives the definitive plan.

Offers fail closed. Pacto asks the apiserver once per namespace whether you may create Operations; a denial, or a review that fails, makes every offer there unavailable and says why. When the delivery identity policy cannot be read, every offer is unavailable with the error, and a NotFound suggests --delivery-namespace; see approvals. Offers only describe: proposing still goes through pacto delivery propose, the dashboard's propose action or an agent's propose tool with your own identity. Admission decides.

docs.title: Follow one version
docs.text:
pacto delivery lifecycle --service payments --version 3.0.0

pacto delivery lifecycle, pacto_delivery_lifecycle and /api/delivery/lifecycle take a service and exactly one of --digest (the artifact), --version (its contract's version) or --contract (a manifest digest or a digest-pinned reference), with an optional domain and namespace. A version or contract is found among at most 200 artifacts the Stages remember; several matches is an error that lists them. When artifacts were left unread, past that limit or because the registry failed, or a Stage listing was refused, a miss says what was not read and a single match says another may share it and makes the answer partial. The dashboard answers 404 LifecycleNotFound only for a miss from a complete search and 400 LifecycleUnresolved otherwise.

signature follows the Publish page's rule: signed when a Stage you can see names the artifact in status.published or status.offered, unsigned only when an entry Stage whose published list never reached its cap does not name it, else unknown. The source revision is an annotation, not signed.

Per Stage, each event has a role: arrived, left or attempted. verified and failed read yes, no or unknown; a partial history or a list at its cap answers unknown, never "never reached". Each Stage lists its newest 50 events. note names a Stage that runs the artifact on a complete history with no arrived event: it was placed before its records began or moved outside Pacto.

docs.title: One record
docs.text:
pacto delivery record get -n prod --stage payments sha256:...

pacto delivery record get, pacto_delivery_record_get and /api/delivery/record take a namespace, a Stage and the record id a history line names (or the short id a text history prints when only one record starts with it), and return that record: the change, who asked and approved, every verdict with how to run it again and whether its signature was checked against a trust config. A record that does not verify is never returned; history lists it as unverifiedRecord. Given a record reference instead, record get and the stdio tool read any record, approvals and intents included, with no kubeconfig (read one record with no cluster).

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
Pacto delivery decides which version of each service runs in each environment, such as test and prod. It uses your contracts to tell a safe change from a risky one, asks a person only when it must and rolls back a version that fails its checks. Flux does the actual switch from one version to the next (Argo CD can do it instead, as an experimental option). Words in links are defined in the glossary.

Delivery is opt-in. It is a separate install, and only with it does Pacto change what runs. To set it up for a service, pactify it: give it a contract and connect it to delivery.

Alpha

Delivery is new: its settings and commands may still change.

docs.title: What happens to a change
docs.text:
A change is a request such as "run payments 2.4.0 in prod". A person, your build pipeline or an AI agent can ask for one. Every change takes the same path:

flowchart LR
  A[Request] --> B[Checks before]
  B -->|safe| D[Apply]
  B -->|could break someone| C[A person decides]
  C -->|approved| D
  D --> E[Checks after]
  E -->|pass| F[Done]
  E -->|fail| G{Safe to roll back?}
  F -->|a later check fails| G
  G -->|yes, once| R[Rolled back]
  G -->|no| Z[Frozen until a person decides]

Before it moves, Pacto checks that this version was published with pacto publish, Pacto's release command, and signed, which proves who published it. It compares the new contract with the one running and looks at every service in that environment that uses this one. If none of them would break, the change goes ahead on its own on an automatic level.

After Flux applies it, Pacto checks that the running version does what its contract says. You can add health checks too, such as error rates from your monitoring. These checks keep running after release, so a problem found an hour later still rolls the version back once, whoever asked for it: the version that ran before is put back. The Stage freezes instead when there is nothing safe to go back to, the rollback itself fails, someone chose the running version by hand (a rollback, or a promote during auto-hold) or someone else already took the name of the rollback Pacto raises. It then waits for a person to roll back or unfreeze it, from the dashboard or the command line. A failure of a version Pacto shipped with no person also costs the Stage one level: see Step-down. None of a Stage's last 50 failed versions is tried again there.

docs.title: Stages and records
docs.text:
A version reaches prod only after it passed in the environment before it, such as test. Each service in each environment is called a Stage, and moving a Stage to a new version is called promoting it. A Stage can promote on its own only once a person has raised it up the autonomy ladder.

Every change that ends, refusals included, can leave a signed record in your registry. The signature shows the record was not changed later. Anyone can check who asked for what, who approved and what each check said. Records are off until you turn on the recorder, and they need a registry that serves OCI Referrers.

docs.title: Who is asked and why
docs.text:
Each contract lists the services it depends on and the versions of each it accepts (its consumer range), for example "checkout accepts payments 2.x". That is how Pacto knows who a change can break.

Say payments 3.0.0 removes a field. In prod, checkout and orders still accept only payments 2.x. The change waits for the checkout and orders teams, whose services it would break.

A breaking change that no contract depends on still waits for a person, who can accept the unknown, because a service without a contract may call it. A Stage whose every consumer has a contract can say so with gates.impact.declaredConsumersOnly: true.

Pacto also says what to update first. If checkout 1.9.0 accepts both payments 2.x and 3.0.0 and already passed in test, Pacto's plan says to ship it first. Then only the orders team is still asked.

Pacto judges by declared version ranges, per consumer. Traffic shows which service calls which; Pacto has no view of the fields or endpoints each call uses. Why you were asked lists every case in which a change waits for a person.

docs.title: Who may approve
docs.text:
AI agents can plan, ask for and cancel their own changes, but only people can approve. The person who asked cannot approve, and neither can the person an agent says it acts for (--on-behalf-of, which the agent claims and Pacto never checks). An agent that leaves it out hides who is behind it, so the two-person rule holds only for changes a person asks for directly or an agent asks for in their name.

A person approves with the sign-in they have, and the record names them. You can also ask for a recent sign-in to decide. That needs a cluster that trusts your company login, untested on EKS, GKE and AKS; where approving works says how to check and what to do without it.

docs.title: What Unknown means
docs.text:
Every check answers Pass, Fail or Unknown. Unknown means Pacto could not see enough to say: too little monitoring data, a registry that did not answer, a breaking change that no contract depends on. Pacto sees only the consumers that have a contract, so a service with no contract may still call the one that changed.

An Unknown check holds the change for a person, who can reject it or accept the unknown. The record marks that check as accepted and names who accepted it.

docs.title: Where you follow it
docs.text:
• The dashboard, the web page pacto dashboard starts, gains a Delivery tab once it knows who you are (you sign in, or run it on your own machine): the changes waiting for your team, what each environment runs, past changes with who asked and who approved, and the publishes Pacto refused.
  • The command line: pacto delivery status shows where each Stage of a service stands and what you may ask for, pacto delivery plan what would happen before you ask, pacto delivery history what already did and pacto delivery lifecycle where one version went. kubectl get pacto-delivery -A lists every Stage, Operation and Approval; name a kind in full, such as stages.delivery.pacto.trianalab.io, where another tool also defines a Stage.
  • AI agents get the same tools through pacto mcp --delivery. MCP is the common way AI agents call tools. There is no approve tool.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
None of these is required reading:

  • Setup and gates: install and Stages by hand
  • Plan, propose and approve: what moves first and who may do what
  • Status, progress and lifecycle: where each Stage stands and why a version cannot move yet
  • Health checks: monitoring, the suites a version ships and the calls a service makes
  • Eval providers: suite runners and their signed answers
  • Approvals: who may approve and the dashboard's delivery settings
  • Agents: the person an agent acts for and agents over the network
  • Signed records and history: records, blame, undo and verification
  • Record keys: trust, key rotation and revocation
  • Appliers and several clusters: Argo CD, Flux HelmRelease and Stages in other clusters
  • Ladder reference: levels, proposals and blockers
  • Publishing details and the contract's publish section

To see all of it run on your machine, try the Kubernetes demo.

docs.title: What Pacto detects
docs.text:
On start and every 5 minutes the operator reads what the cluster provides and writes it to the <release>-detected ConfigMap in its namespace, such as pacto-operator-detected. Each row is inferred and carries its source and when it was read. Nothing is turned on: detection changes no argument, rule or feature.

Row Read from Example Registry Running pods, one vote per namespace ghcr.io/acme in 9 of 11 namespaces, 87% of workloads Cloud Node providerID and labels GKE on 6 of 6 nodes Sign-in API discovery Dex serves dex.coreos.com/v1 Exposure HTTPRoutes and Ingresses, one vote per namespace Gateway API with HTTPRoutes in 4 of 5 namespaces Metrics API discovery Prometheus Operator serves monitoring.coreos.com/v1 Nodes Node kernels kernel 6.1 on 6 of 6 with BTF likely

The rows show under Data sources in the dashboard, in helm upgrade notes and in the CLI:

pacto fleet status --k8s --detected k8s:pacto-operator-system/pacto-operator-detected

A registry or exposure row prints a command to review only when one candidate holds most namespaces and leads every other one. Docker Hub official images are never proposed as a push target. BTF reads likely, unlikely or unknown and is never confirmed. A missing or stale detection shows on its own row and never makes an answer partial.

With controller.watchNamespaces the registry row is partial and names the watched namespaces, and cloud and nodes are unknown. Beyond the ConfigMap it writes and the operator Deployment that owns it, the only grant detection adds is nodes list in the cluster-wide ClusterRole; see Run with least privilege.

docs.title: The Evidence Server
docs.text:
The Evidence Server lets places the operator cannot watch, such as CI runners or edge sites, send signed reports about a service into your cluster. Pacto checks each report against the contract and stores it in your registry. Evidence here means a record of what a tool saw in a running system.

It is off by default (evidence.enabled: false). Turning it on needs three things the chart cannot guess. Settle the first before you publish anything: it decides which registry the contract itself has to live in.

docs.title: Check the registry serves the native Referrers API
docs.text: Each report is stored next to the contract version it is about, in the same registry repository, as an OCI 1.1 referrer (an artifact that points at another artifact). Pacto has no fallback to the older tag-based scheme, so the registry holding the contract must support Referrers lookup. GHCR does not qualify, and neither does CNCF distribution (registry:2, registry:3); see Evidence in OCI. This matters because every other page on this site publishes to ghcr.io. Choose a conformant registry for the contract before you run pacto push.

docs.title: Create the trust store
docs.text:
pacto evidence keygen mints an Ed25519 pair and names the public key after the trust binding the server reads: <producerId>__<keyId>.pub, or a bare <keyId>.pub when there is a single producer:

pacto evidence keygen --out ./keys --producer acme-ci --key-id release-2026

key id:      release-2026
private key: keys/release-2026.key
public key:  keys/acme-ci__release-2026.pub

The Secret is mounted whole and read-only at /etc/pacto/trust, so each Secret key has to be the public-key filename, which is what --from-file gives you. One --from-file per trusted producer:

kubectl create secret generic pacto-evidence-trust \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system \
  --from-file=keys/acme-ci__release-2026.pub

The private .key stays with the producer that signs; the cluster needs only the public key. Evidence security covers rotation and multi-producer trust.

docs.title: Get the subject digest
docs.text:
A subject is one immutable contract revision, and pacto push prints the digest of the revision it just published:

Pushed payments-api@2.1.0 -> registry.example.com/your-org/your-service-pacto:2.1.0
Digest: sha256:<64 hex characters>

Then install:

helm install pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system --create-namespace \
  --set evidence.enabled=true \
  --set 'evidence.registry.subjects[0]=oci://registry.example.com/your-org/your-service-pacto@sha256:<digest>' \
  --set evidence.trust.existingSecret=pacto-evidence-trust
  • At least one subject. evidence.registry.subjects lists the exact, immutable contract revisions evidence may be reported against, each an oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest> reference. The chart's schema rejects an empty list, so helm install fails before anything reaches the cluster: at '/evidence/registry/subjects': minItems: got 0, want 1. It rejects a short or tag-shaped reference the same way: the digest has to be all 64 hex characters.
  • A trust store. evidence.trust.existingSecret names the Secret you created above. The chart does not check this one, so an install without it succeeds and the operator then exits at startup with evidence enabled but no trust secret set: signature verification is mandatory. Verification is mandatory.
  • A registry that serves the native Referrers API, as above. Nothing checks it at install time: the chart installs, the operator starts and the failure surfaces later as an Evidence Server that never becomes ready.

If that registry is private, there is a fourth thing you create yourself: a kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret named by evidence.registry.credentialsSecret, mounted read-only as a DOCKER_CONFIG directory so the server authenticates the way pacto pull does. Leave the value empty for an anonymous or in-cluster registry.

See the Helm reference for the full value list and Operator configuration for the controller flags each value maps to.

docs.title: Verifying the install
docs.text:
evidence.enabled=true adds a third Deployment, pacto-evidence, created by the controller the same way the dashboard is:

NAME              READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
pacto-dashboard   1/1     1            1           16s
pacto-evidence    1/1     1            1           14s
pacto-operator    1/1     1            1           21s

1/1 means more than "the process started". Readiness is GET /api/evidence/v1/ready, which answers 503 until every subject resolves in the registry and answers native Referrers discovery. A pacto-evidence stuck at 0/1 is nearly always a subject the cluster cannot pull or a registry without the Referrers API. Read the server's own log:

kubectl -n pacto-operator-system logs deploy/pacto-evidence

The Service is pacto-evidence on port 8686. Producers inside the cluster POST signed envelopes to it:

http://pacto-evidence.pacto-operator-system.svc:8686/api/evidence/v1/envelopes

A pacto fleet outside the cluster consumes the same server's read-only contribution by base URL. --evidence-url appends /api/evidence/v1/targets itself, so leave it out:

kubectl port-forward -n pacto-operator-system svc/pacto-evidence 8686:8686 &
pacto fleet search --evidence-url http://127.0.0.1:8686

The targets endpoint takes no authentication and knows no caller, so no viewer restriction applies to it. It lists contract references, producers, the external references of provisioned resources and the usage and cost of every consumer's resources, so keep the Service behind the same network and auth boundary as the dashboard.

A pacto fleet or dashboard reads every provisioning and usage record that endpoint lists as signed, because the server checked each signature before it stored the record; the reader re-checks none. Point --evidence-url only at your own Evidence Server over a path you trust, such as TLS to its host or the port-forward above. Anyone who can answer on that URL can make a forged phase or cost read as signed.

docs.title: Provisioning reports
docs.text: A provider adapter reports the state of a resource a consumer's contract asked for as a ResourceProvisioned EvidenceSet, written with pacto evidence provisioned. The report is stored on the consumer's contract revision, so that revision must be one of the evidence.registry.subjects. Use one EvidenceSet subject per resource: the default, <repository>/<environment or default>/<kind>/<name>, keeps each resource's latest report apart.

docs.title: Grant the adapter's key
docs.text:
Only a key whose trust entry lists ResourceProvisioned in allowedObservationKinds may report it, so give the adapter its own key. By default the server trusts every .pub key in the trust Secret, which grants every runtime kind and withholds ResourceProvisioned. To accept provisioning reports, add a structured trust config to the same Secret and name its key in evidence.trust.configKey:

apiVersion: pacto.dev/evidence-trust/v1
keys:
  - keyId: release-2026
    producerId: acme-ci
    publicKeyFile: acme-ci__release-2026.pub
  - keyId: adapter-2026
    producerId: platform-adapter
    publicKeyFile: platform-adapter__adapter-2026.pub
    allowedObservationKinds: [ResourceProvisioned]
    allowedProviderRepos: [ghcr.io/acme/platform/postgresql]

A usage adapter's key lists ResourceUsage instead. Give each adapter its own key, scoped with allowedProviderRepos to the provider repositories it serves. A report is in scope when the consumer's declared configuration or dependency ref names a repository under one of the prefixes, so the PostgreSQL adapter above can never mark a Redis cache Ready. The server refuses a report outside the scope with HTTP 403 and the code provider_not_allowed, and logs a startup warning for every provisioning or usage key with no scope. Reports accepted before a key is narrowed stay until a newer report replaces them or they pass the provisioning window. The field needs Pacto core 4.5.0 or later; older servers refuse the config. The unsigned target-state file has no keys, so the scope cannot protect it.

kubectl create secret generic pacto-evidence-trust \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system \
  --from-file=trust.yaml \
  --from-file=keys/acme-ci__release-2026.pub \
  --from-file=keys/platform-adapter__adapter-2026.pub

Add --set evidence.trust.configKey=trust.yaml to the install command above. The server then starts with --trust /etc/pacto/trust/trust.yaml, and each publicKeyFile names another key of the Secret. The config replaces the directory scan, so list every key you trust: a .pub key it omits is no longer trusted. The chart accepts only a .yaml or .yml key.

docs.title: Read provisioning reports
docs.text:
The targets endpoint answers with schema pacto.dev/evidence-source/v5 when it carries a cluster, which the operator passes, so upgrade older readers that accept only v2 to v4. Without a cluster it answers with pacto.dev/evidence-source/v4 and a usage list when it holds usage reports, with pacto.dev/evidence-source/v3 and a provisioning list when it holds only provisioning reports, and with pacto.dev/evidence-source/v2 otherwise, so an older reader keeps working against a server that holds none. A provider report is never a target.

Nothing durable lives in the cluster: no PersistentVolumeClaim, no data volume, because the registry is the store. Delete and recreate the Deployment and the accepted evidence is still there. Evidence in OCI covers what is written and where; the ingestion API lists all five endpoints.

docs.title: Kargo
docs.text:
Gate every Kargo promotion with one shared ClusterAnalysisTemplate. When Freight lands in a Stage, Kargo runs an AnalysisRun whose Job runs pacto impact --running on the Freight's contract bundle. The Freight verifies only when no consumer that runs breaks.

Kargo verifies after it promotes. A failed verification keeps the Freight from the next Stage and leaves this Stage as promoted: it does not roll back. Pacto writes nothing to Kargo, Argo or Git.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Kargo v1.12 or later, with the Argo Rollouts CRDs and controller: Rollouts runs the AnalysisRun Job.
  • Each service publishes its contract bundle with pacto push, and a Kargo Warehouse subscribes to that bundle repository like an image, with the default SemVer selection.
  • Every cluster Kargo deploys to runs the Pacto operator with the registry value, so it publishes its signed target snapshot.

docs.title: Install the template
docs.text:
Apply the template once per Kargo installation:

# This file is published verbatim in integrations/kubernetes/docs/gitops-kargo.md.
# Kargo runs it after each promotion: impact exit 0 verifies the Freight, exit 1
# fails it, exit 2 (unverified) fails it unless allow-unverified is "true".
# In each Kargo project namespace: kubectl -n <project> create serviceaccount pacto-impact
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterAnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: pacto-impact
spec:
  args:
    - name: new
    - name: targets
      value: snapshot
    - name: allow-unverified
      value: "false"
  metrics:
    - name: pacto-impact
      count: 1
      failureLimit: 0
      provider:
        job:
          spec:
            backoffLimit: 0
            template:
              spec:
                restartPolicy: Never
                serviceAccountName: pacto-impact
                containers:
                  - name: pacto-impact
                    image: ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.6.1
                    command: [sh, -c]
                    args:
                      - |
                        set -u
                        case "$TARGETS" in
                          snapshot) set -- ;;
                          k8s) set -- --k8s ;;
                          *) echo "pacto-impact: targets must be snapshot or k8s, got $TARGETS"; exit 1 ;;
                        esac
                        pacto impact --running "$NEW" --local "" "$@"; rc=$?
                        case "$rc" in
                          0) exit 0 ;;
                          2) if [ "$ALLOW_UNVERIFIED" = true ]; then echo "impact exit 2 passes: allow-unverified is true"; exit 0; fi
                             echo "impact exit 2: unverified fails unless allow-unverified is true"; exit 1 ;;
                          *) echo "impact exit $rc"; exit 1 ;;
                        esac
                    # Args first: a literal below wins over any name an arg could repeat.
                    env:
                      - name: NEW
                        value: "{{args.new}}"
                      - name: TARGETS
                        value: "{{args.targets}}"
                      - name: ALLOW_UNVERIFIED
                        value: "{{args.allow-unverified}}"
                      - name: PACTO_INSECURE_REGISTRIES
                        value: ""
                      - name: PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK
                        value: "1"
                      - name: DOCKER_CONFIG
                        value: /home/pacto/.docker
                      - name: PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST
                        value: /etc/pacto/trust/trust.yaml
                    securityContext:
                      runAsNonRoot: true
                      runAsUser: 65532
                      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                      capabilities:
                        drop: [ALL]
                    volumeMounts:
                      - name: pacto-cache
                        mountPath: /home/pacto/.cache
                      - name: pacto-registry
                        mountPath: /home/pacto/.docker
                        readOnly: true
                      - name: pacto-delivery-trust
                        mountPath: /etc/pacto/trust
                        readOnly: true
                volumes:
                  - name: pacto-cache
                    emptyDir: {}
                  - name: pacto-registry
                    secret:
                      secretName: pacto-registry
                      optional: true
                      items:
                        - key: .dockerconfigjson
                          path: config.json
                  - name: pacto-delivery-trust
                    secret:
                      secretName: pacto-delivery-trust
                      optional: true

In each Kargo project namespace, create the pacto-impact ServiceAccount, the pacto-delivery-trust Secret and, for a private registry, the pacto-registry Secret:

kubectl apply -f kargo-cluster-analysis-template.yaml
kubectl -n <project> create serviceaccount pacto-impact
kubectl -n <project> create secret generic pacto-delivery-trust --from-file=trust.yaml
kubectl -n <project> create secret docker-registry pacto-registry \
  --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=<user> --docker-password=<token>

trust.yaml holds one entry per cluster, from its installation key and scoped to its UID: see Target snapshot consumers. Pacto hands each registry only its own entry from the mounted Docker config. The template takes no registry credentials as args and cannot mark a registry insecure.

docs.title: Verify each Stage
docs.text:
Every Stage carries the same stanza. vars.pactoBundle is the only service-specific value, and the Stage already names it for its subscription:

spec:
  vars:
    - name: pactoBundle
      value: ghcr.io/acme/contracts/payments
  verification:
    analysisTemplates:
      - name: pacto-impact
        kind: ClusterAnalysisTemplate
    args:
      - name: new
        value: oci://${{ vars.pactoBundle }}@${{ imageFrom(vars.pactoBundle).Digest }}
pacto impact The Freight 0 clear Verified 1 blocked, or could not run Failed 2 unverified Failed unless the Stage sets allow-unverified: "true"

That is the policy of the pull request check: an unverified answer never passes by default.

docs.title: What it judges against
docs.text: Kargo cannot name a Stage's previously verified Freight, so --running judges the Freight against every revision of its service that runs on a known target, and the worst answer wins. A revision already running with the Freight's digest is not its own baseline, so Freight that Argo CD has synced is never judged against itself. With no other revision running, only the consumers' version ranges speak, and a running consumer that refuses the new version still blocks. Once every target runs the Freight, the revision it replaced is no longer observed, so a breaking change that consumers' ranges accept clears here; only the pull request check, which runs before promotion, catches it.

docs.title: Choose where targets come from
docs.text:
The targets arg picks the source:

  • snapshot (default) reads the signed target snapshots in <registry>/pacto-targets beside the bundle and needs no cluster RBAC. A missing, unsigned or stale snapshot makes the answer partial, so unverified.
  • k8s reads the Job's own cluster. Use it only when Kargo and every target share this cluster. Apply the reader role and bind it to each project's ServiceAccount:
# This file is published verbatim in integrations/kubernetes/docs/gitops-kargo.md.
# Only for targets: k8s. It is what `pacto impact --k8s` reads: the cluster
# identity, the Pacto CRs and the workload lists. The default targets: snapshot
# needs none of it.
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: pacto-impact-reader
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [namespaces]
    resourceNames: [kube-system]
    verbs: [get]
  - apiGroups: [pacto.trianalab.io]
    resources: [pactos]
    verbs: [get, list]
  - apiGroups: [apps]
    resources: [deployments, statefulsets, daemonsets]
    verbs: [list]
  - apiGroups: [batch]
    resources: [cronjobs]
    verbs: [list]
# For each Kargo project namespace, after creating the pacto-impact
# ServiceAccount there:
#
# apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
# kind: ClusterRoleBinding
# metadata:
#   name: pacto-impact-<project>
# roleRef:
#   apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
#   kind: ClusterRole
#   name: pacto-impact-reader
# subjects:
#   - kind: ServiceAccount
#     name: pacto-impact
#     namespace: <project>
#
# Narrower: a RoleBinding to the same ClusterRole in each namespace the project
# may read. Pacto lists every namespace, so a refused list makes the answer
# partial: at best unverified.
#
# apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
# kind: RoleBinding
# metadata:
#   name: pacto-impact-<project>
#   namespace: <namespace>
# roleRef:
#   apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
#   kind: ClusterRole
#   name: pacto-impact-reader
# subjects:
#   - kind: ServiceAccount
#     name: pacto-impact
#     namespace: <project>

A ClusterRoleBinding gives that project read access to every namespace's Pacto CRs and to the names and images of its workloads. The role lists workloads because an unread workload may run a revision no contract describes, and an unread revision never clears.

docs.title: Read the reason
docs.text:
The AnalysisRun only says the metric failed. The reason is in the Job log:

$ kubectl -n shop get analysisruns.argoproj.io -l kargo.akuity.io/stage=prod
NAME                 STATUS
prod.01jd...         Failed
$ kubectl -n shop logs job/<analysisrun-job>
Impact: payments 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0
...
Running: 1 revision (judged against oci://ghcr.io/acme/contracts/payments:1.0.0@sha256:4f1c...)
...
Release gate: blocked
impact exit 1

The Running: line names the judged revision by tag and digest.

docs.title: Check that it took
docs.text:
kubectl get clusteranalysistemplates.argoproj.io pacto-impact

Then promote Freight whose contract you know is safe and watch its AnalysisRun reach Successful.

docs.title: Fallback: a project-local template
docs.text: A project that cannot use a cluster-scoped template copies the same metric into a namespaced AnalysisTemplate and references it with kind: AnalysisTemplate.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• A ClusterAnalysisTemplate is cluster-wide: every project that references it gets the same exit policy unless its Stage overrides allow-unverified.
  • Verification follows promotion. Gate before a promotion in the pull request that publishes the contract.

docs.title: GitOps promotion gates
docs.text:
Make Flux or Argo CD stop the next rollout step when a service breaks its contract. For Kargo, see Kargo. A NonCompliant Pacto turns the Kustomization unready or the Application Degraded.

The health snippets stop the next step: by the time the operator has a verdict the pods are already serving. The Argo CD plugin stops the render, before Argo CD applies anything. With Flux, catch a breaking change in the pull request with pacto impact.

Flux and Argo CD read status.contractStatus only through an extension point, which the two health snippets below configure.

docs.title: Flux
docs.text:
Flux decides health with kstatus, its built-in status reader, which recognises only the Ready, Reconciling and Stalled conditions. Pacto publishes ContractValid, RuntimeObserved and ReadinessSatisfied, so kstatus discards all three and the object falls through to Current: the gate looks configured and passes everything. spec.healthCheckExprs (kustomize-controller v1.5.0, flux2 v2.5.0 and later) replaces that fallback with a CEL expression:

# Flux promotion gate driven by the Pacto contract verdict.
#
# This file is published verbatim in integrations/kubernetes/docs/gitops.md and
# applied verbatim by tests/acceptance/kind/gitops-flux.sh. Edit it and you edit
# both; the documented snippet cannot drift from the tested one.
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: orders-staging
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  # Must exceed the operator's stabilization window (default 2m) plus one
  # requeue interval, or a real violation arrives as an ambiguous timeout
  # instead of a clean failure.
  timeout: 5m
  prune: true
  wait: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: OCIRepository
    name: orders
  path: ./staging
  healthCheckExprs:
    - apiVersion: pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1
      kind: Pacto
      failed: status.contractStatus in ['NonCompliant', 'Invalid']
      current: status.contractStatus in ['Compliant', 'Reference', 'Warning']
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: orders-production
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  timeout: 5m
  prune: true
  wait: true
  # Production does not start until staging is healthy, and healthy now
  # includes the contract verdict. This line is the promotion gate.
  dependsOn:
    - name: orders-staging
  sourceRef:
    kind: OCIRepository
    name: orders
  path: ./production

sourceRef is whatever you already use. Three things about that snippet, each checked against fluxcd/pkg runtime/cel/status_evaluator.go:

  • The snippet leaves out inProgress on purpose. When no expression matches, Flux falls through to in-progress, so an unrecognised verdict holds the deploy until it times out. It fails closed.
  • Warning sits in the passing set. Move that one word to failed if you want contract warnings to block promotions. That is the whole knob.
  • timeout must exceed the operator's stabilization window, or a real violation reaches you as an ambiguous timeout. See Timing.

A freshly created Pacto has no status and the expression errors while that is true; Flux treats the error as not-yet-healthy and keeps polling.

tests/acceptance/kind/gitops-flux.sh applies that exact file to a kind cluster and asserts the dependent Kustomization never reaches it while the contract is violated.

docs.title: Argo CD
docs.text:
Argo picks a health check from a fixed list of built-in kinds and returns no health for any other kind. The roll-up into Application health skips a resource with no health, so Argo ignores a Pacto. A resource health customization in argocd-cm supplies the missing check:

# Argo CD health customization that makes a violated Pacto contract turn its
# Application red.
#
# This file is published verbatim in integrations/kubernetes/docs/gitops.md.
# Apply it as a MERGE PATCH, never as a plain `kubectl apply` -- argocd-cm holds
# Argo's own keys and a full apply would drop them:
#
#   kubectl -n argocd patch configmap argocd-cm --type merge \
#     --patch-file argocd-cm-pacto-health.yaml
#
# The data key must be typed exactly. Argo silently ignores a key it does not
# recognise, which looks identical to having configured nothing at all.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  resource.customizations.health.pacto.trianalab.io_Pacto: |
    -- Argo runs this with the Lua string library disabled.
    -- Only concatenation, comparison, ipairs and tostring() are available.

    -- Set to "Degraded" to make contract warnings block a promotion.
    local warningHealth = "Healthy"

    local hs = {}

    if obj.status == nil or obj.status.contractStatus == nil then
      hs.status = "Progressing"
      hs.message = "waiting for the first contract evaluation"
      return hs
    end

    if obj.status.observedGeneration ~= obj.metadata.generation then
      hs.status = "Progressing"
      hs.message = "contract not yet evaluated at this generation"
      return hs
    end

    local s = obj.status.contractStatus

    if s == "Compliant" or s == "Reference" then
      hs.status = "Healthy"
      hs.message = "contract satisfied"
      return hs
    end

    if s == "Warning" then
      hs.status = warningHealth
      hs.message = "contract satisfied with warnings"
      return hs
    end

    if s == "NonCompliant" then
      hs.status = "Degraded"
      hs.message = "contract violated"
      if obj.status.findings ~= nil then
        for _, f in ipairs(obj.status.findings) do
          if f.severity == "error" then
            hs.message = "contract violated: " .. tostring(f.code) .. ": " .. tostring(f.message)
            break
          end
        end
      end
      return hs
    end

    if s == "Invalid" then
      hs.status = "Degraded"
      hs.message = "contract is invalid and could not be evaluated"
      return hs
    end

    -- Unknown, NotEvaluated, and anything added later.
    hs.status = "Progressing"
    hs.message = "contract verdict pending: " .. tostring(s)
    return hs

Apply it as a merge patch, because argocd-cm holds Argo's own configuration and a plain kubectl apply would drop it. Then restart the controller:

kubectl -n argocd patch configmap argocd-cm --type merge \
  --patch-file argocd-cm-pacto-health.yaml
kubectl -n argocd rollout restart statefulset/argocd-application-controller

The restart is required. The application controller reads health customizations into its resource cache at startup, and that cached verdict is what it compares to decide whether a changed object needs re-examining. Until it has the customization, every verdict the operator writes compares equal to the last and the Application only catches up on the next periodic resync. On a core install, without argocd-server, a restart is the only way in: hot reload of argocd-cm needs server.secretkey, which only argocd-server creates.

In the Lua, anything unrecognised becomes Progressing. Argo's Unknown ranks worse than Degraded and would mask broken workloads, so the script never returns it. The string library is also disabled, so string.format and s:gsub() fail at runtime, after the script loads.

tests/acceptance/kind/gitops-argocd.sh runs that exact file through the Lua sandbox with no cluster, and then inside a kind cluster where an Application must go Degraded naming the finding and back to Healthy once corrected.

docs.title: Check that it took
docs.text:
Argo ignores a data key it does not recognise, and an ignored key looks exactly like having configured nothing:

# The key must read back exactly, group and kind included.
kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.resource\.customizations\.health\.pacto\.trianalab\.io_Pacto}'

Then ask Argo what it makes of a real object. argocd admin settings evaluates the customization against files on disk, in the same Lua sandbox the controller uses, so it answers without waiting for a sync:

kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o yaml > /tmp/argocd-cm.yaml
kubectl -n <namespace> get pacto <name> -o yaml > /tmp/pacto.yaml

argocd admin settings resource-overrides health /tmp/pacto.yaml \
  --argocd-cm-path /tmp/argocd-cm.yaml

A Compliant Pacto prints STATUS: Healthy and MESSAGE: contract satisfied. A key that did not take prints Health script is not configured while exiting 0, so read the output and ignore the exit code. Both checks read the ConfigMap, so they also pass on a controller that started before the patch.

docs.title: Gate every Argo CD sync
docs.text:
A Config Management Plugin sidecar on argocd-repo-server gates every auto-detected Application whose folder holds a contract pacto.yaml. It renders the folder with helm template or kustomize build, then runs pacto impact --running on the rendered Pacto object's contractRef, or on pacto.yaml when the render holds none. That judges the contract against the revisions that run on known targets, read from the signed target snapshots. Argo CD receives the manifests only after a pass.

An Application that sets spec.source.helm, kustomize or directory skips plugin discovery, so its editors can opt out: restrict who edits Applications with AppProjects and Argo CD RBAC.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: pacto-cmp-plugin
  namespace: argocd
data:
  plugin.yaml: |
    apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
    kind: ConfigManagementPlugin
    metadata:
      name: pacto
    spec:
      discover:
        # A contract has neither top-level key; a Pacto object saved as
        # pacto.yaml has both, and is left to Argo CD's own detection.
        find:
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - 'test -f pacto.yaml && ! grep -qE "^(apiVersion|kind):" pacto.yaml && echo pacto.yaml'
      generate:
        command: [sh, /home/argocd/cmp-server/config/generate.sh]
  generate.sh: |
    # Pacto sync gate: render, judge the contract the render applies against
    # what runs, and print the manifests only after a pass. Stdout is the
    # manifest stream, so nothing else writes to it.
    set -u
    fail() { echo "pacto plugin: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

    # Unpinned (no word, or a word without :cluster-) reads only the clusters
    # that published a tag right now, so a missing one reads as no consumers.
    pinned=false
    for ref in ${PACTO_TARGET_SNAPSHOT:-}; do
      case "$ref" in
        *:cluster-*) pinned=true ;;
        *) pinned=false; break ;;
      esac
    done
    if [ "$pinned" != true ] && [ "${PACTO_ALLOW_CLUSTER_DISCOVERY:-false}" != true ]; then
      fail "pin each destination cluster (oci://<registry>/pacto-targets:cluster-<uid>)"
    fi

    work=$(mktemp -d /tmp/pacto-cmp.XXXXXX) || fail "cannot create a temp folder under /tmp"
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    render="$work/render.yaml"

    # Render with the folder's own tool. Registry credentials meant for Pacto
    # never reach helm or kustomize.
    if [ -f Chart.yaml ]; then
      (
        unset PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
        if [ -f Chart.lock ] && [ ! -d charts ]; then
          helm dependency build . >&2 || exit 1
        fi
        set -- template "${ARGOCD_APP_NAME:-}" . --namespace "${ARGOCD_APP_NAMESPACE:-}" --include-crds
        if [ -n "${KUBE_VERSION:-}" ]; then set -- "$@" --kube-version "$KUBE_VERSION"; fi
        IFS=,
        for v in ${KUBE_API_VERSIONS:-}; do set -- "$@" --api-versions "$v"; done
        unset IFS
        exec helm "$@"
      ) > "$render" || fail "helm template failed"
    elif [ -f kustomization.yaml ] || [ -f kustomization.yml ] || [ -f Kustomization ]; then
      (
        unset PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # build options are a word list
