The limitations page lists what this evidence cannot see.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
When a Pacto shows a status you did not expect, this page tells you why and what to change. Start with the status the operator wrote on the Pacto object: it holds the verdict, the stage that produced it and one finding per problem.

kubectl describe pacto <name>
kubectl get pacto <name> -o yaml                   # the whole object
kubectl get pacto <name> -o yaml | yq '.status'    # only the status, if you have yq

Runtime observations lists every finding code referenced below.

docs.title: Reading the conditions
docs.text:
status.contractStatus says what the verdict is. The conditions say which stage produced it, which is usually what you need to fix. There are three, and each one's reason is a fixed identifier you can match on:

Condition Status Reason What happened ContractValid True Parsed The contract loaded and passed validation. ContractValid True ReferenceOnly Same, and the contract declares no spec.target, so nothing further is observed. ContractValid False Invalid The contract loaded and is structurally wrong. status.validation names the errors. ContractValid False ContractUndeclared The contract does not declare its pactoVersion, service.name or service.version. A bundle in a registry or an inline contract must declare all three: pacto publish writes the version and refuses a contract without the other two. ContractValid Unknown Unavailable The contract could not be obtained -- registry unreachable, auth rejected, tag not found. Validity is undetermined, so status.validation is deliberately left empty. ContractValid Unknown PullSecretNotGranted The operator may not read the pull secret. The message names the grant to add: controller.secretGrants or, for a namespace-list install, the chart's watch Role and RoleBinding in that namespace (Upgrade). RuntimeObserved True Found Runtime evidence was collected. RuntimeObserved False ObservationFailed A cluster query errored. The message carries the API error. ReadinessSatisfied True Satisfied score >= minScore. ReadinessSatisfied False BelowMinScore The gate is not met. The message breaks the score down by claim status. ReadinessSatisfied False Expired The assessment is past its expires: date, which scores it 0. OwnerVerified True OwnerSignerAllowed A member of the current owner or a default approver signed the bundle that changes the owner. OwnerVerified False OwnerSignerNotPerson An agent, CI or workload identity signed the owner change. status.contract.owner is left out. OwnerVerified False OwnerSignerNotAllowed A person outside the owner's members and the default approvers (declare chart values) signed it. status.contract.owner is left out. OwnerVerified Unknown OwnerSignerUnverified No signature verified, or the owner policy, the Sigstore root or the previous revision could not be read. status.contract.owner is left out until it is judged again.

Two absences are meaningful:

  • RuntimeObserved is missing entirely when the reconciliation stopped before observing: a reference-only contract, or one that failed at ContractValid. No observation ran, so none failed.
  • ReadinessSatisfied is missing entirely when the contract declares no readiness: block.
  • OwnerVerified is missing entirely when the bundle keeps the owner of the revision it replaces, is unsigned and carries no declaration, was published by a CI identity the publisher rule accepts, or is inline.

Conditions are sticky: each keeps its lastTransitionTime while its status is unchanged, and carries the observedGeneration it was set from. A condition whose observedGeneration is behind metadata.generation was not re-evaluated on the latest spec.

docs.title: Reading the events
docs.text:
Conditions say what the state is; the Events: block that closes kubectl describe pacto <name> says what changed, including things no field records, such as a tag force-pushed underneath you or a readiness gate flipping.

kubectl describe pacto <name>                       # events are the last block
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<name> \
  --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

The operator emits exactly eight, and no others:

Reason Type Emitted when What it tells you ContractInvalid Warning The contract was obtained and judged invalid Carries the same message as the ContractValid / Invalid condition. Fix the contract. ContractUnavailable Warning The contract could not be obtained at all Registry unreachable, auth rejected, tag missing. See Contract not resolving. ValidationFailed Warning A contract that did load ends the reconcile as anything but Compliant or Reference, and the status differs from the one the previous reconcile persisted Carries the counts -- ContractStatus: NonCompliant, 2 errors, 1 warnings. status.findings names each one. ContractRecovered Normal The contract status returned to Compliant or Reference from any other value The other half of the three warnings above. RevisionCreated Normal A PactoRevision was created for a newly resolved contract Created revision <name> for contract v<version>. Expected on the first resolve and on every version change; not a problem. TagOverwritten Warning A tag that already resolved now points at a different digest Someone force-pushed the tag. See Choosing a reference form. ReadinessGateUnmet Warning The readiness gate went from met to unmet The message breaks the score down by claim status. ReadinessRecovered Normal The readiness gate went from unmet to met The other half of the pair above.

Three things about them are easy to misread:

  • ValidationFailed overstates the Unknown case. In that case an assertion could not be evaluated, and the event's own counts say so: ContractStatus: Unknown, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Trust the counts over the reason.
  • Every event except RevisionCreated and TagOverwritten is transition-gated. A contract that stays broken emits one event for the whole streak, so a Count above 1 means the status flapped, or the same reason recurred after a recovery. Two exceptions still repeat without either: TagOverwritten (see Choosing a reference form) and a revision-mirror failure, which is recorded once per reconcile pass.
  • Events expire, after the API server's --event-ttl of one hour by default. A missing event may have expired, so rely on conditions and status as the durable record.

docs.title: Chasing the evidence behind a finding
docs.text:
Every finding carries evidenceRefs, and this is what they contain:

evidenceRefs:
  - source: k8s
    observedAt: "2026-08-22T21:31:04Z"
    collector: k8s-observer
    detectedAt: "2026-08-22T21:31:04Z"

That is the whole record: which collector saw it and when. collector is k8s-observer for the Kubernetes API alone, k8s-observer+ebpf when node agent evidence decided or qualified the result and ebpf when only the kernel saw it. A finding with no matched observation, such as EVIDENCE_MISSING, carries source and observedAt only. The operator's observations are recomputed every reconcile and never stored, so the reference dates the reading and has no body to fetch. The node agent's raw socket view is the one exception you can read back, in the NodeRuntimeObservation object named after the pod's node. What it is good for is age: an observedAt that stopped advancing while metadata.generation moved on is a leftover from a reconcile that no longer runs.

To re-observe, nudge the Pacto's target Service. Any update to it enqueues a reconcile, and the annotation key is arbitrary. An annotation on the Pacto itself does not, because only a spec change reconciles a Pacto:

kubectl annotate service <target> reconcile-requested-at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" --overwrite

For observations that must outlive the reconcile that made them, such as an audit trail or a signed record, use the Evidence Server, which writes to your registry. Cluster status is a live reading.

docs.title: Status is Unknown
docs.text:
A required assertion could not be evaluated. This is uncertainty, and the finding code says why:

  • EVIDENCE_MISSING: nothing was collected. The target may not exist yet, or spec.target.serviceName does not match a real Service.
  • OBSERVATION_UNSUPPORTED: the dimension cannot be observed here: an ExternalName dependency, or a metrics capability while metrics observation is off for the namespace (chart value controller.metricsObservation, flag --enable-metrics-observation).
  • COLLECTION_FAILED: the cluster query errored, or the node agent could not load its kernel program. Check the RuntimeObserved condition and the operator logs.
  • HEALTH_FAILING: the declared health endpoint answered with a 5xx (other than 501), or the readiness probe on the declared health path keeps every pod out of Ready. The service is failing its own health check; check the pod's events and logs. Compliance stays Unknown because a failing endpoint does not contradict the contract.
  • EVIDENCE_STALE: the node agent on the pod's node stopped reporting. See Node agent evidence is missing.
  • EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT: some evidence arrived but not enough to decide, for example the node agent saw only part of a pod.

A contract that could not be obtained transiently also reads Unknown rather than Invalid.

docs.title: Status is Invalid
docs.text:
Structural validation failed or the artifact could not be parsed (fail-closed). status.validation carries the SCHEMA_VIOLATION or parse error; reproduce it locally:

pacto validate oci://ghcr.io/your-org/my-service-pacto:1.2.0

docs.title: Status is NonCompliant
docs.text: At least one confirmed violation. The two configuration codes do not arrive at the same speed. A mismatch (CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH) is NonCompliant on the first reconcile that observes it. An absence (CONFIGURATION_ABSENT) reads Unknown until the negative streak spans the stabilization window.

docs.title: Status is Reference
docs.text: The contract declares no spec.target: Pacto parses and validates it and observes nothing. Add a spec.target to enable runtime observation.

docs.title: Contract not resolving
docs.text:
• Confirm the OCI reference is reachable and, for private registries, that a pull secret is set via spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef.
  • For an unversioned reference the operator tracks the highest semver tag; a registry with no valid semver tags resolves nothing.
  • Inspect the created PactoRevision resources: kubectl get pactorevisions.

docs.title: Metrics or health always Unknown
docs.text:
The metrics dimension returns Unsupported unless metrics observation is on for the namespace, and active health probing needs probing on. The chart sets them through controller.metricsObservation and controller.probing, which default to auto; see Opt-in features.

The RuntimeObserved condition message ends with where each setting came from:

  • probing off (--enable-probing=auto, namespace has no pacto.trianalab.io/observe label) means label the namespace (kubectl label ns NAMESPACE pacto.trianalab.io/observe=probing) or set controller.probing=on. The operator does not watch namespaces: it reads the label at each Pacto's next check (spec.checkIntervalSeconds, default 5 minutes). To apply it now, annotate the target Service as in Evidence is not stored.
  • namespace label unreadable: forbidden or not found means the operator may not read the namespace; check the namespaces get grant in RBAC. The condition stays True.
  • namespace label unreadable: timeout or unavailable with the condition False is a transient read failure; the next reconcile retries it.

With probing off, health falls back to the workload, which needs an httpGet readiness probe on the container behind the health capability's port plus a Ready endpoint for it. When the capability declares a path, the probe's path must equal it. A liveness-only pod, an exec or tcpSocket probe or no probe leaves nothing to read. Passive observation can confirm health but never contradict it, so the answer here is Unknown. A readiness probe that keeps every pod out of Ready reads HEALTH_FAILING, which is also Unknown. A workload scaled to zero runs no pod, so nothing answers the probe and the answer is EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT.

docs.title: Operator RBAC errors
docs.text: If the logs show forbidden errors reading Services, workloads or EndpointSlices, confirm the operator's ClusterRole is installed. See RBAC. The chart adds read access to ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor only when controller.metricsObservation is on. If you set the controller flag by hand instead, grant that access yourself, as Opt-in features shows.

docs.title: Node agent evidence is missing
docs.text:
The node agent is the optional DaemonSet (one pod per node) behind runtime conformance. If findings never carry collector: k8s-observer+ebpf, check these in order:

kubectl -n pacto-node-agent get daemonset pacto-node-agent
kubectl -n pacto-node-agent get noderuntimeobservations,leases
kubectl -n pacto-operator-system logs deploy/pacto-operator | grep node-agent
  • No DaemonSet. nodeAgent.enabled is off, or the agent runs in another nodeAgent.namespace.
  • DaemonSet with no pods. Something rejects them in the agent namespace. The operator sets its Pod Security labels to privileged at every sync; read kubectl -n pacto-node-agent describe daemonset pacto-node-agent for the admission message, for example from a policy engine of your own.
  • Pods running, no NodeRuntimeObservation or Lease for a node. That node's findings read EVIDENCE_STALE. Read the agent pod's log on that node. A write refused with may only write the objects named after its node or carries no node name comes from the chart's admission policy: the agent's token does not name its node, which needs Kubernetes 1.30 or later.
  • A Lease older than its node's observation. The Lease is the heartbeat; the operator reads whichever of its renewTime and the observation's lastPublished is newer.
  • Collection Failed. The kernel could not load the program, often because it lacks BTF (the kernel type information at /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux). A kernel older than 5.11 can also fail to load it when the container runtime's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is too low for its maps. Turn it on lists what each node needs.

docs.title: A Stage's applier is not adopted
docs.text:
The Stage's status.applier says which manager the promoter found on its workloads and why it disagrees with spec.applyRef:

kubectl get stage <stage> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.status.applier}'
  • ApplierConflict: another manager or another object owns a workload, such as a plain Helm release or an Argo CD Application of the same name in the Argo CD namespace. Point spec.applyRef at the manager status.applier names, or move the workloads to the Stage's applier.
  • ApplierUnknown: Pacto could not tell. The workload carries no mark of the Stage's applier, carries marks of two managers, belongs to a manager Pacto does not support, or the promoter could not read it. Deliver it through Argo CD or Flux so it carries its labels, and check completeness.
  • ApplierNotChartRef: the HelmRelease takes its chart from spec.chart. Point spec.chartRef at an OCIRepository.
  • ApplierUnreadable on a HelmRelease Stage: the chart OCIRepository is missing, outside the Stage's namespace or of another kind. The promoter writes nothing until spec.chartRef names an OCIRepository in the Stage's namespace.

See which manager applies a Stage.

docs.title: Delivery records are not written
docs.text:
With the recorder on, every Stage carries a RecordStoreReady condition. Read its reason:

kubectl get stages.delivery.pacto.trianalab.io -A \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RECORDS:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="RecordStoreReady")].reason

RegistryUnavailable means the registry did not answer or the recorder could not tell whether it serves the OCI Referrers API; the message quotes the registry. When it reads the registry served the Referrers API for this stream and no longer does, the Stage recorded native and the registry now answers as one without the API. The recorder never moves such a Stage to write-once tags on its own; check the registry's configuration: status.stream.registryMode is native and may not narrow, and the records admission policy refuses that change to everyone, the recorder included. WriteOnceTags is healthy: the registry serves no Referrers API, so records are written as tags. Check it works lists the other reasons.

A Stage that follows a new upstream Stage reads no record was found for this stream until the upstream Stage writes its first record, and offers no candidate until then.

docs.title: CI says a target snapshot is unverified or stale
docs.text:
pacto impact in CI prints one Targets: line per cluster snapshot it read. Read what the line ends with:

The line says Why Fix unverified The job has no delivery trust config Set PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST or pass --delivery-trust signed by <key> (not scoped to this cluster) The trust entry has no streams naming the cluster's UID, or is a bare PEM Add streams: ["<uid>/pacto-targets/snapshot"] to the cluster's installation entry stale The snapshot is older than 15 minutes Check the operator logs for target snapshot not published: push credentials for <registry>/pacto-targets or a snapshot over 8 MiB unavailable, not used A pinned tag is missing, or the signature or cluster does not match Check the operator runs in that cluster with registry set and that the trust entry holds the public.b64 of its installation key Secret

A Registry: line that says no pacto-targets means no cluster published: check that the chart's top-level registry value is set. See Target snapshot.

docs.title: An approval does not count
docs.text: With the recorder on, an Approval counts only once its record is written, and an Approval for a person's signed record only once that record verifies. Read the Approval's status.record; when it is empty, the recorder has not signed it. The recorder signs only Approvals made after it first saw the approval admission policy, and it keeps that moment in memory, so an Approval made before a recorder restart never gets a record: approve again. Signed approvals has the rest.

docs.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes operator
docs.text:
An upgrade is one helm upgrade, which updates the CRDs along with the operator. A cluster whose CRDs came from an older chart's crds/ directory needs one extra step the first time, and this page shows it.

The Kubernetes integration has its own version, separate from Pacto core: the operator image, Helm chart, Go module and these docs move together.

docs.title: Upgrade with Helm
docs.text:
The currently published chart:

helm upgrade pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.6.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system

An upgrade reverts hand-patched controller flags

helm upgrade rebuilds the Deployment's args from the chart, so a flag you patched in by hand disappears without an error. Set opt-in features through chart values such as controller.probing, controller.metricsObservation, controller.interfaceNameMatchDiscovery and nodeAgent.enabled, which survive an upgrade. Each operator flag has a chart value or a documented reason to stay off the chart; see Limitations: opt-in features.

docs.title: Deprecated observation keys
docs.text:
controller.enableProbing and controller.enableMetricsObservation still work. Their replacements, controller.probing and controller.metricsObservation, default to auto, which turns each feature on only in namespaces labelled pacto.trianalab.io/observe.

An upgrade that keeps the previous release's values renders the same arguments; set the new key, or reset the values, to move to auto. The new key wins, even auto over a deprecated true:

controller:
  enableProbing: true   # deprecated, ignored once probing is set
  probing: auto

controller.kernelEvidence.enabled: false still follows nodeAgent.enabled; the quoted "off" refuses kernel evidence while the node agent runs.

docs.title: Hand older CRDs to Helm
docs.text:
A CRD (CustomResourceDefinition) tells Kubernetes what a Pacto object looks like. The chart renders its CRDs as part of the release, so helm upgrade updates a changed CRD and adds a new one, and helm uninstall keeps them (helm.sh/resource-policy: keep). Older charts installed the operator CRDs from a crds/ directory that Helm never upgrades and never records as part of the release.

If your CRDs came from such a chart, helm upgrade stops with invalid ownership metadata. Label and annotate them for your release once, then run the upgrade. Change the release name and namespace if yours differ:

for crd in $(kubectl get crd -o name | grep -E '/[a-z]+\.pacto\.trianalab\.io$'); do
  kubectl label "$crd" app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm --overwrite
  kubectl annotate "$crd" --overwrite \
    meta.helm.sh/release-name=pacto-operator \
    meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=pacto-operator-system
done

The loop runs the same in bash and zsh. The grep matches only the operator CRDs. The delivery CRDs, group delivery.pacto.trianalab.io, were already part of the release.

docs.title: Image values
docs.text:
The chart builds each image from global.imageRegistry (default ghcr.io) and a repository without a registry, such as trianalab/pacto/operator. An image's own registry value replaces the global one for that image.

Values from older charts set the whole reference in image.repository or delivery.image.repository, such as ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto-operator/pacto-controller. The chart keeps such a repository as the whole reference and adds no registry, so these values upgrade unchanged. The chart treats a repository as already carrying a registry host when its first path segment holds a . or : or is localhost. The Helm reference lists every image value.

docs.title: Upgrading across a major version (CRD migration)
docs.text:
Helm applies the new CRDs ahead of the new operator, so a major upgrade is the same command as any other:

helm upgrade pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.6.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system

The API version stays v1alpha1 across the major bump and the stored version is unchanged. Every existing Pacto resource therefore remains stored and readable under the new CRD, with no conversion webhook and no decode error, and the upgraded operator reconciles it in place. That holds because spec is additive: v5 adds spec.target.configBindings and spec.target.interfaceBindings and removes nothing, so a contract resource written for v4 still validates unchanged.

docs.title: Status is redesigned
docs.text:
The upgrade drops v4 status observations on sight

v5 redesigns status: it removes 51 status paths and adds 35. status.runtime, status.endpoints, status.ports, status.scaling, status.readiness.checks, status.contract.imageRef and status.summary.{passed,failed,total} are gone, replaced by status.findings, status.evaluationCoverage and status.summary.{errorCount,warningCount,infoCount,unknownCount}. That is why the printer columns change from PASSED/FAILED to ERRORS/WARNINGS.

The apiserver stops serving the removed fields the moment the new CRD lands. A kubectl get pacto -o yaml taken before the new operator writes status therefore shows a resource whose spec is intact and whose status looks half-empty. The CRD causes this. The old values are still in etcd and are lost for good only once something writes status again, so that window is a normal part of the migration.

docs.title: Confirming the migration
docs.text:
Before and after the upgrade:

kubectl get crd pactos.pacto.trianalab.io \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[0].additionalPrinterColumns[*].name}'   # reflects the new schema
kubectl get pacto -A                                                    # existing resources still list + reconcile

If a future release ever ships an incompatible schema change, the upgrade or the resource read fails with an error, so no resource disappears silently. See the CRD reference for the current field set.

This exact flow is exercised against a real cluster by tests/acceptance/kind/upgrade-v4-v5.sh, the upgrade leg of CI's ci-e2e-kind job. It installs the real v4 chart with its v4 CRDs, hands them to Helm as above, then helm upgrades to the current chart and asserts the CRDs migrate and the pre-existing resource survives and reconciles.

docs.title: Upgrading to v6
docs.text:
v6 adds the NodeRuntimeObservation CRD, which helm upgrade creates. Hand the older CRDs to Helm first as above, then check these before helm upgrade:

  • Removed flags and values. --webhook-cert-path, --webhook-cert-name, --webhook-cert-key and --dashboard-oci-secret are gone; the operator refuses to start with an unknown flag. Replace dashboard.ociSecret: <name> with dashboard.ociSecrets: [<name>]: the chart schema rejects the old key.
  • The node agent has its own namespace. It runs in nodeAgent.namespace (pacto-node-agent by default), which the chart creates privileged for Pod Security. Drop the pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged label you may have put on the release namespace for it. At its first sync the operator deletes the agent it ran in the release namespace. A private pull secret for the agent image must exist in the agent namespace too.
  • RBAC is split by namespace. The managed components' lifecycle permissions moved from the ClusterRole to a Role in the release namespace and, with the node agent, a Role in the agent namespace. The chart renders both. An operator installed without the chart needs them added by hand (RBAC lists every rule).
  • Kernel evidence namespace. controller.kernelEvidence.namespace defaults to the agent namespace instead of the operator's.

docs.title: Delivery approvers need update rights
docs.text: Whoever may update a Stage's workload decides its held changes. Owner teams narrow who may answer only when delivery.identities.teamGroupPrefix is set, and requireOwnerTeam defaults to false. To keep the earlier behaviour, set teamGroupPrefix: "" and requireOwnerTeam: true before you upgrade (upgrading).

docs.title: Delivery always installs its admission policies
docs.text:
Delivery no longer runs without its admission policies. The chart refuses delivery.admissionPolicies.enabled and delivery.admissionPolicies.allowUnguarded whatever their value, and names the replacement. Before helm upgrade:

  • Delete both keys from your values.
  • If you set allowUnguarded to skip the Kubernetes 1.30 and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API check for helm lint or helm template, set delivery.admissionPolicies.skipCapabilityCheck=true instead. The policies still render.
  • An upgrade that reuses the earlier release's values carries enabled: true over from the earlier chart's defaults, so it fails. Reuse them with --reset-then-reuse-values.

A promoter started without --admission-policies admits no operation and counts no approval.

docs.title: Delivery records work on every registry
docs.text:
• Stages gain status.stream.registryMode (native or write-once-tags), which only the recorder may write. helm upgrade installs the new field with the CRDs. A Stage that was ready before the upgrade shows the mode after the recorder writes its next record.
  • A streams repository on a registry without the OCI Referrers API, such as GHCR, now holds records as write-once tags and reports the RecordStoreReady reason WriteOnceTags. The earlier reason for such a registry is gone: alerts or scripts that match it match nothing.
  • A Stage that recorded native, or that was ready before the upgrade, and then sees no Referrers API stays RegistryUnavailable instead of switching to tags.

docs.title: Approvals are signed records
docs.text:
• With the recorder on, it signs every Approval into the registry, and the promoter counts an Approval only once its record is written. Operation records then name each approval's record, which an earlier CLI or promoter cannot read. Upgrade the CLIs and every promoter that follows these streams first, then the recorder (details).
  • The recorder signs no Approval made before it first saw the approval admission policy. Such an Approval on a held operation waits and does not count, so its author approves again.
  • Before you set delivery.identities.signers, create the approvals repository (delivery.recorder.approvalsRepository, default <streamsRepository>-approvals) where a registry needs it, such as ECR, and let the recorder push there. The recorder anchors it only once a signer is set. Until it can, keyless approvals wait and operation records keep flowing.
  • Approvals gain a status subresource and the recorder-only fields spec.record and spec.signedAt; helm upgrade installs them with the CRDs.

docs.title: Signatures are checked against publishers
docs.text:
• A revision's signature status (pacto_fleet_get, the dashboard and pacto fleet) is verified only when a publisher rule, a person's pin, a signed policy or an external system's release signer accepts the signer. A signer the contract's own publish.sign declares is no longer enough: scripts that relied on it read unknown or unverified until the installation sets delivery.publishers. The new source field says what decided.
  • New chart values: delivery.publishers.registry, defaultBranch, policy, policySigners and trustedRoot, and delivery.recorder.signing.publicKey. Reused values without a delivery.publishers block render the promoter arguments they had.
  • Stages gain spec.candidates.registry and the promoter-only status.publisher, and Operations gain the type delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/trust with spec.params.publisher; helm upgrade installs them with the CRDs. Existing ociRepositoryRef and upstream Stages keep working unchanged (publishers).

docs.title: Delivery grants Argo CD and Flux access by itself
docs.text:
• delivery.argocd.enabled and delivery.flux.enabled now default to auto.
  • An upgrade that takes the new chart's defaults, such as --reset-then-reuse-values, on a cluster that serves Argo CD Applications grants the promoter patch on Applications. Admission limits that write to spec.source.targetRevision of Applications labelled delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref. Set delivery.argocd.enabled=false to keep it off.
  • Flux access renders as before. On a cluster that serves Flux HelmReleases the promoter also gains HelmRelease read, the --flux-helm flag and the applier-helmrelease admission policy.
  • An upgrade that keeps the earlier chart's defaults keeps enabled: false for Argo CD, and Flux access as it was.
  • auto reads the APIs at install and upgrade: run helm upgrade after you install Argo CD or Flux.

docs.title: The dashboard asks people to sign in
docs.text:
After every upgrade, one that reuses the earlier release's values included, the dashboard asks people to sign in (token sign-in):

  • The new value dashboard.auth.tokenSignIn.enabled defaults to true, and no earlier release has it, so reused values keep it on.
  • dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous defaults to false. To keep serving without sign-in, set dashboard.auth.tokenSignIn.enabled=false and dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous=true. The install notes say so when the previous release served without sign-in.
  • The earlier value that turned token sign-in on is deprecated and ignored. It still validates, so reused values keep working.
  • A ServiceAccount token signs in only when minted with --audience pacto-dashboard, and its session reads the fleet only. A person's own token signs in as before and may now approve.
  • The dashboard's ServiceAccount gains create on tokenreviews through the ClusterRole <fullname>-<namespace>-dashboard-tokenreview, also with controller.watchNamespaces.

A dashboard you run yourself beyond loopback still needs --token-login, --oidc-issuer-url or --allow-anonymous.

docs.title: Pull secrets outside granted namespaces
docs.text:
The operator no longer reads Secrets across the cluster. It reads a pull secret in the release namespace, in each of controller.watchNamespaces and wherever controller.secretGrants names it. Any other pull secret sets ContractValid=Unknown with reason PullSecretNotGranted, and the condition message names the grant to add. Before helm upgrade, list the pull secrets in use:

kubectl get pactos -A \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef}{"\n"}{end}'
  • A cluster-wide install lists each one as namespace/name in controller.secretGrants.
  • A namespace-list install already reads pull secrets in each listed namespace. There the message points at the chart's watch Role and RoleBinding in that namespace.

A rotated pull secret is read within one check interval.

controller.watchNamespace still works and joins controller.watchNamespaces, also when an upgrade reuses earlier values.

Moving from a cluster-wide install to a namespace list leaves the pacto-dashboard ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding behind: the operator may no longer delete them. The helm upgrade notes and a StaleClusterRBAC Warning event on the dashboard Deployment report them. Delete them:

kubectl delete clusterrole,clusterrolebinding pacto-dashboard

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text: Within a major, helm rollback pacto-operator reverts what the chart owns and leaves your Pacto resources untouched; re-apply any hand-patched controller flags afterwards. Across a major it takes more work. A chart from before the CRDs moved into the release does not carry them, so rolling back to it leaves the new CRDs in place. The old controller then writes status fields the new schema lacks, which the API server drops while still reporting success. A real return to that major means rolling the chart back and server-side applying the previous release's CRDs from its config/crd/bases.

docs.title: Turning on the Evidence Server during an upgrade
docs.text: The Evidence Server arrived in chart 5.2.0 and is off by default, so an upgrade changes nothing until you set evidence.enabled. Its requirements, a subject list and a registry serving the native Referrers API, are on The Evidence Server. Turning it back off later removes the whole footprint and loses nothing: every accepted record already lives in your contract registry.

docs.title: Version compatibility
docs.text:
The Kubernetes integration is versioned independently from Pacto core. The table below is generated from integration.yaml and release/release-manifest.json.

Integration artifact Version Supported Pacto core Operator image 6.6.0 >=4.0.0 Operator chart 6.6.0 >=4.0.0 Delivery image 6.6.0 >=4.0.0 Go module 6.6.0 >=4.0.0 Integration docs 6.6.0 >=4.0.0

Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.1" need Pacto core 4.1.0 or later and operator 6.1.0 or later. Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.2" need Pacto core 4.3.0 or later and operator 6.3.0 or later. Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.3" need Pacto core 4.4.0 or later and operator 6.4.0 or later.

This documentation set corresponds to Pacto core 4.6.1. The integration's own version (currently operator/chart 6.6.0, docs 6.6.0) advances on its own release cadence.

docs.title: Version selector
docs.text: The site version selector (top of the page) tracks Pacto core releases. Because the Kubernetes integration ships on its own cadence, a Kubernetes-only release does NOT add a new core version entry to the selector: it republishes the current core version in place with regenerated integration docs, and this compatibility table shows the integration version those docs describe. Pick a core version from the selector to read the integration docs that shipped with it.

docs.title: Published artifacts
docs.text: Published artifact coordinates for the Kubernetes integration. All coordinates and versions are generated from release/release-manifest.json -- the single source of truth for what has been published.

docs.title: Artifact coordinates
docs.text: Artifact Kind Coordinate Version Controller image oci-image ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/operator 6.6.0 Helm chart helm-chart ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator 6.6.0 Delivery image (opt-in) oci-image ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/delivery 6.6.0 Go module go-module github.com/trianalab/pacto/integrations/kubernetes/v6 6.6.0 Documentation docs mkdocs:integrations/kubernetes 6.6.0

docs.title: Verify a published artifact
docs.text:
The controller image, the opt-in delivery image and the Helm chart are signed keylessly by the release workflow through GitHub's OIDC issuer. Verify each one before installing it:

cosign verify \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/TrianaLab/pacto/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/operator:6.6.0

Anything other than a successful verification -- including no signatures found -- means do not deploy it. Not every Pacto artifact is signed; see what is signed and what is not.

docs.title: Artifact Hub repository
docs.text:
• Repository ID: 4d7aef48-84d5-447f-bd73-8590a6801d0e

  image: ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/operator:6.6.0
- name: pacto-delivery
  image: ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/delivery:6.6.0

docs.title: Install from the published chart
docs.text:
helm install pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.6.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system --create-namespace

docs.title: Contract bindings
docs.text: A Pacto resource points at a platform-agnostic contract (inline or in OCI) and binds it to concrete Kubernetes resources to observe. The binding fields below are generated from the Pacto CRD schema.

docs.title: Contract source (spec.contractRef)
docs.text: Field Type Required Enum Description spec.contractRef object yes ContractRef specifies where to find the Pacto contract. spec.contractRef.inline string no Inline allows specifying the contract YAML directly (for testing/dev). spec.contractRef.oci string no OCI is the OCI registry reference for the contract bundle. Three forms are supported: - Unversioned (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto): tracks the latest semver tag. - Tagged (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto:1.2.3): pinned to that exact tag. - Digest (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto@sha256:...): immutable, exact reference. spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef string no PullSecretRef is the name of a Secret in the same namespace containing OCI registry credentials. Supported secret types: - Opaque with "token" key (bearer token) - Opaque with "username"+"password" keys (basic auth) - kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (standard Docker registry auth) For Opaque secrets, add a "registry" key (e.g. "ghcr.io") to bind the credentials to that host; the operator then refuses to send them to any other registry. Recommended to prevent a contract from redirecting a referenced secret to an attacker-controlled registry.

docs.title: Runtime target (spec.target)
docs.text:
When spec.target is omitted the Pacto is reference-only: the operator parses and validates the contract but performs no runtime observation.

Field Type Required Enum Description spec.target object no Target specifies which Kubernetes resources to observe. When omitted, the Pacto acts as a reference-only contract (no runtime validation). spec.target.configBindings []object no ConfigBindings maps contract configurations to the concrete ConfigMap/Secret backing each (B7). spec.target.configBindings[].configuration string yes Configuration is the contract configurations[].name this binding backs. spec.target.configBindings[].format string no yaml, json Format of the value at Key. Required with Key for ConfigMap conformance. spec.target.configBindings[].key string no Key names the single ConfigMap/Secret key to decode and validate. Omit for existence-only. spec.target.configBindings[].kind string yes ConfigMap, Secret Kind of the backing object. spec.target.configBindings[].name string yes Name of the backing ConfigMap/Secret in the Pacto's namespace. spec.target.interfaceBindings []object no InterfaceBindings maps contract interfaces to the Service port that serves each (B4). Kubernetes deployment knowledge, so it lives on the CR and the contract stays platform-agnostic. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].interface string yes Interface is the contract interfaces[].name this binding resolves. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].servicePort object yes ServicePort is the Service port name or number that serves the interface. spec.target.serviceName string no ServiceName is the name of the Kubernetes Service to observe. spec.target.workloadRef object no WorkloadRef identifies the workload (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, or CronJob). If omitted, defaults to name=serviceName, kind=Deployment. spec.target.workloadRef.kind string no Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob Kind of the workload resource. Left unspecified (empty) unless the author sets it explicitly; WORKLOAD_MISMATCH only fires when BOTH name AND kind were explicit (AR7). No default is applied here so the collector can distinguish "author asserted kind X" from "kind was defaulted for the GET". spec.target.workloadRef.name string yes Name of the workload resource.

docs.title: Overrides (spec.overrides)
docs.text: Field Type Required Enum Description spec.overrides object no Overrides specifies partial configuration overrides to apply on top of the resolved contract. This enables environment-specific tuning without duplicating the entire contract inline. Semantics mirror the Pacto CLI --set / -f override model. spec.overrides.configurations []object no Configurations lists per-scope configuration value overrides. Each entry is matched by name to a configurations[] entry in the resolved contract. spec.overrides.configurations[].name string yes Name identifies the configuration scope to override (must match a configurations[] entry in the contract). spec.overrides.configurations[].values object yes Values contains the configuration key-value pairs to merge into the resolved contract. These values take precedence over the values declared in the contract.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A Pacto binding an OCI contract to a Service, with an interface bound to a named Service port and a configuration bound to a ConfigMap:

apiVersion: pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1
kind: Pacto
metadata:
  name: orders-api
  namespace: shop
spec:
  contractRef:
    oci: ghcr.io/acme/orders-api-pacto:1.2.0
  target:
    serviceName: orders-api
    interfaceBindings:
      - interface: http
        servicePort: http
    configBindings:
      - configuration: default
        kind: ConfigMap
        name: orders-api-config
        key: app.yaml
        format: yaml

docs.title: Choosing a reference form
docs.text:
The three contractRef.oci forms are not three styles. They decide what the binding means over time, and the operator records which one it inferred in status.resolutionPolicy -- PinnedDigest, PinnedTag or Latest.

  • Digest (...@sha256:<digest>) is the only form whose meaning cannot change. Every reconcile re-reads the same bytes, so a compliance verdict is reproducible: what the operator asserted last Tuesday is what it asserts today. The cost is real -- publishing a contract revision becomes a change to the Pacto resource too.
  • Tag (...:1.2.3) is a mutable name you control. If someone force-pushes that tag, the operator records a new PactoRevision and emits a TagOverwritten Warning Event naming the old and new digests. It still accepts the new content. Choose a tag when you want a promotable pointer and will treat that Event as a signal.
  • Unversioned (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto) re-resolves the highest semver tag on every reconcile -- every spec.checkIntervalSeconds, 300 by default. It fits an environment whose job is to run whatever is newest, such as a staging namespace or a preview cluster. It fits production badly, because what is being asserted changes without anyone deciding to change it.

With no other constraint: digest in production, unversioned in staging. The middle form is for teams that already run a tag-promotion discipline.

This page covers the binding fields only. The rest of spec -- including checkIntervalSeconds, which sets how often the operator re-checks compliance (default 300) -- is in the CRD reference.

docs.text:
• API group: delivery.pacto.trianalab.io

  • Kind: Approval

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description spec object yes ApprovalSpec is a human decision bound to one operation uid and intent digest. spec.authTime string no AuthTime is the login time the apiserver reported for that user (userInfo.extra["delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/auth-time"], RFC 3339 or Unix seconds). spec.by string yes By must equal the apiserver username of whoever created the Approval. spec.decision string yes approve, reject, accept-unknown Decision is what a human approval says. spec.groups []string no Groups must equal the groups of whoever created the Approval. The promoter accepts it only when one of them names a team the question was routed to. spec.intentDigest string yes spec.note string no spec.operation string yes Operation is the operation's name, for people. Matching uses the uid. spec.operationUID string yes spec.record string no Record names the keyless approval record this Approval is a view of. Only the recorder sets it. spec.signedAt string no SignedAt is the verified signing time of that record (RFC 3339). Only the recorder sets it. status object no Status names the approval's signed record. Only the recorder writes it. status.record object no Record is the approval's signed record, once the recorder wrote it. status.record.digest string yes Digest is the record id: the sha256 of its signed payload. status.record.ref string yes Ref is where it is: <repository>@.

docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description spec object yes OperationSpec is the intent. It is frozen at admission. spec.actor object yes Actor is the apiserver identity that created the operation. spec.actor.groups []string no spec.actor.user string yes spec.cause object no Cause is why an operation was raised. A person or an agent sets one field; a verdict they cite is re-run when the operation is admitted. An automatic rollback names the failed operation and, when a gate failed it, the verdict. spec.cause.operation string no Operation is the uid of the operation that caused this one. spec.cause.reason string no spec.cause.verdict object no Verdict is one gate's answer plus a citation that can be re-run. spec.cause.verdict.citation object no spec.cause.verdict.gate string yes spec.cause.verdict.message string no spec.cause.verdict.phase string yes pre, verify spec.cause.verdict.result string yes Pass, Fail, Unknown Result is a gate verdict. spec.correlationID string no spec.facet string yes pointer, freeze, level, upstream, trust spec.intentDigest string no IntentDigest is what plan() returned; the promoter recomputes it. spec.onBehalfOf object no Principal is a person an agent says it acts for. It is asserted, never verified. spec.onBehalfOf.user string yes spec.params object no Params are the operation parameters. On the pointer facet From and To are OCI manifest digests; on the level facet they are level names. spec.params.from string no spec.params.publisher object no Publisher is the signer a trust operation asks a person to confirm. spec.params.publisher.ci boolean no spec.params.publisher.class string no human, agent, ci ActorClass is who raised an operation, as the promoter classifies the apiserver identity. It is read once, when status.level is empty; after that only an autonomy operation moves the level. Creating a Stage is an admin action, so any level is accepted, and a Stage whose status is lost seeds back to this level. Only observe and advise keep Pacto from shipping without a person. status.policy.workload object no Workload is the workload the service runs as, in the Stage's namespace: the one object pacto.contract and pacto.runtime may judge. The Pacto resource ships inside every version and names its own target, so without this a version could point its own check at a decoy. Empty is the Deployment named spec.service.name. status.policy.workload.kind string yes Kind is the workload kind, such as Deployment or StatefulSet. status.policy.workload.name string yes status.question string no Question is what a human is asked while the operation is Held. status.reason string no Reason is the machine reason for the outcome or the hold (PlanStale, PointerMoved, NoStage, ...). status.record object no Record is the signed record of this operation, once the recorder wrote it. Only the recorder writes it. status.record.digest string yes Digest is the record id: the sha256 of its signed payload. status.record.kind string yes Kind is operation, or unrecordable when a pre-sign check refused it. status.record.refused string no Refused names the check and why, for an unrecordable record. status.record.seq integer yes Seq is the record's place in the stream. status.seq integer no status.stageUID string no StageUID is the uid of the Stage that gave the operation its seq. A Stage deleted and recreated with the same name starts its seqs over, and an operation left over from the old one is not part of the new one. status.times object no Times are RFC 3339 timestamps. status.times.admitted string no status.times.applied string no status.times.approvalDeadline string no status.times.executionDeadline string no status.times.finished string no status.times.held string no Held is when the operation was last held for a person. An approval created before it answered an earlier question and does not count. status.times.started string no status.times.verifyDeadline string no status.verdicts []object no status.verdicts[].citation object no status.verdicts[].gate string yes status.verdicts[].message string no status.verdicts[].phase string yes pre, verify status.verdicts[].result string yes Pass, Fail, Unknown Result is a gate verdict. status.verification string no Verification qualifies a Succeeded outcome.

Written by the promoter only. status.publisher.checkedAt string no status.publisher.message string no status.publisher.pinAt string no status.publisher.pinDigest string no status.publisher.pins integer no status.publisher.policyAt string no status.publisher.policyDigest string no status.publisher.policyRef string no status.publisher.rule object no PublisherRule names the CI identities that may publish. Subject and Repository are anchored regular expressions, both required; Ref, when set, must equal the certificate's; Services are path.Match patterns over service names, and empty means every service. status.publisher.rule.issuer string yes status.publisher.rule.name string no status.publisher.rule.ref string no status.publisher.rule.repository string yes status.publisher.rule.services []string no status.publisher.rule.subject string yes status.publisher.source string no rule, policy, none Source is what the watch judges against: the installation's rule, the signed policy, or none when there is no rule and only a person's pin accepts a signer. status.publisher.verdicts []object no Verdicts are the newest judged digests, newest first (cap 20). status.publisher.verdicts[].at string no status.publisher.verdicts[].digest string yes status.publisher.verdicts[].identity object no PublisherIdentity is who signed a digest, read from the verified Sigstore certificate. status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.ci boolean no status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.class string no human, agent, ci ActorClass is who raised an operation, as the promoter classifies the apiserver identity. It is derived, never asserted by the client. status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.classifiedBy string no status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.issuer string yes status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.ref string no status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.repository string no status.publisher.verdicts[].identity.subject string yes status.publisher.verdicts[].reason string yes status.publisher.verdicts[].source string yes rule, pin, policy, inferred, none status.publisher.verdicts[].verdict string yes accepted, new-signer, refused, unsigned, unknown status.publisher.verdicts[].version string no status.rolledBack []string no RolledBack holds the uids of the failed operations the promoter raised its one automatic rollback for, oldest first (cap 50). A failure listed here never gets a second one. status.shadow []object no Shadow holds the newest would-have decisions while the Stage observes, newest first. status.shadow[].candidate string yes status.shadow[].decision string no Decision is the floor's decision: approve or accept-unknown. status.shadow[].from string no status.shadow[].impactDigest string no status.shadow[].intentDigest string yes status.shadow[].observedAt string no ObservedAt is when GitOps' source reported this candidate (RFC 3339): not proof of rollout. status.shadow[].owners []string no status.shadow[].plannedAt string yes PlannedAt is when Pacto planned it (RFC 3339). status.shadow[].predicted string yes Prediction is what plan() expects the promoter to do. status.shadow[].question string no status.shadow[].verification string no Verification is the shadow verify on the observed digest. status.stream object no Stream numbers a Stage's concluded operations. status.stream.anchor string no Anchor is where the stream's records are listed: <repository>@. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.approvals string no Approvals is where a person's client pushes a signed approval for this Stage: @. Only the recorder writes it, once. status.stream.concluded []object no Concluded are the newest operations given a seq, each with how it concluded, written in the compare-and-swap that took the seq. An operation whose own status write then failed concludes again from here: the same seq and outcome, never a second seq. status.stream.concluded[].cause string no Cause is the uid of the operation whose failure made the promoter raise this one: an automatic rollback, freeze or step-down. status.stream.concluded[].clearedBreaking boolean no ClearedBreaking is a promote of a change that is not NON_BREAKING whose impact verdict passed: every consumer accepts it. status.stream.concluded[].outcome string no Outcome is how a concluded operation ended. status.stream.concluded[].person boolean no Person is true when the operation carried an approval or a person raised it. status.stream.concluded[].reason string no Reason is "Code: message". status.stream.concluded[].seq integer yes status.stream.concluded[].type string no Type is the operation type. status.stream.concluded[].uid string yes status.stream.concluded[].verification string no Verification qualifies a Succeeded outcome. status.stream.head string no Head is the digest of the newest record in the stream. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.id string no ID is <clusterID>/<namespace>/<name>; the cluster id is the kube-system namespace uid. status.stream.recordedSeq integer no RecordedSeq is the newest local seq the recorder wrote or adopted a record for. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.registryMode string no native, write-once-tags RegistryMode is how the recorder writes this stream's records: native OCI referrers, or one write-once tag per record in the streams repository when the registry serves no Referrers API. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.seq integer no status.upstreamAcknowledged []string no UpstreamAcknowledged holds the ids of the unrecordable stand-ins in the upstream stream that a person on this Stage checked and acknowledged, oldest first (cap 50). They no longer stop the Stage offering. status.upstreamSeen object no UpstreamSeen is the newest record this Stage read from the upstream stream it follows (candidates.upstreamRecords). A later read that ends before it, or holds another record at its seq, offers nothing, so records removed from the upstream's tail never go unseen. status.upstreamSeen.record string yes Record is the record's id, the digest of its signed payload. status.upstreamSeen.seq integer yes status.upstreamSeen.stream string yes Stream is the stream id. status.verified []string no Verified holds the newest verified digests, oldest first (cap 10).

docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description status object no status is the agent's published observation. status.agentVersion string no AgentVersion is the node agent build version. status.collection object no Collection is the health of the kernel collection. status.collection.droppedEvents integer no DroppedEvents is the cumulative number of kernel events lost because the ring buffer was full, since the agent started. status.collection.lastDropAt string no LastDropAt is when the agent last saw DroppedEvents increase. status.collection.lastResyncAt string no LastResyncAt is when the agent last completed a /proc baseline scan. status.collection.message string no Message is a human-readable explanation of a non-Running state. status.collection.reason string no Reason is a CamelCase machine-readable cause for a non-Running state. status.collection.state string yes Running, Degraded, Failed State is Running, Degraded or Failed. status.kernelRelease string no KernelRelease is the node's kernel release (uname -r). status.lastPublished string no LastPublished is the heartbeat: the time of the most recent publish. status.nodeName string no NodeName is the Kubernetes node this object describes. status.observingSince string no ObservingSince is when this agent process started. status.pods []object no Pods are the pods running on the node, sorted by UID. status.pods[].baselineAt string no BaselineAt is the last /proc scan that saw the pod. status.pods[].connections []object no Connections are the pod's outbound TCP peers within the retention window. status.pods[].connections[].address string yes Address is the peer IP address. status.pods[].connections[].failures integer no Failures counts handshakes that went from SYN_SENT straight to CLOSE (refused, reset or timed out). status.pods[].connections[].lastFailureAt string no LastFailureAt is the time of the most recent failure. status.pods[].connections[].lastSuccessAt string no LastSuccessAt is the time of the most recent success. status.pods[].connections[].port integer yes Port is the peer port. status.pods[].connections[].successes integer no Successes counts handshakes that reached ESTABLISHED. status.pods[].listeners []object no Listeners are the pod's TCP listening sockets. status.pods[].listeners[].address string no Address is the bound local address (0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses). A loopback-only listener does not serve traffic sent to the pod IP. status.pods[].listeners[].family string yes IPv4, IPv6 Family is the socket address family. status.pods[].listeners[].port integer yes Port is the local (container) port. status.pods[].listeners[].process string no Process is the command name of the process that opened the listener, when the agent saw it happen (empty when only the /proc baseline knows it). status.pods[].netnsShared boolean no NetnsShared is true when the pod's network namespace is not its own (the host namespace for hostNetwork pods). Socket events in it cannot be attributed to the pod, so listeners and connections stay empty. status.pods[].observedSince string no ObservedSince is when the agent first mapped the pod's network namespace. status.pods[].truncated boolean no Truncated is true when a per-pod or per-node bound was hit, so listeners or connections may be missing entries. status.pods[].uid string yes UID is the pod UID, read from the pod's cgroup path. status.publishIntervalSeconds integer no PublishIntervalSeconds is how often the agent publishes; readers derive staleness from it.
