docs.title: Helm reference
docs.text:
• Chart: pacto-operator
  • Chart version: 6.6.0
  • App version: 6.6.0

Values are generated from charts/pacto-operator/values.yaml. Descriptions come from the chart's # -- value annotations.

Key Default Description affinity {} Affinity rules for the controller pod controller.interfaceNameMatchDiscovery false Resolve an unbound interface's Service port by matching a Service port whose name equals the interface name. A positive availability assist only: it never produces an absent or error result. controller.kernelEvidence.callerIgnoreNamespaces null Extra namespaces whose host-network pods are taken not to call workloads. The node agent cannot tell a host-network pod's calls from the node's own, so any such pod makes a Service's caller coverage partial, except in kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease and the node agent's namespace. The default lists the Flannel and Calico namespaces. Keep only namespaces that exist on your cluster and that you control: anyone who can create a listed namespace can call your services from a host-network pod there unseen. controller.kernelEvidence.enabled auto Merge the node agent's kernel observations (NodeRuntimeObservation objects) into interface and dependency evidence. Needs the node agent running. Takes auto, on or "off" (quoted: a bare off is YAML false). auto follows nodeAgent.enabled: a managed agent whose observations nobody merges would be pure cost. Set on alone only for an agent you run yourself; "off" refuses it even with the node agent. false keeps meaning auto. controller.kernelEvidence.namespace "" Namespace the node agent publishes to. Empty uses nodeAgent.namespace. controller.kernelEvidence.staleness "" How old a node's heartbeat may be before its evidence reads stale. Empty uses three times the node agent's publish interval. Accepts a Go duration (e.g. "2m"). controller.metricsObservation "" Observe the metrics capability (annotation, named-port or contract discovery plus an active scrape). Takes auto, on or off; true and false still mean on and off. Empty means auto, and an explicit auto also overrides the deprecated enableMetricsObservation set to true. auto turns it on only in namespaces whose owner labels them pacto.trianalab.io/observe=metrics (or probing.metrics). ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor discovery and the read access it needs come with on only. When off, metrics read unsupported. controller.probing "" Actively probe in-cluster endpoints: the health capability over HTTP and the wire protocol of each present interface. Takes auto, on or off; true and false still mean on and off. Empty means auto, and an explicit auto also overrides the deprecated enableProbing set to true. auto turns probing on only in namespaces whose owner labels them pacto.trianalab.io/observe=probing (or probing.metrics). When off, health uses passive readiness-probe and EndpointSlice signals only and interface protocols read unverified. controller.secretGrants [] Secrets outside the release namespace and watchNamespaces the operator may read, as namespace/name: pull secrets and Secrets that back a contract configuration. Each gets a Role limited to that Secret. controller.stabilizationWindow "" Stabilization window: how long a sustained NEGATIVE observation must persist before it converts to a confirmed violation (a transient blip reads Unknown meanwhile). Empty string uses the controller default (2m). Accepts a Go duration (e.g. "30s", "5m"). controller.watchNamespace "" Deprecated: use watchNamespaces. Merged into it. controller.watchNamespaces [] Namespaces the controller and the managed dashboard watch. Empty means cluster-wide. With a list, the chart renders namespaced Roles, plus the dashboard's TokenReview grant for token sign-in; fleet answers report the rest as unknown. crds.install true Install and upgrade the CRDs with the chart, the delivery CRDs too when delivery.enabled. They are kept on helm uninstall. Only one release in a cluster can own them: every other release, for example one per watched namespace, sets false. Set false to manage them yourself, for example from a separate GitOps source; the operator and delivery need them before they start dashboard.auth.allowAnonymous false Serve the dashboard without sign-in, only with tokenSignIn.enabled=false and no issuer. Everyone who reaches it reads every service the dashboard's ServiceAccount reads. With false and no sign-in the dashboard refuses to start dashboard.auth.oidc.caBundle.configMap "" A ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the PEM certificates of the CAs that sign the issuer's certificate (corporate or self-signed), trusted on top of the image's public roots dashboard.auth.oidc.caBundle.key ca.crt The key of the bundle in that ConfigMap or Secret dashboard.auth.oidc.caBundle.secret "" A Secret in the operator namespace holding that bundle, instead of a ConfigMap dashboard.auth.oidc.clientID "" The dashboard's client id at the issuer dashboard.auth.oidc.clientSecretRef.key client-secret Key of the client secret in that Secret dashboard.auth.oidc.clientSecretRef.name "" Secret in the operator namespace holding the client secret (passed by secretKeyRef) dashboard.auth.oidc.displayName "" The identity provider's name on the sign-in button, as in "Sign in with Keycloak" (empty: "Sign in with OIDC") dashboard.auth.oidc.extraScopes [] Scopes asked for beyond openid, profile and groups (for example a cross-client audience scope) dashboard.auth.oidc.groupsClaim "" ID token claim the API server takes the groups from; must match its claimMappings.groups (empty: groups) dashboard.auth.oidc.groupsPrefix "" Prefix the API server puts before every group; must match its claimMappings.groups.prefix dashboard.auth.oidc.internalIssuerURL "" Where the dashboard reaches the issuer when it differs from issuerURL, the address browsers use (for example an in-cluster Service). Discovery, tokens and keys are read there; ID tokens must still name issuerURL dashboard.auth.oidc.issuerURL "" OpenID Connect issuer URL people sign in with (empty: no sign-in) dashboard.auth.oidc.redirectURL "" The dashboard's /auth/callback URL as browsers reach it dashboard.auth.oidc.usernameClaim "" ID token claim the API server takes the username from; must match its claimMappings.username (empty: sub) dashboard.auth.oidc.usernamePrefix "" Prefix the API server puts before the username; must match its claimMappings.username.prefix (empty: the issuer URL and #, none for the email claim; - for none) dashboard.auth.session.idleTimeout "" A session without a request for this long ends, as a Go duration such as 30m (empty: 1h). The ID token renews with the refresh token in between dashboard.auth.session.maxAge "" A session ends this long after sign-in, renewed or not, as a Go duration such as 8h (empty: 12h) dashboard.auth.tokenSignIn.enabled true Let people sign in with a Kubernetes token. A ServiceAccount token minted with --audience pacto-dashboard reads the fleet only (NOTES prints one for pacto-viewer). A person's own token (an OIDC ID token, an EKS token) acts as them and may approve held changes. The chart grants the dashboard create on tokenreviews and creates the read-only pacto-viewer ServiceAccount dashboard.delivery.miraURL "" Mira's address, to link the health-check citations in delivery views dashboard.delivery.namespace "" Namespace where Pacto delivery runs. The dashboard reads the identity policy it publishes there (agent, break-glass and human groups, team prefix), so it is never configured twice (empty: delivery.namespace when delivery.enabled, else pacto-delivery) dashboard.delivery.trust.configMap "" A ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the trust config the dashboard verifies delivery records with (the recorder's PEM public key or a YAML trust config), so History verifies signed records. Empty: History shows records unverified dashboard.delivery.trust.key trust.yaml The key of the trust config in that ConfigMap dashboard.enabled true Enable the operator-managed dashboard deployment. The dashboard image is controlled by the operator and derived from the bundled Pacto library version. It is not user-configurable. dashboard.externalCatalog "" Organization external catalog merged over Pacto's default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST. The dashboard reads it with the dashboard's OCI credentials. Empty uses only the default catalog. dashboard.httpRoute.enabled false Enable Gateway API HTTPRoute for the dashboard dashboard.httpRoute.hostnames [] Hostnames for the HTTPRoute dashboard.httpRoute.parentRefs [] Parent gateway references dashboard.httpRoute.rules [] HTTPRoute rules. When empty, a single catch-all rule is generated that routes all traffic to the chart-managed dashboard Service on dashboard.service.port. dashboard.ingress.annotations {} Ingress annotations dashboard.ingress.className "" Ingress class name dashboard.ingress.enabled false Enable Ingress for the dashboard dashboard.ingress.hosts null Ingress hosts dashboard.ingress.tls [] Ingress TLS configuration dashboard.observation.sources [] Offline OTLP/JSON trace exports to mount read-only into the dashboard, so its Operational Graph can reconcile declared dependencies against observed ones. Each entry is one named data source: name is its stable Data Source identity (a DNS-1123 label). Reordering this list keeps every name, and each name must be unique across all the dashboard's data sources (the live cluster, OCI, the disk cache, local bundles, an Evidence Server). file is the trace file's name directly inside that source's mount, as a single path segment, so mount a claim whose export sits at the top of its own directory. Exactly one of existingClaim (an existing PVC, for real exports) or configMap (small static exports only, ~1 MiB cap) supplies it. Pacto reads only the declared files, through a root that blocks symlinks out of the mount, and never writes to them or scans the mount. Whoever owns that storage produces and rotates the exports. This configures OFFLINE input only: Pacto ships no OTLP receiver and no trace collector. The optional node agent observes sockets with eBPF and handles no traces. dashboard.ociSecrets [] List of Secret names for OCI registry credentials. Supports Opaque (keys: registry + token, or registry + username + password) and kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson secrets. When set, credentials from all secrets are merged; later secrets override earlier ones for the same registry. dashboard.repositories [] oci:// references the dashboard reads beside the contracts it discovers from Pacto resources, such as golden paths, which are never deployed. dashboard.resources.limits.memory 512Mi Memory limit for the dashboard container. The earlier default of 128Mi was OOMKilled while monitoring several OCI repositories and CRs at once; raise it further if the dashboard tracks a large fleet. dashboard.resources.requests.cpu 50m CPU request for the dashboard container dashboard.resources.requests.memory 128Mi Memory request for the dashboard container dashboard.service.nodePort "" Node port (only used when type is NodePort) dashboard.service.port 3000 Dashboard service port dashboard.service.type ClusterIP Dashboard exposure Service type (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer). The operator manages an internal ClusterIP Service (pacto-dashboard) for pod-to-pod communication. This chart-managed Service provides configurable external access and serves as the backend for Ingress/HTTPRoute resources. Selects dashboard pods via operator-defined labels. dashboard.stats.registry "" Stats repository the dashboard's Metrics page reads run records from, such as ghcr.io/acme/pacto-stats. Empty: the page explains how to turn recording on. Credentials come from dashboard.ociSecrets declare.defaultApprovers.bootstrap [] Signers who may set any service owner, as a list of {name, issuer, subject}: issuer is the OIDC issuer, compared exactly, and subject a pattern anchored with ^ and $ that matches one person, for example ^admin@acme\.com$ declare.emailIssuers [] Issuers whose email subjects match an owner's DRI or email contacts. Empty uses https://accounts.google.com, https://github.com/login/oauth and https://login.microsoftonline.com declare.teams {} Per team, the signers who count as its members, as team: [{name, issuer, subject}]. A signing certificate carries no groups, so without a rule only the owner's DRI or email contacts count declare.trustedRoot "" A Sigstore trusted root (trusted_root.json) the signature of a running bundle that changes its owner must chain to, for an air-gapped install or a private Sigstore. Empty uses delivery.publishers.trustedRoot, else public-good Sigstore. Used only when defaultApprovers.bootstrap or teams holds a rule delivery.admissionPolicies.gitopsUsers null Users besides break-glass that may create or delete an OCIRepository, Kustomization or Application labelled delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/apply-ref: the GitOps controllers that apply them. Deleting one and creating it again is an edit, so a namespace editor may do neither. The namespace controller and the garbage collector are always allowed. delivery.admissionPolicies.skipCapabilityCheck false Skip the chart's Kubernetes 1.30 and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API check (for helm lint or a helm template without --api-versions). The policies still render. delivery.affinity {} Affinity for the promoter pod delivery.argocd.enabled auto (bool or auto) Let Stages name an Argo CD Application as their applier (spec.applyRef.kind: Application). Grants the promoter patch on argoproj.io Applications (it only sets spec.source.targetRevision, and the pointer admission policy holds it to that) and read access to the agent, approver and recorder roles. auto grants it when the cluster serves argoproj.io/v1alpha1 Application at install or upgrade: install Argo CD first, or run helm upgrade after. true or false decide regardless of the API. delivery.createNamespace true Create delivery.namespace. Set false to create it yourself first, for example to put the recorder key Secret in it before the install delivery.enabled false Install Pacto delivery: the promoter, its CRDs (Stage, Operation, Approval), roles and admission policies delivery.flux.enabled auto (bool or auto) Let Stages apply through Flux: an OCIRepository with a Kustomization, or a HelmRelease whose spec.chartRef names an OCIRepository. Grants the promoter patch on OCIRepositories (admission holds it to spec.ref.digest) and Kustomization read. auto grants it when the cluster serves source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1 OCIRepository at install or upgrade, and adds HelmRelease read when it also serves helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2 HelmRelease. true grants both regardless of the API; false grants neither. delivery.gates.caBundle.configMap "" A ConfigMap in delivery.namespace holding the PEM certificates of the CAs that sign your in-cluster providers' https certificates, so they need no allowPlainHTTP. The promoter trusts them on top of the image's public roots. Empty trusts the public roots only. delivery.gates.caBundle.key ca.crt The key in that ConfigMap delivery.gates.providers [] Health gate providers a Stage may name in spec.gates.verify.checks[].provider, each {name, type, url} with type mira (Mira's query API), http (any tool behind the plug-in format) or eval (a runner for the check suites a version ships, named by checks[].suite). The URL is operator configuration: a Stage only names a provider and an agent names nothing. pacto.contract and pacto.runtime are built in. The URL must be https: a verdict ends up in a signed record, so an answer forged in transit could get a Pass signed. Plain http works only on loopback, or with allowPlainHTTP: true on a test cluster. An eval provider also needs signers: the runners whose signed answers it trusts, each {name, publicKey} or {name, identity, issuer, trustedRoot}. An answer no signer signed is Unknown, and the verdict names the runner that signed it. Each provider's name and type (never its URL or signers) is also published in the identity policy ConfigMap, so pacto delivery plan and the dashboard predict an eval check's hold as the promoter does. delivery.identities.agentGroups null Groups whose members are agents. Agents may propose, never approve or unfreeze. Service accounts other than the promoter, other system: users and unauthenticated requests are always agents; every other signed-in identity is a person. Use it for automation that signs in through OIDC. delivery.identities.breakGlassGroups null Groups that may raise an override and edit an OCIRepository's spec.ref.digest directly delivery.identities.humanGroups [] Deprecated: people and agents are told apart by how they sign in. When set, anyone in none of these groups is an agent. delivery.identities.requireOwnerTeam false A held question whose service and consumers declare no owner team is answered by nobody, and only break-glass can override. False lets whoever may update the workload answer it. delivery.identities.signers [] Issuers whose keyless certificates may sign an approval (pacto delivery approve). Each entry has issuer (the OIDC issuer URL), clientID (the OIDC client the CLI logs in with), usernamePrefix (put before the certificate's email to name the Kubernetes user), subjects (required: a regular expression every approver's whole email must match, anchored at both ends, for example [^@]+@acme\.com), fulcioURL, timestampURL and trustedRoot (the Sigstore trusted_root.json the certificate chains to). Empty, keyless approvals never count and the CLI records Approvals in the cluster. Privacy: public-good Fulcio logs every certificate, the approver's email included, to Certificate Transparency. delivery.identities.teamGroupPrefix null Set it to narrow who may answer to the owner teams: a contract owner team T is then the group T (with "") or this prefix followed by T (for example acme:). A system: group is never a team. Unset, whoever may update the Stage's workload answers. delivery.image.digest "" Pins the image by digest (sha256:...), appended to the tag as tag@digest so the runtime pulls exactly that image whatever the tag resolves to later delivery.image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Image pull policy delivery.image.registry "" Promoter and recorder image registry (defaults to global.imageRegistry) delivery.image.repository trianalab/pacto/delivery Promoter and recorder image repository (the pacto-delivery image) delivery.image.tag "" Overrides the image tag (default is the chart appVersion) delivery.imagePullSecrets [] Image pull secrets of the promoter and the recorder, after global.imagePullSecrets delivery.insecureRegistries [] Registry hosts (host:port) the promoter and the recorder reach over plain HTTP. An OCIRepository with spec.insecure: true is read over HTTP anyway. delivery.metrics.enabled true Expose the promoter's metrics (plain HTTP, port 8080) through a Service. The recorder's come with delivery.recorder.monitoring delivery.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled false Create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor for that Service delivery.metrics.serviceMonitor.interval "" Scrape interval (empty uses Prometheus' default) delivery.metrics.serviceMonitor.scrapeTimeout "" Scrape timeout (empty uses Prometheus' default) delivery.namespace pacto-delivery Dedicated namespace the promoter and the recorder run in. The chart creates it; it must not be the release or node agent namespace (the operator can create Deployments, DaemonSets and Secrets there). delivery.nodeSelector {} Node selector for the promoter pod delivery.podAnnotations {} Annotations to add to the promoter and recorder pods delivery.podLabels {} Labels to add to the promoter and recorder pods delivery.podSecurityContext {} Pod securityContext of the promoter and the recorder (defaults to global.podSecurityContext) delivery.promoter.authFreshness "" How old a person's login may be when their approval is given, as a Go duration such as 15m; an older one is ignored, so deciding needs a fresh sign-in. Empty or a zero duration (0, 0s): any signed-in person decides with the session they have. Every Stage publishes it in status.authFreshness delivery.promoter.leaderElect true Elect one active promoter delivery.promoter.poll 3s How often an operation waiting on Flux, Pacto or a person is looked at (a Go duration) delivery.promoter.registryCredentials.secretName "" A kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret with read access to the contract and deploy repositories, for a private registry. Without it the promoter reads only public ones. delivery.promoter.resync 1m How often a Stage is looked at when nothing it watches changed (a Go duration). A change to its operations, upstream Stage or the Flux or Argo CD objects the promoter watches wakes it at once delivery.promoter.upstreamTrust "" The recorder keys of other clusters, as a trust config in YAML (keys per stream glob). A Stage with candidates.upstreamRecords promotes only on records one of these keys signed for that stream; without it such a Stage is not Ready. Public keys only. delivery.promoter.workers 4 How many operations and Stages the promoter reconciles at once, so one slow health provider does not hold up the rest delivery.publishers.defaultBranch main The default branch whose CI the derived rule accepts delivery.publishers.policy "" A signed delivery policy (repository:tag) whose publisher rules replace the derived rule once verified. Needs policySigners delivery.publishers.policySigners "" The keys that sign the delivery policy, as a trust config in YAML with role: policy keys (keys: [{publicKey: <PEM>, role: policy}]). Public keys only delivery.publishers.registry "" The registry (host/org) the installation's services publish to. On ghcr.io and registry.gitlab.com the promoter derives a rule from it: the organization's CI on the default branch. Empty: no publisher rule, so only the signed policy or a person's confirmation in the delivery inbox accepts a signer delivery.publishers.trustedRoot "" A Sigstore trusted root (trusted_root.json) publisher signatures must chain to, for a private Sigstore. Empty uses public-good Sigstore delivery.recorder.approvalsRepository "" Repository (host/path) a person's client pushes signed approvals to, one anchor per Stage stream. Empty is <streamsRepository>-approvals. Approvers need push access here and only here: only the recorder pushes to the streams repository. delivery.recorder.cdeventsSink "" A URL the recorder POSTs a CDEvent (CloudEvents, structured mode) to for every record and when a Stage is created or deleted (environment.created, environment.deleted), best effort. Empty sends none. delivery.recorder.enabled false Run the recorder, which writes a signed record of every concluded operation to the registry as OCI referrers. Off by default. When on, the promoter leaves the record finalizer to it. The recorder detects whether the registry serves the OCI Referrers API and otherwise writes one write-once, content-addressed tag per record in the streams repository. It also signs every Approval into the registry, and the promoter then counts an Approval only once its record is written. Upgrade the CLIs and the promoters that follow these streams first: an older reader refuses an operation record that names its approvals' records. delivery.recorder.extraEnv [] Extra environment for the recorder (for example the credentials a KMS client reads) delivery.recorder.leaderElect true Elect one active recorder delivery.recorder.monitoring.enabled false Scrape the recorder's metrics and alert when records fall behind: a metrics Service, a ServiceMonitor and a PrometheusRule. Needs the Prometheus Operator CRDs. delivery.recorder.operationTTL 168h Keep a recorded operation this long after it concluded, then delete it: its record holds what happened. The operation a Stage runs is never deleted. 0s keeps them all (a Go duration). delivery.recorder.poll 30s How long a registry or signer failure backs off (a Go duration) delivery.recorder.registryCredentials.secretName "" A kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret with push access to the streams, apply and contract repositories. Only the recorder mounts it. delivery.recorder.resources.limits.memory 256Mi Memory limit of the recorder delivery.recorder.resources.requests.cpu 50m CPU request of the recorder. Signing and pushing a record is the costly part. delivery.recorder.resources.requests.memory 64Mi Memory request of the recorder delivery.recorder.serviceAccount.annotations {} Annotations to add to the recorder's ServiceAccount (workload identity for KMS or keyless) delivery.recorder.serviceAccount.create true Create a ServiceAccount for the recorder delivery.recorder.serviceAccount.name "" Name override (defaults to <fullname>-delivery-recorder) delivery.recorder.signing.allowOperatorReadableKey false Say yes to an Ed25519 key in a Secret the operator may read. The operator reads Secrets in the release namespace, in each of controller.watchNamespaces and the ones controller.secretGrants names, so the chart refuses ed25519.secretName unless this is true when delivery.namespace is the release namespace, is watched, or the key is granted by name: the recorder would not be the key's only holder. Prefer KMS or keyless signing delivery.recorder.signing.ed25519.generate false Generate that Secret at install, with a new Ed25519 key kept across upgrades (for evaluation) delivery.recorder.signing.ed25519.key key.pem The key in that Secret delivery.recorder.signing.ed25519.secretName "" A Secret holding a PKCS#8 PEM Ed25519 private key (for kind and tests) delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.enabled false Sign keyless with a Fulcio certificate for the recorder's workload identity, presented as a projected service account token for the sigstore audience. Rekor upload is off; a timestamp authority dates each signature. delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.fulcioURL "" The Fulcio that issues the certificate delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.identity "" The certificate identity keyless signing produces delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.issuer "" The OIDC issuer keyless signing uses delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.timestampURL "" The timestamp authority whose signed time a short-lived certificate verifies at delivery.recorder.signing.keyless.trustedRoot "" The Sigstore trusted root (trusted_root.json) naming that Fulcio and timestamp authority. Required with keyless: without it a self-signed certificate could name the recorder's identity. delivery.recorder.signing.kms "" A KMS key URI (awskms://, gcpkms://, azurekms://, hashivault://). The default image includes every provider; an image built with --build-arg GO_TAGS= has none, and one built with GO_TAGS=kms_aws (or kms_gcp, kms_azure, kms_hashivault) has only that one delivery.recorder.signing.publicKey "" The recorder's public key (PEM) for an Ed25519 or KMS recorder, so the promoter and clients verify the publisher pins it writes. Keyless signing needs none: its identity names the signer. Empty with an Ed25519 or KMS recorder: no new publisher can be confirmed delivery.recorder.streamsRepository "" Repository (host/path) that holds one anchor per Stage stream. Defaults to <registry>/pacto-streams when the top-level registry is set; required otherwise when enabled. delivery.recorder.trust "" Other keys whose records the recorder accepts, as a trust config in YAML (keys: [{publicKey: <PEM>, streams: ["*/prod/*"]}]): list the old key here while you rotate to a new one, and set untilSeq and untilRecord on a leaked key to revoke it after the last record it signed. The recorder's own key is always trusted. A record no listed key signed is skipped as untrusted. delivery.replicaCount 1 Number of promoter replicas. Only the elected leader acts. delivery.resources.limits.memory 256Mi Memory limit of the promoter delivery.resources.requests.cpu 100m CPU request of the promoter. It looks at every waiting operation once per promoter.poll, so raise it with the number of Stages. delivery.resources.requests.memory 128Mi Memory request of the promoter delivery.securityContext {} Container securityContext of the promoter and the recorder (defaults to global.securityContext) delivery.serviceAccount.annotations {} Annotations to add to the ServiceAccount delivery.serviceAccount.create true Create a ServiceAccount for the promoter delivery.serviceAccount.name "" Name override (defaults to <fullname>-delivery) delivery.stats.registryCredentials.secretName "" A kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret in delivery.namespace with push access to delivery.stats.repository. Only the promoter mounts it. Without it the promoter uses delivery.promoter.registryCredentials, which is usually read-only. delivery.stats.repository "" A repository (host/path) the promoter publishes an unsigned run record of every concluded operation to, attached to one anchor per service. Empty records none. Records are statistics for pacto stats and the dashboard Metrics page; nothing that decides reads them. Keep the repository private: pull access to it equals read access to the delivery history of every Stage in every cluster that records to it, so grant pull only to the identities that run pacto stats or the dashboard. A registry without the OCI Referrers API (GHCR) uses the run-record tag fallback, where concurrent writers to one service can lose a record without it being counted. delivery.tolerations [] Tolerations for the promoter pod dex.enabled false Install Dex from its official chart as the dashboard's OpenID Connect issuer. The chart then generates the dashboard's client secret into the Secret dashboard.auth.oidc.clientSecretRef.name names, with the keys client-secret, admin-password and admin-password-hash, and keeps it across upgrades. Its values are the upstream chart's evidence.enabled false Enable the operator-managed Evidence Server deployment. Disabled by default. When enabled the operator reconciles a SEPARATE Evidence Server Deployment and an internal Service; the image is the same runtime image as the dashboard and is not user-configurable. The Evidence Server is single- writer, so its replica count is fixed at one. evidence.httpRoute.enabled false Enable Gateway API HTTPRoute for the Evidence Server. evidence.httpRoute.hostnames [] Hostnames for the HTTPRoute. evidence.httpRoute.parentRefs [] Parent gateway references. evidence.httpRoute.rules [] HTTPRoute rules. When empty, a single catch-all rule routes to the chart-managed evidence Service on evidence.service.port. evidence.ingress.annotations {} Ingress annotations. evidence.ingress.className "" Ingress class name. evidence.ingress.enabled false Enable Ingress for the Evidence Server. evidence.ingress.hosts null Ingress hosts. evidence.ingress.tls [] Ingress TLS configuration. evidence.registry.credentialsSecret "" Optional name of an EXISTING kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret with credentials for that registry, mounted read-only. The chart never creates it and never renders its contents. Empty means anonymous or in-cluster access. evidence.registry.subjects [] Required when evidence is enabled: the exact, immutable contract revisions evidence may be reported against, each an oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest> reference. The registry holding them is the durable evidence store: every accepted record is published as an OCI 1.1 referrer of one of these manifests, so the chart installs nothing durable in the cluster. A mutable tag is rejected, because moving it onto another manifest would change what the stored evidence reports on. That registry must serve the native OCI 1.1 Referrers API. GHCR and CNCF distribution (registry:2, registry:3) lack it, and the Evidence Server stays permanently not-ready against them. evidence.resources.limits.memory 256Mi Memory limit for the Evidence Server container. It verifies and forwards one envelope at a time and stores nothing locally, so this is sized for a single writer. evidence.resources.requests.cpu 25m CPU request for the Evidence Server container evidence.resources.requests.memory 64Mi Memory request for the Evidence Server container evidence.service.nodePort "" Node port (only used when type is NodePort). evidence.service.port 8686 Evidence service port. evidence.service.type ClusterIP Evidence exposure Service type (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer). The operator manages an internal ClusterIP Service (pacto-evidence) for in-cluster access; this chart-managed Service provides optional external access and backs any Ingress/HTTPRoute. evidence.trust.configKey "" Optional key of the existingSecret holding a structured trust config (apiVersion pacto.dev/evidence-trust/v1, a .yaml or .yml key). When set, the Evidence Server starts with that file, so each key can carry subject, contract-repository and observation-kind allowlists: a provisioning adapter needs allowedObservationKinds [ResourceProvisioned], and allowedProviderRepos scopes a provisioning adapter to the provider repositories it serves. Its publicKeyFile entries name other keys of the same Secret. Empty trusts every *.pub key in the Secret for runtime evidence only. evidence.trust.existingSecret "" Name of an existing Secret of trusted producer public keys, mounted read-only. Signature verification is mandatory, so this is required when evidence is enabled. fingerprints.managers [] Tools that apply workloads, each named by a fieldManager, a label or an annotation key it leaves on a workload. A workload one of them manages reads external: <product>, and the delivery promoter runs the gates and writes no pointer for it. fingerprints.promoters null Tools that promote versions, each named by a crd (<plural>.<group>) the cluster serves, or a label or annotation key on a workload. Data sources reads promotion owned by <product> for each one found, with the entry's optional offer (id, text, an https doc) as the Pacto integration that row offers. These three are examples of an open list: add any IDP's promoter, public or private, as one more entry, or set it to null for none. fullnameOverride "" Override the full release name global.commonLabels {} Labels added to every object the chart renders global.imagePullSecrets [] Image pull secrets for every pod the chart runs, before each component's own global.imageRegistry ghcr.io Registry of every image the chart runs (the controller, the delivery promoter and the recorder), unless an image sets its own registry. Set it empty to give each repository as a whole reference. global.podSecurityContext.runAsNonRoot true Run pod as non-root global.podSecurityContext.seccompProfile.type RuntimeDefault Seccomp profile type global.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation false Disallow privilege escalation global.securityContext.capabilities.drop null Drop all capabilities global.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem true Read-only root filesystem global.securityContext.runAsNonRoot true Run as non-root global.securityContext.runAsUser 65532 Run as UID 65532 (nonroot in distroless) image.digest "" Pins the image by digest (sha256:...), appended to the tag as tag@digest so the runtime pulls exactly that image whatever the tag resolves to later image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Image pull policy image.registry "" Controller image registry (defaults to global.imageRegistry) image.repository trianalab/pacto/operator Controller image repository image.tag "" Overrides the image tag (default is the chart appVersion) imagePullSecrets [] Image pull secrets of the controller pod, after global.imagePullSecrets. The managed node agent gets them too insecureRegistries [] Registry hosts (host:port) to reach over plain HTTP, for a controlled in-cluster registry. Scoped per host, so every other registry stays HTTPS-only. The controller, the managed dashboard and the managed Evidence Server all inherit it, because each one resolves contract refs itself. leaderElection.enabled true Enable leader election for HA deployments metrics.enabled true Enable the metrics endpoint metrics.secure true Serve metrics over HTTPS metrics.service.port 8443 Metrics service port metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled false Create a Prometheus ServiceMonitor metrics.serviceMonitor.interval "" Scrape interval metrics.serviceMonitor.scrapeTimeout "" Scrape timeout nameOverride "" Override the chart name nodeAgent.enabled false Deploy the node agent DaemonSet. Off by default. nodeAgent.image "" Full image reference of the node agent. Empty uses the runtime image the operator was built with. nodeAgent.namespace pacto-node-agent Dedicated namespace the agents run and publish in. The chart creates it and labels it privileged for Pod Security; it must not be the release namespace and must not exist outside this release. nodeAgent.publishInterval 30s How often each agent publishes its node's observation. A Go duration; kernel evidence reads stale after three intervals unless controller.kernelEvidence.staleness says otherwise. nodeAgent.resources.limits.cpu 200m CPU limit for the node agent container nodeAgent.resources.limits.memory 256Mi Memory limit for the node agent container. The agent caps the pods and connections it tracks, and the kernel ring buffer is charged here. nodeAgent.resources.requests.cpu 50m CPU request for the node agent container nodeAgent.resources.requests.memory 64Mi Memory request for the node agent container nodeSelector {} Node selector for the controller pod podAnnotations {} Annotations to add to the controller pod podLabels {} Labels to add to the controller pod podSecurityContext {} Pod securityContext of the controller (defaults to global.podSecurityContext) registry "" The installation registry (host[/path], no scheme), such as ghcr.io/acme. The operator publishes the cluster's target snapshot, signed with the installation key it creates once, to <registry>/pacto-targets, which pacto impact reads in CI; empty publishes none. Delivery stays off until delivery.enabled=true. registryPullSecret "" namespace/name of an existing Secret that authenticates to registry, for a registry without workload identity. Pacto proposes one it saw running pods use (helm upgrade notes and Data sources) and never uses it until you name it here. The chart grants get on that Secret only. replicaCount 1 Number of controller replicas resources.limits.memory 256Mi Memory limit of the controller. It caches every Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob and Service it targets. resources.requests.cpu 100m CPU request of the controller resources.requests.memory 128Mi Memory request of the controller securityContext {} Container securityContext of the controller (defaults to global.securityContext) serviceAccount.annotations {} Annotations to add to the ServiceAccount serviceAccount.automount true Automount API credentials serviceAccount.create true Create a ServiceAccount for the controller serviceAccount.name "" Name override (defaults to fullname) tolerations [] Tolerations for the controller pod zot.enabled false Install zot from its official chart as an in-cluster OCI registry with native referrers. Its values are the upstream chart's

docs.title: Operator configuration
docs.text:
Controller flags and their exact defaults are captured from the operator's real --help output.

One dash or two makes no difference. The table shows the single-dash spelling because that is how Go's flag package prints and reports flags, and other pages write --enable-kernel-evidence. The parser accepts both forms identically: --enable-kernel-evidence=x and -enable-kernel-evidence=x produce the same invalid boolean value "x" for -enable-kernel-evidence error. Neither spelling is more correct.

Two different defaults can apply to the same flag. The Default column below is the binary's default -- what you get running the controller with no arguments. The Helm chart renders its own fixed argument list, so where a chart value exists it decides, and its default may differ. -enable-dashboard is the one that catches people out: the binary defaults it off, the chart's dashboard.enabled defaults it on, and a chart install therefore runs the managed dashboard. See the Helm reference for the values and their defaults.

A flag the chart never renders cannot be set on the documented install path. The chart has no extraArgs, so the Via chart column is the whole story: chart value means some value in values.yaml renders this flag; always on means the chart hardcodes it and no value changes it; no means the chart never passes it, and reaching it requires patching the Deployment after install -- which helm upgrade then reverts. See Limitations.

docs.title: Command-line flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Via chart Description -caller-coverage-ignore-namespace value chart value Namespace whose host-network pods are taken not to call workloads, so they leave a Service's caller coverage complete (repeatable). kube-system and the other cluster namespaces and the node agent's are always ignored. -dashboard-allow-anonymous bool chart value Serve the dashboard without sign-in when neither an issuer nor token sign-in is set; everyone who reaches it reads what its ServiceAccount reads. -dashboard-cpu-limit string chart value CPU limit for the dashboard container. Empty uses the built-in default. -dashboard-cpu-request string chart value CPU request for the dashboard container. Empty uses the built-in default. -dashboard-delivery-namespace string chart value Namespace Pacto delivery runs in, whose published identity policy the dashboard reads; empty means pacto-delivery. -dashboard-delivery-trust-configmap string chart value ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the trust config the dashboard verifies delivery records with, so History reads signed records. -dashboard-delivery-trust-key string trust.yaml chart value Key of the trust config in that ConfigMap. -dashboard-external-catalog string chart value Organization external catalog the dashboard merges over Pacto's default, as oci://REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST. -dashboard-fingerprints-configmap string chart value ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the workload manager and promoter fingerprints (fingerprints.yaml) the dashboard reads as --fingerprints. -dashboard-memory-limit string chart value Memory limit for the dashboard container. Empty uses the built-in default. -dashboard-memory-request string chart value Memory request for the dashboard container. Empty uses the built-in default. -dashboard-mira-url string chart value Mira's address, to link the dashboard's health-check citations. -dashboard-oci-secrets string chart value Optional: comma-separated list of Secret names in the operator namespace for OCI registry credentials. Supports Opaque (registry + token, or registry + username + password) and kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson secrets; later Secrets override earlier ones for the same registry. -dashboard-oidc-ca-configmap string chart value ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the PEM bundle of the CAs that sign the issuer's certificate. -dashboard-oidc-ca-key string ca.crt chart value Key of the PEM bundle in that ConfigMap or Secret. -dashboard-oidc-ca-secret string chart value Secret in the operator namespace holding that PEM bundle, instead of a ConfigMap. -dashboard-oidc-client-id string chart value The dashboard's OpenID Connect client id. -dashboard-oidc-client-secret-key string client-secret chart value Key of the client secret in that Secret. -dashboard-oidc-client-secret-name string chart value Secret in the operator namespace holding the client secret, passed to the dashboard by secretKeyRef. -dashboard-oidc-display-name string chart value The identity provider's name on the dashboard's sign-in button, as in Sign in with Keycloak (empty: OIDC). -dashboard-oidc-extra-scopes string chart value Comma-separated scopes beyond openid, profile and groups. -dashboard-oidc-groups-claim string chart value ID token claim the API server takes the groups from; must match its claim mapping (empty: groups). -dashboard-oidc-groups-prefix string chart value Prefix the API server puts before every group; must match its claim mapping. -dashboard-oidc-internal-issuer-url string chart value Where the dashboard reaches the issuer when it differs from the public issuer URL browsers use, such as an in-cluster Service; ID tokens must still name the public issuer. -dashboard-oidc-issuer-url string chart value OpenID Connect issuer people sign in to the dashboard with. Every view and action then runs with each person's own token and RBAC; the delivery views need sign-in. -dashboard-oidc-redirect-url string chart value The dashboard's /auth/callback as browsers reach it; TLS must terminate in front of it. -dashboard-oidc-username-claim string chart value ID token claim the API server takes the username from; must match its claim mapping (empty: sub). -dashboard-oidc-username-prefix string chart value Prefix the API server puts before the username; must match its claim mapping (empty: the issuer URL and #; - for none). -dashboard-owner-policy-configmap string chart value Immutable ConfigMap in the operator namespace holding the owner policy (policy.json) the dashboard mounts. -dashboard-repositories value chart value Comma-separated oci:// references the dashboard reads beside the contracts it discovers from Pacto resources, such as golden paths, which are never deployed. -dashboard-session-idle-timeout duration chart value A dashboard session without a request for this long ends (0: 1h). -dashboard-session-max-age duration chart value A dashboard session ends this long after sign-in, renewed or not (0: 12h). -dashboard-stats-registry string chart value Stats repository the dashboard's Metrics page reads run records from, with the dashboard's OCI credentials; empty: the page explains how to turn recording on. -dashboard-token-login bool chart value Let people sign in to the dashboard with a Kubernetes token; a ServiceAccount token minted for the pacto-dashboard audience reads the fleet only, and a person's own token acts as them. -dashboard-trace-source value chart value Repeatable: an offline OTLP/JSON trace file to mount read-only into the dashboard, as name=NAME,file=RELATIVE_PATH,existingClaim=PVC (or configMap=NAME). NAME is the stable Data Source identity. Configures offline input only; Pacto runs no OTLP receiver. -enable-dashboard bool chart value Enable the managed Pacto dashboard deployment. Disabled by default. -enable-evidence-server bool chart value Enable the managed Pacto Evidence Server deployment. Disabled by default. -enable-http2 bool no If set, HTTP/2 will be enabled for the metrics server -enable-kernel-evidence bool chart value Merge the node agent's kernel observations (NodeRuntimeObservation objects) into interface and dependency evidence. Off by default; when off, evidence comes from the Kubernetes API only. -enable-metrics-observation =mode chart value Metrics observation (discovery and active probe), written =mode: on, off or auto. auto observes metrics only in namespaces labelled pacto.trianalab.io/observe with metrics. The bare flag means on. Off by default; when off, metrics read Unsupported. -enable-node-agent bool chart value Enable the managed node agent DaemonSet, which observes TCP socket state with eBPF on every node and publishes it as NodeRuntimeObservation objects. Disabled by default. -enable-probing =mode chart value Active in-cluster probing (health endpoints over HTTP and each present interface's wire protocol), written =mode: on, off or auto. auto probes only in namespaces labelled pacto.trianalab.io/observe with probing. The bare flag means on. Off by default; when off, health uses passive readiness-probe and EndpointSlice signals only and interface protocols read unverified. -evidence-cpu-limit string chart value CPU limit for the Evidence Server container. Empty uses the built-in default. -evidence-cpu-request string chart value CPU request for the Evidence Server container. Empty uses the built-in default. -evidence-credentials-secret string chart value Optional: name of an existing kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret with contract-registry credentials, mounted read-only. Empty means anonymous or in-cluster registry access. -evidence-memory-limit string chart value Memory limit for the Evidence Server container. Empty uses the built-in default. -evidence-memory-request string chart value Memory request for the Evidence Server container. Empty uses the built-in default. -evidence-subject value chart value Repeatable: an exact contract revision evidence is stored on, as oci://<repo>@sha256:<digest>. The registry holding it is the durable evidence store: accepted records are published as OCI 1.1 referrers of that manifest. At least one is required when the Evidence Server is enabled. -evidence-trust-config-key string chart value Optional: key of the trust Secret holding a structured trust config (pacto.dev/evidence-trust/v1, a .yaml key). Set it to grant per-key allowlists such as ResourceProvisioned. Empty trusts every *.pub key in the Secret. -evidence-trust-secret string chart value Name of a Secret of trusted producer public keys, mounted read-only. Required when the Evidence Server is enabled. -health-probe-bind-address string :8081 always on The address the probe endpoint binds to. -interface-name-match-discovery bool chart value Enable resolving an unbound interface's Service port by matching a Service port whose name equals the interface name (positive availability assist only; never produces an absent or error result). -kernel-evidence-namespace string chart value Namespace the node agent publishes NodeRuntimeObservation objects and heartbeat Leases to. Empty uses --node-agent-namespace. -kernel-evidence-staleness duration chart value How old a node's heartbeat (its Lease renewal, or the observation's lastPublished without a Lease) may be before its evidence reads stale. 0 uses three times the publish interval the node agent reports. -kubeconfig string no Paths to a kubeconfig. Only required if out-of-cluster. -leader-elect bool chart value Enable leader election for controller manager. Enabling this will ensure there is only one active controller manager. -metrics-bind-address string :8080 chart value The address the metrics endpoint binds to. Use :8443 for HTTPS or :8080 for HTTP, or set to 0 to disable the metrics service. -metrics-cert-key string tls.key no The name of the metrics server key file. -metrics-cert-name string tls.crt no The name of the metrics server certificate file. -metrics-cert-path string no The directory that contains the metrics server certificate. -metrics-secure bool chart value If set, the metrics endpoint is served securely via HTTPS. Use --metrics-secure=true to enable HTTPS. -node-agent-cpu-limit string chart value CPU limit for the node agent container. Empty uses the built-in default. -node-agent-cpu-request string chart value CPU request for the node agent container. Empty uses the built-in default. -node-agent-image string chart value Image the node agent runs pacto agent from. Empty uses the dashboard image this binary was built with, the runtime image the Evidence Server runs too. -node-agent-image-pull-secret value chart value Secret the node agent's ServiceAccount pulls its image with (repeatable). -node-agent-memory-limit string chart value Memory limit for the node agent container. Empty uses the built-in default. -node-agent-memory-request string chart value Memory request for the node agent container. Empty uses the built-in default. -node-agent-namespace string pacto-node-agent always on Dedicated namespace the node agent runs and publishes in. The operator labels it privileged for Pod Security, so it must not be the operator namespace. -node-agent-publish-interval duration 30s chart value How often each node agent publishes its node's NodeRuntimeObservation. -owner-policy string chart value File holding the owner policy (policy.json from the chart's declare block): who may set a service owner. Published in the target snapshot; empty publishes none. -publishers-default-branch string main chart value The default branch whose CI the derived publisher rule accepts. -publishers-policy string chart value The signed delivery policy's tag reference (delivery.publishers.policy): once verified, its publisher rules replace the derived rule and its signer class rules classify who signed an owner change, as the fleet does. -publishers-policy-signers string always on A trust config (YAML) whose role: policy keys sign the delivery policy. Required with --publishers-policy. -publishers-registry string chart value The registry (host/org) the installation's services publish to: its derived publisher rule (the organization's CI on the default branch) is the only CI identity whose signed CODEOWNERS or catalog-info.yaml owner counts as attested when an owner change is judged. Empty: no owner is attested. -registry string chart value The installation registry (host/path): Pacto publishes the target snapshot and inferred contracts under it and pushes nowhere else; empty turns those features off. -registry-pull-secret string chart value namespace/name of the Secret that authenticates to the installation registry; used only under the push prefixes. -registry-push-prefix value chart value Repeatable: a repository prefix a Pacto component may push under; the chart renders every one. -stabilization-window duration 2m0s chart value The stabilization window duration for compliance assertions before they trigger a false condition. Assertions must remain unsatisfied for this entire window before being considered a failure. -trusted-root string chart value File holding a Sigstore trusted root (trusted_root.json) that the signatures of an owner change must chain to. Empty fetches public-good Sigstore's root through TUF, caching nothing on disk. -version bool no Print version information and exit. -watch-namespace string no Deprecated: use --watch-namespaces. Merged into the --watch-namespaces list. -watch-namespaces string chart value Restrict the controller and the managed dashboard to these namespaces (comma-separated). Empty (default) means cluster-wide. -zap-devel bool no Development Mode defaults(encoder=consoleEncoder,logLevel=Debug,stackTraceLevel=Warn). Production Mode defaults(encoder=jsonEncoder,logLevel=Info,stackTraceLevel=Error) -zap-encoder value no Zap log encoding (one of 'json' or 'console') -zap-log-level value no Zap Level to configure the verbosity of logging. Can be one of 'debug', 'info', 'error', 'panic' or any integer value > 0 which corresponds to custom debug levels of increasing verbosity -zap-stacktrace-level value no Zap Level at and above which stacktraces are captured (one of 'info', 'error', 'panic'). -zap-time-encoding value no Zap time encoding (one of 'epoch', 'millis', 'nano', 'iso8601', 'rfc3339' or 'rfc3339nano'). Defaults to 'epoch'.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Read directly by the controller entrypoint (cmd/main.go), typically wired through the downward API in the chart's Deployment.

Variable Purpose OPERATOR_DEPLOYMENT_NAME Operator Deployment name, used to set ownerReferences on dashboard resources. OPERATOR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT Operator ServiceAccount name, written as the publisher the target snapshot claims. POD_NAMESPACE Namespace the operator (and its managed dashboard) runs in. Required.

docs.title: RBAC
docs.text:
Every table below is rendered from the Helm chart itself, so it is the permission set an install actually creates. A cluster-wide install (the default) creates a ClusterRole (pacto-operator-manager) bound to the controller's ServiceAccount for what has to be cluster-wide; with controller.watchNamespaces set, it is replaced by namespaced Roles. Every install creates a Role (pacto-operator-manager) in the release namespace for the managed components that run there, a second one of the same name in the node agent's namespace when the agent is on, and a Role (pacto-operator-leader-election) for leader election. The tables render the release namespace as pacto-operator-system.

Note

The repository also contains config/rbac/role.yaml, a kubebuilder-generated manager-role. It is a different object with a different name and is not what helm install creates. It belongs to the config/ kustomize scaffolding, which is not published with a release and is deployed by no test or CI job -- Helm is the only supported install path.

docs.title: Always granted (pacto-operator-manager)
docs.text:
Present in every cluster-wide install, including one with every managed component disabled. Workloads and their wiring are read-only; the writes are on Pacto's own resources, on events, and on the specific named objects a previous install may have created (so the operator can clean them up after you disable a component).

No ClusterRole grants Secrets. The operator reads a pull Secret or a Secret that backs a configuration with get in the release namespace and in each of controller.watchNamespaces, and anywhere else only the Secrets controller.secretGrants names (namespace/name), each through a Role limited to that Secret.

The namespaces get rule limited to kube-system reads the cluster id. The one with no name reads the pacto.trianalab.io/observe label of a target's namespace, names and labels only, and is granted only while controller.probing or controller.metricsObservation is auto (the default). With controller.watchNamespaces each watched namespace's Role carries it instead.

docs.title: Always granted in the release namespace (pacto-operator-manager Role)
docs.text:
The teardown half of the managed components: get and delete on the fixed names a previous install may have created there, the node agent's included (releases before the dedicated agent namespace ran it in the release namespace). The one secrets get rule with no name reads pull Secrets and Secrets that back a configuration in the release namespace. The configmaps rules let detection write <fullname>-detected, the one ConfigMap it publishes: create cannot be limited by name, and get and patch name that ConfigMap only. The deployments get rule naming the operator's own Deployment lets detection set it as the ConfigMap's owner.

docs.title: Additionally granted when a managed component is enabled
docs.text:
When a managed component is on, the operator creates and reconciles that component's Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount and RBAC for you, and the chart widens the ClusterRole accordingly. At chart defaults dashboard.enabled is on and evidence.enabled is off, so every rule below is what a default install adds for the dashboard. Rendering the chart with --set dashboard.enabled=false --set evidence.enabled=false removes every rule in this table.

API groups Resources Verbs Limited to "" (core) namespaces list not name-restricted authorization.k8s.io subjectaccessreviews create not name-restricted delivery.pacto.trianalab.io stages, operations get, list, watch not name-restricted rbac.authorization.k8s.io clusterroles, clusterrolebindings create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch not name-restricted

Their namespaced half is granted by the release namespace's pacto-operator-manager Role, so the operator can create these kinds there and nowhere else:

API groups Resources Verbs Limited to "" (core) secrets, serviceaccounts, services create, delete, get, patch, update not name-restricted apps deployments create, delete, get, patch, update not name-restricted

This grant allows privilege escalation

The rules above include unrestricted create on clusterroles and clusterrolebindings. A subject that can create a ClusterRoleBinding can grant itself any permission in the cluster, so at chart defaults the operator is effectively cluster-admin-capable, not read-only. This is what lets it create the managed components' RBAC.

If your threat model does not allow that, install with --set dashboard.enabled=false --set evidence.enabled=false and deploy those components yourself. The operator then keeps only the Always granted table plus narrow get/delete on the specific objects a previous install may have left behind.

docs.title: Additionally granted with the node agent (nodeAgent.enabled)
docs.text:
The agent runs in its own namespace (pacto-node-agent by default), which the chart creates with the privileged Pod Security level. Cluster-wide, the operator gains a node read (the orphan prune), a read and relabel of that one namespace by name, and a read of the agents' heartbeat Leases (also granted when controller.kernelEvidence.enabled is on):

API groups Resources Verbs Limited to "" (core) namespaces get, patch pacto-node-agent "" (core) nodes get not name-restricted coordination.k8s.io leases get, list, watch not name-restricted

Everything it creates for the agent is granted by the pacto-operator-manager Role in the agent namespace. The agents' own Role (written by the operator) is get, create and patch on their observations and get, create, patch and update on their Leases, and Kubernetes lets the operator grant only what it holds, so it holds those verbs here:

API groups Resources Verbs Limited to "" (core) serviceaccounts create, delete, get, patch not name-restricted apps daemonsets create, delete, get, patch, update not name-restricted coordination.k8s.io leases create, delete, get, patch, update not name-restricted pacto.trianalab.io noderuntimeobservations create, delete, get, patch not name-restricted pacto.trianalab.io noderuntimeobservations/status create, get, patch not name-restricted rbac.authorization.k8s.io roles, rolebindings create, delete, get, patch not name-restricted

Where the API serves ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, the chart also renders one that lets each agent write only the observation and Lease named after the node in its token, which RBAC cannot express.

docs.text:
On by default with the dashboard. The dashboard's ServiceAccount may create TokenReviews, which reveals only whose token it already holds, and the pacto-viewer ServiceAccount the NOTES sign-in link carries a token for reads Pactos and nothing else. docs.text:

docs.title: Runtime observations
docs.text: What the operator looks at in your cluster, and every status and finding it can report. It gathers evidence (typed observations of what is running) from two sources, and the Pacto engine turns that evidence into findings and a contract status. The Kubernetes collector reads Kubernetes resources and always runs. The optional node agent watches TCP sockets in the Linux kernel with eBPF and publishes one NodeRuntimeObservation per node; the operator merges it into some dimensions when kernel evidence is on (--enable-kernel-evidence). See Runtime conformance. This page is generated from the operator's observer and the shared engine packages.

docs.title: Observation dimensions
docs.text:
A dimension is one thing the operator checks, such as interfaces or dependencies. Each is observed only when the contract declares the matching section. Spec sections refer to the operator specification. A dash in the kernel column means the dimension comes from the Kubernetes API alone.

Dimension Spec section Gated by Kernel evidence Interfaces 7.3 / B1 + B4 --interface-name-match-discovery (optional positive-availability assist); --enable-probing for the protocol fact listeners on the ready backing pods Dependencies 7.6 always on outbound connections from the target pods Health 7.4 --enable-probing (Tier A active probe; passive Tier B otherwise) - Metrics 7.5 --enable-metrics-observation - Configurations 7.7 always on - Workload 7.1 + AR7 always on - Persistence 7.2 / B3 always on -

The kernel source also reports one thing no dimension asks for: a successful connection to another Pacto-managed Service that no declared dependency resolves to, which the engine reports as DEPENDENCY_UNDECLARED. It reports none while a declared dependency resolves to no Pacto target by ref or name (a local or other non-OCI ref, or an OCI ref no Pacto carries), because that dependency could be the peer the pod reached.

docs.title: Collectors
docs.text:
Every observation names the collector that produced it in its provenance, and every finding copies that name into evidenceRefs[].collector.

Collector Meaning k8s-observer Kubernetes API only. k8s-observer+ebpf Kubernetes API result merged with node agent evidence that changed or qualified it. ebpf Node agent evidence only (an undeclared peer).

docs.title: Observation outcomes
docs.text:
Every observation carries an outcome. Only Observed can lead to a violation; every other outcome becomes an Unknown finding instead.

Outcome Meaning Observed Collected successfully; a value is present. Unsupported The collector cannot observe this dimension (e.g. external Service, non-HTTP binding). Failed Collection was attempted and errored. Stale Last known data is too old to trust. Insufficient Partial/ambiguous, not conclusive (includes within-stabilization-window negatives).

docs.title: Assertion kinds
docs.text:
An assertion is one claim of the contract the operator can check. These are the kinds of evidence it emits, one per assertion:

  • CapabilityObserved
  • ConfigurationPresent
  • DependencyReachable
  • InterfaceObserved
  • PersistenceObserved
  • WorkloadObserved

Provider-reported kinds: ResourceProvisioned, ResourceUsage. Platform adapters report them through the Evidence Server; the operator never emits them.

docs.title: Facts
docs.text:
Details an observation can carry beyond "it is there", such as the protocol a port answers with. An empty fact means not observed: the engine lists the check in evaluationCoverage.unverified and never treats it as a contradiction. Values are generated from pkg/evidence/facts.go.

Fact Value Meaning Protocol http1 the port answered with an HTTP/1.x status line Protocol http2 the port answered with an HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame Protocol tls encrypted: the protocol inside cannot be read, so it proves nothing Protocol other the port answered with bytes that are neither HTTP nor TLS Exposure external reachable from outside the platform's private network Exposure internal reachable from inside the platform's private network only

docs.title: Contract status
docs.text:
status.contractStatus says whether the service matches its contract. Compliance does not report pod health: a failing health check appears as HEALTH_FAILING with status Unknown. Values are generated from the Pacto API.

Status Meaning Compliant No error, unknown or warning findings. Warning Only warning-severity findings. NonCompliant At least one confirmed violation (error-severity finding). Reference Reference-only contract (no runtime target); parsed and validated, never observed. Unknown A required assertion could not be evaluated, or the contract could not be obtained transiently. Invalid Structural validation failed, or a malformed artifact could not be parsed (fail-closed). NotEvaluated Reserved enum value the operator does not currently emit; used by the engine dashboard for offline sources never runtime-evaluated.

Precedence when summarizing findings (see summarizeFindings in internal/controller/status.go): Invalid (structural) outranks all; then any error -> NonCompliant; else any unknown -> Unknown; else any warning -> Warning; else Compliant. Reference-only contracts short-circuit to Reference.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: A finding is one conclusion from the engine. Findings fall in two families. Confirmed violations (RuntimeDrift, error) need evidence that clearly contradicts the contract. Uncertainty findings (Inconclusive, unknown) mean the evidence could neither confirm nor refute it. A code listed under two severities is an error when the claim it reports on is required and a warning when it is optional, because an optional claim cannot make a contract non-compliant. Generated from pkg/finding/codes.go.
